Then: "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ...", thrice. Psalm 50. And the kissing of the Gospel. Then Glory... "Through the prayers of the Apostles, O Merciful One..."; Both now... "Through the prayers of the Mother of God..."; after this, the sticheron, Tone 6:*

Jesus, having risen from the tomb, as He foretold, hath given unto us eternal life and great mercy.

*Then: "O God, save Thy people..."; and straightway the Canon of the Feast, the composition of John the Monk.*

*Tone 1. The Heirmos twice, and the troparia to 12. Katavasia: "The Day of Resurrection...", both choirs together.*[^449]

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*

Let us all, O ye peoples, sing a song of victory unto Him Who delivered Israel from the bitter bondage of Pharaoh, and led them dryshod through the depth of the sea: for He is glorified.

*Refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*

*Troparion:*

Today is springtime for souls: because Christ, like the sun having shone forth on the third day from the tomb, hath driven away the dark tempest of our sin; let us sing unto Him: for He is glorified.

*Troparion:*

The queen of seasons, most manifestly bringing gifts unto the light-bearing day, the queen of days, adorns the chosen people of the Church, unceasingly singing unto the risen Christ.

*Troparion:*

Neither the gates of death, O Christ, nor the seals of the tomb, nor the bolts of the doors resisted Thee: but having risen, Thou didst stand before Thy friends, O Master, granting peace that surpasses all understanding.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

Establish me, O Christ, upon the immovable rock of Thy commandments, and enlighten me with the light of Thy countenance: for there is none holy above Thee, O Lover of mankind.

*Troparion:*

Having made us new instead of old, and incorruptible instead of corruptible, by Thy Cross, O Christ, Thou hast commanded us to live worthily in renewal of life.

*Troparion:*

Enclosed within the tomb in Thy circumscribed flesh, O uncircumscribed Christ, Thou didst rise; and though the doors were shut, Thou didst stand before Thy disciples, O Almighty One.

*Troparion:*

Having preserved for Thy disciples Thy wounds, which of Thine own will Thou didst endure for our sake, O Christ, Thou didst show them as evidence of Thy glorious Resurrection.

*Hypakoe, Tone 6:*

As Thou camest into the midst of Thy disciples, O Savior, granting them peace: come also unto us, and save us.

*And the reading from the Theologian [Saint Gregory], whereof the beginning is: "It is an ancient law to honor renewals..."*

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

Great is the mystery of Thy dispensation, O Christ: for Habakkuk, beholding God, foresaw this from on high, and cried aloud unto Thee: Thou didst go forth for the salvation of Thy people, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparion:*

Having tasted gall, Thou didst heal the ancient tasting; and now with a honeycomb, Christ gave illumination unto our forefather, and His sweet communion.

*Troparion:*

Thou rejoicest when examined: therefore, O Lover of mankind, Thou dost command Thomas unto this, stretching forth Thy Side unto the disbeliever, confirming Thy third-day Rising unto the world, O Christ.

*Troparion:*

Having drawn wealth from the unstolen divine treasure, O Benefactor, from Thy Side pierced with a spear, the Twin fills the world with wisdom and understanding.

*Troparion:*

Thy most blessed tongue is praised, O twin: for it first piously proclaims the Life-giver Jesus, both God and Lord, filled with grace from touching.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

Rising early from the night, we hymn Thee, O Christ, co-unoriginate with the Father, and Savior of our souls: grant peace unto the world, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparion:*

Standing before His sorrowing friends, the Savior by His coming takes away all sorrow, and rouses them to leap for joy by His Resurrection.

*Troparion:*

O truly lauded and fearful undertaking of Thomas! For boldly he touched the Side that shines with divine fire.

*Troparion:*

Thou hast shown the disbelief of Thomas to be the begetter of faith for us: for in Thy wisdom Thou providest all things profitably, O Christ, as the Lover of mankind.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

Thou didst save the Prophet from the sea monster, O Lover of mankind: lead me up also from the depth of transgressions, I pray Thee!

*Troparion:*

Thou didst not leave Thomas engulfed by the depth of disbelief, O Master, stretching forth Thy palms for examination.

*Troparion:*

Our Savior said: Touch Me, and see that I bear bones and flesh; I have not changed.

*Troparion:*

Thomas touched the Side, and having believed, he recognized Him, though he was not present at Thy first entrance, O our Savior.

*Kontakion, Tone 8:*[^450]

With an inquisitive right hand, Thomas examined Thy life-giving Side, O Christ God: for when Thou didst enter though the doors were shut, he cried aloud unto Thee with the rest of the Apostles: Thou art my Lord and my God!

*Ikos:*

Who preserved the disciple's hand unburnt at that time, when he approached the fiery Side of the Lord? Who gave it boldness, and enabled it to touch the flaming bone, altogether untouchable? For if the Side had not imparted power unto the earthen right hand, how could it have touched the wounds that shook things above and things below? This grace was given unto Thomas, to touch these things, and to cry aloud unto Christ: Thou art my Lord and my God!

*Synaxarion for the Sunday of Saint Thomas.*

*Verses:*
*If the seals or keys of the tomb hindered not / Thy course, O Savior, how should the locks of the doors hinder it?*

On this Sunday we celebrate the Renewal of Christ's Resurrection, and the Touching of the holy Apostle Thomas. For it was an ancient custom that renewals should take place: when a certain notable event, as years roll by, occurred on that day on which it had been accomplished, they kept the memory of that thing active, lest those great deeds should fall into oblivion; and in manifold ways, as was done of old with the festival of Tabernacles, and others, not to speak of each one in detail; and the Lord's Resurrection itself—a deed more excellent and higher than all things pertaining unto life, and surpassing all thought—we not only celebrate and renew each year, but continually also after eight days: for the first renewal of this is the present Sunday, which is truly called both the eighth and the first: the eighth, indeed, as being from Pascha; and the first, as the beginning of the others; and again the eighth, as being set forth as an image of that unending day in the age to come, which shall be the first and altogether one, not divided by night. These things, then, concerning renewals.

Now that which concerns Thomas came about thus: when Christ appeared late unto the disciples on the very day on which He arose, Thomas was not there; for he had not gathered together with the others because of the fear of the Jews. Then, having arrived a little later, and having learned of Christ's appearance, he did not believe—not only that the disciples had seen Him risen, but that the Lord had risen at all; and he being one of the Twelve, God, Who is marvelous in wisdom, taking such care for even one, and together with this by a greater dispensation that the Resurrection might be even more confirmed for those who should come after, permitted eight days to elapse: that He might thoroughly sharpen his love, and that he who had disbelieved more than all might furnish unto all a more certain assurance of the Resurrection; He comes again, and the doors being shut as before, Thomas also being present, He enters; and having imparted the customary peace, thereafter He stretches forth unto Thomas, and says: "Bring hither thy finger, and behold My hands; and bring thy hand, and thrust it into My Side; and be not unbelieving, but believing: for since thou didst seek to be confirmed not only by sight, holding the common things of vision to be a phantom, but being forward, didst also demand touch"; and by these words He showed that when Thomas had spoken these things unto the disciples, He had heard him: "Thrust thy hand into My Side"; and it shows that the wound upon the Side was broad, so as even to admit a hand within it. And Thomas, having examined carefully and received faith through touch—[for it was permitted him to see these things and to do them, even unto a Body altogether incorruptible and deified]—cried aloud at that examination: "My Lord and my God!"—the one because of the flesh, and the other because of the Godhead. And Christ says unto Thomas: "Because thou hast seen Me, thou hast believed; blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed."

Now Thomas is called the Twin: either because he was born with another, or because of his doubting concerning the Resurrection, or because by nature two fingers of his right hand were conjoined together—namely, the middle finger and that which is before it, called the forefinger—as one might say, because he was to doubt and to touch with them; and others say, which is more certain, that the name Thomas is interpreted "Twin". This was the second appearance of Christ; the third was at the Sea of Tiberias at the catching of the fish, when He also partook of food baked by divine fire, as He Himself knows, prefiguring the most certain Resurrection; then He appears at Emmaus; the fifth time in Galilee unto the Eleven, as they say; and He continued to appear until He ascended, working many and supernatural signs before the disciples after the Resurrection; which things, having shown them unto not many, the Evangelists omitted to write down all of them, since it was not possible for many men living in the world to hear them, being exceedingly supernatural. By the prayers of Thine Apostle Thomas, O Christ our God, have mercy upon us. Amen.[^451]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

When musical harmony summoned the people to worship the image, the youths of David, singing ancestrally from the songs of Zion, destroyed the tyrant's wicked decree, and changed the flame into dew, chanting the hymn: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers, Who art supremely exalted!

*Troparion:*

As this day is the first of days and the Lord's own radiant day, wherein it is meet for the new and divine people to rejoice with trembling: for it also bears the image of the age to come, as an eighth day fulfilling that which is to come: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers, Who art supremely exalted!

*Troparion:*

Thomas the Twin, alone daring, but having benefited us by his disbelieving faith, dispels the dark ignorance of all the ends of the earth by his faithful disbelief, and openly weaves a crown for himself, saying: Thou art the Lord God of our fathers, Who art supremely exalted, blessed art Thou!

*Troparion:*

Not in vain did Thomas doubt concerning Thy Rising: he was not cast down, but was zealous to show this beyond doubt unto all nations, O Christ; whence, having assured all through his disbelief, he taught them to say: Thou art the Lord God of our fathers, Who art supremely exalted, blessed art Thou!

*Troparion:*

Having with fear thrust his hand into Thy life-giving Side, O Christ, Thomas with trembling perceived the twofold operation, O Savior, unconfusedly united in Thee in two natures; and in faith he cried aloud, saying: Thou art the Lord God of our fathers, Who art supremely exalted, blessed art Thou!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

Him Who preserved the Children in the fiery burning furnace, and descended unto them in the form of an Angel: praise ye the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*

Having longed for Thy joyful sight, Thomas previously disbelieved; but having been vouchsafed thereof, he called Thee God and Lord, O Master, Whom we supremely exalt unto all ages.

*Troparion:*

Him Who patiently endured the disbelief of Thomas, and showed His Side, and was touched by his hand: praise ye the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*

Thy treasure difficult to attain, kept secret, Thomas hath opened unto us: for theologizing with a God-bearing tongue, he said: Praise ye the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*We do not sing "More honorable than the Cherubim".*

*We sing the refrains of the Ninth Ode:*
*Magnify, O my soul, Him Who came forth as man from hades, and granted us the Resurrection.*
*Magnify, O my soul, Him Who assured the disbelief of Thomas.*

*Then the Heirmos:*

Thee, the radiant lamp, and Mother of God, the most marvelous glory, and higher than all creatures, in hymns we magnify.

*Troparion:*

Thy radiant day and most radiant grace, O Christ, wherein Thou, comely in beauty, didst stand before Thy disciples, in hymns we magnify.

*Troparion:*

Thee, touched in the Side by an earthen hand, which was not consumed by the fire of the immaterial Divine Essence, in hymns we magnify.

*Troparion:*

Thee, as Christ God risen from the tomb, not having seen with our eyes, but having believed with heartfelt love, in hymns we magnify.

*Katavasia: "Shine, shine..."*

*Then: "Holy is the Lord our God", in Tone 1, thrice.*

*Exaposteilarion, Tone 1, Podoben: "Thou Who didst adorn heaven with stars" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ ѕвѣзда́ми):*[^452]

Having examined the wounds of My limbs with thy hand, be not faithless unto Me, O Thomas, Who was wounded for thy sake: be of one mind with the disciples, and proclaim the living God. *(Twice)*

*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen.*

Today spring breathes sweet fragrance, and the new creation dances; today the keys of the doors are taken away, and of the disbelief of Thomas the friend, who cries aloud: My Lord and my God!

*At the Praises, 4 stichera:*

*Tone 1, Podoben: "O all-lauded martyrs" (Прехва́льнїи мꙋ́ченицы):*

After Thy fearful Rising from the tomb, O Giver of life, just as Thou didst not break the seals of the sepulchre, O Christ, so when the doors were shut didst Thou enter unto Thine all-glorious Apostles, making them joyful, and granting them Thy right Spirit, according to Thy boundless mercy.

Thomas, who is also called the Twin, had not come when Thou didst appear unto the disciples, O Lord; therefore he disbelieved Thy Resurrection, and cried aloud unto those who had seen Thee: Unless I thrust my finger into His Side, and into the wounds of the nails, I will not believe that He is risen.

Touch as Thou desirest, Christ cried aloud unto Thomas: Thrust thy hand, and know Me to have bones, and an earthly body, and be not faithless, but be assured equally with the others! And he cried aloud: Thou art my God and Lord, glory to Thy Rising!

*Glory... Tone 6:*

After eight days from Thy Rising, O Jesus King, Only-begotten Word of the Father, Thou didst appear unto Thy disciples when the doors were shut, imparting Thy peace; and unto the disbelieving disciple Thou didst show the tokens: Come and touch My hands and feet, and My incorruptible Side! And he, having believed, cried aloud unto Thee: My Lord and my God, glory to Thee!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen.*
*Thou art most blessed...*
*The Great Doxology.*
*And the Troparion of the Feast. The litanies, and the dismissal.*
*And from today the litiya processions begin, that is, processions into the narthex. Likewise also the catecheses of our venerable father Theodore the Studite,[^453] at which we chant: Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen., the Evangelical Sticheron, Tone 1:*

When the disciples were going up into the mountain for the earthly ascension, the Lord stood before them; and having worshipped Him, and having been instructed concerning the authority given everywhere, they were sent into all the world under heaven, to proclaim the Resurrection from the dead, and the Ascension into the heavens; with whom also Christ God, the Savior of our souls, being true, promised to remain unto the ages.

*Take heed that the litiya processions in the narthex take place before the First Hour, and the catecheses of the Studite. And the First Hour. And the rest as customary. And the full dismissal.*

*Be it known that the office of the saints that fall on all the Sundays of Holy Pentecost, we chant at Compline. The Liturgy is celebrated early on account of the labor of the Vigil. The Hours are chanted in three psalms according to the Typikon in the narthex, at which we say the Troparion and Kontakion of the Feast.*

*Be it known that from the New Sunday until the Apodosis of the Feast of Pascha, the beginning of the Liturgy takes place thus: After the deacon says: "Bless, Master", and the priest: "Blessed is the Kingdom": the priest chants: "Christ is risen...", thrice, the entire troparion, without the verses: "Let God arise..." Then the litany, and the rest of the Liturgy.*

*Instead of "It is truly meet", we chant:*
*The Angel cried aloud unto her that is full of grace: Pure Virgin, rejoice! And again I say, rejoice! Thy Son is risen on the third day from the tomb, and hath raised the dead: O ye people, make merry!*
*Then the Heirmos: "Shine, shine..." And when the priest says: "With the fear of God...", we say: "Blessed is He that comes in the name of the Lord; God is the Lord and hath appeared unto us." The priest: "O God, save Thy people..."; and instead of the troparion: "We have seen the true Light", we chant: "Christ is risen...", once; and so until the Apodosis of Pascha. And the rest of the Liturgy takes place according to custom. And at the dismissal, when he says: "Glory to Thee, O Christ God, our hope, glory to Thee", we say: "Christ is risen...", thrice. Then the dismissal of the Liturgy according to custom.*

*At the Liturgy we begin the Typika [Beatitudes], and we chant at the Beatitudes, from the Canon of the Feast, Odes 3 and 6.*
*After the Entrance, the Troparion: "Though the tomb was sealed..."; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen., the Kontakion: "With an inquisitive right hand..."*

*Prokeimenon of the Apostle, Tone 3:*
*Great is our Lord, and great is His power, and of His understanding there is no number. (Ps. 146:5)*
*Verse:*

*Verse: Praise ye the Lord, for a psalm is good: to our God let praise be sweet. (Ps. 146:1)*

*The Reading from the Acts of the Apostles, pericope 14 (Acts 5:12-20):*[^454]
*In those days, by the hands of the Apostles...*

*Alleluia, Tone 8:*
*Come, let us rejoice in the Lord; let us shout with jubilation unto God our Savior. (Ps. 94:1)*
*Verse: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King over all the earth. (Ps. 94:3)*

*The Reading from the Holy Gospel according to John, pericope 65 (John 20:19-31):*
*The same day at evening... Communion Hymn: Praise the Lord, O Jerusalem; praise thy God, O Zion! (Ps. 147:1). Alleluia, thrice.*

*At the table there is great consolation for the brethren. And having risen from the table, we recite all the things written previously on Saturday of Bright Week.*

## ON THE SUNDAY OF ANTIPASCHA, AT VESPERS

*After the priest gives the blessing, we say: "Christ is risen...", thrice.*
*Then the Trisagion; after "Our Father...": "Lord, have mercy", 12 times. "Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen.": "O come, let us worship...", thrice. And we recite the customary Ninth Hour in three psalms. The Troparion and Kontakion of the Feast.*
*Then we chant Vespers without a kathisma.*
*At "Lord, I have cried", we chant in Tone 1. 6 stichera: 3 of the Feast:*

*Tone 1, Podoben: "O all-lauded martyrs" (Прехва́льнїи мꙋ́ченицы):*

After Thy fearful Rising from the tomb, O Giver of life, just as Thou didst not break the seals of the sepulchre, O Christ, so when the doors were shut didst Thou enter unto Thine all-glorious Apostles, making them joyful, and granting them Thy right Spirit, according to Thy boundless mercy.

Thomas, who is also called the Twin, had not come when Thou didst appear unto the disciples, O Lord; therefore he disbelieved Thy Resurrection, and cried aloud unto those who had seen Thee: Unless I thrust my finger into His Side, and into the wounds of the nails, I will not believe that He is risen.

Touch as Thou desirest, Christ cried aloud unto Thomas: Thrust thy hand, and know Me to have bones, and an earthly body, and be not faithless, but be assured equally with the others! And he cried aloud: Thou art my God and Lord, glory to Thy Rising!

*And 3 prosomoia of the saint from the Menaion. Glory... of the saint. If there is none:*
*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the Feast, Tone 1:*

When the doors were shut and the disciples were gathered together, Thou didst suddenly enter, O Almighty Jesus our God; and standing in their midst, having given peace, Thou didst fill them with the Holy Spirit; and Thou didst command them to wait, and by no means to depart from Jerusalem, until they should be clothed with power from on high: therefore we cry aloud unto Thee: O our Enlightenment, and Resurrection, and Peace, glory to Thee!

*The Entrance.*
*O Gladsome Light.*

*Great Prokeimenon, Tone 7:*[^455]
*Who is so great a god as our God? Thou art the God Who workest wonders. (Ps. 76:14)*
*Verse: Thou hast made known Thy power among the peoples. (Ps. 76:15)*
*Verse: And I said: Now have I begun; this is the change of the right hand of the Most High. (Ps. 76:11)*
*Verse: I remembered the works of the Lord; for I will remember Thy wonders from the beginning. (Ps. 76:12)*
*And again: Who is so great a god as our God? Thou art the God Who workest wonders.*

*Then the litany: "Let us all say..."; and "Vouchsafe, O Lord, this evening..."; and the litany: "Let us complete our evening prayer unto the Lord..."*

*At the Aposticha, a sticheron of the Octoechos.*
*Tone 1:*
Accept our evening prayers, O Holy Lord, and grant us remission of sins: for Thou alone art He Who hath revealed the Resurrection in the world.

*Verse: Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes, O Thou that dwellest in heaven. Behold, as the eyes of servants look unto the hands of their masters... (Ps. 122:1-2a)*
*Penitential [Katanyktikon]:*
As a great abyss is the multitude of my transgressions, O Savior, and grievously am I engulfed by my sins: give me a hand, as unto Peter, O God, and save me, and have mercy upon me!

*Verse: Have mercy upon us, O Lord, have mercy upon us: for we are utterly filled with contempt. (Ps. 122:3a)*
*Martyricon:*
By the supplications, O Lord, of all the saints and of the Mother of God, grant us Thy peace, and have mercy upon us, as Thou alone art compassionate.

*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 1:*
After eight days from Thy Rising, O Lord, Thou didst appear unto Thy disciples in the place where they were gathered; and having proclaimed unto them: Peace be unto you! Thou didst show Thy hands and Thy most pure Side unto the disbelieving disciple; and he, having believed, cried aloud unto Thee: My Lord and my God, glory to Thee!

*Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart in peace...*
*After the Trisagion, the Troparion of the Feast. But if there is a troparion of the saint, say it first. Then: Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen., of the Feast: "Though the tomb was sealed..."; and the dismissal.*

*Thus takes place the order of Vespers on all Sundays of Holy Pentecost.*
*From today we say Small Compline. And we chant the Supplicatory Canon of the Most Holy Mother of God in the Octoechos, and the triodia of the Triodion of the day, the creation of Lord Joseph.[^456] Wherever we recite a triodion, the ode of the Canon of the Mother of God is omitted.*
*After "It is truly meet", and after "Our Father...", we say the Kontakion of the Feast, throughout the entire Pentecostarion.*
*At the Liturgies, there is chanted at the Beatitudes, from the Canon of the Feast of the Sunday, the assigned ode for each day, with the Heirmos, to 6.*
*Thus: on Monday, Ode 1; on Tuesday, Ode 4; on Wednesday, Ode 5; on Thursday, Ode 7; on Friday, Ode 8; on Saturday, Ode 9.*

## ON MONDAY OF THOMAS WEEK, AT MATINS

*When the priest has made the beginning: "Glory to the holy...": We say: "Christ is risen...", thrice, in a quiet voice.*
*For this beginning, "Christ is risen...", we say at the beginning of every service—that is, at Matins, at the Hours, at Vespers, and at Compline—from this Matins of the Sunday of Antipascha even unto the Ascension of the Lord.*
*[As for the Midnight Office, it is not specified, as it is evident that this is chanted privately in the cells, since there also the beginning is thus made].[^457] And straightway after "Christ is risen...": "Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace..."; and the customary Six Psalms; the Great Litany. Then "God is the Lord", in Tone 7; the Troparion of the Feast: "Though the tomb was sealed...", thrice.*
*This troparion is recited throughout the entire week.*
*And we recite two kathismata of the Psalter, and the third in course at Vespers. And thus we chant the Psalter until the 24th of September.*

*After the First Kathisma, a resurrectional Sessional Hymn.*
*Tone 1:*
While the soldiers were guarding Thy tomb, O Savior, they became as dead men at the lightning flash of the Angel who appeared, proclaiming the Resurrection unto the women: Thee do we glorify, the Destroyer of corruption; before Thee do we fall down, Who didst rise from the tomb, our only God!

*Verse: O Lord, rebuke me not in Thine anger, nor chasten me in Thy wrath. (Ps. 6:1)*
*Penitential [Katanyktikon]:*
In iniquities was I, the prodigal, conceived, and I dare not look up unto the height of heaven; yet daring upon Thy love for mankind, I cry aloud: O God, cleanse me a sinner, and save me!

*Verse: Marvelous is God in His saints, the God of Israel. (Ps. 67:36)*
*Martyricon:*
With the boast of suffering and the dignity of crowns were the glorious passion-bearers robed by Thee, O Lord: for by endurance of wounds they conquered the lawless, and by divine power from heaven they received the victory: by their prayers, O Savior, deliver me from the invisible enemy, and save me!

*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*
Beholding in thee the miracle of miracles, O full of grace, creation rejoices: for thou didst conceive without seed, and didst bear ineffably Him Whom the ranks of Angels cannot behold: Him, as God, entreat for our souls!

*Then a reading from the Commentary on the Gospel of John.*[^458]

*After the Second Kathisma, a Sessional Hymn.*
*Tone 1, Podoben: "While the soldiers were guarding Thy tomb" (Гро́бъ тво́й):*

Having touched with his hand the unendurable Side, Thomas the Twin was not consumed by the touch, but continued examining the wounds more thoroughly, and believed on Him Who was pierced for our sake: Thou art my Lord and my God, even though Thou hast suffered Passion!

*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. The same. And a reading.*

*Then: "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ...", once, and Psalm 50.*
*For thus we do until the Ascension of the Lord. And we make the beginning from the heirmoi, which we also repeat; and we chant the troparia to 6, and 4 of the saint from the Menaion.*
*After the Third Ode, the Kontakion and Sessional Hymn of the saint; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen., Sessional Hymn of the Feast.*
*After the Sixth Ode, the Kontakion and Ikos of the Feast. And we recite the Magnifications ["More honorable than the Cherubim"].*
*After the Ninth Ode, the Exaposteilarion of the Feast, twice; Glory... of the saint, if there is one; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen., the other Exaposteilarion of the Feast.*

*At the Praises, we set 3 stichera of the Octoechos, to 4.*
*Tone 1:*

We hymn Thy saving Passion, O Christ, and we glorify Thy Resurrection. *(Twice)*

*Penitential [Katanyktikon]:*

Another world awaits thee, O my soul, and the Judge is about to expose thy hidden and grievous deeds: abide not therefore in things here below, but anticipate, crying aloud unto the Judge: O God, cleanse me and save me!

*Martyricon:*

O passion-bearers of Christ, come, all ye people, let us honor them with hymns and spiritual songs, the luminaries of the world and preachers of the faith, the ever-flowing fountain from which healings pour forth unto the faithful: by their prayers, O Christ our God, grant peace unto the world, and unto our souls great mercy!

*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 1:*

Thomas, called the Twin, was not with them when Thou didst enter, O Christ, when the doors were shut; therefore he did not believe what was told him, passing from disbelief into assurance of faith: nor didst Thou refuse, O God, to show him Thy most pure Side, and the wounds of Thy hands and feet; and having touched and seen, he confessed Thee to be not bare God, nor mere man, and he cried aloud: My Lord and my God, glory to Thee!

*Then: "Glory to Thee Who hast shown us the light!"*
*And the litany: "Let us complete our morning prayer unto the Lord..."*

*At the Aposticha, stichera.*
*Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме Є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*

With pure lips, O ye men, chant together with the Angels unto Him Who arose on the third day from the tomb, and hath raised the world with Himself!

*Verse: Praise the Lord, O Jerusalem: praise thy God, O Zion! (Ps. 147:1)*

Thou didst appear, O Savior, unto Thine holy Apostles when the doors were shut, through them renewing for us Thy divine Spirit.

*Verse: For He hath strengthened the bars of thy gates; He hath blessed thy children within thee. (Ps. 147:2)*

Now beholding Thee, O King of all, not with our eyes, but with the love of our heart, believing Thee to be God, we magnify Thee in hymns.

*Glory... of the saint, if there is one; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 1:*

When the disciples were doubting, on the eighth day the Savior stood in the place where they were gathered; and having imparted peace, He cried aloud unto Thomas: Come, O Apostle, touch the palms into which they drove the nails! O good disbelief of Thomas, which brought the hearts of the faithful unto understanding, and with fear cried aloud: My Lord and my God, glory to Thee!

*Troparion of the Feast: "Though the tomb was sealed..."; then the litany: "Have mercy upon us, O God..."; after this the priest: "Blessed is Christ our God Who is..."; Choir: "Establish, O God...";*
*And straightway we join the First Hour, in three psalms, according to custom. Troparion and Kontakion of the Feast, and of the saint. But if the saint is ranked with 4 stichera, the Kontakion of the Feast is recited without change, and the Kontakion of the saint is not said.*
*And the full dismissal takes place. And the customary litiya procession in the narthex.*
*And from today we also begin the Inter-Hours [Mesoria],[^459] according to the prescribed Typikon.*
*And it should be known: just as the headpiece was written here on Sunday evening with the Lucernarium prayers, and on Monday at Matins, so let it be done in all the weeks until the Ascension of the Lord, taking the stichera of the Octoechos and the sessional hymns according to custom.*
*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the Triodion, Ode 1, of the Feast, to 6. And from this day throughout all Pentecost. After the Entrance, the Troparion of the Feast: "Though the tomb was sealed..."; and of the temple of the Mother of God, and of the temple of the saint. After this, of the saint of the day, if there is one. Then the Kontakion of the temple of the saint; and: Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen., of the Feast: "With an inquisitive right hand..." But the Kontakion of the temple of Christ and of the Mother of God we do not say throughout all Pentecost.*

*Prokeimenon of the Apostle, Tone 3:*
*Great is our Lord, and great is His power, and of His understanding there is no number. (Ps. 146:5)*
*Verse: Praise ye the Lord, for a psalm is good. (Ps. 146:1)*

*The Reading from the Acts of the Apostles, pericope 8 (Acts 3:19-26):*[^460]
*Peter said unto the people: Repent ye...*

*Alleluia, Tone 8: Come, let us rejoice in the Lord... (Ps. 94:1)*
*Verse: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King over all the earth. (Ps. 94:3)*

*The Reading from the Holy Gospel according to John, pericope 6 (John 2:1-11):*
*There was a marriage in Cana of Galilee... Communion Hymn: Praise the Lord, O Jerusalem... (Ps. 147:1). And throughout the entire week we do thus, and in all the fifty days across all the weeks. And the rest of the order of the Liturgy. And the dismissal.*

*It should be known that these TRIODIA in the former printed Triodia were printed to be chanted at the Liturgies; but among the Greeks they are recited at Compline together with the Canon of the Mother of God (wherever there is a Triodion, the odes of the Canon to the Mother of God are omitted); while at the Liturgies they chant from the Canon of the Feast, for each day one ode, thus: on Sunday, Odes 3 and 6; on Monday, Ode 1; on Tuesday, Ode 4; on Wednesday, Ode 5; on Thursday, Ode 7; on Friday, Ode 8; on Saturday, Ode 9.*[^461]

*Yet because in our Slavonic codices these Triodia are set down here, we also, not opposing concordant custom, have arranged them throughout all Pentecost.*

*On Monday of Thomas Week, the Triodion,*
*whose acrostic is: ᾄδει δὲ σὲ Ἰωσήφ, that is: JOSEPH ALSO HYMNS THEE.*[^462]

*Tone 1. Ode 1. Heirmos:*

Thy victorious right hand hath been glorified in power in manner becoming God: for it, O Immortal One, being almighty, shattered the adversaries, having made a new way through the deep for the Israelites.

*Troparion [A]:*

Let us chant unto God, as unto the Victor Who by death hath overthrown death, and hath raised up with Himself the human race, and hath most richly honored those in incorruption.

*Troparion [D]:*

Having been bound, as mighty Thou didst tear asunder the bonds of death by Thy strength; and having delivered men from corruption, Thou didst raise from hades those who praise Thy dominion, O Plenteous in mercy!

*Glory...*
*Troparion [E]:*

O Compassionate Christ, Who for my sake wast willingly even unto hades: having raised me up by Thy visitation, who lie in the tomb of sin and in the pit of transgressions, have mercy!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion [I]:*

Having beheld Christ risen in the flesh from the dead, O Mother of God, thou didst rejoice: entreat Him also to grant me now joy-making weeping, that I may then find divine consolation, O Pure One!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

In the furnace the Children of Israel, as in a crucible, in the beauty of piety shone purer than gold, saying: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; praise the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion [D]:*

By Thy Cross Thou hast dissolved the curse; and having been laid in the tomb, O my Jesus Christ, Thou didst overthrow the dark kingdom of hades; and having risen, Thou didst raise all creation with Thyself: therefore we hymn Thee unto all ages!

*Troparion [E]:*

When Thou didst ascend upon the Cross, the sun was extinguished; but when Thou didst descend into hades, O Lover of mankind, light shone forth unto the souls that were in darkness and buried under bitter death: therefore we hymn Thee unto all ages!

*Glory...*
*Troparion [S]:*

Bound with the cords of sins, loose me, O Christ, and illumine me with the divine radiance of repentance, O Savior, delivering men from eternal darkness by Thy fearful Rising, which we hymn unto all ages!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion [E]:*

O Virgin, who didst bear in thine arms Christ incarnate from thee: entreat Him now to accept me also, who have wandered in every dissolute way of life and through innumerable sins, my sluggish disposition always meeting me!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

The unburnt bush showed the types of thy pure childbearing, being burned with fire and yet unconsumed; and now we pray thee to quench the furnace of temptations raging against us: that we may unceasingly magnify thee, O Mother of God!

*Troparion [I]:*

When the sun beheld Thee crucified in the midst of thieves, O Word, the Sun that knows no setting, it was darkened; and the mountains, the hills, the earth, and the sea shrank back; hades trembled, having loosed the prisoners which it held, who hymn Thee.

*Troparion [O]:*

Thou didst appear as the great Sun, having gone down beneath the earth, and Thou didst shine forth as the never-setting Luminary from the dead, gloriously illumining the ends of the earth: therefore, O Giver of life, unceasingly we magnify Thee!

*Troparion [S]:*

O Savior Jesus, Who by Thy death didst destroy death, and having risen didst release all that were held captive there: raise me also who am in the lowest pit, subject unto deadly passions and sins, as I cry aloud unto Thee, O Lover of mankind!

*Glory...*
*Troparion [E]:*

The Myrrh-bearing Women came weeping early unto the tomb; and not having found Thee, they saw an Angel sitting before them in white robes, and crying aloud: The Lord is risen; make haste to proclaim the Rising unto His disciples!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion [Ph]:*

All creation is amazed, O Sovereign Lady, at the mystery of thy childbearing surpassing understanding: for thou, all-immaculate one, barest God Emmanuel, Who became man for our sake, and hath destroyed the tyrannies of death by His Cross!

## ON MONDAY OF THOMAS WEEK, AT VESPERS

*At "Lord, I have cried", we set 6 verses, and we chant prosomoia stichera.*
*Tone 4, Podoben: "As one valiant among martyrs" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*[^463]

Having risen from the tomb, when the doors were shut, Thou didst stand before Thy friends, O Almighty One; and unto Thomas who had disbelieved, Thou didst show the wounds of the nails, and Thy Side, which was pierced by the spear, confirming and assuring him, O Word, that Thou art He Thyself Who for loving-kindness didst endure the saving Passions.

Beholding My emptying, according to My great condescension and boundless mercy, doubt not, but be assured, O Twin, the Lord said: for I Myself am He Who suffered, and on the third day arose from the tomb, and emptied the treasures of hades, and gave life unto those dead from the ages!

Being amazed when he beheld, Thomas cried aloud when he saw Thee, O Almighty One: Thou art my God and Lord! I believe, O Lover of mankind, that Thou art He Thyself Who suffered and healest the passions of our souls; I bow down before Thy dominion, and I proclaim unto the world Thy fearful and almighty Rising!

*And 3 of the Menaion.*
*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 1:*

When the disciples were doubting, on the eighth day the Savior stood in the place where they were gathered; and having imparted peace, He cried aloud unto Thomas: Come, O Apostle, touch the palms into which they drove the nails! O good disbelief of Thomas, which brought the hearts of the faithful unto understanding, and with fear cried aloud: My Lord and my God, glory to Thee!

*O Gladsome Light.*
*At the Aposticha, stichera.*
*Tone 1:*

Encompass Zion, O ye peoples, and embrace it, and give glory within it unto Him Who is risen from the dead: for He is our God, Who hath delivered us from our iniquities.

*Verse: Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes, O Thou that dwellest in heaven. Behold, as the eyes of servants look unto the hands of their masters... (Ps. 122:1-2a)*

Because by evil thoughts and deeds I am condemned, O Savior: grant me a mind of turning, O God, that I may cry aloud: Save me, O Good Benefactor, and have mercy upon me!

*Verse: Have mercy upon us, O Lord, have mercy upon us: for we are utterly filled with contempt. (Ps. 122:3a) For the Martyrs:*

Your confession before the judgment-seat, O holy ones, spat upon the demonic power and delivered men from delusion; therefore also when your heads were severed, ye cried aloud: May the sacrifice of our souls be acceptable before Thee, O Lord; for having loved Thee, we took no thought for temporal life, O Lover of mankind!

*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 2:*

After Thy Resurrection, O Lord, when Thy disciples were gathered and the doors were shut, Thou didst stand in the midst, imparting peace unto them; and Thomas, having believed by the beholding of Thy hands and Thy ribs, confessed Thee to be Lord and God, Who savest them that hope in Thee, O Lover of mankind!

*Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart... Festal Troparion: "When the stone had been sealed..." (see fol. 250)[^464] And the Dismissal.*

## ON TUESDAY OF THOMAS WEEK, AT MATINS

*At "God is the Lord", the festal Troparion, thrice.*

*After the first stichology, Sessional Hymn.*
*Tone 1, Podoben: "When the stone had been sealed" (Ка́мени запеча́танꙋ):*

The women came early unto the tomb, and having seen the angelic vision, they trembled; the tomb shone forth life, the wonder amazed them; therefore, having gone, they proclaimed the Resurrection unto the disciples: Christ hath despoiled hades, as alone mighty and powerful, and hath raised up together all that were corrupt, having destroyed the fear of condemnation by the Cross!

*Verse: O Lord, rebuke me not in Thine anger, neither chasten me in Thy wrath. (Ps. 6:2)*

If the righteous scarcely be saved, where shall I appear, a sinner, who have not borne the burden and heat of the day? But number me with the laborers of the eleventh hour, O God, and save me![^465]

*Verse: God is marvelous in His saints, the God of Israel. (Ps. 67:36 [68:35])*
*For the Martyrs:*

As good soldiers, having believed with one accord, ye feared not the threats of the torturers, O holy ones; ye went forth zealously unto Christ, having taken up the precious Cross; and having finished your course, ye received victory from heaven. Glory to Him Who strengthened you! Glory to Him Who crowned you! Glory to Him Who through you works healings for all!

*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*

Having the Theotokos Mary as an unbreakable wall, O ye faithful, come, let us bow down and fall before Her; for She hath boldness toward Him Who was born of Her, both to pray and to save our souls from wrath and death.

*After the second stichology, Sessional Hymn.*
*Tone 5, Podoben: "The Word co-unoriginate" (Собезнача́льное Сло́во):*

Let us all praise in hymns Christ's Apostle and disciple in his memory; for having touched the wounds of the nails and sought out certain faith, he faithfully confirmed our thoughts in the world, and he prays to the Savior that our souls may be shown mercy.

*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. The same.*
*Then: "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ..." Psalm 50.*
*Canon of the feast with the Heirmos to 8; and of the Menaion to 4.*
*After the Sixth Ode, Sessional Hymn of the Menaion; Kontakion and Exaposteilarion of the feast.*
*At the Praises, stichera to 4.*

Thou Who didst endure the Cross, and didst abolish death, and didst rise from the dead: give peace unto our life, O Lord, as alone almighty! *(Twice)*

Despise me not, O my Savior, who am held fast by sinful slothfulness: raise up my mind unto repentance, and show me forth as a skilled laborer of Thy vineyard, granting me the reward of the eleventh hour, and great mercy!

*For the Martyrs:*

These soldiers of the Great King valiantly resisted the commands of the torturers, took no thought for torments, and having trampled down all delusion and been worthily crowned, they ask of the Savior peace and great mercy!

*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 2:*

When the doors were shut, Jesus, having stood before the disciples, gave fearlessness and peace; then He saith unto Thomas: Why dost thou not believe Me, that I arose from the dead? Bring hither thy hand and put it into My ribs, and see; for because thou didst disbelieve, all have learned to cry aloud with thee unto My Passions and My Resurrection: My Lord and my God, glory to Thee!

*At the Aposticha, stichera of the feast.*
*Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме Е҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*

Let us, O faithful, unceasingly hymn with the Angels Christ risen on the third day from the tomb, and Who hath raised up the world together with Himself!

*Verse: Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world. (Ps. 18:5 [19:4])* Thomas, having touched Thy ribs, O Compassionate One, ascended unto faith, and through him we have henceforth known Thee as God!

*Verse: The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims the work of His hands! (Ps. 18:2 [19:1])*

Thou dost bestow peace upon Thy people, O Redeemer, having risen from the tomb and raised up the world together with Thyself from hades, O Almighty One!

*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 6. By John the Monk:*[^466]

When the doors were shut, Thou camest, O Christ, unto the disciples; then Thomas by divine dispensation was not found with them, for he said: I will not believe unless I also behold the Master; I shall behold the ribs whence came forth blood, water, baptism; I shall behold the wound whence the great human sore was healed; I shall behold how He was not like a spirit, but flesh and bones! O Thou Who hast trampled down death and assured Thomas: Lord, glory to Thee!

*Dismissal Troparion, and the Dismissal.*

*On Tuesday of Thomas Week, Triodion.*
*Tone 1. Whose acrostic is: Ψαλῶ Θεῷ Ἰωσήφ, that is: I Joseph will sing unto God.*[^467]

*Ode 2. Heirmos:*

See, see that I am God, Who commanded Moses to guide the enslaved people of Israel in the wilderness, and saved them as mighty by My power!

*Troparion [Ps]:*

Let us sing today unto the Lord, crying aloud unto Him Who was crucified for our sake, and cast down the author of evil, the enemy, and was laid in the tomb, and brought the dead to life by His Resurrection!

*Troparion [A]:*

Holy is the Lord Who arose from the dead on the third day as Mighty, Who appeared creditably unto the disciples, and filled with ineffable joy their souls, which before were filled with sorrow!

*Glory...*
*Troparion [L]:*

O Word co-beginningless, enthroned together with the unoriginate Father, Who wast crucified and numbered among the dead, and didst rise as Mighty: quicken my soul, which hath been put to death by transgressions!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion [O]:*

O thy wonders! O fearful hearing! For in the flesh thou bearest God, Who hath dissolved the bonds of death and delivered men from corruption, O pure, God-graced Lady!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

Him Whom the Angels and all the hosts dread as Creator and Lord: praise, ye priests; glorify, ye children; bless, ye peoples, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion [Th]:*

All creation laments at Thy Passion, O Good One; the sun was darkened when Thou didst set upon the Cross, and they that sat in darkness beheld a great light, praising Thee, O Bountiful One!

*Troparion [E]:*

Hades trembled when it beheld Thee coming unto it with Thy soul, O Christ, King of all, and gave up the dead from the ages, who hymn Thy love for mankind!

*Glory...*
*Troparion [O]:*

Thou didst appear, O Christ, having risen from the tomb, unto the godly women that brought spices, and didst transform their lamentation, being the Consolation of all unto ages!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion [I]:*

Having seen Him Whom thou barest, God, risen from the dead, thou wast shown forth full of joy, O Virgin Mary; Him therefore implore, O pure one, utterly to consume every sorrow of our heart!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

The light-bearing cloud, whereon the Master of all descended as rain from heaven upon the fleece, and was incarnate for our sake, having become man, the Unoriginate: all of us magnify as the pure Mother of our God!

*Troparion [O]:*

When he beheld Thee crucified upon the Tree, the wise thief cried aloud: Remember me, O Jesus, when Thou comest in Thy Kingdom! And he became a dweller of Paradise, having been justified by faith alone.

*Troparion [S]:*

When hades beheld Thee among the dead, O Savior, it was slain, and gave up the dead whom it had swallowed of old, that glorified, O Christ, Thine ineffable power and much tender mercy, whereby Thou hast saved us, O King of all!

*Glory...*
*Troparion [I]:*

The women that brought myrrh came unto the tomb, and having seen Thee, O Christ, risen from the tomb, they were filled with great joy, and proclaimed unto Thine Apostles that Thou art risen and hast appeared, having raised up the whole world together with Thyself!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion [Ph]:*

Having seen the never-setting Light that shone forth from the dead, O pure one, and having been filled with great joy, thou didst rejoice with the all-holy disciples, with whom do thou also entreat for us the forgiveness of immeasurable transgressions, O Theotokos, Protectress of the faithful!

## ON TUESDAY OF THOMAS WEEK, AT VESPERS

*At "Lord, I have cried", we set 6 verses, and we chant prosomoia stichera.*
*Tone 1, Podoben: "O all-lauded martyrs" (Прехва́льнїи мꙋ́ченицы):*[^468]

Touch, saith the Lover of mankind Who arose on the third day from the dead unto Thomas, and behold the wounds of My hands and feet, and the piercing of My ribs; and know Me to be the changeless God, fashioned according to essence in earthly mixture, and having accepted passion therein!

The Twin was in perplexity as he beheld the wounds healed and the piercings of the hands, and he was struck with awe by the fearful wonder; and touching with his hand and beholding the most pure rib, from these he showed forth unto the nations the undoubted three-day Resurrection from the tomb!

I receive exceeding great joy, beholding Thy Resurrection confirmed, O my Savior, whereof Thomas was vouchsafed to touch with daring deed; therefore we proclaim Thee to be simple God and man, bearing two essential operations, whereof Thou art composed![^469]

*And 3 of the Menaion.*
*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 2:*

O Lord, with the unendurable lightning of Thy Divinity, when the doors were shut Thou camest, and having stood in the midst of the disciples, Thou didst lay bare Thy rib, and displaying the wounds of the sores of Thy hands and feet, dissolving their grief and sorrow, Thou didst openly proclaim: In like manner as ye behold in Me, O friends, the assumption of flesh, I bear not the nature of a spirit! And unto the doubting disciple Thou didst command to touch with trembling, saying: Having examined all, come henceforth, doubt not! And he, feeling with his hand Thy twofold essence, with fear cried aloud, drawn by faith: My Lord and my God, glory to Thee![^470]

*O Gladsome Light.*
*At the Aposticha, Cross-sticheron. Tone 1:*

The Cross was planted on the Place of the Skull, and immortality blossomed forth for us from the ever-flowing spring of the Savior's rib.

*Verse: Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes, O Thou that dwellest in heaven. Behold, as the eyes of servants look unto the hands of their masters... (Ps. 122:1-2a [123:1-2a])*

Come, ye peoples, let us hymn and bow down before Christ, glorifying His Resurrection from the dead; for He is our God, Who hath delivered the world from the enemy's delusion!

*Verse: Have mercy upon us, O Lord, have mercy upon us: for we are utterly filled with contempt. (Ps. 122:3a [123:3a]) For the Martyrs:*

O your good barter, O holy ones! For ye gave blood and inherited heaven, and having been tried for a time, ye rejoice eternally; truly good was your barter: for having left corruptible things, ye received incorruptible things; and rejoicing with the Angels, ye unceasingly hymn the consubstantial Trinity!

*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 8:*

Touch My ribs with thy hand, O Thomas, saith Christ, and come, feel the wounds of the nails; examine with faith, and be thou faithful unto Me, and be not faithless! And when Thomas touched the Master with his finger, he cried aloud with a great voice: Thou art my God and Lord, O Compassionate One, glory to Thee!

*Then: "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart..." Dismissal Troparion: "When the stone had been sealed..." (see fol. 250)[^471] Litany, and the Dismissal.*

*Be it known that on Wednesday and Friday the Cross-stichera precede, as do also the Resurrectional Sessional Hymns: because our Lord was first crucified, and after this arose from the dead.*[^472]

## ON WEDNESDAY OF THOMAS WEEK, AT MATINS

*At "God is the Lord", the festal Troparion, thrice.*

*After the first stichology, Cross-Sessional Hymn.*
*Tone 1:*

When Thou wast crucified, O Christ, tyranny perished, the power of the enemy was trampled down; for neither an Angel nor a man, but Thou Thyself, O Lord, hast saved us: glory to Thee!

*Verse: Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship at His footstool; for He is holy. (Ps. 98:5 [99:5])*

Isaac was led up unto the hill, Jonah was cast down into the deep, and both prefigured Thy Passion, O Savior: the one indeed the bonds and slaughter, and the other the Burial and the life of Thy most glorious Resurrection: O Lord, glory to Thee![^473]

*Verse: God is marvelous in His saints, the God of Israel. (Ps. 67:36 [68:35])*

By the sufferings which the holy ones endured for Thy sake, be Thou entreated, O Lord, and heal all our sicknesses, O Lover of mankind, we pray!

*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Stavrotheotokion:*

Having thy protection, O all-pure one, and being delivered from cruel ills by thy prayers, preserved everywhere by the Cross of thy Son, as is our due we all piously magnify thee.

*After the second stichology, Sessional Hymn.*
*Tone 1, Podoben: "While the soldiers were guarding Thy tomb" (Гро́бъ тво́й Сп҃се):*[^474]

The Twin Thomas, having touched with his hand the unendurable ribs, was not burned by the touching; but he continued feeling the wounds more certainly, and believing in Him Who was pierced for our sake: Thou art my Lord, and Thou art my God, though Thou didst endure passion!

*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. The same.*
*Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ... Psalm 50.*
*Canon of the feast with the Heirmos to 8; and of the Menaion to 4.*
*After the Sixth Ode, Sessional Hymn of the Menaion; Kontakion and Exaposteilarion of the feast.*
*At the Praises, the present Cross-stichera to 4.*
*Tone 1:*

Thee Who wast nailed upon the Tree and didst grant us life, as Savior and Master we unceasingly hymn! *(Twice)*

Thou Who didst despoil hades, and didst raise up man by Thy Resurrection, O Christ: vouchsafe us with a pure heart to hymn and glorify Thee!

*For the Martyrs:*

Neither tribulations, nor distress, nor famine, nor persecution, nor wounds, nor the fury of wild beasts, nor the sword, nor threatening fire were able to separate you from God, O all-lauded martyrs; but rather through love for Him, as if contending in alien bodies, ye forgot nature and despised death; therefore also according to the worthiness of your labors ye received reward, and became heirs of the Heavenly Kingdom. Having boldness toward God the Lover of mankind, entreat peace for the world, and for our souls great mercy!

*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 8:*

When the doors were shut and the disciples were gathered, the Savior stood where they were assembled, and having stood in their midst, He saith unto Thomas: Come, feel, and see the marks of the nails; stretch forth thy hand and touch My ribs, and be not faithless, but with faith proclaim My Resurrection from the dead!

*At the Aposticha, stichera.*
*Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме Е҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*

O new wonder! O most glorious sight! How was the grass not consumed, the Apostle's hand, by the fire of the Godhead?

*Verse: Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world. (Ps. 18:5 [19:4])*

Let us also strive to cleanse our hands by the cessation of passions, and thus let us touch the Master's ribs!

*Verse: The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims the work of His hands! (Ps. 18:2 [19:1])*

Renew, O soul, all thy senses unto divine contemplation; for Christ thus desires: to be perfected by renewal!

*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion. Podoben:*

Behold for me thoughtfully the transformation of the world, and adorn that which is within with virtues as with foliage, O soul, and thou shalt be adorned!

*Then: "It is good to give thanks..." The First Hour, and the Dismissal.*

*On Wednesday of Thomas Week, Triodion.*
*Whose acrostic is: Αἰνῶ Θεόν, Ἰωσήφ, that is: I praise God, Joseph.*[^475]

*Tone 1. Ode 3. Heirmos:*

Unto the Son begotten incorruptibly of the Father before the ages, and in these last days incarnate without seed of the Virgin, Christ God, let us cry aloud: Thou Who hast exalted our horn, holy art Thou, O Lord!

*Troparion [A]:*

O Holy of holies, desiring to sanctify the world, Thou wast voluntarily lifted up upon the Tree of the Cross and slain as a lamb, and by Thy beneficent Blood Thou renewest us that hymn Thee!

*Troparion [I]:*

The strength of the enemy was taken away, death was made captive, corrupt human essence was made immortal, when Thou wast put to death, O Christ Jesus; and the world was renewed, crying aloud: Holy art Thou, O Lord!

*Glory...*
*Troparion [N]:*

Now be ye not amazed! the Angel cried aloud unto the women: Go ye rather zealously, proclaiming words of joy unto the grieving disciples, that Christ is risen, the Life of all and the Resurrection!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion [O]:*

Thou wast shown forth higher than the Angels, O pure Virgin, having incarnate God Who was crucified and buried, and Who poured forth incorruption for the dead: Him do thou entreat to save us that hymn thee!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

The dew-bearing furnace prefigured an image of a supernatural wonder; for it burned not the youths whom it had received, even as neither did the fire of the Godhead burn the Virgin's womb into which it entered; therefore chanting let us sing: Let all creation bless the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion [Th]:*

Thou didst voluntarily accept death, being lifted up in the flesh upon the Tree, and beholding Thee, the sun was extinguished, and the temple veil was rent in twain, O Almighty One; therefore chanting unto Thee we cry: Let all creation bless the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto ages!

*Troparion [E]:*

They that of old sat in the shadow of death beheld Thee, the never-setting Radiance; and when Thou, O Lord, didst descend unto them with Thy soul, they were loosed from eternal bonds, greatly hymning Thee and saying: Let all creation bless the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto ages!

*Glory...*
*Troparion [O]:*

The women having come early unto the tomb beheld a shining Angel, who said: The Redeemer is risen; why do ye still think of the Living among the dead? Being filled with joy, cry ye aloud: Let all creation bless the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto ages!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion [N]:*

Thy Son, O pure one, wrought slaying unto hades, even as He said before, having risen from the dead; Him do thou entreat, that deliverance from corrupting sin and torment may be granted unto all that cry aloud with faith: Let all creation bless the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

A strange and most glorious mystery do I behold: heaven, the cave; the Cherubic throne, the Virgin; the manger, the receptacle: wherein reclined the Uncontainable, Christ God, Whom chanting we magnify!

*Troparion [I]:*

Healing the infirmities of the first-created, Thou wast pierced by a spear voluntarily upon the Tree, O Savior; and having been laid in the lowest pit, Thou didst raise up the dead whom death was able previously to swallow up!

*Troparion [O]:*

When the choir of the Apostles of old beheld Thee risen, O Lord, it bowed down with fear and joy; and unto them Thou didst cry aloud: Behold the fulfillment of My words; grieve ye not, but rejoice!

*Troparion [S]:*

Having wrapped Thee in a winding sheet, righteous Joseph with love laid Thee in a new tomb, O Savior; and having shattered the gates of hades, both bars and bolts, Thou didst raise up the dead whom death was able previously to swallow up!

*Glory...*
*Troparion [I]:*

The myrrh-bearing women rejoiced, having heard of Christ's Resurrection; therefore they cried aloud unto the Apostles: Running with haste, behold, no longer grieve ye, but rejoice: for the Lord of all is risen from the dead!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion [Ph]:*

Beholding Christ, shining completely in beauty without compare, as a Bridegroom come forth in the flesh from the bridal chamber of the tomb, O Maiden, thou wast filled with joy; Him do thou entreat to deliver us from corruption and torment!

## ON WEDNESDAY OF THOMAS WEEK, AT VESPERS

*At "Lord, I have cried", we set 6 verses, and we chant prosomoia stichera.*
*Tone 2, Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Є҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*[^476]

Without having left the Father's bosom, Thou appearedst on earth bearing flesh through tender compassion, O Christ; and having accepted the Passion and death, Thou didst rise on the third day; when the doors were shut Thou didst enter within, as almighty; therefore Thomas, having touched Thy divine rib with joy, glorified Thee as Lord and Creator!

With nails Thou wast nailed upon the Cross, with a spear Thou wast pierced in the ribs, of gall Thou didst taste, O Christ; Thou didst endure death, having been laid in the tomb as dead, but as God Thou didst shatter the bonds of hades, and didst raise up together the dead from the ages; therefore, without having broken the seals, Thou appearedst unto Thy disciples, confirming Thy Resurrection!

Pascha is the present feast: mystical Pascha, divine Pascha, saving Pascha, Pascha that leads us over unto immortal life, Pascha that removs every sorrow from our midst, Pascha that gives all-embracing grace unto the disciples! Therefore Thomas cried aloud: Thou art my Lord and God, Who hast made captive the kingdoms of hades![^477]

*And 3 of the Menaion.*
*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 4:*

O most marvelous wonder! Disbelief hath given birth to most certain faith; for Thomas said: Unless I see, I will not believe; but having touched the ribs, he theologizes Him Who was incarnate, and recognized Him to be the same Son of God, as having suffered in the flesh; he proclaimed the risen God, and cried aloud with a radiant voice: My Lord and my God, glory to Thee![^478]

*At the Aposticha, Resurrectional sticheron.*
*Tone 1:*

By Thy Passion, O Christ, we have been set free from passions, and by Thy Resurrection we have been delivered from corruption: O Lord, glory to Thee!

*Verse: Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes, O Thou that dwellest in heaven. Behold, as the eyes of servants look unto the hands of their masters... (Ps. 122:1-2a [123:1-2a])*

The all-honorable apostolic harp, moved by the Holy Spirit, hath abolished the shrines of shameless demons; and having proclaimed the one Lord, it delivered the nations from idolatrous delusion, and taught them to worship the Consubstantial Trinity!

*Verse: Have mercy upon us, O Lord, have mercy upon us: for we are utterly filled with contempt. (Ps. 122:3a [123:3a])*
*For the Martyrs:*

O all-lauded martyrs, the earth hid you not, but heaven received you; the gates of paradise were opened unto you, and having entered within, ye delight in the Tree of Life: pray unto Christ, that He grant our souls peace and great mercy!

*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 4:*

O most marvelous wonder! Grass touching fire was preserved; for Thomas, having put his hand into the fiery ribs of Jesus Christ God, was not burned by the touching; for having transformed the evil belief of his soul into good faith, he warmly cried aloud from the depths of his soul: Thou art my Master and God, Who art risen from the dead, glory to Thee![^479]

*Then: "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart..." The Trisagion. And after "Our Father": Festal Troparion, and the Dismissal.*

## ON THURSDAY OF THOMAS WEEK, AT MATINS

*At "God is the Lord", the Troparion of the feast, thrice.*
*After the 1st stichology, Sessional Hymn, Tone 1. Podoben: "When the stone had been sealed" (Ка́мени запеча́танꙋ):*

Thou wast nailed to the Cross, O Life of all, and wast numbered among the dead, O immortal Lord; Thou didst rise on the third day, O Savior, raising Adam up with Thyself from corruption; therefore the heavenly hosts cried aloud unto Thee, O Giver of life: Glory to Thy divine Passion, O Christ! Glory to Thy Resurrection! Glory to Thy condescension, O Thou Who alone lovest mankind!

*Verse: Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world. (Ps. 18:5a [19:4a])*

O most wise fishers of the inhabited earth, having received mercy from God, pray even now for us who cry aloud: O Lord, save the Emperor,[^480] and Thy city, and from surrounding afflictions deliver our souls!

*Verse: God is marvelous in His saints, the God of Israel. (Ps. 67:36a [68:35a])*
*Tone 1, Podoben: "While the soldiers were guarding Thy tomb" (Гро́бъ тво́й Сп҃се): For the Martyrs:*[^481]

All we entreat Christ's martyrs, for they make intercession for our salvation, and let us all draw near unto them in faith; they pour forth the grace of healings, they drive away demonic hosts, as guardians of the faith.

*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*

The prophets clearly proclaimed thee beforehand, O Maiden, to be the Mother of God, and the divine Apostles proclaimed it in the world, and we have believed; therefore all we, honoring thee with pious mind, hymn thee, and truly ever name thee the Mother of God.

*After the 2nd stichology, Sessional Hymn, Tone 1. Podoben: "While the soldiers were guarding Thy tomb" (Гро́бъ тво́й Сп҃се):*

Beholding My ribs, do not disbelieve Me, O impetuous one,[^482] cried the Word unto Thomas who disbelieved: touch Me with thy finger, and examine with thy hand; and having recognized the marks of My wounds, proclaim unto the world My life-bearing Resurrection from the tomb!

*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. The same.*
*Having seen the Resurrection of Christ... Psalm 50.*
*Canon of the feast, with the heirmoi to 8, and of the Menaion to 4.*
*After Ode 3, Sessional Hymn of the Menaion. Kontakion and Exapostilarion of the feast.*

*At the Praises, stichera to 4. Tone 1. Resurrectional:*

Glorifying Thy divinely fitting condescension, we hymn Thee, O Christ: Thou wast born of the Virgin, yet wast not separated from the Father; Thou didst suffer as man, and of Thine own will didst endure the Cross; Thou didst rise from the tomb as from a bridal chamber, that Thou mightest save the world: O Lord, glory to Thee!

*Twice.*

Peter and Paul let us praise in unison, Luke, Matthew, Mark, John, Andrew, Thomas, Bartholomew, Simon the Cananaean, James, Philip: and the entire assembly of the disciples let us worthily extol!

*For the Martyrs:*

Rejoice in the Lord, O martyrs, for ye fought the good fight: ye resisted emperors, and vanquished tyrants; ye feared neither fire nor sword, nor wild beasts devouring your bodies; sending up song unto Christ with the Angels, from Whom ye received crowns from heaven, pray that peace be granted unto the world, and unto our souls great mercy!

*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 8:*

O most marvelous wonder! John reclined upon the breast of the Word, and Thomas was counted worthy to touch the ribs; but the one drew forth dreadly from thence the profound mystery of theology, while the other was counted worthy to initiate us into mystery, presenting clear proof of His Rising, crying aloud: My Lord and my God, glory to Thee![^483]

*At the Aposticha, stichera.*
*Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме Еѵ҆фра́ѳовъ):*[^484]

Let the sorrow of passions and the tempest of thoughts be driven far away, and so let the springtime of faith blossom forth!

*Verse: Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world. (Ps. 18:5a [19:4a])*

Thou appearedst, O Savior, unto Thine holy Apostles when the doors were shut, renewing through them the Holy Spirit for us this day.

*Verse: The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims the work of His hands. (Ps. 18:2a [19:1a])*

Now beholding Thee, O King of all, not with eyes of flesh, but having believed in God with heartfelt love, with songs we magnify Thee.

*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 6:*

After eight days from Thy Resurrection, O Jesus the King, Only-begotten Word of the Father, Thou appearedst unto Thy disciples when the doors were shut, granting Thy peace, and unto the disbelieving disciple Thou didst show the tokens: Come, and touch My hands and feet, and My incorruptible ribs; and he, having believed, cried aloud unto Thee: My Lord and my God, glory to Thee!

*First Hour, and the Dismissal.*

*On Thursday of Thomas Week, Triodion,*
*Whose acrostic is: Ὑμνῳδία Ἰωσήφ, that is:*
*The Hymnody of Joseph:*[^485]
*Tone 1. Ode 4. Heirmos:*

Let the prophet Habakkuk, crying aloud of God, stand with us upon the divine watch, and show forth a radiant Angel clearly saying: Today is salvation come unto the world, for Christ is risen, as almighty!

*Troparion (Υ):*
For the sake of us humble ones Thou wast led unto death, O Christ, the Life of all; and having made captive the realms of hades, Thou didst snatch away souls as sheep, raising them up with Thyself, as a mighty and all-powerful King!

*Troparion (Μ):*
Why seek ye the Living among the dead? The Angel, flashing radiant upon the tomb, appeared unto the women and said: He is risen! Come, behold the grave-clothes lying alone, and make haste to announce it unto His disciples!

*Glory... (Ν)*
Hades was slain by the descent of Christ; utterly despoiled, it gave up all the dead, and its all-devouring belly was brought completely to naught by the all-powerful will of God, the King of all!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion (Ω):*
As into a most beautiful temple, Jesus the King of all took up His abode in thee, O pure Virgin; yet by His descent He brought to naught the murky dwelling of hades, and arose, raising mankind up with Himself, as almighty!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

This chosen and holy day is the first of Sabbaths, the king and lord of feasts, and the triumph of triumphs, on which we bless Christ unto the ages!

*Troparion (Δ):*
Glory to Christ, Who cast down the enemy and made hades captive by His descent unto it, and Who made alive the dead whom it had power to swallow, that they may hymn Him unto the ages!

*Troparion (Ι):*
Behold, the Angel flashing radiant cried aloud unto the myrrh-bearing women: Having seen the place where He was laid, Who by His own power made death and hades captive, no longer seek the Living among the dead!

*Glory... (Α)*
Hades was embittered, meeting Thee below, O Word, being unable to draw near unto Thee; and those dead whom it had swallowed it quickly gave up at Thy command, singing in unison the praise of Thy dominion!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion (Ι):*

Thou didst behold Him Who is risen from the dead, O Virgin, the Word Whom thou didst ineffably bear in the flesh, and thou didst fill thy soul with joy, hymning His descent, O pure Lady, unto all ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

Shine, shine, O new Jerusalem, for the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee! Dance now and be glad, O Zion, and thou, O pure Mother of God, rejoice in the rising of Thy Child!

*Troparion (Ω):*
Being the Creator of hours and days, O Redeemer, in the day and at the sixth hour Thou didst willingly endure the Crucifixion as guilty, O compassionate Lord, that Thou mightest still our reproaches and reconcile us unto the Father!

*Troparion (Σ):*
Hades groaned, having met Thee, O Redeemer, and quickly released the prisoners whom it held, who with divine voices hymn Thy power beyond comprehension, O Word, and Thy dread condescension!

*Glory... (Η)*
The women came with myrrh early in the morning with haste to anoint the most pure Body, and the bodiless one said unto them: The Author of life is risen; be ye filled with divine joy!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion (Φ):*
Having borne the Light that shone forth upon those sitting in darkness and the shadow of death, when thou didst behold Him, O all-immaculate Lady, risen from the dead, do thou with all the myrrh-bearing women glorify Him, rejoicing!

## ON THURSDAY OF THOMAS WEEK, AT VESPERS

*At "Lord, I have cried", we set 6 verses, and we chant prosomoia stichera.*
*Tone 1, Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly hosts" (Небе́сныхъ чино́въ):*[^486]

Arrayed in the garment of righteousness, whiter than snow, let us rejoice in the present day of Pascha, in which Christ, having shone forth from the dead as the Sun of Righteousness, hath illumined all of us with incorruption!

The King and Lord, the feast of feasts is the present day, which in truth the Lord hath made: in it, as David sings, let us mystically rejoice, O ye people; for unto the disciples when the doors were shut He granted peace!

The disbelief of Thomas, which touched more boldly with inquiring right hand the wounds of hands and feet, confirms unto the whole world the world-saving Rising of the God-Man Word from the prison of hades!

*And 3 of the Menaion.*
*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 2:*

When the doors were shut, Jesus stood before the disciples, granting fearlessness and peace; then He saith unto Thomas: Why dost thou not believe Me, that I am risen from the dead? Bring hither thy hand, and place it into My ribs, and see; for through thy disbelief all have learned to call upon My Passion and My Resurrection, crying with thee: My Lord and my God, glory to Thee!

*O Gladsome Radiance:*
*At the Aposticha, stichera.*
*Tone 1. For the Cross:*

An unbreakable wall unto us is the precious Cross of the Savior; for hoping in it, all we are saved.

*Verse: Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes, O Thou that dwellest in heaven. (Ps. 122:1a [123:1a])*
*Resurrectional:*

Accept our evening prayers, O holy Lord, and grant us remission of sins, for Thou alone art He Who hath manifested the Resurrection unto the world!

*Verse: Have mercy upon us, O Lord, have mercy upon us. (Ps. 122:3a [123:3a])*
*For the Martyrs:*

By the prayers of all the saints and of the Mother of God, O Lord, grant us Thy peace, and have mercy upon us, as Thou alone art compassionate!

*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 8:*

Touch My ribs with thy hand, saith Christ, and come, feel the marks of the nails: examine with faith, and be believing unto Me, and be not disbelieving. And Thomas, when he touched the Master with his finger, cried aloud with a loud voice: Thou art my God and Lord, O compassionate One, glory to Thee!

*Then: "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart..."*
*And the rest as usual, as was indicated beforehand.*

## ON FRIDAY OF THOMAS WEEK, AT MATINS

*At "God is the Lord", the Troparion of the feast, thrice.*
*After the 1st stichology, Sessional Hymn.*
*Tone 1, Podoben: "When the stone had been sealed" (Ка́мени запеча́танꙋ):*[^487]

We venerate the Tree of Thy Cross, O Lover of mankind, for upon it Thou wast nailed, O Life of all; Thou didst open paradise, O Savior, unto the thief who came unto Thee with faith, and he was counted worthy of delight, confessing Thee: Remember me, O Lord! Receive even as that one also us who cry: We all have sinned; in Thy tender compassion despise us not!

*Verse: Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship the footstool of His feet, for He is holy. (Ps. 98:5 [99:5])*
*Resurrectional:*

The soldiers guarding Thy tomb, O Savior, became as dead from the gleaming of the Angel who appeared, proclaiming the Resurrection unto the women: Thee do we glorify, the Destroyer of corruption; before Thee do we fall down, Who didst rise from the tomb, and our only God!

*Verse: God is marvelous in His saints, the God of Israel. (Ps. 67:36a [68:35a])*
*For the Martyrs:*

With the praise of suffering and the honor of crowns were the glorious passion-bearers clothed by Thee, O Lord; for by the endurance of wounds they vanquished the lawless, and by the power of God received victory from heaven; by their prayers, O Christ God, grant us great mercy!

*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Stavrotheotokion:*
*Tone 1, Podoben: "While the soldiers were guarding Thy tomb" (Гро́бъ тво́й Сп҃се):*[^488]

The undefiled Ewe-lamb, beholding hanging dead upon the Tree the Lamb and Shepherd, lamented and cried aloud with a mother's voice: How shall I endure Thy condescension beyond all telling, O my Son, and Thy voluntary Passions, O most good God?

*After the 2nd stichology, Sessional Hymn.*
*Tone 1, Podoben: "While the soldiers were guarding Thy tomb" (Гро́бъ тво́й Сп҃се):*

Blessed art thou, who didst feel the wounds of the exalted rib; this greatest wonder, which healed Adam and procured for us who have believed the bliss that was lost, through the very words of the honored Apostles, is His Resurrection!

*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. The same.*
*Then: Having seen the Resurrection of Christ... Psalm 50.*
*Canon of the feast, with the heirmoi, to 8;*
*And of the Menaion to 4.*
*After Ode 3, Sessional Hymn of the Menaion.*
*Kontakion and Exapostilarion of the feast.*
*At the Praises, stichera to 4.*
*Tone 1. For the Cross:*

By Thy Cross, O Christ, there became one flock of Angels and men, and one Church; heaven and earth rejoice: O Lord, glory to Thee!

*Twice.*

*Resurrectional:*

We hymn Thy saving Passion, O Christ, and we glorify Thy Resurrection!

*For the Martyrs:*

O passion-bearers of Christ, come, all ye people, let us honor them with songs and spiritual hymns: the luminaries of the world and preachers of the faith, the ever-flowing fountain from which healings pour forth unto the faithful; by their prayers, O Christ our God, grant peace unto the world, and unto our souls great mercy!

*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 8. By Anatolius:*

When the doors were shut and the disciples were assembled, the Savior stood where they were gathered; and standing in the midst of them, He saith unto Thomas: Come, feel and see the marks of the nails; stretch forth thy hand and touch My ribs, and be not disbelieving, but with faith proclaim My Resurrection from the dead!

*At the Aposticha, stichera of the feast.*
*Tone 4, Podoben: "As noble among the martyrs" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*[^489]

Having been crucified, Thou didst open paradise unto men, and didst raise up together the dead, O our Life; and Thou didst rise, having made death captive by Thy power, and didst unite earthly things in truth unto heavenly things, and didst fill the apostolic choir with boundless joy, O Word of God, Who Thyself didst announce peace!

*Verse: Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world. (Ps. 18:5a [19:4a])*

Corruption hath been overthrown, incorruption hath blossomed forth, the temporary bond hath been broken; let the heavens rejoice, the earth, and the nether regions! For Christ is risen, death is made captive, the joyful day hath appeared; when the doors were shut, Thou didst enter within, O Giver of life and Lord!
