## ON THE SUNDAY OF THE MYRRH-BEARING WOMEN, AT VESPERS

*At "Lord, I have cried", we set 6 verses, and chant 3 stichera of the feast. Stichera of the feast:*

*Tone 5, Podoben: "Rejoice, O container of ascetics" (Ра́дꙋйся по́стникѡмъ):*
Nailed with nails, Thou didst destroy through the Tree the curse which came upon the tree; laid in a tomb, Thou didst raise by Thy divine power those who had died from the ages, who loudly glorify Thy power: O divine Pascha, Jesus our joy, our Life, Radiance of the Father! Therefore the heavenly things rejoice with the earthly, chanting songs of victory unto Thee, O victorious Word, Christ Almighty, Who grantest unto the world great mercy!

Behold, Life is with the dead, and the unwaning Sun is beneath the earth even now! The choir of Myrrh-bearing women cried aloud, lamenting: Come, let us hasten diligently, and let us see at the tomb of the Holy One! But seeing an Angel shining within it, they were perplexed and dismayed; and he, changing their lamentation, cried aloud: The Giver of life is risen! Be not dismayed, ye noble women: He blossoms forth, granting unto the world great mercy!

Early in the morning the women's choir sought the existing Sun before the sun, Who had then set into the tomb; and the radiant Angel proclaimed unto them: The Light hath shone forth, illuminating those who sleep in darkness! Announce ye unto the radiant disciples, turn weeping into joy, and singing with unwavering heart celebrate the joyful and world-saving Pascha: Christ is risen, granting unto the world great mercy!

*And 3 of the Menaion.*

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 1:*
O Myrrh-bearing women, why came ye unto the tomb? Why seek ye the Living among the dead? The Lord is risen; be of good cheer! cries the Angel.

*Then: "O Gladsome Light..."*

*At the APOSTICHA, the Resurrectional sticheron. Tone 2:*
Come, let us worship God the Word, Who was begotten of the Father before the ages, and became incarnate of the Virgin Mary; for having endured the Cross, He was delivered over unto Burial, as He Himself willed; and having risen from the dead, He saved me, an erring man!

*Verse: Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes, O Thou that dwellest in heaven. (Ps. 122:1 LXX)*

*Penitential [sticheron]:*
I have sinned against Thee, O Savior, like the prodigal son; receive me, O Father, as I repent, and have mercy upon me, O God!

*Verse: Have mercy upon us, O Lord, have mercy upon us: for we are utterly filled with contempt. (Ps. 122:3 LXX)*

*Martyricon:*
Having not loved earthly enjoyment, the passion-bearing martyrs were accounted worthy of heavenly good things, and became fellow-citizens with the Angels; O Lord, by their prayers, have mercy and save us!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 1:*
With fear the women came unto the tomb, hastening to anoint Thy Body with spices; and having not found It, they were perplexed one with another, not knowing of the Resurrection; but an Angel stood before them and said: Christ is risen, granting unto us great mercy!

*Then: "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart..." Troparion: "The noble Joseph..." Glory... "When Thou didst descend...", Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. "Unto the Myrrh-bearing women..." If the saint has a troparion, we say first the troparion: "The noble Joseph...", Glory... of the saint, Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. "Unto the Myrrh-bearing women..." Troparion: "The noble Joseph...", and the Resurrectional troparion: "When Thou didst descend unto death..." In the evening we say them alternating throughout the entire week, even as was shown concerning this previously, and the Litany, and the Dismissal.*[^531]

*The service of the saint of the Menaion that occurred on this Sunday is chanted at Compline. After the Trisagion, one Kontakion of the Triodion for the feast. Thus do we say even until the Sunday of All Saints.*

## ON MONDAY OF THE MYRRH-BEARING WOMEN, AT MATINS

*The customary beginning, even as was indicated on Monday of the second week after Pascha.*[^532]

*At "God is the Lord", Troparion, Tone 2: "The noble Joseph...", twice. Glory... "When Thou didst descend...", Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. "Unto the Myrrh-bearing women..." These troparia are said thus throughout the entire week. If there is a troparion of the saint, we say the troparion first: "The noble Joseph...", once; and the troparion: "When Thou didst descend...", once; Glory... of the saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. "Unto the Myrrh-bearing women..."*

*After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 2:*
Having not hindered the sealing of the sepulchral stone, in rising Thou didst grant unto all the rock of faith: O Lord, glory to Thee!

*Verse: O Lord, rebuke me not in Thine anger, neither chasten me in Thy wrath. (Ps. 6:2 LXX)*

Like the waves of the sea mine iniquities have risen up against me, and like a ship in the deep, I alone am submerged by many sins; but guide me, O Lord, by repentance unto a quiet haven, and save me!

*Verse: Wondrous is God in His saints, the God of Israel. (Ps. 67:36 LXX)*

*Martyricon:*
Having Thee, Who clothest heaven with clouds, as their vesture, the saints endured torments from the lawless in the world, and abolished the deceit of idols; by their prayers free us also from the invisible enemy, O Savior, and save us!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*
Being a fountain of compassion, account us worthy of mercy, O Mother of God; look down upon the people who have sinned; show forth as always thy power: for hoping in thee, we cry aloud unto thee "Rejoice!", even as once did Gabriel, the Archistrategos of the bodiless hosts!

*And a reading.*

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn.*
*Tone 2, Podoben: "Seeking the highest" (Вы́шнихъ и҆щѧ̀):*
The women fervently brought myrrh unto the tomb, O Savior; they gladdened their souls with the brightness of the Angel, and proclaimed Thee to be the God of all, crying aloud unto the disciples: Truly from the tomb is the Life of all risen!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. The same.*

*And a reading. Then: "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ...", once.*

*The Canon of the Myrrh-bearing Women, with the heirmoi to 8, and the Menaion to 4.*[^533]

*After Ode 3, the Sessional Hymn of the saint.*

*After Ode 6, the Kontakion of the feast: "Thou didst command the Myrrh-bearing women to rejoice...", and the Ikos.*

*And we read the Prologue.*[^534] *The Exapostilarion of the Myrrh-bearing Women.*

*Glory... of the saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the Myrrh-bearing Women.*

*At the PRAISES, stichera on 4. Tone 2:*

*Sticheron:*
Every breath and all creation glorifies Thee, O Lord, for by the Cross Thou didst abolish death, that Thou mightest show forth unto the peoples Thy Resurrection from the dead, as the only Lover of mankind! Twice.

*Sticheron:*
Reflecting upon the enormity of the grievous deeds done by me, I flee unto Thy compassions, imitating the publican, the weeping harlot, and the prodigal son; therefore I also fall down before Thee, O Merciful One: before Thou judgest me, spare me, O God, and have mercy upon me!

*Martyricon:*
Having suffered for Christ even unto death, O passion-bearing martyrs: ye have your souls in the hand of God in the heavens, and throughout all the world your relics are venerated, priests and kings and kings bow down, and all peoples rejoice, and we customarily cry aloud: Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His saints! (Ps. 115:6 LXX)

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 2:*
Magdalene and the other Mary came unto the tomb seeking the Lord; and they saw an Angel sitting like lightning upon the stone, and saying unto them: Why seek ye the Living among the dead? He is risen, as He said; in Galilee shall ye find Him; unto Whom let us cry aloud: O Thou Who art risen from the dead, Lord, glory to Thee!

*At the APOSTICHA, stichera of the feast.*

*Tone 6, Podoben: "Having risen on the third day" (Тридне́венъ):*
Begin, O ye people, with psalms; chant unto Christ with joy: a great Pascha hath shone forth unto us; Christ the Giver of life, and the Redeemer of all creation, is risen from the tomb!

*Verse: Thou hast been favorable, O Lord, unto Thy land; Thou hast turned back the captivity of Jacob. (Ps. 84:2 LXX)*

*Sticheron:*
Having said "Rejoice" unto the Myrrh-bearing women, Thou didst dissolve the condemnation of Eve; and having risen, Thou sendest joy unto the disciples, to proclaim Thy third-day Resurrection from the tomb!

*Verse: Mercy and truth have met together; righteousness and peace have kissed each other. (Ps. 84:11 LXX)*

*Sticheron:*
Christ hath illumined for us the precious and holy Pascha; come, let us all be enlightened in our souls: for behold, now the day hath shone forth; in this rejoice and be glad!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 2:*
The women poured out myrrh with tears upon Thy tomb, and their mouths were filled with joy when they said: The Lord is risen!

*Then: "It is good to give thanks unto the Lord..." Troparia as customary. The First Hour. And the Dismissal.*

*At the Liturgy, at the Beatitudes, Ode 1 of the feast, on 6.*

*After the Entrance, troparia: "The noble Joseph...", "When Thou didst descend unto death...", "Unto the Myrrh-bearing women...", and of the temple of the saint; and the troparion of the saint, if there be one; and if there be also a troparion of a second saint, say it, then the kontakion of the temple.*

*Glory... of the saint; and if there be also a kontakion of a second saint, likewise say it; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. The kontakion of the feast: "Thou didst command the Myrrh-bearing women to rejoice..." We say the troparia likewise throughout all the days of this holy week, except if there be a saint with a Polyeleos.*[^535]

*Thus is the service celebrated at Vespers and at Matins across all the days of this week.*

*On Monday of the Myrrh-bearing Women, the Three-Ode Canon, whose acrostic is: ᾍδει τάδε Ἰωσήφ, that is: Joseph sings these.*[^536]

*Tone 2. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Come, O ye peoples, let us chant a song unto Christ God, Who divided the sea and guided the people whom He led forth from the bondage of Egypt: for He hath been glorified!

*Troparion [A]:*
Suspended upon the Cross of Thine own will, O Christ, Thou didst shatter the strong dominion of hades, and by Thy might didst lead forth the eternal prisoners: glory to Thy dominion!

*Troparion [δ]:*
Come, said the Angel unto the Myrrh-bearing women: having seen the place where the Lord of all lay, proclaim His Resurrection unto His friends!

*Glory... [ει]*
In a new tomb of old did the righteous Joseph lay Thee, Who by Thy Resurrection hast made new the corrupt human nature, O Giver of life!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion [Ἰ]:*
Thou didst behold Christ risen from the dead, the Sun of righteousness, O woman full of divine grace, made joyful of God: pray Him to enlighten the hearts of all who hymn thee!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Unto God Who descended into the fiery furnace unto the Hebrew children, and changed the flame into dew, chant, ye works, as unto the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion [τ]:*
Him Who was lifted up upon the Cross, and was buried in the flesh willingly, and shattered the gates of iron and the bars of hades, let us glorify as the Lord Who arose on the third day in glory!

*Troparion [ά]:*
Let heaven rejoice, and let the earth be glad with mankind: Christ is risen, and appeared unto His disciples, and abiding with them, He filled their hearts with gladness!

*Troparion [δ]:*
Unto the weeping women the Giver of life proclaims joy, as they touched His sacred feet, whose sound of old the first-mother Eve feared within paradise!

*Glory... [ε]*
We glorify the One God, in three Hypostases, yet in one Nature: Father, and Word, and Divine Spirit, right-believingly crying: Chant unto the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto the ages!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion [Ἰ]:*
With sacred voices let us hymn in song the Mother of God, as truly holier than the hosts on high, and the divine bridge which leads men over unto celestial choirs!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
God the Word of God, Who by unutterable wisdom came to renew Adam, who fell grievously into corruption through eating, and Who for our sake was ineffably incarnate of the Holy Virgin: let us the faithful magnify with one mind in songs!

*Troparion [ω]:*
O frenzy of the Hebrews! How upon the Tree unrighteously do they condemn to die Christ, Who alone is righteous, and Who divinely breathed life into the dead who were in hades: Whose divine Resurrection let us chant in unison!

*Troparion [σ]:*
While the seals remained upon it, Thou didst arise from the tomb, O Christ, the Resurrection of all; and Thou didst appear unto the disciples, teaching them unfathomable things, and crying: Go ye into the world, proclaiming My glory!

*Glory... [η]*
This glad day of the Rising, being the comfort of souls and joyful gladness, calls together the faithful to keep festival divinely and to cry aloud: Father, and Son, and Divine Spirit, glory to Thee!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion [φ]:*
O Virgin, Mother of the Light: illuminate our minds and hearts with divine light by thy prayers, dispersing the mists of the passions, and making all partakers of the unwaning day by grace!

## ON MONDAY OF THE MYRRH-BEARING WOMEN, AT VESPERS

*At "Lord, I have cried", we set 6 verses, and chant 3 stichera of the feast.*

*Tone 2, Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Є҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*
When the Myrrh-bearing women sought Thee, O Christ, the Life of all, very early in the morning, they went bearing myrrh and spices, and weeping with love; and they heard a young man speaking from the tomb: Cease weeping, and rejoicing rather at your salvation, cry aloud unto all: The Lord is risen!

We know thee, O noble Joseph, as a Cherubic chariot, who didst bear the King Christ upon thy shoulders and take Him down from the Cross; we bless thy hands and thy divine eyes; we venerate thy palms with which, bearing the Sun, the Word and God, thou didst lay Him in the tomb; therefore we also honor thy memory with love!

The solemnity of the divinely crowned Myrrh-bearing women and of honorable Joseph hath appeared unto us like a second paradise, granting a fountain of life: pouring forth gracious waters unto the world, it bountifully wells forth the streams of Christ's Rising; the multitudes of the faithful keep festival and cry aloud: Glory to Him Who gave His Resurrection unto the ends of the earth!

*And 3 of the Menaion.*

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 2:*
The Myrrh-bearing women having arisen early and reached Thy tomb with diligence, sought Thee, O Christ, in order to anoint Thy most pure Body; and having been informed by the words of the Angel, they proclaimed tokens of joy unto the Apostles: that the Author of our salvation is risen, having despoiled death, and granting unto the world eternal life and great mercy!

*Then: "O Gladsome Light..."*

*At the APOSTICHA, stichera, Tone 2:*

*Resurrectional:*
Christ our Savior, having nailed unto the Cross the handwriting that was against us, blotted it out, and abolished the dominion of death; we worship His third-day Resurrection!

*Verse: Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes, O Thou that dwellest in heaven. (Ps. 122:1 LXX)*

*Penitential:*
I cry unto Thee, O Christ Savior, with the voice of the publican: cleanse me even as him, and have mercy upon me, O God!

*Verse: Have mercy upon us, O Lord, have mercy upon us: for we are utterly filled with contempt. (Ps. 122:3 LXX)*

*Martyricon:*
While the holy martyrs pray for us and hymn Christ, all deceit hath ceased, and the human race is saved by faith!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen.*
Why do ye mingle myrrh with tears, O women disciples? The stone is rolled away; the tomb is empty; see corruption trampled down by life, the seals clearly bearing witness, the guards of the disobedient fast asleep; mortality hath been saved by the flesh of God; hades laments; run with joy and say unto the Apostles: Christ, having put death to death, the Firstborn from the dead, goes before you into Galilee!

*Then: "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart..." The Trisagion. The troparia as customary. And the Dismissal.*

## ON TUESDAY OF THE MYRRH-BEARING WOMEN, AT MATINS

*At "God is the Lord", troparia of the feast according to what was indicated previously.*[^537]

*After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns.*

*Tone 2:*
Without having emptied the bosom of the Most Pure [Father] on high, Thou didst accept Burial and Resurrection for the sake of all: O Lord, glory to Thee!

*Verse: O Lord, rebuke me not in Thine anger, neither chasten me in Thy wrath. (Ps. 6:2 LXX)*

I am a barren tree, O Lord, bearing no fruit of compunction whatsoever; and I fear felling, and dread that unquenchable fire; therefore I pray Thee: before that extremity, turn me back and save me!

*Verse: Wondrous is God in His saints, the God of Israel. (Ps. 67:36 LXX)*

*Martyricon:*
Thou Who hast enlightened Thy saints more than gold, and glorified Thy venerable ones as Good: being entreated by them, O Christ God, grant peace unto our life as Lover of mankind, and direct our prayer as incense, O Thou Who alone restest in the saints!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*
Having transcended the laws of nature, thou didst unite virginity unto divine childbearing: for thou alone didst give birth unto Him Who was begotten timelessly before thee; therefore, O Mother of God, we magnify thee!

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn of the feast.*

*Tone 2, Podoben: "Seeking the highest" (Вы́шнихъ и҆щѧ̀):*
The Myrrh-bearing women having come early in the morning and seen the tomb empty, said unto the Apostles: The Mighty One hath overthrown corruption, and snatched those in hades from bonds; proclaim with boldness that Christ God is risen, granting unto the world great mercy!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. The same.*

*Then: "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ..." Psalm 50.*

*The Canon of the Myrrh-bearing Women, with the heirmoi, to 8; and the Menaion to 4.*

*The Kontakion and Exapostilarion of the feast.*

*At the PRAISES, we appoint 4 verses, and we chant the present automelic stichera.*

*Tone 2:*

Let the Jews say: How did the soldiers lose the King whom they were guarding? For why did the stone not preserve the Rock of life? Either let them produce Him that was buried, or worship Him that is risen, saying with us: Glory to the multitude of Thy compassions, our Savior, glory to Thee! Twice.[^538]

Overlook my transgressions, O Lord born of the Virgin, and purify my heart, making it a temple of Thy Holy Spirit: that Thou cast me not away from Thy presence, Thou Who hast measureless mercy.

*For the Martyrs:*
Having taken up the Cross of Christ, O holy martyrs, as an invincible weapon, ye abolished all the might of the devil; and having received heavenly crowns, ye have become a wall for us, praying on our behalf.

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 2:*
The Myrrh-bearing women, very early in the morning, having taken sweet spices, reached the tomb of the Lord, and found what they did not expect; they pondered, reverently beholding the rolling away of the stone, and said one to another: Where are the seals of the tomb? Where is Pilate's watch, and the secure safeguarding? And there appeared a herald unto the unknowing women, an Angel gleaming with light, who said unto them: Why seek ye with weeping the Living One, Who hath given life unto the human race? Christ our God is risen from the dead as Almighty, granting unto us all incorruption and life, enlightenment, and great mercy!

*At the APOSTICHA, stichera of the feast.*

*Tone 2, Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Є҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*[^539]
The thrice-radiant Light clearly shines forth upon the earth today, and removes the darkness of the passions; the Resurrection of Christ is made manifest, preserving the faithful: the angelic ranks rejoice with love, Joseph is glad, and the radiant memory of the venerable Myrrh-bearers crowns those who faithfully praise them, and who glorify the divine Rising!

*Verse: Thou hast been favorable, O Lord, unto Thy land; Thou hast turned back the captivity of Jacob. (Ps. 84:2 LXX)*

Having taken upon thy shoulder, O Joseph, the Son Who sits at the right hand of the Father, the inexhaustible Myrrh, thou didst bury Him with myrrh; Him Who is the Resurrection unto the world thou didst lay in the tomb; Him Who clothes Himself with light as with a garment thou dost ineffably cover with a stone: therefore in songs do we praise His light-bearing Passions and Resurrection!

*Verse: Mercy and truth have met together; righteousness and peace have kissed each other. (Ps. 84:11 LXX)*

The multitude of Angels marvels, and beholding thee, O Joseph, burying Christ, the world blesses thee, and we the faithful wonder: divinely honoring the precious Resurrection, we warmly revere thee together with the Myrrh-bearing women: therefore we also cry aloud unceasingly: Pray with them that we may be saved from perils and afflictions!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 1:*

With fear did the women come unto the tomb, hastening to anoint Thy Body with sweet spices; and not finding it, they were perplexed one with another, not knowing of the Resurrection; but an Angel stood before them and said: Christ is risen, granting unto us great mercy!

*Then, the First Hour. And the Dismissal.*

*On Tuesday of the Myrrh-bearing Women, the Three-Ode Canon, whose acrostic is: ΧΡΙΣΤΕ ΣΩΣΟΝ ΜΕ, that is: Christ, save me.*[^540]

*Tone 2. Ode 2. Heirmos:*
Give ear, O my people, unto my law: incline your ear unto the words of my mouth; for I have called upon Thy Name, O Lord!

*Troparion [Χ]:*
Having fashioned man with Thine own hands, Thou didst nail Thy hands unto the Tree, O Almighty One, delivering us from the hands of the enemy!

*Troparion [ρ]:*
Having destroyed the gloomy prison of hades, O Christ, Thou didst take the prisoners whom it had gained, and as the Mighty One, Thou didst raise Thyself!

*Troparion [ι]:*
Having beheld Thee, O Christ, risen from the tomb on the third day, the Apostles worshipped Thee, and proclaimed Thy Rising everywhere!

*Glory... [σ]*
Groaning and shedding tears, the divine women reached the holy tomb, and became disciples of Christ's Resurrection!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion [τ]:*
Thou didst receive the Ruler of all, O all-immaculate Sovereign Lady, Who crushed the gates of hades and arose, as He said, on the third day!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Unto Him Who of old on Mount Sinai prefigured the wonder of the Virgin unto Moses in the bush: chant, bless, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion [ε]:*
Being lifted up upon the Cross, Thou didst raise up the world with Thyself, and having been laid in the tomb, O Savior, Thou raisest up those sleeping in the tombs, who glorify Thy great power!

*Troparion [σ]:*
Descending unto the dead, Thou didst put hades to death, and didst shatter the gates and bars of death, and by Thy valor didst lead forth the bound, unto salvation for all!

*Glory...:*
Thou didst appear, O Merciful One, unto Thy disciples in many signs during forty days; being confirmed by them, and proclaimed unto all the world, as God Who art risen!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*

*Troparion [σ]:*
Thou art the life of all, Thou art the consolation of the dead and the living, O Word, both joy and enlightenment, Who didst shine forth from the Virgin, and didst arise from the tomb on the third day in glory!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Who among the earthborn ever heard of such a thing? Or who hath ever seen that a Virgin was found to have conceived in her womb, and without travail gave birth unto an Infant? Such is thy wonder, and thee, O pure Mother of God, do we magnify!

*Troparion [ω]:*
Being crucified, Thou didst arise on the third day, as Thou saidst beforehand, and having arisen from the dead, Thou didst raise the world together with Thyself by Thy Resurrection; and Thou didst appear first unto the Myrrh-bearing women, proclaiming: "Rejoice!", O Joy of all, unto those who love Thee from the soul, O Plenteous in mercy!

*Troparion [ν]:*
Now is corruption abolished, for Christ, being incorruption and life, arose from the dead and abides with His Apostles, teaching them higher and divine things, and summoning them not to depart from Jerusalem!

*Glory... [μ]*
Unto the women who of old brought sweet spices with tears, the Angel said: Why seek ye today the Living One among the dead? As He said beforehand, He is risen, He is not here, Who emptied the tombs and breathed immortality into the dead, as the Lover of mankind!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion [ε]:*
Beholding thy Son and God risen from the dead, O Mother of God, thou wast filled with joy, being the cause of joy and gladness unto all: therefore doth every soul joyfully praise thee and glorify thee, O Ever-Virgin!

## ON TUESDAY OF THE MYRRH-BEARING WOMEN, AT VESPERS

*At "Lord, I have cried", stichera of the feast, 3.*

*Tone 2, Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Є҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*
The women disciples of Christ rejoice, having heard the words from the Angel; thence do they learn the Resurrection of Him Who for our sake became dead, even though the Myrrh-bearing women had previously stood before the tomb, and weeping for Christ, suddenly saw the stone rolled away, at whose removal they were perplexed!

Bestowing unceasing and divine joy upon the divine and sacred disciples, the women disciples and Myrrh-bearers of Christ appeared, fulfilling the command of the divine Angel, at whose white garments they were terrified as he said: Hades hath been despoiled by the all-saving Resurrection of the King Who died for our sake!

Having poured forth streams of lamentation from the wellspring of tears, the divine women disciples of Christ now bring words of joy unto the eyewitnesses of grace, announcing unto them the Rising of the Word, and the joy from the tomb; therefore instead of sorrow did they hear most sweetly the voice commanding: "Rejoice!"

*Then 3 of the Menaion.*

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 6:*
The Myrrh-bearing women, having reached Thy tomb, and seen the sepulchral seals, yet not finding Thy most pure Body, weeping, came with haste, saying: Who hath stolen our Hope? Who hath taken the dead man naked, anointed with myrrh, the only consolation of His Mother? O how hath He that made the dead alive died! How is He that despoiled hades buried! But arise, O Savior, of Thine own sovereign will, as Thou saidst, on the third day, saving our souls!

*Then: "O Gladsome Light..."*

*At the APOSTICHA, stichera.*

*Tone 2:*
Save me, O Christ Savior, by the power of the Cross, Thou Who didst save Peter in the sea, and have mercy upon me, O God!

*Verse: Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes, O Thou that dwellest in heaven. (Ps. 122:1 LXX)*

*Sticheron:*
With the Archangels let us hymn the Resurrection of Christ: for He is the Redeemer and Savior of our souls; and in fearful glory and mighty power He comes again to judge the world which He created!

*Verse: Have mercy upon us, O Lord, have mercy upon us: for we are utterly filled with contempt. (Ps. 122:3 LXX)*

*For the Martyrs:*
The choirs of martyrs resisted the tormentors, saying: We wage war for the King of hosts; though ye deliver us to fire and torments, we reject not the power of the Trinity!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 6:*
Joseph asked for the Body of Jesus, and laid It in his own new tomb; for it was fitting for Him to go forth from the tomb as from a bridal chamber; O Thou Who didst crush the dominion of death, and open the gates of paradise unto men, O Lord, glory to Thee![^541]

*Then: "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart..." Troparia as customary. And the Dismissal.*

## ON WEDNESDAY OF THE MYRRH-BEARING WOMEN, AT MATINS

*At "God is the Lord", troparia according to what was indicated previously.*[^542]

*After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymn.*

*Tone 2:*
Thou hast wrought salvation in the midst of the earth, O Christ God; upon the Cross Thou didst stretch out Thy most pure hands, gathering all the nations who cry: O Lord, glory to Thee!

*Verse: Arise, O Lord my God, let Thy hand be lifted up; forget not Thy poor unto the end. (Ps. 9:33 LXX)*

Having arisen from the tomb, and torn asunder the bonds of hades, Thou didst abolish the condemnation of death, O Lord, delivering all from the snares of the enemy; and having shown Thyself unto Thine Apostles, Thou didst send them forth to preach, and through them Thou didst grant Thy peace unto all the world, O only Plenteous in mercy!

*Verse: Wondrous is God in His saints, the God of Israel. (Ps. 67:36 LXX)*

*For the Martyrs:*
O passion-bearers of the Lord, blessed is the earth that was watered with your blood, and holy are the dwellings that received your bodies; for in the stadium ye conquered the enemy, and with boldness preached Christ: entreat Him as good, we pray, that our souls may be saved!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Stavrotheotokion:*
She who without seed gave birth unto Thee, standing beside Thy Cross, and not enduring to see Thee suffering unrighteously, lamented with weeping, and cried unto Thee: How dost Thou suffer, Who by nature art passionless, O most sweet Son? I hymn Thine extreme goodness!

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn.*

*Tone 2, Podoben: "Being the wellspring of loving-kindness" (Бл҃гоꙋтро́бїа):*[^543]
Having come unto Thy tomb, O Savior, the venerable Myrrh-bearing women, anointing the casket with sweet spices, deemed Thee to be a mere man; but the Angel announced joy unto them: The Lord is risen; therefore preach ye also unto the Apostles His fearful Resurrection from the tomb in truth!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. The same.*

*Then: "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ..." Psalm 50.*

*The Canon of the feast with the heirmoi to 8; and the Menaion to 4.*

*The Kontakion and Exapostilarion of the feast.*

*At the PRAISES, we appoint 4 verses, and we chant the present stichera.*

*Tone 2:*
Having voluntarily impoverished Thyself with Adam's poverty, O Christ God, Thou camest upon the earth, incarnate of the Virgin, and didst accept the Cross, that Thou mightest deliver us from the bondage of the enemy: O Lord, glory to Thee! Twice.

Rejoice, O ye peoples, and be glad! An Angel sat upon the sepulchral stone; he proclaimed good tidings unto us, saying: Christ is risen from the dead, the Savior of the world, and hath filled all things with fragrance: rejoice, O ye peoples, and be glad!

*For the Martyrs:*
The multitudes of Thy saints entreat Thee, O Christ: have mercy upon us, as Lover of mankind!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 1:*
With fear did the women come unto the tomb, hastening to anoint Thy Body with sweet spices; and not finding it, they were perplexed one with another, not knowing of the Resurrection; but an Angel stood before them and said: Christ is risen, granting unto us great mercy!

*At the APOSTICHA, stichera.*

*Tone 2, Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Є҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*
Is the Redeemer then among the dead? cried the Myrrh-bearing women with lamentations, disciples of Christ: Is the most great Sun even until today beneath the earth, or is He risen as He said? And as they wept thus, the Angel from the tomb spoke divine joy in truth: Christ is risen! Run and preach unto all His divine Resurrection from the tomb!

*Verse: Thou hast been favorable, O Lord, unto Thy land; Thou hast turned back the captivity of Jacob. (Ps. 84:2 LXX)*

The venerable women prepared sweet spices while it was yet dark on the first day of the week, and came unto Thy tomb, O Christ, to anoint Thy most pure and divine Body; therefore, having learned of Thy Resurrection, they hastened to announce it unto the initiates: meeting them from the tomb, Thou didst cry: "Rejoice!", O most loving Lord!

*Verse: Mercy and truth have met together; righteousness and peace have kissed each other. (Ps. 84:11 LXX)*

His women disciples hasten to anoint with venerable spices the High God buried on the earth as dead, and seeing a young man sitting in the new tomb, they were terrified at his gleaming countenance; therefore, having learned of the third-day Rising of the Word from the tomb, they announced it unto the Apostles!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 5:*[^544]
Thee Who clothest Thyself with light as with a garment, Joseph with Nicodemus took down from the Tree, and beholding Thee dead, naked, unburied, he took up a heartfelt lamentation, and weeping said: Woe is me, O most sweet Jesus! Whom a little while ago the sun, seeing hanging upon the Cross, veiled itself in darkness, and the earth quaked with fear, and the veil of the temple was torn in twain; but lo, now I see Thee, Who for my sake hast voluntarily accepted death. How shall I bury Thee, O my God? Or how shall I wrap Thee in a winding sheet? With what hands shall I touch Thy incorruptible Body? Or what dirges shall I chant unto Thy departure, O Merciful One? I magnify Thy Passions, I praise in song also Thy Burial, together with the Resurrection, crying: O Lord, glory to Thee!

*Then the troparia of the feast. The First Hour. And the Dismissal.*

*On Wednesday of the Myrrh-bearing Women, the Three-Ode Canon, whose acrostic is: Ἠγέρθη ὁ Σωτήρ, that is: The Savior is risen.*[^545]

*Tone 2. Ode 3. Heirmos:*
The wilderness hath blossomed as a lily, O Lord, the barren church of the Gentiles, by Thy coming, wherein my heart hath been established!

*Troparion [Η]:*
Beholding Thee upon the Cross, suffering of Thine own will, O Lord, creation was altered and confounded, and the dead arose from the tombs!

*Troparion [γ]:*
When Thou, O Life-giving Lord, wast in hades with Thy soul, all-destroying death, seeing it, was dismayed, releasing the prisoners whom it had swallowed!

*Glory... [ε]*
All creation was filled with joy, O Merciful Lord, by Thy Rising from the dead; for Thou didst raise the whole world with Thyself, having overthrown the kingdom of death!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion [ρ]:*
A sword pierced thy soul, O Pure and all-immaculate Lady, when thou didst behold Christ being crucified; but thou didst rejoice, seeing Him risen from the tomb!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
The fiery furnace of old in Babylon divided its operation by the command of God, consuming the Chaldeans, but moistening with dew the faithful who chant: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion [θ]:*
Thou diest upon the Cross, O Life of all, and as a lifeless corpse wast laid in the tomb, O Long-suffering One, and didst arise on the third day for the rising of the world; therefore, O Giver of life, do we glorify Thee with gladness!

*Troparion [η]:*
Zion heard the Rising of the Lord, and now is filled with gladness, and its daughters manifestly rejoiced, and preached unto the disciples, saying: Grieve not, the Giver of life is risen!

*Glory... [ο]*
When the morning came, the women came with haste unto the tomb, and stooping down with trembling, seeing the Angels in white garments, and seized with fear, they heard: Fear not, the Giver of life is risen!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion [σ]:*
Hymning thee, the radiant Cloud of the noetic Sun, O full of the grace of God, we glorify thee: enlighten our hearts, driving away all the darkness of despondency and passions, O Bride of God!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
The Son of the Unoriginate Begetter, God and Lord, incarnate of the Virgin, hath appeared unto us, to enlighten those in darkness, and to gather the dispersed: therefore do we magnify the all-hymned Mother of God!

*Troparion [ω]:*
When the sun saw Thee stretched upon the Cross for the sinful servant, it hid its light, the rocks split, and hades quickly yielded up the dead who chant Thy dominion, O Almighty Giver of life!

*Troparion [τ]:*
Having most gloriously emptied the gloomy belly of hades, the More-than-Divine One, as Almighty, arose again in glory, and was seen by the divine disciples: let us worship Him together with the Father and the Spirit!

*Glory... [η]:*
The Lord is risen! said the holy Angel who appeared in the tomb unto the Myrrh-bearing women: Go, and tell this unto His disciples, who weep and lament in Galilee, that they shall see Him there!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion [ρ]:*
Pray unceasingly unto Christ our God for those who ever bless thee, O All-immaculate One, that we may be delivered from tribulations and afflictions, from the tempest and darkening of passions, and from the manifold snares of the evil one!

## ON WEDNESDAY OF THE MYRRH-BEARING WOMEN, AT VESPERS

*At "Lord, I have cried", we appoint 6 verses. Of the feast, 3; and of the Menaion, 3. Stichera of the feast.*

*Tone 2, Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Є҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*
Having heard the words of joy from the young men sitting by the tomb of the Word, they showed the course of most diligent haste, and abandoning the previous task of carrying myrrh, they appeared as heralds of good tidings, announcing unto the initiates the Rising from the nethermost parts of hades of Him Who was born for our sake!

Anticipating the deep dawn, with fear the Myrrh-bearing women stood before the tomb, bringing myrrh unto Christ the Giver of life, reckoning Him among the dead Who put hades to death; but the divine Angel stood before them, crying aloud: Why seek ye the Life-bearing and Living One among the dead? Go, preaching the Rising!

Thou bearest upon thy shoulder Him Who rests upon the Cherubim, O blessed Joseph, like another bier upon thy shoulders: Him Who was formerly incarnate and now slain, Who made us alive who were dead: beholding Whose Resurrection, thou rejoicest with the venerable Myrrh-bearing women, even though beforehand ye wept over His slaying!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 1:*
Magdalene and the other Mary came unto the tomb seeking the Lord; and they saw an Angel sitting like lightning upon the stone, and saying unto them: Why seek ye the Living among the dead? He is risen, as He said; in Galilee shall ye find Him; unto Whom let us cry aloud: O Thou Who art risen from the dead, Lord, glory to Thee!

*Then: "O Gladsome Light..."*

*At the APOSTICHA, Resurrectional sticheron.*

*Tone 2:*
Thy Resurrection, O Christ Savior, hath enlightened all the world, and Thou hast called back Thine own creation: O Almighty Lord, glory to Thee!

*Verse: Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes, O Thou that dwellest in heaven. (Ps. 122:1 LXX)*

*For the Apostles:*[^546]
Thou didst magnify, O Savior, throughout the world the names of the preeminent Apostles: they were instructed in ineffable heavenly things, and gave healings unto those upon the earth; their very shadows healed passions, and the one from among the fishermen worked wonders, and the one from among the Jews theologically proclaimed the doctrines of grace: through them, O Compassionate One, grant us Thy great mercy!

*Verse: Have mercy upon us, O Lord, have mercy upon us: for we are utterly filled with contempt. (Ps. 122:3 LXX)*

*For the Martyrs:*
Great is the glory that ye acquired by faith, O holy ones; for not only when ye suffered did ye conquer the enemy, but even after death ye drive away spirits, and heal the sick, being physicians of souls and bodies: pray unto the Lord that our souls may find mercy!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 2:*
The women poured out myrrh with tears upon Thy tomb, and their mouths were filled with joy when they said: The Lord is risen!

*Then: "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart..." The Trisagion. The troparia. And the Dismissal.*

## ON THURSDAY OF THE MYRRH-BEARING WOMEN, AT MATINS

*At "God is the Lord", troparia according to what was indicated previously.*

*After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymn.*

*Tone 2, Podoben: "Most blessed art thou" (Пребл҃гослове́нна):*[^547]
Bearing the myrrh of Thy burial, the women secretly came early unto the tomb, fearing the boldness of the Jews, and foreseeing the security of the soldiers; yet frail nature conquered valor, for their prayerful intent was well-pleasing unto God: therefore fittingly they cried: Arise, O Lord, help us, and deliver us for Thy Name's sake!

*Verse: Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world. (Ps. 18:5 LXX)*

*For the Apostles:*
Thou Who didst make fishermen wiser than orators, and didst send them as preachers into all the earth, through Thine unutterable love of mankind, O Christ God: through them establish Thy Church, and send down Thy blessing upon the faithful, O only Merciful One and Lover of mankind!

*Verse: Wondrous is God in His saints, the God of Israel. (Ps. 67:36 LXX)*

*For the Martyrs:*
O Apostles, martyrs, and prophets, hierarchs, venerable and righteous ones, who have finished the course well, and kept the faith, having boldness before the Savior: entreat Him as good on our behalf, we pray, that our souls may be saved!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*
We have become partakers of the divine nature through thee, O Mother of God, Ever-Virgin: for thou didst give birth unto God incarnate for us; therefore as is due do we all piously magnify thee!

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn.*

*Tone 2, Podoben: "Seeking the highest" (Вы́шнихъ и҆щѧ̀):*
Bringing myrrh, O Savior, the women sought diligently to anoint Thee, O Lover of mankind; but the Angel cried unto them from the tomb: The Giver of life and the Lord is risen, having trampled down hades and death!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. The same.*

*Then: "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ..." Psalm 50.*

*The Canon of the feast, and the rest of the order, as previously prescribed.*

*At the PRAISES, we appoint 4 verses, and we chant the present stichera.*

*Tone 2:*

An Angel, on the one hand, brought the "Rejoice!" unto her that is Full of grace before Thy conception, O Lord; while an Angel rolled away the stone from Thy glorious tomb at Thy Resurrection: the one, in place of sorrow, announcing signs of gladness; and the other, in place of death, proclaiming unto us the Master and Giver of life: therefore do we cry unto Thee: O Benefactor of all, Lord, glory to Thee! Twice.[^548]

Always burned by unrighteous deeds, and fleeing unto Thee, Who art truly God, we bring unto Thee the voice of Thy disciples, saying: Save us, O Master, we perish! Show now also unto our enemies, we pray, that Thou protectest Thy people and savest them from tribulations, through the prayers of the Apostles, overlooking sins because of Thy great goodness, O Lord!

*For the Martyrs:*

Every city and country honors your relics, O passion-bearing martyrs! For having suffered lawfully, ye received a heavenly crown; and therefore are ye the boast of priests, the victory of kings, and the beauty of churches!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 2:*

The Myrrh-bearing women, very early in the morning, having taken sweet spices, reached the tomb of the Lord, and found what they did not expect; they pondered, reverently beholding the rolling away of the stone, and said one to another: Where are the seals of the tomb? Where is Pilate's watch, and the secure safeguarding? And there appeared a herald unto the unknowing women, an Angel gleaming with light, who said unto them: Why seek ye with weeping the Living One, Who hath given life unto the human race? Christ our God is risen from the dead as Almighty, granting unto us all incorruption and life, enlightenment, and great mercy!

*At the APOSTICHA, stichera.*

*Tone 2, Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Є҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*

When Thou didst rise as God, then Thou gavest joy, O Word, saying unto the Myrrh-bearing women: I have not yet ascended unto My Father, and touch Me not henceforth, but go only and tell My friends: Behold, He goes before you; and thereafter Thou wast seen by them, and by breathing upon them, O Savior, Thou gavest them the Holy Spirit.

*Verse: Thou hast been favorable, O Lord, unto Thy land; Thou hast turned back the captivity of Jacob. (Ps. 84:2 LXX)*

Unto the words of the Myrrh-bearing women, who proclaimed from among the dead the Resurrection of Christ, the initiates of mysteries believed not, but hastened to see the tomb; and the linen shroud and napkin were seen in the tomb, but He Himself Whom they sought was not seen: therefore, having recognized the Resurrection, they were seen as preachers unto the world, announcing this also unto the nations!

*Verse: Mercy and truth have met together; righteousness and peace have kissed each other. (Ps. 84:11 LXX)*

The unapproachable Light hath appeared unto us, radiant Christ the Lord shining forth from the tomb; hades is despoiled, Satan hath vanished; the ends of the world rejoice, creation leaps for joy, the Church of Christ sings in feast, and honors in triumph the memory of all-wise Joseph and of the Myrrh-bearing women with him!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 2:*

Why do ye mingle myrrh with tears, O women disciples? The stone is rolled away, the tomb is emptied! Behold corruption trampled down by life, the seals bearing clear witness, the guards of the disobedient sleeping soundly; what was mortal hath been saved by the flesh of God; hades wails! Therefore with joy say unto the Apostles: Christ, having put death to death, the First-born from the dead, goes before you into Galilee!

*Then: the troparion, and the First Hour. And the Dismissal.*

*On Thursday of the Myrrh-bearing Women, the Three-Ode Canon,*[^549]
*the acrostic of which is: ᾎσμα ᾄδω τῷ Θεῷ, that is:*
*A song I sing unto God.*

*Tone 2. Ode 7. Heirmos:*

I sing unto Thee, for by hearing, O Lord, I have heard and was afraid, for Thou comest unto me, seeking me who am gone astray; therefore Thy great condescension toward me do I glorify, O Many-merciful One!

*Troparia:*

Thou wast lifted up upon the Cross by Thine own will, O Lord, girded with power; and descending with Thy soul into hades, O Tender-hearted One, Thou didst loose the souls from eternal bonds, and with Thyself, O Compassionate One, didst raise them up with Thee!

Having dreadfully shattered the bars and gates of hades by Thy might, O Master, Thou didst empty its wealth; therefore Thy great condescension and Thy precious Resurrection do we glorify!

*Glory...*

Unto the tomb the women came to anoint Thy most pure Body, and they found the Angel sitting upon the stone, O Christ, and being afraid they marveled; with whom we sing in hymnody Thy Rising!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*

Thou hast given birth beyond comprehension unto the Holy of holies, O Mother of God, Who grants sanctification, deliverance, and forgiveness of sins unto the faithful through thine intercession, as they glorify His Resurrection!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

The three venerable youths, not yielding unto the great tormentor, cast into the furnace, confessed God, singing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparia:*

Thou hast exalted human nature, O Christ, by Thy lifting up upon the Cross; and the enemy who fell from the heights Thou didst cast down into the abyss; and being buried, Thou didst arise, having despoiled death!

Thou hast shattered the bars of hades, O Christ, and didst lead forth with boldness the chained prisoners who glorify Thy power and Thy three-day Rising from the tomb!

*Glory...*

When of old the choir of holy Apostles beheld Thee, risen in glory from the tomb, O Christ, being filled with gladness, they cried aloud: Glory to Thy Rising!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*

Thy weeping, O all-pure and holy Lady, was turned into joy, when thou didst behold thy Son and Master, Christ, risen from the dead on the third day in glory, and having enlightened the world!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

Thou who ineffably didst give flesh from a virginal womb unto God, the Luminary Who shone forth before the sun and came bodily unto us: O blessed and all-pure Lady, we magnify thee as the Mother of God!

*Troparia:*

Thou wast seen crucified between two thieves, O Many-merciful One, and laid in the pit of the nethermost parts, and Thou didst raise up those who were in darkness and the shadow of death, who sing in hymnody Thy three-day Resurrection, O Tender-hearted One!

Death no longer hath dominion over men, as it is written, since Christ the Immortal One arose, having emptied the insatiable kingdoms of hades: let the whole universe rejoice in feast!

*Glory...*

The Angel, flashing with light before the tomb, said unto the Myrrh-bearing women: Why do ye seek with weeping Him Who is free among the dead? As He said beforehand, He is already risen; go hence rejoicing!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*

Thou hast appeared more spacious than the heavens, having contained God Who was laid beneath the earth for the sake of goodness, and Who through death granted immortality unto all: Whom piously glorifying, we bless thee as is due!

## ON THURSDAY OF THE MYRRH-BEARING WOMEN, AT VESPERS

*At "Lord, I have cried", we appoint 6 verses, and we chant 3 stichera of the feast, and 3 of the Menaion. Stichera of the feast.*

*Tone 8, Podoben: "O marvelous wonder" (Ѽ пресла́внагѡ чꙋдесѐ):*[^550]

Following the footsteps of Christ when He appeared, O venerable women, and serving Him with upright zeal, in uprightness, O Myrrh-bearers, ye did not forsake Him even when dead; but going, ye brought myrrh with tears, moved by compassion: therefore do we celebrate your all-sacred memory!

The assembly of divine women, desiring to see the Life that had been slain in the tomb, came by night, and heard the Angel say: As Christ foretold, He is risen! With haste tell this unto His disciples, and drive away despondency from your souls, having received ineffable joy instead of weeping!

Today let us the faithful dance for joy in your memory, O Myrrh-bearers, glorifying the all-good Lord Who glorified you: Whom do ye unceasingly entreat, O all-venerable ones, that we may obtain everlasting glory and the brightness of the saints, having boldness before Him always, O divinely blessed women!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 2:*

The Myrrh-bearing women, having arisen early and reached Thy tomb with haste, sought Thee, O Christ, that they might anoint Thy most pure Body; and having been instructed by the words of the Angel, they proclaimed glad tidings unto the Apostles: that Thou art risen, O Author of our salvation, having despoiled death, granting unto the world eternal life and great mercy!

*Then: "O Gladsome Light..."*

*At the APOSTICHA, stichera.*

*Tone 2. For the Cross:*

Let Him be crucified! cried those who continually enjoyed Thy gifts, and they asked to receive a criminal in place of their Benefactor, those murderers of the righteous; yet Thou didst keep silence, O Christ, enduring their cruelty, willing to suffer and save us, as the Lover of mankind!

*Verse: Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes, O Thou that dwellest in heaven. (Ps. 122:1 LXX)*

*Resurrectional:*

Come, let us worship God the Word, begotten of the Father before the ages, incarnate of the Virgin Mary; for having endured the Cross, He surrendered Himself unto Burial as He Himself willed, and having risen from the dead, He hath saved me, a wandering man!

*Verse: Have mercy upon us, O Lord, have mercy upon us: for we are utterly filled with contempt. (Ps. 122:3 LXX)*

*For the Martyrs:*

Having not desired earthly pleasures, the passion-bearers were accounted worthy of heavenly goods, and became fellow-citizens with the Angels: O Lord, through their prayers have mercy and save us!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 6:*

Joseph asked for the Body of Jesus, and laid It in his own new tomb; for it was fitting for Him to come forth from the tomb as from a bridal chamber: O Thou Who didst shatter the dominion of death and open the gates of paradise unto men, Lord, glory to Thee!

*Then: "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart..." The Trisagion. The troparia. And the Dismissal.*

## ON FRIDAY OF THE MYRRH-BEARING WOMEN, AT MATINS

*At "God is the Lord", troparia according to what was indicated previously.*[^551]

*After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymn.*

*Tone 2:*[^552]

We venerate Thine immaculate icon, O Good One, asking forgiveness of our transgressions, O Christ God; for of Thine own will Thou wast well-pleased to ascend the Cross in the flesh, that Thou mightest deliver those whom Thou didst create from the bondage of the enemy: therefore thankfully do we cry unto Thee: Thou hast filled all things with joy, our Savior, Who camest to save the world!

*Verse: I will give thanks unto Thee, O Lord... (Ps. 110:1 LXX)*

Having not forbidden the sealing of the tombstone, having risen, Thou didst grant the Rock of faith unto all: Lord, glory to Thee!

*Verse: Marvelous is God in His saints, the God of Israel. (Ps. 67:36 LXX)*

*For the Martyrs:*

When the martyrs of the Lord contended in trials of suffering, then the audacity of the ungodly was confounded by faith; and when they divinely abolished the delusion of idols, then they received crowns of victory from on high, and they pray for our souls!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Stavrotheotokion:*

Beholding Thee stretched out dead upon the Tree, O Christ, the Virgin and Thy Mother bitterly weeping, cried aloud: My Son, what is this dread mystery? Thou Who grantest eternal life unto all, how dost Thou suffer a shameful death of Thine own will upon the Cross?

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn.*

*Tone 2, Podoben: "Seeking the highest" (Вы́шнихъ и҆щѧ̀):*

Ardently the women brought myrrh unto the tomb, O Savior; by the brightness of the Angel their souls were gladdened, and they proclaimed Thee as God of all, and cried unto the disciples: Truly from the tomb is the Life of all arisen!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. The same.*

*Then: "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ..." Psalm 50.*

*The Canon of the Myrrh-bearers with the heirmoi to 8, and of the Menaion to 4.*

*Kontakion and Exapostilarion of the Myrrh-bearers.*

*At the PRAISES, we appoint 4 verses, and we chant the present stichera:*

*Tone 2:*

We venerate the wood of Thy Cross, O Christ God; for Thou hast shown the Tree of life unto us who believe in Thee; and having thereby abolished the dominion of him who had the power of death, Thou hast given life unto us who were slain by sin: therefore do we cry unto Thee: O Benefactor of all, Lord, glory to Thee! Twice.

Every breath and all creation glorifies Thee, O Lord, for by the Cross Thou hast abolished death, that Thou mightest show unto the people Thy Resurrection from the dead, as the only Lover of mankind!

*For the Martyrs:*

Having suffered for Christ even unto death, O passion-bearing martyrs, ye have your souls in the hand of God in the heavens, and your relics are honored throughout the whole world; priests and kings bow down, and all people rejoice, and we customarily cry aloud: Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His saints!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 1:*

O Myrrh-bearing women, why have ye come unto the tomb? Why seek ye the Living among the dead? The Lord is risen: take courage! cries the Angel.

*At the APOSTICHA, stichera of the feast.*

*Tone 2, Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Є҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*

The women disciples of Christ rejoice, having heard the words from the Angel; and having understood the Resurrection, they learned of Him Who was reckoned among the dead for our sake; for although the Myrrh-bearing women previously stood before the tomb weeping for Christ, when they suddenly beheld the stone rolled away, they were amazed at this change!

*Verse: Thou hast been favorable, O Lord, unto Thy land; Thou hast turned back the captivity of Jacob. (Ps. 84:2 LXX)*

Granting unceasing and divine joy, the women disciples, the Myrrh-bearers of Christ, appeared unto the divine and sacred disciples, having fulfilled the command of the divine Angel, whose white-robed garments terrified them, who said: Hades hath been despoiled by the all-saving Resurrection of the King Who died for our sake!

*Verse: Mercy and truth have met together; righteousness and peace have kissed each other. (Ps. 84:11 LXX)*

Having shed a stream from the fountain of tears as they wept, the divine women disciples of Christ now bring words of joy unto the eyewitnesses of grace, announcing unto them the Rising of the Word, and the joy from the tomb; therefore instead of sorrow, having gone forth, they most gloriously heard the voice commanding them: Rejoice!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 1:*

With fear the women came unto the tomb, striving to anoint Thy Body with sweet spices; and not having found It, they wondered one with another, not knowing of the Resurrection; but the Angel stood before them and said: Christ is risen, granting us great mercy!

*Then the troparia. And the Dismissal. And the First Hour.*

*On Friday of the Myrrh-bearing Women, the Three-Ode Canon,*[^553]
*the acrostic of which is: Δόξα Θεῷ, ἀμήν, that is:*
*Glory to God, amen.*

*A composition of Joseph. Tone 2. Ode 5. Heirmos:*

O Christ my Savior, Enlightenment of those lying in darkness, and Salvation of the despairing, unto Thee do I rise early, O King of peace: enlighten me with Thy radiance, for no other God beside Thee do I know!

*Troparia:*

The council of lawless Jews of old, having lifted Thee up upon the Tree, put Thee to death, O Lover of mankind; but being laid in the tomb, Thou didst break all the bonds of hades, and didst raise up the dead of all ages!

When Thou didst taste of corruption, O Immortality of all, then didst Thou valiantly lead forth all who were bound, and didst raise them from the tomb, O Giver of life, having destroyed death and enlightened us by Thy Rising!

*Glory...*

Beholding of old at the tomb the Angel flashing in strange raiment, the women marveled; but he cried unto them: Fear ye not; Christ is risen; go, announce it unto His friends!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*

Thou hast appeared as the Dayspring of the never-setting Sun, O Virgin Mother: Whom beholding risen from the dead as He said, and having enlightened the whole world, thou didst rejoice, singing praise unto Him, O Pure One, as the Lover of mankind!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

Not caring for the golden image, the thrice-blessed youths, having beheld the immutable and living Image of God, cried aloud in the midst of the fire: Let all united creation sing praise unto the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!

*Troparia:*

Being God, O Word of God, Thou wast well-pleased to become man, and of Thine own will to be crucified upon the Tree, for the salvation of those who ever cry in faith: Let all united creation sing praise unto the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!

In the pit of the nethermost parts Joseph laid Thee, having bound Thee with grave-clothes and with myrrh and aloes; but Thou didst arise, saving those who cry in faith: Let all united creation sing praise unto the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!

*Glory...*

Thou didst appear unto the disciples, O Joyful One, having risen from the tomb, and saidst unto them: Go into the world, preach My dispensation, singing: Let all united creation sing praise unto the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*

Gladden our hearts, O all-holy Virgin, Bride of God, who hast beheld the all-holy God the Word arisen, and calling us unto joy: Let all united creation sing praise unto the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

Every tongue is at a loss to praise thee as is due, and an intellect even of the world above is in amazement to sing praise unto thee, O Mother of God; yet being good, accept our faith, for thou knowest our divine love; for thou art the Protectress of Christians, and thee do we magnify!

*Troparia:*

No sooner was Thy Cross set up on Calvary, O Savior, than all the dwelling of death was shaken from the depths; and those who sat in the shadow of death were truly loosed, all of them, from their former bonds, crying aloud: Glory to the dominion of Thy power!

The earth was shaken, the rocks were rent with fear, all the mountains and hills were shaken, and the sun was darkened, beholding Thee hanged upon the Cross; the bars of hades and the gates of iron were shattered, O Christ, when by Thy Rising from the dead Thou didst raise the world with Thyself!

*Glory...*

Beholding Thee of old dead upon the Cross, the noble counselor of Arimathea took Thee down from the Tree, and having wrapped Thee in a clean shroud, laid Thee with much fear and diligence in a new tomb; yet Thou, as Thou didst foretell, didst arise on the third day, O Word!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*

Apart from the laws of nature, O all-immaculate Lady, thou didst ineffably give birth unto the Word: Whom beholding crucified by the counsel of the lawless, and laid in the tomb, and risen from the dead, thou wast filled with joy: pray unto Him on behalf of us who sing praise unto thee!

## ON FRIDAY OF THE MYRRH-BEARING WOMEN, AT VESPERS

*At "Lord, I have cried", idiomel stichera of the Myrrh-bearers:*

*Tone 2:*

The Myrrh-bearing women, very early in the morning, having taken sweet spices, reached the tomb of the Lord, and found what they did not expect; they pondered, reverently beholding the rolling away of the stone, and said one to another: Where are the seals of the tomb? Where is Pilate's watch, and the secure safeguarding? And there appeared a herald unto the unknowing women, an Angel gleaming with light, who said unto them: Why seek ye with weeping the Living One, Who hath given life unto the human race? Christ our God is risen from the dead as Almighty, granting unto us all incorruption and life, enlightenment, and great mercy!

Why do ye mingle myrrh with tears, O women disciples? The stone is rolled away, the tomb is emptied! Behold corruption trampled down by life, the seals bearing clear witness, the guards of the disobedient sleeping soundly; what was mortal hath been saved by the flesh of God; hades wails! Therefore with joy say unto the Apostles: Christ, having put death to death, the First-born from the dead, goes before you into Galilee!

The Myrrh-bearing women, having arisen early and reached Thy tomb with haste, sought Thee, O Christ, that they might anoint Thy most pure Body; and having been instructed by the words of the Angel, they proclaimed glad tidings unto the Apostles: that the Author of our salvation is risen, having despoiled death, granting unto the world eternal life and great mercy!

*And 3 of the Menaion.*

*Glory... Tone 6:*[^554]

The Myrrh-bearing women, having reached Thy tomb, and having seen the seals of the tomb, yet not having found Thy most pure Body, weeping, came with haste, saying: Who hath stolen our hope? Who hath taken away a naked corpse anointed with myrrh, the sole consolation of His Mother? O, how hath He Who gave life unto the dead been put to death? How hath He Who despoiled hades been buried? But arise, O Savior, by Thine own power, as Thou didst say, on the third day, saving our souls!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*

*Tone 2:*

The shadow of the law hath passed away, now that grace hath come; for as the Bush was not burned while on fire, so though a Virgin thou gavest birth, and a Virgin thou didst remain: in place of a pillar of fire, the Sun of righteousness hath shone forth; in place of Moses, Christ, the Salvation of our souls!

*At the APOSTICHA, the present Resurrectional stichera.*

*Tone 2:*

Come, let us worship God the Word, begotten of the Father before the ages, incarnate of the Virgin Mary; for having endured the Cross, He surrendered Himself unto Burial as He Himself willed, and having risen from the dead, He hath saved me, a wandering man!

*Verse: The Lord is King, He is clothed with majesty. (Ps. 92:1 LXX)*

Christ our Savior, having nailed unto the Cross the handwriting that was against us, wiped it out and by His death abolished the dominion of death: we worship His three-day Resurrection!

*Verse: For He hath established the world, which shall not be shaken. (Ps. 92:1 LXX)*

With the Archangels let us sing in hymnody the Resurrection of Christ; for He is the Redeemer and Savior of our souls, and in dreadful glory and mighty power He comes again to judge the world which He hath made!

*Verse: Holiness becomes Thy house, O Lord, unto length of days. (Ps. 92:5 LXX)*

Thy Resurrection, O Christ Savior, hath enlightened the whole universe, and Thou hast called back Thine own creation: O Almighty Lord, glory to Thee!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 5:*[^555]

Thee Who clothest Thyself with light as with a garment, Joseph, taking Thee down from the Tree with Nicodemus, and beholding Thee dead, naked, unburied, took up compassionate mourning, and weeping said: Woe is me, sweetest Jesus! Whom a little while ago the sun, seeing suspended upon the Cross, veiled itself in gloom, and the earth was shaken with fear, and the veil of the temple was rent in twain; but behold, now I see Thee, having willingly undergone death for my sake: how shall I bury Thee, O my God? Or how shall I wrap Thee with a shroud? Or with what hands shall I touch Thine incorruptible Body? Or what hymns shall I sing unto Thine exodus, O Compassionate One? I magnify Thy Passions, I sing praise unto Thy Burial together with Thy Resurrection, crying aloud: Lord, glory to Thee!

*Then: "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart..." The Trisagion. Troparion: "The noble Joseph..."*

*Glory... "When Thou didst descend..." Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. "Unto the Myrrh-bearing women..."*

*The Litany, and the Dismissal.*

*In this manner the service is performed also on all Fridays of Pentecost.*[^556]

## ON SATURDAY OF THE MYRRH-BEARING WOMEN, AT MATINS

*At "God is the Lord", the troparia of the feast, as previously indicated.*

*After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymn.*

*Tone 2:*

Having not forbidden the sealing of the tombstone, having risen, Thou didst grant the Rock of faith unto all: Lord, glory to Thee!

*Verse: Arise, O Lord my God, let Thy hand be lifted up! (Ps. 9:33 LXX)*

Having not emptied the bosom of the Most Pure on high, Thou didst accept Burial and Resurrection for the sake of all: O Lord, glory to Thee!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*

All beyond understanding, all most glorious are thy mysteries, O Theotokos; sealed in purity and preserved in virginity, thou wast acknowledged to be an unfeigned Mother, having given birth to the true God: Him do thou entreat that our souls may be saved!

*After the 2nd Kathisma Psalmody, Sessional Hymn.*

*Tone 2, Podoben: "Unto the Myrrh-bearing women" (Мѵроно́сицамъ жена́мъ):*

The choir of Thy disciples rejoices in unison with the Myrrh-bearing women; for with them we celebrate a common feast, unto the glory and honor of Thy Resurrection, and through them we cry aloud unto Thee: O Lord, Lover of mankind, grant great mercy unto Thy people!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. The same.*

*"Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ..." Psalm 50.*

*The Canon of the Myrrh-bearers, with the heirmos, to 6; and of the temple saint, to 4; and of the Menaion saint, to 4.*[^557]

*The Kontakion and Exapostilarion of the Myrrh-bearers.*

*At the Praises, we set 4 verses, and we sing the following stichera:*

*Tone 2:*

Every breath and every creature glorifies Thee, O Lord, for by the Cross Thou hast abolished death, that Thou mightest show unto the people Thy Resurrection from the dead, as the only Lover of mankind.

Let the Jews say how the soldiers who guarded the King lost Him; for why did the stone not safeguard the Rock of life? Either let them surrender Him Who was buried, or let them worship Him Who is risen, saying with us: Glory to the abundance of Thy tender mercies, O our Savior, glory to Thee!

Rejoice, O ye peoples, and make glad: an Angel seated upon the stone of the tomb, he brought good tidings unto us, saying: Christ is risen from the dead, the Savior of the world, and hath filled all things with fragrance! Rejoice, O ye peoples, and make glad!

An Angel indeed brought "Rejoice!" unto her who was full of grace before Thy conception, O Lord; and an Angel rolled away the stone of Thy glorious tomb at Thy Resurrection: the former instead of sorrow announcing signs of gladness, the latter instead of death proclaiming unto us the Master and Life-giver; therefore we cry aloud unto Thee: O Benefactor of all, Lord, glory to Thee!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 1:*[^558]

Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came unto the tomb, seeking the Lord, and they saw an Angel like lightning sitting upon the stone, and saying unto them: Why seek ye the Living One with the dead? He is risen as He said; ye shall find Him in Galilee; unto Whom let us cry aloud: O Thou Who art risen from the dead, Lord, glory to Thee!

*At the Aposticha, stichera of the Feast.*

*Tone 2, Automela (Samopodobny):*

When from the Tree Joseph of Arimathea took Thee down dead, Who art the Life of all, he wrapped Thee, O Christ, with myrrh and a winding-sheet, and with love was moved in heart and lips to kiss Thy most pure Body; yet restrained by fear, rejoicing he cried aloud unto Thee: Glory to Thy condescension, O Lover of mankind!

*Verse: Lord, Thou hast been favorable unto Thy land; Thou hast turned away the captivity of Jacob. (Ps. 84:2 LXX)*

When in a new tomb Thou wast laid for the sake of all, O Redeemer of all, hades, laughed to scorn, seeing Thee was dismayed; the bars were broken, the gates were shattered, the tombs were opened, the dead arose; then Adam, gratefully rejoicing, cried aloud unto Thee: Glory to Thy condescension, O Lover of mankind!

*Verse: Mercy and truth are met together; righteousness and peace have kissed each other. (Ps. 84:11 LXX)*

When the heavenly powers beheld Thee, O Christ, slandered by the lawless as a deceiver, they were struck with awe at Thine ineffable long-suffering, and at the stone of the tomb sealed by the very hands that pierced Thy corruption-free Side; yet rejoicing in our salvation they cried aloud unto Thee: Glory to Thy condescension, O Lover of mankind!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 6:*

Joseph asked for the Body of Jesus, and laid It in his own new tomb; for it was fitting for Him to come forth from the tomb as from a bridal chamber, Who crushed the dominion of death and opened the gates of paradise unto men: Lord, glory to Thee!

*Then: "It is good to give thanks..." and the Troparion. The First Hour, and the Dismissal.*

*On Saturday of the Myrrh-bearers, the Four-Ode Canon.*[^559]

*Tone 2. Ode 6. Heirmos:*

"Lead me up from the depths!" Jonah cried aloud unto Thee, being an image of the Burial and the Resurrection which Thou hast bestowed upon us, O Almighty Savior!

*Troparia:*

The Myrrh-bearing women, having reached Thy tomb, were shedding tears; but an Angel announced joy unto them, crying aloud: Christ is risen, proclaim it unto the world!

When Thou wast lifted up upon the Cross, the sun hid its radiance; but Israel did not recognize Thee as God and Creator, Who didst willingly lay down Thy life for all!

*Glory...*

Let all creation rejoice, for Christ hath arisen from the tomb, taking hades captive and shattering all its power; and let them celebrate a common feast of gladness!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*

Though thou didst give birth to an Infant, yet thou didst remain a Virgin, even as thou wast before giving birth, O pure Virgin Theotokos: for He Who was born renewed nature as God!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

"O Thou Who extinguished of old the all-blazing furnace, and bedewed the youths with spiritual moisture: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!"

*Troparia:*

The senseless people of the Jewish assembly, in return for the benefits which Thou hadst bestowed upon them, nailed Thee, O Christ, unto the Cross!

O Wellspring of mercy, Thou wast laid down for all, that we, having all been released from the debt of death, may hymn Thee, O Lover of mankind!

*Glory...*

By Thy three-day death and life-bearing Burial, Thou hast granted eternal life unto those in the tombs, who faithfully hymn Thee, O Savior!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*

Unto thee, the only mediatress of joy, it is fitting to receive from the Angel the "Rejoice!", which we faithful cry aloud unto thee, O Mary Ever-Virgin!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

"The unwearied fire, which was nurtured in boundless matter, stood in fear before the pious youths—whose unblemished bodies were fashioned in harmony with their souls—and withdrew from them; and as the ever-living flame was cleft, an everlasting song was sung: Hymn the Lord, all ye works, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!"

*Troparia:*

The godless counsel is destroyed, and the seals became vain for the Jews: He Who was buried hath arisen, having laughed all to scorn; for God willingly accepts suffering, but by His own authority He orders all things as He wills: as the Lord do we unceasingly hymn Him and exalt Him above all unto all ages!

"Go," said he whose appearance was shining like lightning unto the women: "Christ is risen! Proclaim henceforth His Resurrection unto the whole world, and weep not, for it is no time for tears: for death reigns no longer, hades rules no more, the guilt of condemnation shall no longer prevail!"

*Glory...*

Our life was hidden in Thee, O Christ the Word, Who didst suffer in the flesh and art risen from the dead, O Word, and Who livest for ever: in Whom we Christians hope to have part at Thy dread second coming, we faithful worthily hymning Thy Divine Sufferings and Thy Resurrection from the dead!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*

Through thee our ancestral mother received release from the ancient condemnation: no longer does she give birth in sorrow, for thou hast given birth to Christ, O Mother of God; therefore we worthily call thee blessed, singing praise unto Him Who was born of thee without seed, and exalting Him above all unto all ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

"Thou hast magnified her that gave Thee birth, O Christ, the Theotokos, from whom, O our Creator, Thou didst clothe Thyself in a body of like passions with us, which released us from our transgressions: calling her blessed, all generations, we magnify Thee!"

*Troparia:*

"Hear the voice of thy Bridegroom, O Church!" cries the divine David; for unto thee from His Side was granted water with Divine Blood for the cleansing of sins: for He hath delivered thee from the deceit of idols, as the Lover of mankind!

Thou hast shone forth life unto the multitude of the Gentiles by Thy three-day Arising, O Christ: unto those that asked not, nor sought Thee, Thou wast revealed in divine glory; but the Jewish people who did not believe in Thee Thou hast condemned!

*Glory...*

The curse that sprouted for me through the deceit of the tree in Eden Thou hast dissolved, O Word, being obedient even unto the Cross to the Father's counsels of Thine own sovereign will: therefore I hymn and magnify unceasingly Thine ineffable self-emptying!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*

Thou hast drawn near unto Thyself a holy nation that was afar off, having taken flesh of the Virgin, O Savior, and those who were not Thy people Thou hast named Thy divine people: therefore we all now worship Thee, O Almighty One!

*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes: Ode 9 to 6.*[^560]

*Prokeimenon and Alleluia of the Feast.*

*Epistle: Acts, Pericope 22 (Acts 9:19–31): "Saul was certain days with the disciples which were at Damascus..."*[^561]

*Gospel: John, Pericope 52 (John 15:17–16:2): "These things I command you..."*[^562]

# PART IV: SUNDAY OF THE PARALYTIC, FEAST OF MID-PENTECOST, AND FOURTH WEEK AFTER PASCHA

## SUNDAY OF THE PARALYTIC AND MID-PENTECOST

## FOURTH SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA, OF THE PARALYTIC

*On Saturday evening, at Little Vespers:*

*At "Lord, I have cried", 4 Resurrectional stichera.*

*Tone 3:*

*By Thy Cross, O Christ Savior... (see fol. 330)*[^563]  
*All things have been enlightened... (see fol. 330)*  
*I glorify the power of the Father and the Son... (see fol. 330)*  
*To Thy precious Cross... (see fol. 331)*  

*Glory... Tone 5:*

*Jesus went up to Jerusalem... (see fol. 331)*  

*Seek all these stichera at Great Vespers.*

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion Dogmatikon:*

*Tone 3:*

A surpassing marvelous wonder! The Virgin hath given birth, and the One born is God before the ages, a birth revealed beforehand, and accomplished beyond nature! O dreadful mystery, which even when conceived remains ineffable, and when beheld cannot be comprehended! Blessed art thou, O most pure Maiden, daughter of earthly Adam, who hast been revealed as the Mother of God the Most High: Him do thou entreat that our souls may be saved!

*At the Aposticha, Resurrectional sticheron.*

*Tone 3:*

By Thy Passion, O Christ, Thou hast darkened the sun, and by the light of Thy Resurrection Thou hast enlightened all things: receive our evening hymn, O Lover of mankind!

*Then stichera of the Theotokos.*

*Tone 3, Podoben: "Great is the power of Thy Cross" (Ве́лїѧ крⷭ҇та̀):*[^564]

*Verse: Hear, O daughter, and see, and incline thine ear. (Ps. 44:11 LXX)*

Having received a great benefit through thee, O Most Pure, with the Angels we glorify thy Childbearing, which deigned to be born from thy womb by reason of extreme loving-kindness, and which hath refashioned the human race!

*Verse: I will remember thy name in every generation and generation. (Ps. 44:18 LXX)*

All of us sinners have acquired thee in life as a refuge and divine protection, O Pure One; therefore we all entreat thy loving-kindness: depart not from us, we pray, but have mercy and save us!

*Verse: The rich among the people shall entreat thy face. (Ps. 44:13 LXX)*

Worthily do we, thine earthly servants, bring "Rejoice!" unto thee, O Theotokos, Mother and Ever-Virgin, together with Gabriel the divine commander of the angelic ranks; for thou hast been the mediatress of joy and the rejoicing of the world!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 8:*

*In Solomon's porch...*

*Seek at Great Vespers, at the Aposticha, Glory.*[^565]

*The Troparion of the Tone, and the Dismissal.*

## AT GREAT VESPERS
