*At "Lord, I have cried", we set 10 verses. And we sing 3 Resurrectional stichera, and 4 Anatolian [Eastern] stichera, and 2 idiomela of the Paralytic, repeating the first.*

*Resurrectional stichera, Tone 3:*

By Thy Cross, O Christ Savior, the dominion of death was destroyed and the deceit of the devil was abolished; and the human race, saved by faith, ever offers a hymn unto Thee!

All things have been enlightened by Thy Resurrection, O Lord, and paradise is opened once more; and all creation, praising Thee, ever offers a hymn unto Thee!

I glorify the power of the Father and the Son, and I hymn the authority of the Holy Spirit: the undivided, uncreated Godhead, the Consubstantial Trinity, Which reigns unto ages of ages!

*Other stichera, Anatolian [Eastern]:*

We worship Thy precious Cross, O Christ, and we hymn and glorify Thy Resurrection: for by Thy wound were we all healed!

We hymn the Savior Who was incarnate of the Virgin; for for our sake He was crucified, and on the third day He arose, granting unto us great mercy!

Unto those in hades Christ descended, preaching good tidings: "Take courage," He said, "I have now conquered! I am the Resurrection, I shall lead you forth, having destroyed the gates of death!"

Unworthily standing in Thy most pure house, we send up an evening hymn, crying out from the depths, O Christ God: O Thou Who hast enlightened the world by Thy three-day Resurrection, deliver Thy people from the hand of Thine enemies, O Lover of mankind!

*Other idiomel stichera, of the Paralytic.*

*Tone 1:*

Having fashioned man with Thy most pure hand, O Compassionate One, Thou didst come to heal the ailing, O Christ: the paralytic at the Sheep Pool Thou didst raise up by Thy word; the disease of the woman with an issue of blood Thou didst cure; the tormented daughter of the Canaanite woman Thou didst have mercy upon; and the petition of the centurion Thou didst not despise; therefore we cry aloud: O Almighty Lord, glory to Thee! *(Twice)*

Being an unburied corpse, the paralytic, seeing Thee, cried aloud: Have mercy on me, O Lord, for my pallet became a tomb unto me; what is the gain of life unto me? I need not the Sheep Pool, for I have no man to put me in when the waters are troubled; but unto Thee, the Wellspring of healings, do I come, that I too with all may cry: O Almighty Lord, glory to Thee!

*Glory... Tone 5:*

Jesus went up to Jerusalem unto the Sheep Pool, called Bethesda in Hebrew, having five porches; for in them lay a multitude of the sick: for an Angel of God went down every year and troubled the water, and granted health unto those who stepped in with faith; and the Lord, seeing a man of many years in sickness, said unto him: Wilt thou be made whole? The sick man answered: Lord, I have no man, when the water is troubled, to put me into the pool; I have spent all my living upon physicians, and was not accounted worthy to obtain mercy. But the Physician of souls and bodies said unto him: Take up thy pallet and walk, proclaiming My power and great mercy unto the ends of the earth!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion: Tone 3:*

How should we not marvel at thy theanthropic Childbearing, O Most Pure? For without having accepted the trial of a man, O All-blameless One, thou gavest birth without a father unto a Son in the flesh, Who before the ages was begotten of the Father without a mother, Who in no wise suffered change, or confusion, or division, but preserved intact the property of both essences; therefore, O Lady, Virgin Mother, entreat Him that the souls of those who in Orthodox fashion confess thee to be the Theotokos may be saved!

*The Entrance.*

*"O Gladsome Light..."*

*Prokeimenon: "The Lord is King..." with its verses.*

*At the Litiya, the sticheron of the temple.*

*Glory... Tone 5:*

A man lay in sickness at the Sheep Pool, and seeing Thee, O Lord, he cried aloud: "I have no man, when the water is troubled, to put me into it; but when I am coming, another steps down before me and receives healing, while I lie sick!" And straightway the Savior had compassion on him and said unto him: "For thy sake I became man, for thy sake I clothed Myself in flesh, and sayest thou: 'I have no man'? Take up thy pallet and walk! All things are possible unto Thee, all obey Thee, all submit unto Thee: remember us all, and have mercy, O Holy One, as the Lover of mankind!"

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion, the same Tone:*

Thou art the temple and the door, the palace and the throne of the King, O all-honored Virgin, through whom my Redeemer, Christ the Lord, shone forth unto those sleeping in darkness, being the Sun of righteousness, willing to enlighten that which He fashioned with His own hand according to His image; therefore, O All-hymned One, as thou hast acquired motherly boldness toward Him, unceasingly entreat Him that our souls may be saved!

*At the Aposticha, Resurrectional sticheron.*

*Tone 3:*

By Thy Passion, O Christ, Thou hast darkened the sun, and by the light of Thy Resurrection Thou hast enlightened all things: receive our evening hymn, O Lover of mankind!

*And the Paschal Stichera with their verses: seek in the Sunday of Pascha at Matins, folio 65.*[^566]

*Glory... Tone 8:*

In Solomon's porch, there lay a multitude of the sick; and when the feast was at its midpoint, Christ found a paralytic who had lain for thirty-eight years, and with a Master's voice said unto him: "Wilt thou be made whole?" The sick man answered: "Lord, I have no man, when the water is troubled, to put me into the pool." But He said unto him: "Take up thy pallet and walk: behold, thou art made whole; sin no more!" By the intercessions of the Theotokos, send down upon us great mercy!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen.*

*"This is the day of Resurrection..." "Christ is risen from the dead..." once.*

*And the rest as prescribed for the past Sunday.*

*Troparion, Tone 3:*

Let the heavens be glad, let earthly things rejoice, for the Lord hath wrought strength with His arm; He hath trampled down death by death, He became the First-born from the dead; He delivered us from the belly of hades, and granted great mercy unto the world!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*

We hymn thee who mediated the salvation of our race, O Virgin Theotokos; for taking upon Himself suffering through the Cross in the flesh assumed from thee, Thy Son and our God delivered us from corruption, as the Lover of mankind!

*If there be no Vigil, at the Midnight Office we sing the Triadic Canon in the Octoechos, Tone 3, and "It is truly meet..."; and the rest as usual. And the Dismissal.*[^567]

## ON THE FOURTH SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA, OF THE PARALYTIC, AT MATINS

*At "God is the Lord", the Resurrectional Troparion twice:*

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*

*After the 1st Kathisma Psalmody, Sessional Hymns.*

*Tone 3:*

Christ is risen from the dead, the First-fruits of them that slept, the First-born of creation, and Maker of all things made; He renewed in Himself the corrupted nature of our race: no longer dost thou hold dominion, O death! For the Master of all destroyed thy power!

*Verse: Arise, O Lord my God! (Ps. 9:33 LXX)*

Having tasted death in the flesh, O Lord, by Thine Arising Thou hast cut off the bitterness of death, and having strengthened man against it, summoning him to victory over the ancient curse, O Defender of our life, Lord, glory to Thee!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen.*

Awed by the beauty of thy virginity and the exceeding brilliance of thy purity, Gabriel marveled and cried aloud unto thee, O Theotokos: "What worthy praise can I bring unto thee? What shall I call thee? I am in doubt and dismay! Therefore, as I was commanded, I cry unto thee: Rejoice, thou that art full of grace!"

*After the 2nd Kathisma Psalmody, Sessional Hymn.*

*Tone 3, Podoben: "Beholding the beauty of thy virginity" (Красотѣ̀ дѣ́вства):*

Having assumed all human things, and having accomplished all that was ours, Thou wast well-pleased to be nailed upon the Cross, O my Creator, accepting to endure death as man, that Thou mightest deliver mankind from death as God; therefore, as unto the Life-giver, we cry aloud unto Thee: Glory, O Christ, to Thy tender-hearted compassion!

*Verse: I will give thanks unto Thee, O Lord, with my whole heart. (Ps. 9:2 LXX)*

The incomprehensible Crucifixion and ineffable Arising do we faithful confess in theology as an unutterable mystery: for today death and hades have been despoiled, and the human race is clothed in incorruption; therefore with thanksgiving we cry aloud unto Thee: Glory, O Christ, to Thine Arising!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*

Heavenly things were rejoicing with love, and earthly things were dismayed with trembling, when the most pure voice came upon thee, O Theotokos; for one celebration shone forth for both, when He delivered the first-fashioned from death; therefore with the Angel we cry aloud unto thee: Rejoice, O pure Virgin Mother!

*After the Evlogetaria: "Blessed art Thou, O Lord..." Then:*[^568]

*Hypakoe, Tone 3:*

Striking awe by his appearance, yet refreshing with his words, the gleaming Angel said unto the Myrrh-bearing women: "Why seek ye the Living One in the tomb? He is arisen, Who emptied the tombs! Understand the Changeless One to be the Transformer of corruption; say ye unto God: How awesome are Thy works! For Thou hast saved the human race!"

*The Anavathmoi (Hymns of Ascent), Tone 3.*

*Antiphon 1:*

The captivity of Zion Thou didst lead forth from Babylon; lead me also from passions unto life, O Word!

They that sow in the South with divine tears shall reap the ears of everlasting life with joy!

*Glory...*

Unto the Holy Spirit belongs every thanksgiving, as He shines forth together with the Father and the Son, in Whom all things live and move!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. The same.*

*Antiphon 2:*

Except the Lord build the house of virtues, in vain do we labor; and if He protect our soul, no one shall destroy our city!

By the Spirit the fruit of the womb made adopted sons unto Thee, O Christ, even as unto the Father, are the saints always!

*Glory...*

Through the Holy Spirit is every holiness and wisdom foreseen, for He brings into essence every creature: let us serve Him, for He is God, even as the Father and the Word!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. The same.*

*Antiphon 3:*

Blessed are they that fear the Lord, walking in the paths of the commandments; for they shall eat the all-fruitful sustenance of life!

Round about thy table rejoice, O Chief Shepherd, beholding thine offspring bearing the branches of well-doing!

*Glory...*

Through the Holy Spirit is every wealth of glory, from Whom comes grace and life unto every creature: for He is hymned together with the Father and with the Word!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. The same.*

*At Matins*

*Prokeimenon, Tone 3:*
Say among the nations that the Lord reigns; for He has established the world, which shall not be moved.[^569]
*Verse:* Sing to the Lord a new song; sing to the Lord, all the earth!

*Let every breath praise the Lord.*

*Gospel from Luke, 4th Resurrection Gospel, Pericope 114:*[^570]

*Then: Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ, let us worship:*
*After Psalm 50, according to the custom. Then:*

*CANON OF PASCHA,*
*written on the Sunday of Pascha, with its heirmoi and with its Theotokia, to 8, which are written on the Sunday of the Holy Myrrh-bearing Women (see fol. 320);*[^571] *and of the Paralytic to 6.*

*Katavasia: It is the Day of Resurrection: both choirs together.*

*Canon of the Paralytic, Tone 3.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Marvelously and gloriously working wonders art Thou, O God, Who turned the abyss into dry land, and overwhelmed the chariots, and saved the people that sing to Thee as to our King and God!

*Troparion:*
Working signs, performing wonders, O only King, Thou didst willingly endure the Crucifixion as the Compassionate One, and having slain death by death, Thou hast made us alive!

*Troparion:*
In the Resurrection of Christ let the peoples make festival today with faith: hades has been despoiled, and with haste it surrendered the prisoners whom it held, who sing the mighty acts of God!

*Troparion:*
By Divine power, O Christ, having of old strengthened the paralytic by Thy word and commanded him to take up his bed, heal my soul, grievously afflicted by illness for a long time!

*Troparion:*
An Angel of old descended into the Sheep Pool and healed one man each year; but now Christ cleanses countless multitudes by Divine Baptism!

*To Archangel Michael:*[^572]
Leader of the Angels, Commander of the celestial ministers, protect and preserve from all temptations those who are gathered in thy venerable temple and hymn God!

*Glory... Triadikon:*
In three Persons, yet in one nature, we unceasingly hymn the unoriginate God with the bodiless powers: the Father, the Word, and the Spirit, Who possess an undivided Kingdom and dominion!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*
O Pure One, save thy city which ever faithfully honors thee from calamities, barbarian captivity, civil strife, the sword, and every other threatening affliction!

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
O barren and childless soul, acquire glorious fruit, and crying aloud with gladness, exclaim: I have been established through Thee, O God; there is none holy, there is none righteous beside Thee, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
Beholding Thee of old hanging upon the Tree, O Word, the sun hid its light, and all the earth was shaken; the dead arose when Thou didst become dead, O All-powerful One!

*Troparion:*
When Thou didst descend with Thy soul into the bowels of the earth, hades with haste gave up the souls which it held, as they cried to Thy dominion a hymn of thanksgiving, O only Lord!

*Troparion:*
Heal my soul, O All-good One, grievously ailing through many years, even as Thou didst the paralytic of old, that I may follow Thy paths which Thou hast shown to those who love Thee!

*To Archangel Michael:*
Together with the celestial ranks, O Archangel of God, make supplication for those who hymn thee with faith, guarding and protecting us who are assaulted by worldly passions!

*Glory... Triadikon:*
Glory to the Father, let us cry aloud, and to the Son, and to the Spirit; for God is one by nature, Whom all the heavenly powers glorify with fear, crying: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*
A seedless Conception and a birth beyond understanding hast thou had, O Virgin Pure Mother: an awesome work, an exceedingly great wonder, honored by Angels and glorified by men, O Maiden Lady!

*KONTAKION OF PASCHA AND IKOS, AND SESSIONAL HYMN, TONE 3:*

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 3:*
A voice alone strengthened the paralytic, as the one universal Word, Who appeared upon earth for our sake through tender mercy; therefore, carrying his bed, he passed along, even if the scribes could not endure to see what was done, being held by malice and envy which paralyzes souls!

*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*
Marveling at the beauty of thy virginity and the exceedingly radiant brightness of thy purity, Gabriel cried aloud unto thee, O Theotokos: What worthy praise shall I bring unto thee? And what shall I call thee? I am at a loss and astounded; therefore, as I was commanded, I cry to thee: Rejoice, O full of grace!

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Foreseeing the overshadowing mountain, even thy most pure womb, O Pure One, Habakkuk cried: God shall come from Teman, and the Holy One from the mountain overshadowed and densely wooded![^573]

*Troparion:*
The assembly of the Hebrews, consumed by envy, crucified Thee upon the Tree, O Lord; but having destroyed the condemnation of death, as Mighty Thou hast arisen, raising up the world together with Thyself!

*Troparion:*
Ye women with myrrh, why seek ye the inexhaustible Myrrh? He has arisen! said he who sat in white garments to the Myrrh-bearing women, filling them with the zealous spiritual fragrance!

*Troparion:*
Having taken the form of a servant, through Thine abundant tender mercy Thou didst come walking, O Word, and didst make whole him who had been lying prostrate for many years, commanding him also to take up his bed!

*Troparion:*
The Angel of the Lord indeed descended each year and troubled the water in the pool, making whole only one man; but Christ saves a countless multitude by Divine Baptism!

*To Archangel Michael:*
Leader of Angels and guide of the wandering, supreme Captain of the Lord, come into our midst at this hour, and offer the prayers of all to the only Creator and Master!

*Glory... Triadikon:*
United in nature, yet distinct in Persons, is the Holy Trinity: the transcendent Father, the co-eternal Son, and the Holy and one All-powerful Spirit!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*
O Pure One, how dost thou give suck? How hast thou given birth to an Infant, Who is older than Adam? How dost thou bear upon thine arms the Son, Who sits upon the shoulders of the Cherubim? Even as He knows, Who brought all things into being!

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
With Thy never-setting light, O Christ God, illumine my humble soul, and guide me in Thy fear, for Thy commandments are light!

*Troparion:*
Having been lifted up upon the Tree of the strong, Thou didst raise up the whole world together with Thyself; and having been numbered among the dead, O God, Thou raisest up the dead of all ages!

*Troparion:*
Christ has arisen, as He said, having emptied all the realms of hades; and He appears to the Apostles, granting everlasting joy!

*Troparion:*
An Angel flashing with light was seen by the women, clothed in white: Weep no more! Your Life has arisen, Who has made alive the dead in the tombs!

*Troparion:*
Even as Thou didst raise up the paralytic, O Christ, make whole my soul, which is paralyzed by transgressions, and prosper me to walk along Thy straight paths!

*To Archangel Michael:*
Guide of Angels, Michael, save the people who are gathered today in thy temple and proclaim the mighty acts of God!

*Glory... Triadikon:*
Equal in honor is the Tri-numbered Unity, which is indeed faithfully divided in Hypostases, yet united in nature: Father, Son, and Divine Spirit!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*
We hymn thy seedless childbearing, O Pure One, and thy incomprehensible giving of birth, magnifying thee as the Mother of the Creator and Master of all!

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
The deep of passions and a tempest of contrary winds have risen against me; but come before me and save me, O Savior, and deliver me from corruption, even as Thou didst save the Prophet from the beast![^574]

*Troparion:*
Having willingly been lifted up upon the Tree, Thou wast laid as one dead in the tomb; and having made alive all the dead in hades together, O Christ, Thou hast raised them by Thy Divine power!

*Troparion:*
Hades, having met Thee below, O Compassionate One, was embittered, as with haste it surrendered the bound, who hymn Thy fearsome Resurrection, O Savior, with unceasing voices!

*Troparion:*
The Divine disciples, beholding the Life of all, Christ, risen from the tomb, worshiped with great love, an upright heart, and spiritual gladness!

*Troparion:*
He who of old lay prostrate upon a bed of pain for many years, having been healed by Thy command, O Christ, glorifies and hymns Thy tender mercy, O Giver of Life!

*To Archangel Michael:*
Michael, guide of Angels, standing before the throne of the Master, come into our midst, guiding toward the paths of life us who have acquired thee as a fervent protector!

*Glory... Triadikon:*
I honor Thee as Trinity in Persons, and I proclaim Thee as Unity in essence, O unoriginate Father, Son, and right Spirit, God of all, together with the celestial, awesome hosts!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*
He Who upholds all things by His Divine nod is held in thine arms, O Virgin Theotokos, snatching us all from the hand of the servitude of the evil one, as the Compassionate One!

*Kontakion, Tone 3, Podoben: "Today the Virgin" (Дѣ́ва дне́сь):*
My soul, O Lord, grievously paralyzed by all manner of sins and improper deeds, raise up by Thy Divine intercession, even as Thou didst raise up the paralytic of old, that being saved I may cry unto Thee: O Compassionate One, glory, O Christ, to Thy dominion!

*Ikos:*
Thou Who holdest the ends of the earth in the hollow of Thy hand, O Jesus God, Who art co-unoriginate with the Father and co-equal with the Holy Spirit throughout the ages, hast appeared in the flesh, healing illnesses and driving away passions; Thou didst enlighten the blind, and by Thy Divine word Thou didst raise up the paralytic, commanding him forthwith to walk and to take upon his shoulders the bed that had carried him; therefore we all sing with him and cry aloud: O Compassionate One, glory, O Christ, to Thy dominion!

*Synaxarion on the Fourth Sunday after Pascha, of the Paralytic:*[^575]

*Verses:*
*The word of Christ was strength unto the paralytic;*
*Thus this word alone was his healing.*

On this same day, the Fourth Sunday after Pascha, we commemorate the Paralytic, and as is meet, we celebrate this miracle of our Lord, God, and Savior Jesus Christ. It was placed here because Christ performed this during the Jewish Pentecost; for having entered Jerusalem for the feast, and being in the porch of five porticoes which Solomon built, which was also named the Sheep Pool, because they washed the entrails of the sheep slaughtered in the sanctuary for sacrifice there; or because whoever entered there first, whenever the water was troubled once a year by an Angel, was shown to be healed. He finds there a man who had been ill for thirty-eight years, and who was in perplexity as to who might cast him, lying there, into the water; from whom also we are instructed how great a good are waiting and patience, and that since baptism was to be given which purges away every sin, God ordained that miracles should be wrought through water in the Old Dispensation, so that when that baptism should come, it might be easily accepted. Jesus comes to this Paralytic, who was so named, and asks him; and he presents his lack of anyone to assist him. And Christ, knowing that the man had languished in weakness for so long, says: Take up thy bed and walk. And immediately he is shown to be healed, and taking his bed upon his shoulder, lest the deed be thought an apparition, he carried it to his home. Since it was the Sabbath, he was forbidden by the Jews to walk. But he pointed to Him Who had healed him, as having told him to walk on the Sabbath, not knowing who He was; for Jesus, he says, had slipped away and hidden Himself, as a crowd had gathered there. Afterward Jesus found him in the sanctuary, and says to him: Behold, thou hast been made whole; sin no more, lest a worse thing come upon thee; Christ showed that the infirmity of paralysis had happened to him on account of sins. Yet not every sickness is from sins, but also comes upon us from natural illness, from gluttony, from neglect, and from many other causes. The paralytic man, having realized that it was Jesus Who had made him whole, makes this known to the Jews. And they, being provoked to anger, seek to kill Christ, because He was breaking the Sabbath. But He spoke many things to them, establishing that it is righteous to do good even on the Sabbath, and that He Himself is the One Who commanded the Sabbath to be kept, that He is equal to the Father, and even as the Father works hitherto, so also He works. It is to be known that this Paralytic is distinct from the one in Matthew; for that one was performed in a house, with men ministering to him, and he heard: Thy sins are forgiven thee; but this one was performed in a portico, and he had no man, as the Holy Gospel says, though he also took up his bed like that one. It is celebrated now because this also occurred during Pentecost, as did the accounts of the Samaritan Woman and the Blind Man. For Thomas and the Myrrh-bearers we celebrate for the assurance of Christ’s Resurrection from the dead; and the rest until the Ascension because He variously performed these during the time of the Jewish Pentecost, and because John briefly recorded them thus.

Through Thine ineffable mercy, O Christ our God, have mercy on us. Amen.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
Thou Who didst dew the flame of the furnace and save the youths unburned, blessed art Thou unto the ages, O Lord, the God of our fathers![^576]

*Troparion:*
Beholding Thee stretched out upon the Tree, the sun hid its light, unable to shine upon the world when Thou, O King of all, didst willingly set for the enlightenment of all the nations!

*Troparion:*
Thou hast arisen, having emptied the tombs and despoiled hades by Thine all-powerful might; therefore we sing of Thy venerable and Divine Arising, O Christ!

*Troparion:*
Why seek ye the Living as dead? When He is not in the tomb! cried of old the Divine Angel, flashing in appearance, unto the Myrrh-bearing women!

*Troparion:*
Having healed by Thy word the paralytic who had lain prostrate for many years, Thou didst cry aloud: Take up thy bed and walk, singing the mighty acts of God!

*To Archangel Michael:*
Michael, supreme Captain of the Lord, guide those who gather with faith in thy Divine temple for the praise of God, and protect them from every evil through thine intercession!

*Glory...:*
O Trinity, save from all calamities those who sing to Thee with faith as to the God and Master of all, and make them partakers of Thy good things!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*
Thou remainest a virgin after bearing beyond word Him Who was incorruptibly begotten before all ages from the unoriginate Father; therefore, O Pure One, we call thee blessed!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
God, Who is unceasingly glorified on high by the Angels, let the heavens of heavens, the earth, the mountains, the hills, the abyss, and all mankind bless with hymns as Creator and Redeemer, and exalt Him above all unto all ages![^577]

*Troparion:*
The veil was torn when Thou wast crucified, O our Savior, and it surrendered the dead whom death had swallowed up; and hades was stripped bare, beholding Thee having come into the lowest parts of the earth!

*Troparion:*
Where is thy sting, O death? Where is thy victory now, O hades? Christ the King having arisen, thou hast been put to death and perished, thou rulest no longer; for the Mighty One has taken away those whom thou didst hold bound!

*Troparion:*
Run quickly, announce the Resurrection to the Apostles! cried the young man who appeared to the Myrrh-bearing women: The Master has arisen, and with Him most gloriously the dead from the ages!

*Troparion:*
Lying prostrate for many years, the paralytic cried out: Have mercy on me, O Redeemer, who am held fast in perplexity! But He commands him to take up his bed with diligence, and to walk upright!

*To Archangel Michael:*
As commander of the immaterial powers, O supreme Captain, with them entreat for us deliverance from transgressions, the amendment of life, and the enjoyment of the eternal good things there!

*We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord!*

*Troparion:*
The uncreated, undivided Essence, the Tri-hypostatic Godhead, God the unoriginate Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, let us hymn in unison, crying aloud the fearsome song of the Seraphim!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*
Isaiah of old beheld thee as a scroll, O Prophetess, wherein by the Father’s finger the timeless Word was written, saving from all irrationality us who hymn thee with sacred words!

*We praise, we bless, we worship the Lord. And the Katavasia.*

*We do not sing More honorable than the Cherubim.*

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Upon Mount Sinai Moses beheld thee in the bush, who didst unconsumed conceive the fire of the Godhead in thy womb; and Daniel beheld thee as the unhewn mountain; a budded rod, Isaiah cried aloud, from the root of David![^578]

*Troparion:*
O Jesus, lifted up upon the Tree, Thou didst raise us up together with Thyself; and willingly laid in the tomb, Thou didst raise from the tombs all the dead, who hymn Thine incomprehensible dominion and Thine unconquerable might!

*Troparion:*
Most comely, Thou didst shine forth from the tomb like a bridegroom from his chamber, O most comely Word; and Thou didst destroy the gloom of hades, and didst lead forth the prisoners, who cry with one accord: Glory to Thy glory! Glory, O Jesus God, to Thine Arising!

*Troparion:*
Bearing sighs and tears, with myrrh the women reached the all-holy tomb in haste; and they were taught with faith of Christ's glorious Arising, which we celebrate, rejoicing in gladness of soul!

*Troparion:*
The health of the body followed Thy command, O Christ, and he who was formerly paralyzed was seen running with haste and carrying the bed upon which he had lain for many years, chanting the praise of Thy great might!

*To Archangel Michael:*
Entreat enlightenment for us, O great Captain, who standest favorably before the great Light, and pacify our life, which is ever shaken by the most grievous trials and the circumstances of this life, O praiseworthy one!

*Glory...:*
Light and Lights, Life and Lives, I glorify Thee in all piety, O Father, Word, and Holy Spirit, Tri-hypostatic Unity, undivided Dominion, unconfused Godhead, crying: Holy, Holy, Holy! with the celestial powers!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*
From thy light-bearing womb came forth the great Sun, Christ, and He enlightened the world, O Most Pure One, with radiant beams, and took away the darkness of transgression; therefore we sing to thee as the cause of all good things, O Bride of God!

*Then, Holy is the Lord our God, thrice, in Tone 3.*

*Exapostilarion of Pascha, once:*
Having fallen asleep in the flesh as a mortal, O King and Lord, on the third day Thou didst arise, raising Adam from corruption and abolishing death: O Pascha of incorruption, the salvation of the world!

*Another, Podoben: "Give ear, ye women" (Жены̀ ᲂу҆слы́шите):*

*Glory...:*
The Lover of mankind and all-merciful Lord stood by the Sheep Pool to heal diseases; and He found a man lying prostrate for many years, and cried unto him: Take up thy bed, and go into the right paths!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. The same.*

*AT THE PRAISES, we set 8 verses. And we sing the Resurrection stichera.*
*Tone 3:*

*Sticheron 1:*
Come, all ye nations, understand the power of the awesome mystery; for Christ our Savior, the Word Who was in the beginning, was crucified for us and was willingly buried, and arose from the dead to save all things: let us worship Him!

*Sticheron 2:*
Thy guards recounted all the wonders, O Lord; but the assembly of vanity filled their right hand with bribes, thinking to hide Thy Resurrection, which the world glorifies: have mercy on us!

*Sticheron 3:*
All things were filled with joy, having received the proof of the Resurrection; for Mary Magdalene came to the tomb and found an Angel sitting upon the stone, gleaming in his raiment, and saying: Why seek ye the Living among the dead? He is not here, but has arisen, as He said, going before you into Galilee!

*Sticheron 4:*
In Thy light, O Master, we shall see light, O Lover of mankind; for Thou hast arisen from the dead, granting salvation to the human race, that all creation may glorify Thee, the only Sinless One: have mercy on us!

*And Anatolian stichera, the same Tone:*[^579]

*Sticheron 5:*
A morning hymn the Myrrh-bearing women brought unto Thee with tears, O Lord; for having sweet spices of fragrance, they reached Thy tomb, striving to anoint Thy most pure Body. The Angel sitting upon the stone announced the good tidings to them: Why seek ye the Living among the dead? For having trampled down death, He has arisen as God, granting great mercy unto all!

*Sticheron 6:*
The flashing Angel at Thy life-giving tomb said to the Myrrh-bearing women: The Redeemer has emptied the tombs, despoiled hades, and arisen on the third day, as the only God and All-powerful!

*Sticheron 7:*
Seeking Thee at the tomb, having come on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene, when she found Thee not, wept with mourning, crying aloud: Woe is me, my Savior! Thou hast been stolen away, O King of all! But a pair of life-bearing Angels within the tomb cried aloud: Why weepest thou, O woman? I weep, she says, because they have taken my Lord from the tomb, and I know not where they have laid Him! And having turned back, when she saw Thee, she immediately cried: My Lord and my God, glory to Thee!

*Sticheron 8:*
The Hebrews enclosed Life in the tomb, but the thief opened Paradise by his tongue, crying and saying: He Who with me was crucified for my sake, hung with me upon the Tree, and appeared to me sitting upon the throne with the Father: for He is Christ our God, Who has great mercy!

*Glory... Tone 8:*
O Lord, it was not the pool that healed the paralytic, but Thy word renewed him; nor did his disease of many years hinder him: for the swift working of Thy voice was shown forth, and he cast away the unbearable burden and took up the weight of his bed as a testimony to the abundance of Thy compassions: glory to Thee!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen.*
*Most blessed art thou...*

*Great Doxology. Resurrection troparion, litanies, and dismissal, and the procession into the narthex.*

*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Gospel Sticheron, Tone 3:*[^580]
While Mary Magdalene announced the Savior's Resurrection from the dead and His manifestation, the disciples, not believing, were reproached for their hardness of heart; but having been armed with signs and wonders, they were sent forth unto preaching; and Thou indeed, O Lord, didst ascend to the Father, the primal Light; while they preached the word everywhere, confirming it with wonders; therefore, having been enlightened by them, we glorify Thy Resurrection from the dead, O Lord, Lover of mankind!

*And the Catechesis of St. Theodore the Studite.*[^581] *And the final dismissal. The First Hour.*

*At the Hours, the Resurrection troparion. After the Trisagion, the kontakion of the Triodion: My soul, O Lord...*

*At the LITURGY, the Beatitudes of the Tone, Tone 3, on 4:*

*Troparion 1:*
Forefather Adam, who cast aside Thy commandment, O Christ, Thou didst drive out from paradise; but the thief who confessed Thee upon the cross, O Compassionate One, Thou didst settle therein, crying: Remember me, O Savior, in Thy Kingdom!

*Troparion 2:*
Having arisen from the dead, Thou hast raised us up together from passions by Thy Resurrection, O Lord, and hast destroyed all the power of death, O Savior: therefore with faith we cry to Thee: Remember us also in Thy Kingdom!

*Troparion 3:*
By Thy three-day Burial, having made alive as God those put to death in hades, Thou didst raise them up together with Thyself; and as Good Thou hast poured forth incorruption upon all of us who ever cry with faith: Remember us also in Thy Kingdom!

*Troparion 4:*
When we had sinned, Thou didst condemn us with the curse of death, O Giver of Life and Lord; yet having suffered in Thy Body, O sinless Master, Thou didst make alive mortals who cry: Remember us also in Thy Kingdom!

*And from the canon, Ode 6, on 4.*

*After the Entrance, the Resurrection troparion; Glory, the kontakion of the Triodion; Both now, of Pascha: Though Thou didst descend into the tomb... But the troparion and kontakion of a temple of Christ, or of the Theotokos, or of the saints, we do not say.*

*Prokeimenon, Tone 1:*
Let Thy mercy, O Lord, be upon us, according as we have hoped in Thee.[^582]
*Verse:* Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous; praise is meet for the upright!

*Epistle from the Acts of the Apostles, Pericope 23:*[^583]
In those days, it came to pass, as Peter went through all quarters...

*Alleluia, Tone 5:*
I will sing of Thy mercies, O Lord, unto ages of ages.[^584]
*Verse:* For Thou hast said: Mercy shall be built up for ever!

*Gospel from John, Pericope 14:*[^585]
At that time, Jesus went up to Jerusalem...

*Kinonikon: Receive the Body of Christ... Another: Praise the Lord from the heavens...*

*It is meet to know that the office of the Paralytic is sung on Sunday and on Monday; and on Tuesday is its Apodosis.*[^586]

## ON THE SUNDAY OF THE PARALYTIC, AT VESPERS

*At Lord, I have cried, stichera of the feast, 3; and of the Menaion, 3. Stichera of the feast.*
*Tone 8, Podoben: "O most marvelous wonder" (Ѽ пресла́внагѡ чꙋдесѐ):*

*Sticheron 1:*
O most marvelous wonder! The Creator of all, having become clothed in flesh, willingly impoverished Himself for the sake of our nature as the Compassionate One; and having lived with men, He showed a multitude of wonders to the Hebrews; therefore, having come to Bethesda, He healed of old the paralytic, saying unto him: Take up thy bed!

*Sticheron 2:*
O Savior, my God and Lord, desiring to raise up fallen man, Thou didst walk upon earth as a man, healing the illnesses of all because of Thine abundant tender mercy; therefore, having come to the Sheep Pool, by Thy word Thou didst raise up whole the paralytic of old, who had been lying prostrate for thirty-eight years!

*Sticheron 3:*
Consumed by envy, O all-good Lord, making a pretext of Thy benefactions and burning with fury, while themselves continually acting lawlessly against the Law, the Hebrews sought to slay Thee Who art truly Life, because of the Sabbath, when Thou didst make whole the entire man who had formerly been paralyzed!

*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 5:*
At the Sheep Pool a man lay in infirmity, and beholding Thee, O Lord, he cried: I have no man, that, when the water is troubled, he might put me into it; and while I am coming, another steps down before me and receives healing, while I lie ailing! And immediately having had compassion, the Savior says to him: For thy sake I became man, for thy sake I clothed Myself in flesh, and sayest thou: I have no man? Take up thy bed and walk! All things are possible for Thee, all things give ear to Thee, all things obey Thee: remember us all, and have mercy, O Holy One, as the Lover of mankind!

*AT THE APOSTICHA, stichera, Tone 3:*

*Sticheron 1:*
By Thy Cross, O Christ Savior, the dominion of death has been destroyed, and the delusion of the devil has been abolished; while the human race, being saved by faith, ever offers a hymn to Thee!

*Verse: Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes, O Thou that dwellest in heaven!*[^587]

*Sticheron 2:*
An evening hymn we offer unto Thee, O Christ, with incense and spiritual songs: have mercy, O Savior, on our souls!

*Verse: Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us; for we are utterly filled with contempt.*[^588]

*Martyrion:*
Great is the power of Thy Cross, O Lord! For it was planted in one place, yet it operates in all the world; and it showed forth Apostles from fishermen, and Martyrs from the nations, that they may pray for our souls!

*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 1:*
Thou Who with Thy most pure palm didst fashion man, didst come, O Compassionate One, to heal the ailing, O Christ; by Thy word Thou didst raise up the paralytic at the Sheep Pool; and Thou didst heal the illness of the woman with an issue of blood; Thou didst have mercy on the tormented daughter of the Canaanite woman; and Thou didst not despise the petition of the centurion: therefore we cry: O All-powerful Lord, glory to Thee!

*Then the Resurrection troparion. And the dismissal.*

## ON MONDAY OF THE PARALYTIC, AT MATINS

*At God is the Lord, the Resurrection troparion, twice; Glory, of the saint, if there be one; Both now, the Theotokion of the first class in the tone of the troparion of the saint; but if not, Glory... Both now, the Theotokion of the first class of the Tone.*[^589]

*After the first Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 3:*
Christ has arisen from the dead, the first-fruits of those who have fallen asleep, the First-born of creation, and the Creator of all things that have been made; He has renewed in Himself the corrupted nature of our race: no longer dost thou hold dominion, O death, for the Master of all has destroyed thy power!

*Verse: O Lord, rebuke me not in Thine anger, neither chasten me in Thy wrath.*[^590]

O my soul living upon earth, repent: dust in the grave sings no hymns, nor delivers from transgressions; cry aloud unto Christ God: O Knower of hearts, I have sinned; before Thou judgest me, have mercy on me!

*Verse: God is wonderful in His saints, the God of Israel.*[^591]

The courage of your endurance conquered the wiles of the author of evil, O blessed passion-bearers; therefore were ye accounted worthy of eternal beatitude; but pray to the Lord to save the flock of Christ-loving people, as ye are martyrs of truth!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*

Marveling at the beauty of thy virginity and the exceedingly radiant brightness of thy purity, Gabriel cried aloud unto thee, O Theotokos: What worthy praise shall I bring unto thee? And what shall I call thee? I am at a loss and astounded; therefore, as I was commanded, I cry to thee: Rejoice, O full of grace!

*After the 2nd Kathisma Psalmody, Sessional Hymn.*
*Tone 3, Podoben: "Beholding the beauty of thy virginity" (Красотѣ̀ дѣ́вства):*

Those who were paralyzed found the all-healing cure of the paralytic, yet being bound by envy, they pondered the strengthening of the paralytic on the Sabbath, saying: It is not lawful to heal on the Sabbath, nor to break the ancestral Sabbath rest of the Law; for they knew not Thee, the Master of the Law and the Healer of our souls!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. The same.*

*Then: Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ... Psalm 50. Then:*
*The Canon of the Paralytic, with the heirmoi, to 8; and of the Menaion, to 6.*[^592]
*The Kontakion and Exapostilarion of the Paralytic.*

*At the Praises, we set 6 verses, and we sing the following stichera from the Octoechos.*
*Tone 3:*

*Sticheron 1:*
Come, all ye nations, understand the power of the dread mystery: for Christ our Savior, the Word Who was in the beginning, was crucified for our sake, and was willingly buried, and arose from the dead, that He might save all things: let us worship Him! *Twice.*

*Sticheron 2:*
Often as I offer hymnody, I am found fulfilling sin, uttering hymns with my tongue, while meditating on improper things with my soul; but set both aright through repentance, O Christ God, and have mercy on me!

*Martyrion:*
Come, all ye peoples, let us honor the memory of the holy passion-bearers; for having become a spectacle unto Angels and men, they received from Christ the crown of victory, and they pray for our souls!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 1:*

Being an unburied corpse, the paralytic, beholding Thee, cried aloud: Have mercy on me, O Lord, for my bed has become my grave! What is the gain of my life? I have no need of the Sheep Pool, for I have no man to cast me in when the waters are troubled; but unto Thee, the Wellspring of healings, do I come, that I also may cry with all: O Almighty Lord, glory to Thee!

*At the Aposticha, stichera.*
*Tone 3, Podoben: "Great is the power of Thy Cross, O Lord" (Ве́лїѧ крⷭ҇та̀):*

*Sticheron 1:*
Beholding the power of signs and wonders, those paralyzed by envy and strong in malice did not believe that Thou art the Son of God and the Disposer of all, Who didst show the paralytic whole by a word.

*Verse: Thy mercies, O Lord, I will sing for ever.*[^593]

*Sticheron 2:*
Beholding the paralytic strengthened on the Sabbath, the keepers of the sabbaths were darkened in soul, and cried aloud: It is not lawful to heal on the Sabbath and to defile the Sabbath, as if they were lawful scribes!

*Verse: For Thou hast said: Mercy shall be built up for ever.*[^594]

*Sticheron 3:*
Not knowing Thee, the Creator and Lord of the sabbaths, they who observe the sabbaths murmured at the strengthening of the paralytic that took place on the Sabbath, saying: It is not good to take up a bed on the sabbath day!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 5:*

Jesus went up to Jerusalem, to the Sheep Pool, called Bethesda in Hebrew, having five porches; for in them lay a multitude of the sick: for an Angel of God descended at certain seasons and troubled the water, and granted health to those who stepped down with faith; and the Lord, seeing a man sick for a long time, says unto him: Wilt thou be made whole? The sick man answered: Lord, I have no man, that, when the water is troubled, he might put me into the pool: I have spent all my living upon physicians, and was not accounted worthy to obtain mercy; but the Physician of souls and bodies says unto him: Take up thy bed and walk, proclaiming My power and great mercy unto the ends of the earth!

*Then: It is good to give thanks unto the Lord... The First Hour. And the Dismissal.*

*On Monday of the Fourth Week after Pascha, the Triode, whose acrostic is: Anestē ho Sōtēr, that is:*[^595]
*The Savior is Risen.*

*Tone 3. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Israel of old passed through the sea divided by the rod as through a wilderness, and manifestly prepared paths in the likeness of the Cross; therefore let us sing in praise unto our marvelous God, for He has been glorified!

*A. Troparion:*
Having ascended on high, Thou didst take captivity captive that was held in hades, as the Mighty One, O Savior, and didst raise up all together with Thyself, having risen on the third day from the grave, O Lover of mankind, as Almighty!

*N. Troparion:*[^596]
Beholding Thee of old slain, O Savior, and buried in a new tomb, hades remained entirely dead and inactive; while all the dead, rejoicing at Thy life-bearing Arising, were loosed from their bonds!

*Glory...*
*E. Troparion:*
Why seek ye the Living among the dead? said the radiant Angel appearing of old to the Myrrh-bearing women at the tomb: Go ye quickly, and make haste to announce His Arising unto the Apostles!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*
*S. Theotokion:*
Beholding Him Who was ineffably incarnate from thy most pure blood, O Theotokos, and Who willingly accepted death in the flesh for our sake, risen from the tomb, thou didst magnify Him, glorifying Him with joy!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
The Babylonian furnace did not burn the Children, nor did the fire of the Godhead consume the Virgin; therefore with the Children let us, the faithful, cry aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*T. Troparion:*
Beholding the crucified Lord of old, the sun hid its light, the rocks were rent, the mountains quaked, the earth trembled, and they who of old were prisoners were loosed from their bonds!

*I. Troparion:*
When notorious hades beheld Thee, O Almighty Word, visibly descending unto it, it trembled, and released all the dead, who hymn Thy dominion and loving-kindness!

*Glory...*
*O. Troparion:*
The Lord has arisen! Let us all cry aloud, and clap our hands with faith, and form choral dances, proclaiming His power, and crying: Praise the Lord, all ye works, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*
*S. Theotokion:*
Thou didst conceive, O All-immaculate One, Him Who upholds all things, and gavest birth to Him in the flesh, Who led death captive by His three-day death: Him do thou entreat to put to death the passions of my soul, and to save me!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Her that was prefigured upon Sinai in the bush and in the fire unto Moses the Lawgiver, and that conceived the Fire of the Godhead unburnt in her womb, the all-radiant and unquenchable lamp, the true Theotokos, honoring her in hymns we magnify!

*Ō. Troparion:*
O most beautiful Christ, how did Thy radiant beauty set upon the Cross? How does the earth endure seeing Thee hanging? How did it bear Thine unjust slaying? We hymn Thine abundant and ineffable descent, O Word!

*T. Troparion:*
By Thy three-day Burial the enemy was taken captive, and the dead were released from the bonds of hades, death was put to death, and the realms of hades were despoiled; therefore, honoring Thee in hymns, O Giver of life, we magnify Thee!

*Glory...*
*I. Troparion:*
O Eternal Life, how didst Thou willingly taste of death for our sake, O Savior? How didst Thou mingle with the dead, O Resurrection of all, and despoil the treasures of hades? Therefore, honoring Thee with thanksgiving in hymns, we magnify Thee!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*
*R. Theotokion:*
Deliver this city and the people who flee unto thee, O pure Mother of God, who gavest birth to Christ, from every adversarial wrath, and captivity, and the invasion of nations, that we may worthily magnify thee in hymns!

## ON MONDAY OF THE PARALYTIC, AT VESPERS

*At Lord, I have cried, we set 6 verses. And we sing the following two idiomela, repeating the first; and 3 from the Menaion.*[^597]

*Tone 1:*

*Sticheron 1:*
Having fashioned man with Thy most pure palm, Thou didst come, O Compassionate One, to heal the ailing, O Christ; by Thy word Thou didst raise up the paralytic in the Sheep Pool; and Thou didst heal the disease of the woman with an issue of blood; Thou didst have mercy on the tormented daughter of the Canaanite woman; and Thou didst not despise the request of the centurion: therefore we cry aloud: O Almighty Lord, glory to Thee! *Twice.*

*Sticheron 2:*
Being an unburied corpse, the paralytic, beholding Thee, cried aloud: Have mercy on me, O Lord, for my bed has become my grave! What is the gain of my life? I have no need of the Sheep Pool, for I have no man to cast me in when the waters are troubled; but unto Thee, the Wellspring of healings, do I come, that I also may cry with all: O Almighty Lord, glory to Thee!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 5:*

Jesus went up to Jerusalem, to the Sheep Pool, called Bethesda in Hebrew, having five porches; for in them lay a multitude of the sick: for an Angel of God descended at certain seasons and troubled the water, and granted health to those who stepped down with faith; and the Lord, seeing a man sick for a long time, says unto him: Wilt thou be made whole? The sick man answered: Lord, I have no man, that, when the water is troubled, he might put me into the pool: I have spent all my living upon physicians, and was not accounted worthy to obtain mercy; but the Physician of souls and bodies says unto him: Take up thy bed and walk, proclaiming My power and great mercy unto the ends of the earth!

*And straightway:*
*O Joyous Light:*
*The Prokeimenon of the day:*

*At the Aposticha, stichera from the Octoechos.*
*Tone 3:*

*Sticheron 1:*
All things have been enlightened by Thy Resurrection, O Lord, and paradise is opened once more; and all creation, praising Thee, ever offers a hymn unto Thee!

*Verse: Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes, O Thou that dwellest in heaven.*[^598]

*Sticheron 2:*
Save me, O Lord my God, for Thou art the salvation of all; the storm of passions confounds me, and the burden of transgressions drowns me: reach forth a hand of help unto me, and lead me up unto the light of compunction, as the only Compassionate One and Lover of mankind!

*Verse: Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us; for we are utterly filled with contempt.*[^599]

*Martyrion:*
Great is the power of Thy martyrs, O Christ! For they lie in their tombs, yet they cast out spirits, and have abolished the power of the enemy through Trinitarian faith, having fought the good fight according to piety!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 8:*

In Solomon's porch, there lay a multitude of the sick; and when the feast was halfway through, Christ found a man lying paralyzed for thirty-eight years, and with the voice of the Master He says unto him: Wilt thou be made whole? The sick man answered: Lord, I have no man, that, when the water is troubled, he might put me into the pool. But He says unto him: Take up thy bed and walk: behold, thou art made whole; sin no more! Through the intercessions of the Theotokos, send down upon us Thy great mercy!

*Then: Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart... After the Our Father, the Troparion, and the Dismissal.*

## ON TUESDAY OF THE PARALYTIC, AT MATINS

*At God is the Lord, the Resurrectional troparion, twice.*
*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*

*After the 1st Kathisma Psalmody, Sessional Hymn.*
*Tone 3:*

Having tasted of death in the flesh, O Lord, Thou didst cut short the bitterness of death by Thine Arising, and didst strengthen man against it, recalling the victory over the ancient curse: O Defender of our life, Lord, glory to Thee!

*Verse: O Lord, rebuke me not in Thine anger, neither chasten me in Thy wrath.*[^600]

How long, O my soul, dost thou remain in sins? How long dost thou postpone repentance? Call to mind the judgment to come, and cry aloud unto the Lord: I have sinned, O Sinless One, have mercy on me!

*Verse: God is wonderful in His saints, the God of Israel.*[^601]

*Martyrion:*
Ye shine forth by faith as exceedingly radiant luminaries, O holy ones, lovers of piety, all-lauded passion-bearers; for having feared not the wounds inflicted by tormentors, ye cast down the delusion of idols, possessing an invincible victory, even the true Cross!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*
Refuge and strength, O Theotokos, mighty help of the world, by thine intercessions save thy servants from every necessity, O only Blessed One!

*After the 2nd Kathisma Psalmody, Sessional Hymn.*
*Tone 1 [Tone 3], Podoben: "Beholding the beauty of thy virginity" (Красотѣ̀ дѣ́вства):*[^602]

Those who were paralyzed found the all-healing cure of the paralytic, yet being bound by envy, they pondered the strengthening of the paralytic on the Sabbath, saying: It is not lawful to heal on the Sabbath, nor to break the ancestral Sabbath rest of the Law; for they knew not Thee, the Master of the Law and the Healer of our souls!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. The same.*

*Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ... Psalm 50.*
*The Canon of the Paralytic, with the heirmos, to 8; and of the Menaion, to 6.*
*The Kontakion and Exapostilarion of the Paralytic.*

*At the Praises, we set 6 verses, repeating the first.*
*Tone 3:*

*Sticheron 1:*
Thy guards proclaimed all the wonders, O Lord; but the council of vanity, having filled their right hand with a bribe, thought to conceal Thy Resurrection, which the world glorifies: have mercy on us! *Twice.*

*Sticheron 2:*
Gather my scattered mind, O Lord, and cleanse my frozen heart, giving me repentance as to Peter, sighs as to the publican, and tears as to the harlot, that with a great voice I may cry unto Thee: O God, save me, as the only Compassionate One and Lover of mankind!

*Martyrion:*
Casting away the fear of kings and tormentors, the soldiers of Christ boldly and manfully confessed Him to be the Lord, God, and King of all; and they pray unceasingly for our souls!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 8:*

O Lord, not the pool healed the paralytic, but Thy word renewed him, nor did his long-standing disease hinder him; for the most swift operation of Thy voice was shown, and he cast away the unbearable weight, and carried the burden of his bed, as a testimony of the multitude of Thy tender mercies: glory to Thee!

*At the Aposticha, stichera.*
*Tone 3, Podoben: "Great is the power of Thy Cross, O Lord" (Ве́лїѧ крⷭ҇та̀):*

*Sticheron 1:*
Thy word was revealed to the paralyzed limbs as a life-bearing announcement, O my Life-creating Word, whose testimony was the taking up of the bed beyond all hope, which he carried at Thy command, having lain upon it for a long time!

*Verse: Thy mercies, O Lord, I will sing for ever.*[^603]

*Sticheron 2:*
Rejoicing, the paralytic fulfills the command of Thine almighty Masterly power, and walked carrying his bed, and cried out in testimony: He that made me whole commanded me to do this!

*Verse: For Thou hast said: Mercy shall be built up for ever.*[^604]

*Sticheron 3:*
He that had lain prostrate for many years and seasons, being paralyzed in limbs, cries: Have mercy on me, O Christ Deliverer, declared in perplexity; and having strengthened the man's limbs, the Savior commanded him to take up his bed!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 5:*

At the Sheep Pool a man lay in infirmity, and beholding Thee, O Lord, he cried: I have no man, that, when the water is troubled, he might put me into it; and while I am coming, another steps down before me and receives healing, while I lie ailing! And straightway the Savior, having had compassion, says unto him: For thy sake I became man, for thy sake I clothed Myself in flesh, and sayest thou: I have no man? Take up thy bed and walk! All things are possible for Thee, all things give ear to Thee, all things obey Thee: remember us all, and have mercy, O Holy One, as the Lover of mankind!

*Then: It is good to give thanks unto the Lord... The Resurrectional troparion, and its Theotokion. And the Dismissal.*

*On Tuesday of the Paralytic, the Triode, whose acrostic is: Psalmōdia Iōsēph, that is:*[^605]
*The Psalmody of Joseph.*

*Tone 3. Ode 2. Heirmos:*[^606]
As the shower upon the herb, and as the frost upon the grass, so let my words come down upon the earth!

*Ps. Troparion:*
Let us shout aloud in psalms, let us clap our hands joyfully: the Giver of life has arisen from the dead!

*A. Troparion:*
Thou didst ascend Thy Cross, O Christ, girded with power, and Thou didst arise from the dead, as Thou hadst foretold!

*L. Troparion:*
Clothed in white garments, an Angel was seen by the women, crying: He is risen, Who is the Resurrection and salvation of the faithful!

*Glory...*
*M. Troparion:*
Hastening to anoint Thee, the women went unto the tomb; and seeing Him risen, they worshiped Him!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*
*Ō. Theotokion:*
As a morning Sun, bearing Him upon thine arm, O Virgin, thou hast shone forth upon us who are in darkness!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
God, Who is unceasingly glorified in the highest by Angels, let the heavens of heavens, the earth, and the mountains, and the hills, and the abyss, and all the human race bless in hymns as Creator and Deliverer, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!

*D. Troparion:*
The law-transgressing council of the Jews crucified Thee upon the Tree, O Master, Who dost divinely heal the harm that came upon men through the tree; therefore with joyful voices we ever hymn Thee!

*I. Troparion:*
Being equal with the Father and the Spirit, O Christ, Thou didst endure the Cross; and being numbered among the dead, Thou didst despoil the realms of hades most gloriously; and having arisen, Thou didst raise up all creation with Thyself!

*Glory...*
*A. Troparion:*
O all-devouring hades, where is thy sting? Where is thy victory, O death? Thou hast been put to death by Him Who arose from the dead, Christ the Savior, the only Life-giver, Whom we the faithful hymn together with the Father and the Spirit!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*
*I. Theotokion:*
That God might deify humanity, He became man of thee, O all-immaculate, pure Maiden: Whom thou didst behold, more beautiful than all, come forth from the tomb as Conqueror of hades, and thou wast filled with joy!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*[^607]
Upon Mount Sinai Moses beheld thee in the bush, having conceived the Fire of the Godhead unburnt in thy womb; and Daniel beheld thee as the unhewn mountain; a budded rod, cried Isaiah, from the root of Jesse!

*Ō. Troparion:*
As a lamb led to the slaughter Thou wast brought of Thine own will, O Master Jesus, not crying aloud nor lifting up Thy voice, as it is written: by Thy death, O Word, Thou hast made us immortal who praise Thy most pure Passion and Thy dread reviving from hades!

*S. Troparion:*
Having been crushed, Thou didst renew us, O Jesus, King of all, by Thy precious and dread Resurrection; and having appeared unto the disciples, Thou Thyself didst grant Thy peace, O Lover of mankind: grant this also unto us who praise Thy Divine Arising!

*Glory...*
*I. Troparion:*
The honorable assembly of the Myrrh-bearing women came in haste unto Thy holy tomb, O Master, that they might faithfully anoint Thee; and they beheld an Angel sitting in white garments, and saying unto them: Why seek ye to see the Living among the dead?

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*
*Ph. Theotokion:*
Thou hast given birth to the Light-giver and Lord, being the gate of light; beholding Him shining forth from the tomb, thou wast filled with joy: but entreat Him, O Virgin, to grant me joyful weeping, which procures that future consolation, O Pure One!

## ON TUESDAY OF THE FOURTH WEEK AFTER PASCHA, AT VESPERS

*We celebrate Mid-Pentecost.*[^608]

*The beginning according to custom, and the Kathisma in order.*
*At Lord, I have cried, we set 6 verses. And we sing the following 3 stichera, repeating them.*
*Tone 4, Podoben: "O Lord, having ascended the Cross" (Гдⷭ҇и возше́дъ на крⷭ҇тъ):*

*Sticheron 1:*
The midpoint of the days has arrived, beginning from the saving Arising, and sealed by the Divine Pentecost; and it shines, having splendor on both sides, and uniting both, and prefiguring the glory to come, it is honored before the Master's Ascension!

*Sticheron 2:*
Zion heard and was glad when the Resurrection of Christ was announced; and His faithful ones in Zion rejoiced, beholding Him and cleansing by the Spirit the defilement of Christ-slaying: keeping festival, the joyful midpoint prepares itself on both sides!

*Sticheron 3:*
The abundant outpouring of the Divine Spirit upon all has drawn near, as it is written: the midpoint, proclaimed beforehand, after Christ's Death, Burial, and Resurrection, points to the manifestation of the Comforter, which was given to the disciples according to His true promise!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 6:*

As the feast of Thy Resurrection and of the Divine coming of Thy Holy Spirit is at its midpoint, O Christ, having assembled, we hymn the mysteries of Thy wonders: whereon send down upon us Thy great mercy!

*Entrance.*
*The Prokeimenon of the day. Three Readings:*

*Reading from the Prophecy of Micah (Chapter 4):*[^609]

Thus says the Lord: Out of Zion shall go forth the Law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem; and He shall judge between many peoples, and shall rebuke strong nations afar off; for all peoples shall walk each in his own way, but we will walk in the Name of the Lord our God for ever. Thus says the Lord Almighty: Hear, O ye hills, the judgment of the Lord, and ye valleys, the foundations of the earth; for the Lord has a controversy with His people, and will plead with Israel, saying: O My people, what have I done unto thee? Or wherein have I grieved thee? Or wherein have I wearied thee? Answer Me! For I brought thee up out of the land of Egypt, and redeemed thee out of the house of bondage, and sent before thy face Moses, Aaron, and Miriam. O My people, [remember now] what counsel they took against you, even the adversaries;[^610] who has declared it unto thee? For I have declared unto thee, O man, what is good, or what the Lord requires of thee, but to do justice, to love mercy, and to be ready to walk with the Lord thy God: for the Lord shall be magnified in strength, and shall feed His flock in peace, even unto the ends of the earth!

*Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Chapter 55):*[^611]

Thus says the Lord: Ye that thirst, go to the water, and as many as have no money, go and buy, and eat and drink without money and without price, wine and fatness. For thus says the Lord Almighty unto you: O My people, draw water with gladness from the wells of salvation! And in that day thou shalt say: Hymn the Lord, call upon His Name, proclaim His glorious deeds among the Gentiles, remember that His Name is exalted! O My people, give ear unto Me, and ye shall eat good things, and your soul shall delight itself in good things. Incline your ears, and follow My paths; give ear unto Me, and your soul shall live in good things, and I will make an everlasting covenant with you, and call upon Me. And when ye draw near unto Me, let the ungodly forsake his ways, and the unrighteous man his counsels, and return unto Me, and I will have mercy on you, and will forgive your sins. For My counsels are not as your counsels, neither are My ways as your ways, says the Lord; but as heaven is distant from the earth, so is My way distant from your ways, and your thoughts from My thoughts. For as rain or snow descends from heaven, and returns not thither until it has watered the earth, and brought forth and budded, and given seed to the sower, and bread for food: so shall My word be, whatsoever goes forth ...from My mouth, it shall not return unto Me empty, until it accomplishes all whatsoever I willed; and I will make straight thy ways and My commandments. For ye shall go forth with gladness, and be instructed with joy; for the mountains and hills shall skip, expecting you in joy, and all the trees of the field shall clap with their branches; and instead of the bramble shall come up the cypress, and instead of the nettle shall come up the myrtle; and the Lord shall be for a name, and for an everlasting sign, and shall not fail, says the Lord God, the Holy One of Israel.

*Reading from Proverbs (Chapter 9):*[^612]

Wisdom has built a house for herself, and set up seven pillars. She has killed her beasts; she has mingled her wine in a bowl, and prepared her table. She has sent forth her servants, calling with a high proclamation to the bowl, saying: Whosoever is foolish, let him turn aside unto me; and to them that want understanding she said: Come, eat of my bread, and drink wine which I have mingled for you. Leave foolishness, and ye shall live; and seek understanding, that ye may live, and make straight understanding in knowledge. He that reproves the wicked shall get to himself dishonor, and he that rebukes an ungodly man shall make himself blameworthy, for reproofs to the ungodly are wounds to him. Rebuke not the wicked, lest they hate thee; rebuke a wise man, and he will love thee. Give an opportunity to a wise man, and he will be yet wiser; declare unto a just man, and he will continue to receive it. The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and the counsel of the saints is understanding; for to know the Law is the character of a good mind. For in this way thou shalt live long, and years of thy life shall be added unto thee.

*Then the Litany: Let us all say... and the Exclamation. Then: Vouchsafe, O Lord...*
*After this: Let us complete our evening prayer...*
*At the Aposticha, idiomela stichera, Tone 1 (By the Monk John):*

The midpoint of the fifty days has arrived, wherein Christ, having manifested a glimpse of His Divine power, strengthened the paralytic by a word, raising him up from his bed; and working wonders in a God-befitting manner in a created body, He granted eternal life and great mercy unto mankind.

*Verse: Remember Thy congregation, which Thou hast purchased from the beginning.*[^613]

Into the sanctuary Thou didst come, O Wisdom of God, when the feast was halfway through, teaching and refuting the disobedient Jews, Pharisees, and Scribes, and crying aloud with boldness unto them: Let him that is thirsty come unto Me and drink living water, and he shall never thirst for ever; he that believes in My goodness, rivers of living water shall flow out of his belly! O the goodness and tender compassion of Thine, Christ our God, glory to Thee!

*Tone 2:*
*Verse: But God is our King before the ages, He has wrought salvation in the midst of the earth.*[^614]

When the midpoint of the feast had arrived, Jesus went up into the sanctuary and taught the disobedient Jews, saying: Let him that is thirsty come unto Me and drink living, eternal water, and he shall never thirst for ever; he that believes in Me, rivers shall flow out of his belly, and he shall have the light of life.

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 8:*

When the feast was halfway through, as Thou didst teach, O Savior, the Jews said: How does this man know letters, having never learned? For they understood not that Thou art the Wisdom that established the world: glory to Thee!

*After: Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart... and after: Our Father...*
*Troparion, Tone 8:*

Having reached the midpoint of the feast, quench the thirst of my soul with the waters of piety, for Thou didst cry aloud unto all, O Savior: Let him that is thirsty come unto Me and drink! O Wellspring of our life, Christ our God, glory to Thee!

*Then the Priest: Wisdom! And the Dismissal according to custom.*
*At Compline, we sing the stichera and canon of the saint of the day. The Kontakion of the feast of Mid-Pentecost.*
*At the Midnight Office, after the 1st Trisagion, the troparion of the feast; after the 2nd Trisagion, the kontakion of the feast. Then: Lord, have mercy (12 times). And the Dismissal. We do not say the prayers for the reposed: Remember, O Lord, in hope...*

## ON WEDNESDAY OF MID-PENTECOST, AT MATINS

*At God is the Lord, the Troparion of the feast, thrice.*
*After the 1st Kathisma Psalmody, Sessional Hymn.*
*Tone 4, Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*

Knowing the thoughts of the hearts of all, standing in the midst of the sanctuary, Thou didst call aloud, speaking the truth unto the deceitful: Why seek ye to kill Me, the Giver of life? As the feast was halfway through, Thou didst boldly cry: Judge not according to appearance, but judge righteous judgment, O transgressors of the Law!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. The same.*
*And a reading from the Commentary on the Gospel of John.*
*After the 2nd Kathisma Psalmody, Sessional Hymn.*
*Tone 5, Podoben: "The Word co-unoriginate" (Собезнача́льное Сло́во):*

Standing in the temple, as the honorable feast of Pentecost was halfway through, speaking unto the Hebrews, the Master of all clearly refuted in great boldness, as being King and God, their insolent tyranny; and unto us all, through His tender compassion, He grants great mercy.

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. The same.*
*Then: Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ... and Psalm 50.*
*Two canons of the feast of Mid-Pentecost, with heirmoi to 14: the first with heirmoi to 8, and the second to 6.*
*Afterwards the Katavasia, the heirmos of the second canon, both choirs together.*

*The Canon of Lord Theophanes, whose acrostic is: Mésin eortōn tōn megistōn ainesō, that is: I will praise the midpoint of the greatest feasts.*[^615]
*Tone 4. Ode 1. Heirmos:*[^616]

Having traversed on foot with dryshod steps the deep of the Red Sea, ancient Israel conquered the might of Amalek in the wilderness by the hands of Moses stretched out crosswise.

*M. Troparion:*
All the benefactions of Thy Divine Incarnation, O Master, which surpass the mind, shine upon us: gifts and graces and Divine splendors flowing forth abundantly.

*E. Troparion:*
Thou didst come, O Christ, sending forth the splendors of the Godhead openly in the midst of the feast; for Thou art the joyful Feast of those who are saved, and the Mediator of our salvation.

*S. Troparion:*
Thou wast made unto us from God wisdom, righteousness, and redemption, O Lord, leading us from earth unto heavenly height, and granting the Divine Spirit.

*I. Troparion:*
Thy flesh saw no corruption in the grave, O Master, but as it was composed without seed, so it received no corruption, not having been subject to the succession of nature in a supersubstantial manner.

*Another Canon, the work of Lord Andrew of Crete.*
*Tone 8. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Thou didst thicken the sea...

*Troparion 1:*
Ye nations, clap your hands; weep, ye Hebrews! For Christ the Giver of life has burst the bonds of hades, and raised the dead, and healed infirmities by a word: He is our God, Who gives life unto them that believe in His Name!

*Troparion 2:*
Thou didst show forth a wonder, turning water into wine, O Master Who didst turn the rivers into blood in Egypt; and Thou didst raise the dead, having accomplished this second sign: glory, O Savior, to Thine ineffable counsel; glory to Thine emptying, whereby Thou hast renewed us!

*Troparion 3:*
Being the ever-flowing stream of true life, O Lord, Thou art our Resurrection: Thou wast willing to labor, O my Savior, and of Thy will Thou didst thirst, submitting to the laws of nature; and having come in the flesh to Sychar, Thou didst ask water to drink of the Samaritan woman.

*Troparion 4:*
Thou didst bless the loaves, Thou didst multiply the fishes, O incomprehensible God, and didst bountifully satisfy the people; and Thou didst promise the ever-flowing spring of wisdom unto them that thirst: Thou art our Savior God, Who hast given life unto them that believe in Thy Name.

*Glory... Triadicon:*
Three co-unoriginate and co-enthroned Hypostases I glorify: God the unoriginate Father, and the co-unoriginate Son, and the Spirit co-ever-existing with the Son; one tri-hypostatic essence, one supreme unoriginate principle I hymn, and I revere the unoriginate Godhead and essence.

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*
Thou alone, O Mother of God, didst contain thy Creator in thy womb, and in the flesh didst give birth to Him ineffably, and didst remain a Virgin, with thy virginity in nowise impaired: Him, O Pure One, as thy Son and God, pray unceasingly ever for thy flock.

*Katavasia:*
Thou didst thicken the sea, drowning proud Pharaoh with his arms; and Thou didst save the people dryshod, O Lord, and didst lead them into the mountain of sanctuary, who cry: Let us sing a song of victory unto Thee, our God, for He has been glorified!

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Thy Church rejoices in Thee, O Christ, crying: Thou art my strength, O Lord, and refuge, and confirmation!

*N. Troparion:*
Thou didst open the fountains of life-creating waters unto the Church, crying: If any man thirst, let him come eagerly and drink, O Good One!

*E. Troparion:*
Manifestly Thou didst declare that Thou wouldst ascend from earth unto heaven, and didst promise to send down from heaven the Holy Spirit.

*O. Troparion:*
He that by nature is life-creating, the Lord Who was born of the Virgin, granted immortality unto all the faithful, as being tenderly compassionate.

*Another. Heirmos:*
My heart is established in the Lord...

*Troparion 1:*
Judge not according to appearance, O Jews! the Master said, teaching when He came into the sanctuary, as it is written, when the legal feast was halfway through.

*Troparion 2:*
Judge not according to appearance, O Jews! For Christ has come, Whom the Prophets proclaimed, coming forth from Zion and calling the world.

*Troparion 3:*
Though ye believe not words, O Jews, believe the works of the Master: why are ye deceived, rejecting the Holy One of Whom Moses wrote in the Law?

*Troparion 4:*
If it was needful for the Messiah to come, O Jews, Christ the Messiah is now come: why are ye deceived, rejecting the Righteous One of Whom Moses wrote in the Law?

*Glory... Triadicon:*
Unto Thee we bow down, O Father unoriginate in essence; we hymn Thy unoriginate Son, and piously the all-holy Spirit: as One God by nature, yet Three.

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*
Being One of the Trinity, Thou didst clothe Thyself in flesh, without altering Thine essence, O Lord, nor burning the incorrupt womb of Her that bare Thee, being wholly God and fire.

*Katavasia:*
My heart is established in the Lord, my horn is exalted in my God, my mouth is enlarged over mine enemies; I have rejoiced in Thy salvation.

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "The Wisdom and Word of God" (Премꙋ́дрости сло́ва):*
Standing in the midst of the sanctuary, as the feast was divinely halfway through, Thou didst cry aloud: Let him that is thirsty come unto Me and drink! For he that drinks of this My Divine water shall pour forth from his belly rivers of My commandments; and he that believes in Me, sent from the Divine Begetter, shall be glorified with Me: therefore we cry unto Thee: Glory to Thee, Christ our God, for Thou hast richly poured out the waters of Thy love for mankind upon Thy servants!

*Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Podoben:*
Pouring forth the water of wisdom and life unto the world, Thou callest all men, O Savior, to draw the waters of salvation; for receiving Thy Divine Law, man extinguishes within himself the coals of delusion, whence he shall never thirst for ever, nor cease from Thy satisfaction, O Master, most heavenly King: therefore we glorify Thy dominion, Christ our God, asking that remission of transgressions be richly sent down upon Thy servants.

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Beholding Thee lifted up upon the Cross, O Sun of righteousness, the Church stood in her order, worthily crying aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*P. Troparion:*
Having broken through the gates of death by Thy power, Thou didst make known the paths of life, and didst open the doors of immortality unto those who cry with faith: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*T. Troparion:*
Holding the midpoint and the end of all things, and possessing the beginning as unoriginate, Thou didst stand in the midst, crying: Come, ye divinely-wise, enjoy the Divine gifts!

*O. Troparion:*
As God, having dominion over all, as the Mighty One having cast down the power of death, Thou didst promise to send the Holy Spirit proceeding from the Father, O Christ.

*N. Theotokion:*
Thou givest grace richly unto them that hymn thee and the pre-eternal Word born of thee, O unwedded Mother, asking for them remission of transgressions, O Most-pure One.

*Another. Heirmos:*
The Prophet Habakkuk...

*Troparion 1:*
If it was needful for the Messiah to come, and Christ is the Messiah, why do ye not believe in Him, O lawless ones? Behold, He has come, and the things that He does bear witness: He made water wine; He strengthened the paralytic by a word!

*Troparion 2:*
Not understanding the Scriptures, ye are all deceived, O lawless Hebrews: for truly Christ has come and enlightened all, and showed forth among you many signs and wonders, and ye renounce your own true Life!

*Troparion 3:*
One work I showed unto you, and ye all marvel already, Christ cried unto the Jews: ye circumcise a man even on the Sabbath, said He; why then do ye slander Me, Who raised the paralytic by a word?

*Troparion 4:*
Many good works have I wrought, and for which of these works do ye stone Me? Christ cried, refuting the Jews: Is it because I made an entire man whole by a word? Judge not according to appearance, O ye men!

*Troparion 5:*
Thou Who didst work in the Apostles and Thyself didst rest in the Prophets with the Spirit, the unoriginate Offspring of the Father's Nature, O Christ, Thou hast called the Gentiles unto knowledge by Thy signs.

*Glory... Triadicon:*
