O indivisible Trinity, Monad, unoriginate Father, Son, and Holy Spirit; Trinity in Unity, equal in honor, co-enthroned, life-creating, uncreated God: save them that praise Thee, and deliver us from perils and afflictions.

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*
Thou that didst contain in thy womb the uncontainable God, O Bride of God, pure Virgin-Mother, cease not to pray for us, that through thee we may be delivered from tribulations; for unto thee do we ever have recourse.

*Katavasia. Heirmos:*[^617]
With noetic eyes the Prophet Habakkuk foresaw Thy coming, O Lord; therefore he cried: God shall come from Theman! Glory to Thy power, glory to Thy condescension!

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Thou, O my Lord, didst come into the world as Light, Holy Light turning from dark ignorance those who praise Thee in faith.

*T. Troparion:*
Having reached the midpoint of the Divine feasts, let us make haste to be enlightened with perfect Divine virtue, O ye divinely-wise!

*Ō. Troparion:*
Truly radiant is the present solemn festival of the midpoint, for it is the root of the greatest feasts, and shines on both sides.

*N. Theotokion:*
The mind of the archangels cannot comprehend Thine ineffable and most-pure Nativity from the Virgin, O most merciful Savior.

*Another. Heirmos:*
O Lord our God, give us peace...

*Troparion 1:*
Thou didst adorn Thine Apostles with wonders; Thou didst marvelously magnify Thy disciples, glorifying them throughout the whole world, O our Savior, and giving them Thy Kingdom.

*Troparion 2:*
The disciples enlightened all the ends of the earth by wonders and teachings, and in diverse manners preaching the word of Thy Kingdom, O Christ Savior.

*Troparion 3:*
Praise do we send up unto Thy Kingdom, and hymnody do we bring unto Thee Who for our sake didst appear upon earth, and didst enlighten the world, and didst recall Adam.

*Glory... Triadicon:*
Glory to Thee, O Holy Father, unbegotten God; glory to Thee, O timeless Word, Only-begotten; glory to Thee, O Divine Spirit, co-enthroned and consubstantial with the Father and the Son!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*
Thy womb became a holy table, having the Bread of heaven: of Which everyone that eats does not die, as the Nourisher of all said, O Mother of God.

*Katavasia:*
O Lord our God, give us peace; O Lord our God, acquire us: O Lord, besides Thee we know no other, we call upon Thy Name![^618]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*[^619]
I will sacrifice unto Thee with the voice of praise, O Lord, the Church cries aloud unto Thee, having been cleansed from the blood of demons by the Blood that flowed through tender mercy from Thy side.

*M. Troparion:*
The midpoint of the fifty days has arrived today, on this side illumined with the most Divine splendor of the Divine Pascha, and on the other shining with the grace of the Comforter.

*E. Troparion:*
Standing in the temple, O Christ, Thou didst speak, revealing Thy glory unto the assemblies of the Jews, and showing forth Thy kinship unto the Begetter.

*G. Theotokion:*
Be thou my protector and an indestructible wall, delivering me from worldly scandals, O only Mother of God, and enlightening me with the Divine pouring-forth of light.

*Another. Heirmos:*
As the waters of the sea...

*Troparion 1:*
Holding all the ends of the earth, Thou didst go up, O Jesus, and didst teach the peoples the word of truth in the sanctuary, as the feast was halfway through, even as John cries aloud.

*Troparion 2:*
Thou didst open Thy lips, O Master, and didst proclaim unto the world the unoriginate Father and the all-holy Spirit, preserving the kinship of Thine own even after the Incarnation.

*Troparion 3:*
Thou didst accomplish the Father's work, and by works Thou didst confirm Thy words, performing healings and signs, O Savior: making whole the paralytic, cleansing lepers, and raising the dead.

*Troparion 4:*
The unoriginate Son took a beginning, receiving our nature; He became man, and taught in the midst of the feast, saying: Run to the ever-flowing Wellspring, draw forth life!

*Glory... Triadicon:*
The One Godhead in the Trinity, essence tri-hypostatic, uncreated, indivisible, do we all glorify: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, as being Three, and One.

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*
We hymn thee as Virgin after child-birth; we glorify thee as Virgin and Mother, thee alone, O pure Bride of God, Maiden: for truly from thee was God incarnate, having renewed us.

*Katavasia:*
As by the waters of the sea, O Lover of mankind, am I overwhelmed by the waves of this life; therefore like Jonah do I cry unto Thee: Bring up my life from corruption, O tenderly compassionate Lord![^620]

*Kontakion, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou Who wast lifted up upon the Cross" (Вознесы́йсѧ):*
As the legal feast was halfway through, O Creator and Master of all, Thou didst say unto those present, Christ our God: Come and draw the water of immortality! Therefore we fall down before Thee, and cry in faith: Grant us Thy tender compassions, for Thou art the Wellspring of our life!

*Ikos:*
My soul, made barren through the iniquities of transgressions, water with the streams of Thy blood, and show it forth fruitful in virtues: for Thou didst say unto all to come unto Thee, O holy Word of God, and to draw the water of incorruption, living and cleansing sins, who hymn Thy glorious and Divine Arising, granting, O Good One, the power of the Spirit that truly descended from on high upon Thy disciples, who know Thee to be God: for Thou art the Wellspring of our life!

*Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*

*Verses:*
*Standing in the midst of the feast, He teaches:*
*Christ the Messiah in the midst of the doctors.*

On Wednesday of the Paralytic, we celebrate the feast of Mid-Pentecost, on account of the honor of the two great feasts: of Pascha, I say, and of Pentecost, as connecting and uniting both. And this came to pass thus: after Christ had wrought the supernatural wonder upon the paralytic, the Jews, being scandalized concerning the paralytic because it was done on the Sabbath, sought to kill Him. He therefore departed into Galilee, and staying in the mountains there, He worked a miracle with five loaves and two fish, feeding five thousand men besides women and children. Afterwards, when the feast of Tabernacles was at hand—and that also was a great feast among the Jews—He went up to Jerusalem and walked secretly. And in the midst of this feast, entering into the sanctuary, He taught. [Now the sanctuary is a sacred place for God alone, wherein love and peace, wherein faith and chastity dwell. Therefore also the bishop, doing good unto God, ought to be peaceful and meek, not contentious, not deceitful, not a lover of money, that first he may cause God to dwell in his own soul, and afterwards may unite the people after his own manner and path. And the soul of every faithful person may likewise be called a sanctuary, having been exceedingly purified: for I will dwell in you and walk in you, says the Lord.][^621] And all marveled at His teaching, and envying Him they said: How does this man know letters, having never learned? For being the New Adam, He knew even as the first Adam, and was filled with all wisdom, and as God. Again, all murmured, and were all intent on murdering Him. But Christ, employing refutations against them, as they were contending concerning the Sabbath, said: Why seek ye to kill Me? And they said: Hast thou a demon? Who seeks to kill thee? But He again addresses what went before, saying: If ye contend concerning the Law, why are ye angry with Me, because I made an entire man whole on the Sabbath? If Moses gave this commandment, he bids you to break the Sabbath for the sake of circumcision. Having spoken many things unto them concerning this, He showed Himself to be the Giver of the Law and equal unto the Father. And especially on the last great day of the feast, He had stones cast at Him by them, but the stone touched Him not at all; and passing by from thence, He found a man blind from his birth, and granted him sight. Now it is to be known that the Jews had three very great feasts: The first is the Passover, which is celebrated in the first month, having a commemoration of the crossing of the Red Sea. The second is Pentecost, commemorating the sojourn in the wilderness after the passing through of the Red Sea: for they spent fifty days in the wilderness until they received the Law of Moses; and also in honor of the number seven, which was held in honor among them. And the third feast was the veneration of the tents and tabernacles, making commemoration of the Tabernacle which Moses saw in the cloud on the mountain, and commanded Bezaleel, the chief craftsman, to construct; which was celebrated for seven days, having a remembrance of the ingathering of the fruits and of the resting in the wilderness. When that feast was celebrated, Jesus stood and cried with a loud voice: If any man thirst, let him come unto Me and drink! Thus in His teaching Christ the Messiah showed Himself so great, being our Mediator and Reconciler with His eternal Father. Therefore, having this present celebration and naming it Mid-Pentecost, we hymn Christ the Messiah, and set forth the honor which comes from both of the two great feasts. For this reason also, I believe, the feast of the Samaritan Woman is celebrated after it, because there also many things were spoken concerning Christ the Messiah, and concerning water and concerning thirst, as here in John the Evangelist; and the Blind Man stands before the Samaritan Woman.[^622] By Thine immeasurable mercy, Christ our God, have mercy on us. Amen.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*[^623]
In the Persian furnace the Abrahamic youths, burning with love of piety rather than with flame, cried aloud: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!

*I. Troparion:*
By Thy strength, O Savior, destroying the power of death, Thou didst show forth the path of life unto mankind, who gratefully cry unto Thee: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!

*S. Troparion:*
Beholding Thee bearing flesh, the assemblies of the Hebrews knew Thee not to be the Word of God; but we hymn Thee: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!

*T. Theotokion:*
Rejoice, O consecrated Divine habitation of the Most High! For through thee joy was given, O Theotokos, unto those who cry: Blessed art thou among women, O all-immaculate Lady!

*Another. Heirmos:*
The Chaldean furnace...

*Troparion 1:*
In the flesh Thou didst labor, O Rest of all; of Thine own will Thou didst thirst, O Wellspring of wonders: Thou didst ask for water, O Jesus, Who dost announce the water of life.

*Troparion 2:*
Thou didst converse with the Samaritan woman, O Lord, refuting the folly of the lawless Hebrews: she indeed believed Thee to be the Son of God, but they rejected Thee.

*Troparion 3:*
Thou didst promise to grant living, outpouring water, water of immortality, the ever-living spring, unto those who receive in faith Thy Spirit, O Savior, Which proceeds from the Father.

*Troparion 4:*
With five loaves Thou didst feed thousands of the hungry, and the fragments of satisfaction Thou didst multiply unto other thousands, O Savior, showing forth Thy glory unto Thy sacred disciples.

*Troparion 5:*
He that eats Thy Body shall live for ever, and he that drinks Thy Blood shall abide in Thee, O my Savior, and Thou abidest in him, and Thou shalt raise him up at the last moment.[^624]

*Troparion 6:*
Thou didst make marvelous Thy dispensation, O Master, having confirmed Thy Divine authority by wonders: Thou didst cast out infirmities, didst raise the dead, and didst enlighten the blind, as God.

*Troparion 7:*
Thou didst cleanse lepers, didst make the lame to walk, didst strengthen the paralyzed, and didst heal the woman with the issue of blood: Thou didst walk upon the deep, showing forth Thy glory unto Thy sacred disciples.

*Glory... Triadicon:*
We bow down before Thine all-pure Father, O Lord, and the grace of the Spirit, which, being God, Thou didst distribute unto Thine Apostles, sending them forth unto the proclamation.

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*
In thy womb thou didst contain the uncontainable Word, from thy breasts thou didst suckle the Nourisher of the world, in thine embrace thou didst carry our Sustainer, O pure Mother of God.

*Katavasia:*
The Chaldean furnace, kindled with fire, was bedewed by the Spirit at God's presence; the youths sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*[^625]
Daniel, having stretched forth his hands, shut the gaping mouths of lions in the pit; and the youths, lovers of piety, girded with virtue, quenched the power of the fire, crying: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Ō. Troparion:*
Having arisen radiant from the tomb, adorned with the glory of the Godhead, Thou didst appear unto Thine Apostles, O Lord, promising to send unto them the operation of the Spirit, who cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*N. Troparion:*
Having put hades to death as God, O most Sovran-source of life, Thou didst pour forth eternal life unto all: which the joys of these light-bearing days now more clearly prefigure, as we cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*A. Troparion:*
Having shone forth as rays, like the Sun of righteousness, O Christ, Thou didst send Thine Apostles into the world, bearing Thee, the incomprehensible Light, and dispelling the mist of ignorance, and crying: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*I. Theotokion:*
Behold, now a prince and ruler has manifestly ceased from the tribe of Judah; for thou, O all-immaculate one, didst give birth to Christ God, the previously promised Expectation of the nations, unto Whom we sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^626]

*Another. Heirmos:*
Angels and heavens, upon the throne of glory...

*Troparion 1:*
Come, ye peoples, behold Him Who is hymned upon the throne of glory, blasphemed by lawless people; and beholding, sing ye unto the Messiah foretold in the Prophets!

*Troparion 2:*
Thou art truly the Christ Who didst come into this world, from Whom is salvation and remission of ancestral sins: Thou art truly Life unto them that have believed in Thee.

*Troparion 3:*
The Wisdom of God, as the feast was halfway through, as it is written, stood in the sanctuary and taught: for truly He was the Messiah Christ, through Whom is salvation.

*Troparion 4:*
On the Sabbaths and every day Christ showed forth the works of signs, healing those who were in diverse diseases; but the deceived people burned with fury.

*Troparion 5:*
This man, said they, healed on the Sabbath the paralytic who had lain for many years, and transgressed the Law! Thus the Jews bitterly reproached Christ.

*Troparion 6:*
Did not Moses, who gave you the Law, command you to be circumcised? And ye circumcise a man on the Sabbath, lest the ancestral Law be broken! said Christ unto the Jews.

*Troparion 7:*
Always ungrateful, they that lived in the wilderness provoked the Benefactor to anger through envy, blaspheming, moving unrighteous tongues, and meditating vain things.

*Let us bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit: the Lord!*
*Triadicon:*
One God is the Trinity: the Father having not passed over into sonship, nor the Son turned into procession; but the proper properties of each: Light, God, Three, do I glorify for ever!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*
Tell us, how didst thou give birth unto Him Who timelessly shone forth from the Father, and is hymned with the Holy Spirit? Even as the One Light Who was well pleased to be born of thee, O Theotokos!

*Then: We praise, we bless, and we worship the Lord...*
*Katavasia:*
Angels and heavens, bless, sing, and exalt above all unto all ages Him Who sits upon the throne of glory and is unceasingly glorified as God!

*More honorable than the Cherubim is not sung.*
*Ode 9. Heirmos:*[^627]
A cornerstone was cut out from thee, O Virgin, the uncut mountain, not by the hand of man: Christ, Who joined together the sundered natures: therefore rejoicing, we magnify thee, O Theotokos!

*N. Troparion:*
Having been instructed by Christ in a new and pure manner of life, let us all zealously strive to preserve it profitably unto the end, that we may receive the coming of the Holy Spirit.

*E. Troparion:*
Having been called back unto heavenly citizenship by the power of mediation of Him Who emptied Himself even unto the form of a servant and exalted us: Him let us worthily magnify!

*Ode 9. Troparion (S):*
Having clothed my mortal nature, O Giver of Life, with the investiture of immortality, and having arrayed it in the grace of incorruption, O Savior, Thou didst raise it up with Thyself, and didst bring it unto the Father, having brought to naught my temporal warfare.

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion (O):*[^628]
Knowing thee, O Virgin, to be the root, fountain, and cause of incorruption, all we the faithful honor thee with praises: for thou didst pour forth hypostatic immortality unto us.

*Another Canon. Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Virginity is foreign to mothers...

*Troparion 1:*
As the Jewish feast was halfway through, Thou didst go up, O my Savior, unto Thy sanctuary, and didst teach all: and the Jews marveled, and said: From whence knows this Man letters, having never learned?[^629]

*Troparion 2:*
Pouring forth gifts of healings, my Deliverer performed miracles and signs, driving away diseases, healing those that were infirm: yet the Jews were enraged at the multitude of His miracles.

*Troparion 3:*
Rebuking the disobedient Jews, my Deliverer cried aloud: Judge not according to appearance, but judge righteous judgment: for the Law commands that every man be circumcised even on the Sabbath.[^630]

*Troparion 4:*
Greater miracles, as Thou didst promise, didst Thou grant unto Thy disciples, O Savior, sending them unto the Gentiles to proclaim Thy glory: and they proclaimed unto the world Thy resurrection, grace, and incarnation.[^631]

*Troparion 5:*
If ye circumcise a man on the Sabbath, lest the Law should be broken, why now are ye angry at Me, because I made a whole man well by a word? Ye judge according to the flesh, saith Christ unto the Jews.[^632]

*Troparion 6:*
O Word, Who by a word didst heal the withered hand: having healed the long-withered earth of my heart, show me forth fruitful, that I also, O Savior, may bring forth fruits in fervent repentance.[^633]

*Troparion 7:*
Having cleansed my leprous heart and enlightened the eyes of my soul, O Word, raise me up as I lie upon the bed of sickness, even as Thou didst raise up the paralytic lying upon a bed.[^634]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.*
*Triadicon:*
It is alien to the lawless to glorify the Unoriginate Trinity, the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit: the uncreated almighty sovereignty, by Which the whole world was created through the power of Its might.

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*
Thou didst contain in thy womb, O Virgin Mother, One of the Trinity, Christ the Giver of Life, Whom all creation hymns and the heavenly thrones tremble before: Him implore, O all-blessed one, to save our souls.

*Katavasia:*
Virginity is foreign to mothers, and childbearing is strange to virgins: yet in thee, O Theotokos, both were accomplished: therefore all the tribes of the earth unceasingly magnify thee.

*Exaposteilarion, Podoben: "Thou Who didst adorn heaven with stars" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ ѕвѣзда́ми):*
Thou Who hast the chalice of inexhaustible gifts, grant me to draw water for the remission of sins, for I am gripped by thirst, O only Tender-Hearted and Compassionate One. *(Thrice)*

*At the Praises, "Let every breath praise the Lord": we set 4 stichoi, and sing 3 prosomoia of the Feast, repeating the first.*

*Tone 4, Podoben: "As one valiant among martyrs" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*
The Wisdom and Power, the Father's Radiance, the Co-Eternal Word and Son of God came in the flesh unto the sanctuary, and taught the Jewish people, hard-hearted and ungrateful; and they marveled at the richness of His wisdom, crying aloud: From whence knows this Man letters, having learned from no one? *(Twice)*[^635]

*Sticheron 2:*
The Messiah and Lord muzzled the mouths of the scribes and rebuked the Jews, crying aloud unto them: Judge not according to appearance, O lawless ones, as unrighteous men; for on the Sabbath I raised up the paralytic; therefore I am Lord of the Sabbath and of the Law: why seek ye to kill Me, Who have raised up the dead?[^636]

*Sticheron 3:*
The cruel and lawless ones, the ungrateful Jewish gathering, stoned Naboth with stones; they sawed Isaiah asunder with a wooden saw; they cast wise Jeremiah into the mire; and having lifted up the Lord upon the Cross, they cried: Thou that destroyest the temple, save Thyself, and we will believe![^637]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 4. By Anatolius:*
Enlightened, O brethren, by the Resurrection of Christ the Savior, and having reached the Midpoint of the Master's feast, let us earnestly keep the commandments of God, that we may be worthy also to celebrate the Ascension, and to receive the coming of the Holy Spirit.

*Great Doxology. After the Trisagion, the troparion of the Feast.*

*Litanies, and the Dismissal; and the First Hour.*

*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes from the Canon of the Feast: of Tone 4, Ode 3, on 4; and of Tone 8, Ode 6, on 4.*

*After the Entrance, the troparion of the Feast. Glory... both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen., Kontakion.*

*Prokeimenon, Tone 3:*
Great is our Lord, and great is His power, and of His understanding there is no number.[^638]

*And until the Apodosis.*

*Verse:* Praise the Lord, for a psalm is good: unto our God let praise be sweet.[^639]
*Epistle from the Acts of the Apostles, Pericope 34: Paul and Barnabas fled unto the cities of Lycaonia...*[^640]
*Alleluia, Tone 1:* Remember Thy congregation, which Thou hast purchased from the beginning.[^641]
*Verse:* But God is our King before the ages: He hath wrought salvation in the midst of the earth.[^642]
*Gospel from John, Pericope 26: In the midpoint of Pentecost...*[^643]

*At the Liturgy we sing, as also at the Apodosis of Mid-Pentecost, instead of "It is truly meet," the heirmos: "Virginity is foreign to mothers..." But on the other days we sing: "Shine, shine [O new Jerusalem]..." even until the Apodosis.*

*Communion Hymn:*
He that eats My Flesh, and drinks My Blood, abides in Me, and I in him, saith the Lord. Alleluia. *(Thrice)*[^644]

*At table there is consolation for the brethren.*

*And this feast is celebrated for 8 days.*

## ON WEDNESDAY OF MID-PENTECOST, AT VESPERS

*The usual Kathisma.*

*At "Lord, I have cried," stichera of the Feast, 6:*

*Tone 4, Podoben: "Being called from on high" (Зва́нный свы́ше):*
Having previously destroyed the dominion of death by Thy death, O Christ, Thou hast granted life unto men; in Thy glorious Resurrection, having raised up mankind with Thyself through Thy condescension: therefore we sing a thanksgiving praise unto Thee, celebrating the feast of Thy three-day and radiant Resurrection, wherein the Midpoint of these all-honorable days hath now shone forth unto us all, O Jesus Giver of Life, Benefactor of our souls.

*Sticheron 2:*
Before Thy precious Cross and Passion, performing most glorious miracles among the people, even as it is written, in the midst of the feast of the Law Thou didst stand, O all-powerful Christ, and didst cry aloud unto all: If any man thirst, let him come freely unto Me, and draw a drink of divine water, even of the water of life: for water of life, and of power, and of wisdom do I give unto all, since of Mine own will I became like unto men, as Lover of mankind.[^645]

*Sticheron 3:*
As I lie upon the bed of the sickness of my sins, and am paralyzed in my members: by the great abyss of Thy love for mankind, O most merciful Christ, having voluntarily become man, do Thou now invisibly raise me up even as the paralytic, and make me to run prosperously in the paths of Thy divine commandments: Thou Who before Thy Passion wast confirmed unto the Hebrew people by the multitude of miracles, O Savior, that being God, Thou sufferest voluntarily in the flesh.[^646]

*And from the Menaion, 3. Glory... of the saint, if there be one; if not:*
*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the Feast.*

*Tone 2:*
When Thou didst come unto the sanctuary, O Christ God, as the feast was halfway through, then didst Thou teach the people, crying aloud: He that believs in Me, though he die, yet shall he live. But the Jews were enraged, with the Pharisees and Sadducees and scribes, saying: Who is this Man that speaks blasphemies? Not considering that Thou art before all ages, glorified with the Father and the Spirit, our God: glory to Thee![^647]

*Prokeimenon of the day.*

*At the Aposticha, the Resurrection sticheron.*
*Tone 3:*
O Christ, Who by Thy Passion didst darken the sun, and by the light of Thy Resurrection didst enlighten all things: accept our evening hymn, O Lover of mankind.[^648]

*Verse:* Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes, O Thou that dwellest in the heavens.[^649]
*Sticheron of the Apostles:*
Into all the earth went forth your sound, O holy Apostles; ye destroyed the delusion of idols, preaching the knowledge of God: this is your good fight, O blessed ones: therefore we sing and glorify your memories.[^650]

*Verse:* Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us: for we are greatly filled with contempt.[^651]
*Martyricon:*
Thy martyrs, O Lord, established by faith, strengthened by hope, spiritually united through the love of Thy Cross, brought to naught the enemy's tyranny; and having obtained crowns, they pray with the bodiless powers for our souls.

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 3. By Germanus:*
As the feast is halfway through, we glorify Him Who hath wrought salvation in the midst of the earth: for in the midst of two thieves Life hung upon the Tree; and unto the one that blasphemed He was silent, but unto the one that believed He cried: Today shalt thou be with Me in paradise! He descended into the tomb, despoiled hades, and arose on the third day, saving our souls.[^652]

*Troparion of the saint, if there be one; but if not, only of the Feast. Litany, and the Dismissal.*

## ON THURSDAY AFTER MID-PENTECOST, AT MATINS

*At "God is the Lord," the troparion of the Feast, thrice.*

*After the 1st chanting of the Psalter, Sessional Hymn.*
*Tone 3, Podoben: "Beholding the beauty of thy virginity" (Красотѣ̀ дѣ́вства):*
Having assumed all that is human and made all that is ours Thine own, Thou wast well pleased to be nailed unto the Cross, O my Creator, having chosen to endure death as man, that Thou mightest deliver mankind from death as God: therefore as unto the Giver of Life we cry unto Thee: Glory, O Christ, to Thy Resurrection!

*Verse:* Into all the earth went forth their sound, and into the ends of the world their words.[^653]
*Troparion of the Apostles:*
The memory of Thine Apostles, O Lord, Thou hast made radiant, as Almighty; for Thou didst strengthen them to imitate Thy Sufferings, and they manfully overcame the power of Belial: therefore also they received gifts of healings: by their supplications, O Lover of mankind, grant peace unto Thy people.

*Verse:* God is marvelous in His saints, the God of Israel.[^654]
*Martyricon:*
Having put on the whole armor of Christ, and arrayed yourselves in the armor of faith, ye manfully cast down the enemy's regiments: for zealously through hope of life, ye endured all the threats and wounds of the tormentors: therefore also ye received crowns, O patient-spirited martyrs of Christ.

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*
The Prophets proclaimed, the Apostles taught, the Martyrs confessed, and we have believed thee to be truly the Theotokos: therefore also we magnify thine ineffable Childbearing.

*After the 2nd chanting of the Psalter, Sessional Hymn.*
*Tone 8, Podoben: "The Wisdom and Word of God" (Премꙋ́дрости сло́ва):*
Standing in the midst of the sanctuary, as the feast was divinely halfway through, Thou didst cry aloud: Let him that thirsts come unto Me and drink: for he that drinks of this My divine water shall pour forth from his belly rivers of My commandments: and he that believs in Me Who was sent from the Divine Begetter shall be glorified with Me: therefore we cry unto Thee: Glory to Thee, O Christ God, for Thou hast richly poured forth the waters of Thy love for mankind unto Thy servants![^655]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. The same.*

*"Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ..." Psalm 50.*

*Canon of the Feast of Mid-Pentecost with heirmoi, on 8; and of the Menaion, on 4.*

*Kontakion, and the exaposteilarion of Mid-Pentecost.*

*At the Praises, stichera of the Octoechos.*

*Tone 3:*
In Thy light, O Master, shall we see light, O Lover of mankind: for Thou art risen from the dead, granting salvation unto mankind, that all creation may glorify Thee, the only Sinless One: have mercy on us. *(Twice)*[^656]

*Sticheron 2:*
Having blamelessly kept the commandments of Christ, O holy Apostles, freely ye received, freely ye give, healing the passions of our souls and bodies: therefore having boldness, implore Him that our souls may find mercy.[^657]

*Sticheron 3:*
As luminaries in the world do ye shine even after death, O holy martyrs, having fought the good fight: therefore having boldness, implore Christ that our souls may find mercy.[^658]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 4:*
O Lord, before Thy precious Cross, when the feast was halfway through, Thou didst enter into the sanctuary, teaching the Jews with boldness concerning the things legislated by Thee through Moses and in the Law; and they, being astonished, O Christ, at the ineffable mystery of Thy wisdom, instigated one another through envy to murmur against Thee: How knows this Man letters, having never learned? not knowing Thee to be the Savior of our souls.[^659]

*At the Aposticha, stichera whose acrostic is: Mid-Pentecost.*[^660]

*Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме Є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*
Great art Thou, O King, and great is Thy dominion: for having become exceedingly poor, Thou hast filled the inhabited earth with great gifts.[^661]

*Verse:* Remember Thy congregation, which Thou hast purchased from the beginning.[^662]
Thou didst stand in the temple, pouring forth Thy streams, as the feast was halfway through, and watering those that thirst with divine grace, O Tender-Hearted One.

*Verse:* But God is our King before the ages: He hath wrought salvation in the midst of the earth.[^663]
Desiring to save me, Thou didst become incarnate most gloriously from the Virgin who knew not wedlock; and in the midst of Thy temple Thou didst pour forth grace unto me.

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 8. By John the Monk:*[^664]
As the feast was halfway through, before Thy Passion and glorious Resurrection, O Lord, Thou wast teaching in the sanctuary the disobedient Jews, and Pharisees, and scribes, and crying aloud unto them: Let him that thirsts come unto Me and drink; he that believs in Me, rivers of the water of the life of the Divine Spirit shall flow from his belly! O ineffable praise of Thy wisdom! O our God Who fillest all things, glory to Thee!

*On Thursday after Mid-Pentecost, the Triodion,*
*Whose acrostic is: Αἴνεσις Κυρίῳ, that is: Praise unto the Lord:*[^665]

*Tone 3. Ode 4. Heirmos:*[^666]
Habakkuk foresaw the overshadowed mountain, even thy most pure womb, O Pure One; therefore he cried aloud: God shall come from Theman, and the Holy One from the mountain overshadowed and densely wooded.

*Troparion 1 (A):*
By an ineffable union having become like unto men, O only Transcendent One, Thou didst endure the Cross in the flesh, and being reckoned among the dead, Thou didst arise on the third day, O Life of all.[^667]

*Troparion 2 (I):*
O Jesus our God, being the Water of Life, while walking Thou wast wearied in the flesh at the fountain; and sitting down, Thou didst mystically pour forth the water of Thy wisdom unto the Samaritan woman.[^668]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. Troparion (N):*
Cleansing by Thy command those that came unto Thee with diverse diseases, O Word, Thou didst voluntarily endure the Cross; and having been laid in the tomb, Thou didst raise up corrupt human nature.

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion (E):*
Upon thee the Wisdom of the Unoriginate Father came down as rain upon the fleece, O Pure One; and having become incarnate without change, He showed forth unto us the paths of life, who know thee to be a Virgin after childbearing and a Mother.[^669]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*[^670]
Him Who descended in divine power into the flame unto the Hebrew youths, and was revealed as Lord: ye priests, bless; and exalt above all unto all ages.

*Troparion 1 (S):*
Having been lifted up upon the Cross, Thou didst lift up all human nature with Thyself, O Word; and having been laid in the tomb, Thou didst raise up those sleeping in the tombs by Thy divine Resurrection, O Compassionate One.[^671]

*Troparion 2 (I):*
Having passed beyond Jericho and Salim with their many waters, the Wellspring of wisdom came unto Jacob's well, giving the water of salvation unto the Samaritan woman.[^672]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. Troparion (S):*
Thou Who didst enlighten the blind man by a word, and by Thy command didst strengthen the paralytics, and as One dead didst shine forth on the third day from the tomb: raise Thou up my deadened soul.[^673]

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion (K):*
Unto the whole world, O Theotokos Mary, thou art a refuge: deliver me from vile temptations and bodily passions and from eternal Gehenna, that I may hymn thee in song.

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*[^674]
Thee, the unburnt bush, and holy Virgin, Mother of Light, and Theotokos, the hope of us all, do we magnify.

*Troparion 1 (Y):*
Thou didst stretch forth Thy palms upon the Tree, destroying the harm of the forefather's hands evil-stretched forth to eat of the tree, O most merciful Christ.[^675]

*Troparion 2 (R):*
Having strengthened the paralytic by a word and made the lame to walk upright, Thou wast crucified, O Jesus, and didst arise, appearing unto the disciples for many days.[^676]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. Troparion (I):*
The Samaritan woman beheld Thee when she came to draw water, and having received the water of life from Thee, she was filled to satisfaction, O Christ God, praising Thee.[^677]

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion (O):*
O wonders beyond understanding that are thine, O most pure Virgin! For thou gavest birth unto God incarnate, Who through His divine Resurrection hath saved all.

## ON THURSDAY AFTER MID-PENTECOST, AT VESPERS

*At "Lord, I have cried," prosomoia stichera of the Feast, 3; and of the Menaion, 3.*

*Tone 5, Podoben: "Rejoice, O container of ascetics" (Ра́дꙋйсѧ):*
Today the light-manifest and beautiful, all-holy Midpoint of the Savior's Resurrection, like a radiant midday, illuminating the world with divine graces of Christ's Resurrection, irradiating miracles of incorruption, flashes forth signs, and shows forth the Ascension unto the heights, manifesting the long-desired coming of the Spirit, the most radiant solemnity of all-honorable Pentecost: therefore also it grants unto our souls peace and great mercy.

*Sticheron 2:*
Like a river of divine glory, as the feast is now halfway through, the Lord, granting streams of loving-kindness unto all, cries aloud: Let him that thirsts come unto Me, and drink fervently: for being Himself the wellspring of compassion and an abyss of mercy, He pours forth remission unto the world, washes away transgressions, and cleanses diseases: He saves them that celebrate His Resurrection, covers with love them that honor His Ascension with glory, and grants unto our souls peace and great mercy.[^678]

*Sticheron 3:*
Standing in the midst of the sanctuary, the Uncircumscribed God and Lord—for He was God by nature, even though for our sake He became man and was manifested circumscribed in body—poured forth life-bearing words unto all, saying unto all: Cleanse your souls, and cool the heat of the passions, lest in any wise ye be deprived of drinking of the cup: for I bestow divine grace, of the immortal, better, and heavenly Kingdom, to partake with Me, the Creator, and to be glorified!

*And of the Menaion, 3.*

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 6:*
As the feast is halfway through, between Thy Resurrection, O Christ, and the divine coming of Thy Holy Spirit, we have come together to hymn the mysteries of Thy miracles: whereon do Thou send down upon us great mercy.

*At the Aposticha, stichera of the Octoechos.*

*Tone 3:*
The tree of disobedience brought forth death unto the world, but the Tree of the Cross brought forth life and incorruption: therefore we worship Thee, the Lord Who wast crucified: let the light of Thy countenance be signed upon us, O Lord.[^679]

*Verse:* Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes, O Thou that dwellest in the heavens.[^680]
By Thy Cross, O Christ Savior, the dominion of death was destroyed, and the delusion of the devil was brought to naught: and mankind, saved by faith, ever offers a hymn unto Thee.

*Verse:* Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us: for we are greatly filled with contempt.[^681]
*Martyricon:*
Great is the power of Thy Cross, O Lord, for it was planted in one place, yet it works in the world; and from fishermen it showed forth Apostles, and from Gentiles Martyrs, that they may pray for our souls.

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 8. By John the Monk:*[^682]
As the feast was halfway through, before Thy Passion and glorious Resurrection, O Lord, Thou wast teaching in the sanctuary the disobedient Jews, and Pharisees, and scribes, and crying aloud unto them: Let him that thirsts come unto Me and drink; he that believs in Me, rivers of the water of the life of the Divine Spirit shall flow from his belly! O ineffable praise of Thy wisdom! O our God Who fillest all things, glory to Thee!

## ON FRIDAY AFTER MID-PENTECOST, AT MATINS

*Troparion of the Feast:*

*After the 1st chanting of the Psalter, we say the following Sessional Hymns.*
*Tone 3, Podoben: "Beholding the beauty of thy virginity" (Красотѣ̀ дѣ́вства):*
Having chosen to suffer the Cross and death, Thou didst plant it in the midst of creation: when Thou wast well pleased, O Savior, to have Thy Body nailed, then also the sun hid its rays: and the thief beholding these things upon the cross, cried unto Thee: Remember me, crying aloud, O Savior, and having believed, He received paradise.[^683]

*Verse:* Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship the footstool of His feet, for it is holy.[^684]
*Troparion:*
Let us the faithful speak divine theology of the unsearchable mystery of the Crucifixion and the ineffable wonder of the Resurrection: for today death and hades have been brought to naught, and mankind hath been clothed in incorruption: therefore giving thanks we cry unto Thee: Glory, O Christ, to Thy Resurrection![^685]

*Verse:* God is marvelous in His saints, the God of Israel.[^686]
*Martyricon:*
The courageous patience of your endurance overcame the wiles of the evil-originating enemy, O all-praised passion-bearers; therefore were ye accounted worthy of eternal beatitude: but pray ye unto the Lord, that He may save the flock of Christ-loving people, being martyrs of the truth.

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Stavrotheotokion:*
Having obtained the rod of power, even the Cross of thy Son, O Theotokos, therewith we cast down the insolence of enemies, unceasingly magnifying thee with love.[^687]

*After the 2nd chanting of the Psalter, Sessional Hymn.*
*Tone 8, Podoben: "The Wisdom and Word of God" (Премꙋ́дрости сло́ва):*
Pouring forth unto the world the water of wisdom and life, Thou callest all, O Savior, to draw the waters of salvation: for man, having received Thy divine Law, quenches in himself the coals of delusion: thenceforth he shall not thirst unto the ages, nor cease from Thy satisfaction, O Master, King most high: therefore we glorify Thy dominion, O Christ God, entreating Thee to send down richly the remission of transgressions unto Thy servants.[^688]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. The same.*

*Then: "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ..." Psalm 50. Then,*
*The Canon of Mid-Pentecost with heirmoi, on 8; and of the Menaion, on 4.*
*Kontakion, and the exaposteilarion of the Feast of Mid-Pentecost.*

*At the Praises, stichera of the Octoechos, repeating the first.*
*Tone 3:*
Through envy I was banished from sweetness, having fallen with a grievous fall; but Thou didst not despise me, O Master, having accepted for my sake the Crucifixion concerning me, and having saved me, bringing me into glory, O my Redeemer: glory to Thee.

Come, all ye nations, understand the power of the awesome mystery: for Christ our Savior, the Word Who was in the beginning, was crucified for our sake, and was voluntarily buried, and arose from the dead to save all things: unto Him let us bow down.

*Martyricon:*
Come, all ye peoples, let us honor the memory of the holy passion-bearers, for having become a spectacle unto Angels and men, they received the crown of victory from Christ, and they pray for our souls.

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 8:*
As the feast of Pascha was halfway through, Thou didst enter into the temple, O our Savior of the sanctuary, and standing in the midst of the people, Thou didst teach them with boldness, and didst say: I am the Light of the world; he that follows Me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of immortal life.[^689]

*At the Aposticha, stichera.*
*Tone 8, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме Є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*
Being wholly with God, O Thou Word, desiring to deliver me perishing from transgressions, Thou didst unite Thyself unto me, O Lover of mankind.

*Verse:* Remember Thy congregation, which Thou hast purchased from the beginning.[^690]
The shadow hath ceased: for behold, the Messiah, as the feast is halfway through, hath shone forth grace like another daystar.

*Verse:* But God is our King before the ages: He hath wrought salvation in the midst of the earth.[^691]
Come with good obedience, ye that desire to drink of the water of life, cried my Savior, and drink of grace, rejoicing divinely.

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 6:*
Having purified the treasures of our thoughts, and made bright the lamps of our souls, and beheld Christ our Life coming to the sanctuary by the abundance of His goodness, that He might conquer the enemy and save our race by the Passion of the Cross and the Resurrection, let us cry aloud unto Him: O Incomprehensible Lord, glory to Thee!

*On Friday after Mid-Pentecost, the Triodion,*[^692]
*Whose acrostic is: Δόξα σοὶ ὁ Θεός, that is: Glory to Thee, O God:*

*Tone 3. Ode 5. Heirmos:*[^693]
When Isaiah saw figuratively upon the throne God lifted up on high, borne in triumph by the Angels of glory, he cried: Woe is me, wretched one! For I foresaw God becoming incarnate, the Unwaning Light, and ruling over peace.

*Troparion 1 (Δ):*
Being bound, O Compassionate One, and voluntarily nailed to the tree, Thou dost deliver them that were bound by all manner of transgressions; and being laid in the tomb, Thou dost raise up the dead that slept in the tombs, who hymn Thy fearsome Resurrection.

*Troparion 2 (Ο):*
The Lord is risen from the dead on the third day, even as He said, and dwelling together with the Apostles, He cried: Go ye into all the world, and proclaim clearly the great wonders of Mine which ye see.[^694]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. Troparion (Ξ):*
Heart and hearing marvel, O Savior, at Thy compassion, and dispensation, and condescension: for walking on earth in the flesh, Thou didst grant the water of life of divine understanding unto the Samaritan woman who asked of Thee.[^695]

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion (Α):*
O Holy Theotokos, who gavest birth unto the Holy of holies, the Word Who shone forth from the Unoriginate Father: Him do thou entreat unceasingly, that He may sanctify and enlighten our souls and the hearts of them that hymn thee with love.

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*[^696]
Joined unto the unbearable fire, the youths championing piety, unhurt by the flame, sang a divine hymn: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages.

*Troparion 1 (Σ):*
Having been lifted up voluntarily upon the Cross, Thou didst lift up all human nature with Thyself, and being reckoned among the dead, though Thou art Life, Thou didst quicken, O Savior, them that hymn Thy dispensation and Thine ascension with glory, O Compassionate One.[^697]

*Troparion 2 (Ο):*
The world celebrates with joy in Thy holy Resurrection, O Giver of life, whereby Thou didst trample down all the power of hades, and didst blunt the sting of death, O Word, and didst pour forth incorruption unto mankind.[^698]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. Troparion (Ι):*
The Samaritan woman, beholding Thee wearied, O Compassionate One, and asking to drink water, received the waters of immortality, crying aloud: Give me living water, O Lord, that I may not thirst all the time of my life.[^699]

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion (Ο):*
Thou wast shown to be the house of God, O most pure Virgin Theotokos, having lent Him ensouled flesh from thy most pure blood, O Maiden: therefore we honor thee unto all ages.

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*[^700]
In the shadow and letter of the Law we the faithful see an image: every male that opens the womb is holy unto God: therefore the Firstborn Word of the Unoriginate Father, the Son Who is made firstborn of a Mother that knew not man, do we magnify.

*Troparion 1 (Θ):*
The sun was astonished, beholding Thee nailed upon the tree, O Christ; the ends of the earth were shaken, and the whole earth quaked, and the rocks were split, and hades below released the prisoners from ages, who hymn Thee.[^701]

*Troparion 2 (Ε):*
Thou wast laid in the tomb, O Christ, Who art Life and Resurrection; and having arisen in glory, dwelling together with Thy disciples for many days, Thou didst send them forth into all the world as preachers of Thine awesome dispensation.[^702]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. Troparion (Ο):*
Thou showest me the paths of life, O Merciful One; with great mercy Thou didst walk, and sitting down, Thou wast wearied from the journey: and unto the woman that asked, Thou didst send forth the waters of immortality, as she sang of Thy great dispensation.[^703]

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion (Σ):*
Christ is incarnate of thee beyond words, being the Father's Word, O Virgin Theotokos, and is crucified willingly for our sake, and by His three-day Resurrection enlightens the ends of the world: with them we duly call thee blessed.

## ON FRIDAY AFTER MID-PENTECOST, AT VESPERS

*The customary kathisma.*

*At "Lord, I have cried," stichera of the Feast, 6.*

*Tone 1, Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly ranks" (Небе́сныхъ чинѡ́въ):*
The Creator of all and Giver of life, the Word co-everlasting with the Divine Father, having voluntarily taken flesh from the Virgin and become man, as Good poured forth the teachings of ineffable wisdom unto all.

When the Jewish feast was halfway through, O Christ, Thou didst present Thyself in the sanctuary, O Master of the Law, teaching with authority and rebuking the scribes, as it is written, and astonishing them by the wisdom of Thy words and the demonstrations of wonders.[^704]

The Giver of wisdom and Pourer forth of good things, Who pours forth divine streams from the ever-flowing fountain, cries: Come unto Me, draw the water of life, ye that thirst; and rivers of divine gifts shall flow forth from the belly as from rock, He saith.[^705]

*And of the Menaion, 3.*

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. Tone 1. By John the Monk:*[^706]
The midpoint of the days of Pentecost hath arrived, wherein Christ, having slightly revealed His divine power, strengthened the paralytic by a word, raising him from his bed; and working wonders in a manner befitting God in a created body, He granted eternal life and great mercy unto men.[^707]

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion. Tone 3:*
How should we not marvel at thy theandric Childbearing, O Most Pure One? For without receiving the trial of man, O All-Blameless One, thou gavest birth in the flesh without a father unto the Son, Who was begotten without a mother of the Father before the ages, Who underwent neither change, nor mingling, nor division, but preserved whole the property of each of the two essences: therefore, O Mother, Virgin, Lady, entreat Him that the souls of them that confess thee in orthodox manner to be the Theotokos may be saved.[^708]

*At the Aposticha, stichera of the Octoechos.*
*Tone 3:*
By Thy Cross, O Christ Savior, the dominion of death was destroyed, and the delusion of the devil was brought to naught: and mankind, saved by faith, ever offers a hymn unto Thee.

*Verse:* The Lord is King, He is robed in majesty.[^709]
All things have been enlightened by Thy Resurrection, O Lord, and paradise is opened again: and all creation, praising Thee, ever offers a hymn unto Thee.

*Verse:* For He hath established the world, so that it cannot be moved.[^710]
I glorify the power of the Father and of the Son, and I praise the authority of the Holy Spirit: undivided, uncreated Godhead, Trinity Consubstantial, reigning unto the age of the age.

*Verse:* Holiness becomes Thine house, O Lord, unto length of days.[^711]
By Thy Passion, O Christ, Thou didst darken the sun, and by the light of Thy Resurrection Thou didst enlighten all things: accept our evening hymn, O Lover of mankind.

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 2:*
Thou didst come into the sanctuary, O Wisdom of God, when the feast was halfway through, teaching and rebuking the disobedient Jews, Pharisees, and scribes, and crying aloud with boldness unto them: Let him that thirsts come unto Me, and drink living water, and he shall never thirst unto eternity; he that believs in My goodness, rivers of eternal life shall flow from his belly! O the goodness and compassion of Thine, O Christ our God, glory to Thee![^712]

*Troparion of the Feast. And the dismissal.*

## ON SATURDAY AFTER MID-PENTECOST, AT MATINS

*Troparion of the Feast.*

*After the 1st chanting of the Psalter, Resurrectional Sessional Hymns.*
*Tone 3:*
Christ is risen from the dead, the firstfruits of them that slept, the Firstborn of creation, and Maker of all things that have been made: He hath renewed in Himself the corrupted nature of our race: no longer dost thou rule, O death! For the Master of all hath destroyed thy dominion.[^713]

*Verse:* Arise, O Lord my God, let Thy hand be lifted up.[^714]
Having tasted death in the flesh, O Lord, Thou didst cut off the bitterness of death by Thy Resurrection, and having strengthened man against it, recalling the defeat of the ancient curse: O Defender of our life, Christ God, glory to Thee!

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*
We hymn thee who didst mediate the salvation of our race, O Theotokos Virgin: for having accepted the Passion through the Cross in the flesh taken from thee, Thy Son and our God delivered us from corruption, as Lover of mankind.

*After the 2nd chanting of the Psalter, Sessional Hymn.*
*Tone 8, Podoben: "The Wisdom and Word of God" (Премꙋ́дрости сло́ва):*
When the feast of the Law was halfway through, Thou wast teaching in the sanctuary, O my Savior, and rebuking the folly of the unbelieving Hebrews, and crying aloud unto the peoples with a divine voice, as Lover of mankind: Let him that thirsts, Thou didst cry, come unto Me and drink; therefore also Thou didst promise to grant the waters of joy from the incorruptible fountain unto them that believe; therefore we cry unto Thee: Send down the Holy Spirit, O Christ God, and save us, for Thou alone art abundant in mercy![^715]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. The same.*

*Then: "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ..." Psalm 50.*
*Canons of the Feast with heirmoi, on 6; and of the holy temple, on 4; and of the Menaion, on 4.*
*Kontakion, and the exaposteilarion of the Feast.*

*At the Praises, we set 4 verses, and we sing Resurrectional stichera.*
*Tone 3:*
Come, all ye nations, understand the power of the awesome mystery: for Christ our Savior, the Word Who was in the beginning, was crucified for our sake, and was voluntarily buried, and arose from the dead to save all things: unto Him let us bow down.

*Sticheron 2:*
Thy guards recounted all the wonders, O Lord; but the council of vanity filled their right hand with a bribe, thinking to hide Thy Resurrection, which the world glorifies: have mercy on us.[^716]

*Sticheron 3:*
All things were filled with joy, having received the proof of the Resurrection: for Mary Magdalene came unto the tomb, and found an Angel sitting upon the stone, flashing in garments, and saying: Why seek ye the Living among the dead? He is not here, but is risen, even as He said, going before you into Galilee.[^717]

*Sticheron 4:*
In Thy light, O Master, shall we see light, O Lover of mankind: for Thou art risen from the dead, granting salvation unto the human race, that all creation may glorify Thee, the only Sinless One: have mercy on us.[^718]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 6. By Anatolius:*[^719]
Having been enlightened, brethren, by the Resurrection of Christ the Savior, and having reached the midpoint of the Master's feast, let us earnestly keep the commandments of God, that we may be worthy also to celebrate the Ascension and to receive the coming of the Holy Spirit.

*At the Aposticha, stichera.*
*Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме Є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*
The flowing fountain of Thy wisdom pours forth spiritual water, drinking whereof we are filled with divine dogmas.

*Verse:* Remember Thy congregation, which Thou hast purchased from the beginning.[^720]
The fierce race of the Hebrews was truly wounded, hearing Thee, O Word, teaching the peoples with saving doctrine.

*Verse:* But God is our King before the ages: He hath wrought salvation in the midst of the earth.[^721]
Thou didst come unto Zion, O Maker, and didst stand in the midst of Thy temple, and gavest saving grace unto the people.

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 4:*
O Lord, before Thy precious Cross, when the feast was halfway through, Thou didst enter into the sanctuary, teaching the Jews with boldness concerning the things legislated by Moses and by Thee in the Law; and they, being astonished, O Christ, at the ineffable mystery of Thy wisdom, instigated one another through envy to murmur against Thee: How knows this Man letters, having never learned? not knowing Thee to be the Savior of our souls.[^722]

*On Saturday after Mid-Pentecost, the Four-Ode Canon,*[^723]
*Whose acrostic is: Τρίτος ἦχος πέφηνε, that is: The third tone hath appeared:*

*Tone 3. Ode 6. Heirmos:*[^724]
The lowest abyss of sins hath encompassed me, and my spirit fails; but stretch forth Thy high arm, O Master, and save me, O Helmsman, even as Peter.

*Troparion 1 (Τ):*
Pierced with a spear in Thy divine ribs, O Giver of life, Thou didst heal man wounded by transgression by Thy divine Sufferings: therefore, O Master, we hymn Thy dominion.[^725]

*Troparion 2 (Ρ):*
Thou didst endure blows, O Jesus, destroying the kingdoms of hades, and having shattered the bars, by Thine all-sovereign hand Thou didst save all, and didst arise on the third day.[^726]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. Troparion (Ι):*
Thou didst stand before the judgment seat of Pilate like a condemned man, O Lord, the Judge of all the earth; and desiring to deliver from hades him whom Thou didst create, Thou didst descend unto him, O only Merciful One.[^727]

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion (Τ):*
Without birth-pangs thou gavest birth unto the Son Who was begotten of the Father before the ages, O Pure One; and over Him thou didst grieve, beholding the Prince crucified in the flesh; but when He arose as God, thou didst rejoice radiantly.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*[^728]
Of old the youths did not bow down to the golden image, the Persian idol, singing, the three of them in the midst of the furnace: Blessed art Thou, O God of our Fathers.

*Troparion 1 (Ο):*
Being Inaccessible unto the Cherubim and Seraphim, Thou didst endure the Crucifixion in the flesh for the tender compassions of Thy mercy, that Thou mightest save Adam corrupted by transgression.

*Troparion 2 (Σ):*
Having descended with Thy soul into hades, Thou didst destroy its dominion, O Master, and didst raise up the bound that were therein, who hymn Thy dominion, O Giver of life.

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. Troparion (Η):*
Let the despondency of grief be taken away: hasten, ye Myrrh-Bearers, to reach the tomb, and seeing Christ risen from the tomb, preach ye unto the world.[^729]

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion (Χ):*
Adorn thyself, seeing Christ, Whom thou didst bear, O Pure One, risen from the dead on the third day with glory; and as His Mother entreat Him for all the world.

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*[^730]
Joined unto the unbearable fire, the youths championing piety, unhurt by the flame, sang a divine hymn: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages.

*Troparion 1 (Ο):*
He that created every breath by a word is voluntarily hanged upon the tree in the flesh by the Jews, and is given gall to drink; and all creation seeing it was troubled, mourning the madness of the ungrateful.[^731]

*Troparion 2 (Σ):*
The all-devouring hades received Thee, the Author and Savior of the world, like a mere man; but having bound it as Lord, Thou didst take those whom it had of old as captives, and didst raise them together with Thyself on the third day from the tomb.

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. Troparion (Π):*
Without parting from the Father's bosom, Thou didst take flesh for our sake from the Virgin, and didst willingly deliver Thyself to death; and being laid in the tomb, Thou didst arise on the third day, O Word of God: therefore we hymn Thee, the only Giver of life.

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion (Ε):*
Without travail thou gavest birth, O Pure One, unto the Son Who was before the ages with the Father and the Holy Spirit; beholding Him hanging upon the Cross, thou didst indeed suffer grief, but seeing Him arisen from the tomb, thou rejoicest unto the ages.

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*[^732]
In the shadow and letter of the Law we the faithful see an image: every male that opens the womb is holy unto God: therefore the Firstborn Word of the Unoriginate Father, the Son Who is made firstborn of a Mother that knew not man, do we magnify.

*Troparion 1 (Φ):*
The luminaries, seeing Thee hanging in the flesh upon the Cross, O Christ, hid their light, and the thief beholding this spoke divine theology; the whole earth quaked, and the veil being rent cried aloud: Glory to Thy long-suffering, O Master![^733]

*Troparion 2 (Η):*
Thy descent into the nethermost parts, O King, was truly fearsome: for Thou didst shatter the gates and bars of hades, and didst despoil all the captives it held, and didst raise up in sovereign might them that confessed Thee to be God.

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. Troparion (Ν):*
Having taken Thee down dead from the tree with faith, O Christ, and having with love and grief anointed Thee with myrrh, ointment, and a Plashchanytsia, Joseph poured forth a multitude of tears and laid Thee in a tomb of the dead: therefore with him we magnify Thee.[^734]

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion (Ε):*
Rejoice, O Pure One, seeing Thy Son and God arisen in glory from the dead, together with the Myrrh-Bearing women, the holy Apostles, as well as glorious Joseph and Nicodemus; and we magnify thee, O Most Pure One.

*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes: Ode 5. And the prokeimenon of the Feast of Mid-Pentecost.*
*The Epistle of the Acts, pericope 24: "Herod the king stretched forth his hands..."*[^735] *Alleluia of Mid-Pentecost.*
*The Gospel according to John, pericope 31: "The Lord said unto those Jews which believed on Him..."*[^736]
*Communion Hymn: of the Feast of Mid-Pentecost.*

# PART V: SUNDAY OF THE SAMARITAN WOMAN AND FIFTH WEEK AFTER PASCHA

## FIFTH SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA, OF THE SAMARITAN WOMAN

*On Saturday evening, at Small Vespers:*

*At "Lord, I have cried," 4 Resurrectional stichera.*

*Tone 4:*

*To Thy life-creating Cross... (see fol. 385)*[^737]  
*Of the tree of disobedience... (see fol. 385)*  
*The gates of hades hast Thou shattered, O Lord... (see fol. 385)*  
*Come, ye peoples, let us hymn... (see fol. 385)*  

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. Tone 6:*

*At Jacob's well... (see fol. 386)*[^738]  

*Seek all these ahead at Great Vespers.*

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Dogmatic Theotokion. Tone 4:*
Without seed thou didst conceive, and ineffably gavest birth unto Him Who put down the mighty from their seats, and exalted the humble, and raised up the horn of His anointed who glorify Christ's Cross and Burial, and glorious Resurrection: therefore, O Theotokos, mediatress of so many good things, with unceasing hymns we call thee blessed, as thou ever entreatest that our souls may be saved.[^739]

*At the Aposticha, Resurrectional sticheron:*
*O Lord, having ascended the Cross... (see fol. 386)*[^740]  
*Seek this at Great Vespers.*

*Then the following prosomoia stichera of the Most Holy Theotokos.*
*Tone 4, Podoben: "Being called from on high" (Зва́нный свы́ше):*

*Verse:* I will remember thy name in every generation and generation.[^741]
The Son Who is from the Unoriginate Father without beginning of years, for the sake of condescension and the salvation of men, God became man, that He might grant paradise unto the first-created now; then also all nature shall be delivered from the delusion of the serpent, and He shall save the fallen image, as Well-Changer; on both sides He hath made a Mother, a pure Bride-Chamber, as undefiled: whom, as anchor and haven, all of us call blessed.

*Verse:* Hear, O daughter, and see, and incline thine ear.[^742]
Thou didst hold in thy womb the incarnate Creator of all, O Divinely Blessed One, Who re-formed man who of old had fallen through the transgression of the serpent; for thou gavest birth unto God ineffably for us, and by thy Childbearing didst set free all our corrupted and aged nature: therefore we hymn and glorify thy grace, O Unwedded Virgin; cease not to pray that our souls may be saved.

*Verse:* The rich among the people shall entreat thy countenance.[^743]
That thou mayest reveal unto all the multitude of thy mercy, and unto us the abyss of goodness that never passes away, blot out all the sins of thy servants: for, O All-Blameless One, as Mother of God, thou hast authority over creation, and thou guidest all things as thou wilt by thy power: for the grace of the Holy Spirit having manifestly dwelt in thee, works together with thee in all things ever, O Most Blessed One.

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. Tone 8:*
When Thou wast manifested in the flesh, O Christ God, in Thine ineffable dispensation, the Samaritan woman, hearing Thy word, O Lover of mankind, left her water-pot by the well, and ran, saying unto them that were in the city: Come, see the Knower of hearts! Is not this indeed the expected Christ, Who hath great mercy?[^744]

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. The same:*
When the feast was halfway through, as Thou wast teaching, O Savior, the Jews said: Whence knows this Man letters, having never learned? not understanding that Thou art the Wisdom that fashioned the world: glory to Thee![^745]

*Dismissal Troparion. Tone 4:*
Having learned from the Angel the radiant proclamation of the Resurrection, and cast off the ancestral condemnation, the women disciples of the Lord boasting said unto the Apostles: Death is overthrown! Christ God is risen, granting great mercy unto the world!

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Troparion of the Feast:*[^746]
When the feast is halfway through, give my thirsty soul to drink of the waters of piety, for unto all, O Savior, Thou didst cry aloud: Let him that thirsts come unto Me and drink! O Wellspring of our life, Christ God, glory to Thee!

*And the dismissal.*

*On the Sunday of the Samaritan Woman, at Great Vespers.*

## AT GREAT VESPERS

*We set 10 verses. And we sing 3 Resurrectional stichera, and 1 Anatolian; and 3 prosomoia of Mid-Pentecost; and 3 Idiomela of the Samaritan Woman.*

*Resurrectional stichera, Tone 4:*

*Sticheron 1:*
Unto Thy life-creating Cross, unceasingly bowing down in worship, O Christ God, we glorify Thy third-day Resurrection; for thereby hast Thou renewed the corrupted human nature, O Almighty One, and hast renewed for us the ascent unto heaven, as the only good One and Lover of mankind.

*Sticheron 2:*
The condemnation of the tree of disobedience hast Thou dissolved, O Savior, by being willingly nailed unto the tree of the Cross; and having descended into hades, O Mighty One, Thou didst tear asunder the bonds of death as God; therefore we bow down in worship unto Thy Resurrection from the dead, crying out with joy: O Almighty Lord, glory to Thee!

*Sticheron 3:*
The gates of hades hast Thou shattered, O Lord, and by Thy death hast Thou destroyed the kingdom of death; and the human race hast Thou freed from corruption, granting life and incorruption unto the world, and great mercy.

*Another sticheron, Anatolian:*

*Sticheron 4:*
Come, ye peoples, let us hymn the Savior's third-day Arising, whereby we have been delivered from the unbreakable bonds of hades, and have all received incorruption and life, crying aloud: O Thou Who wast crucified, and buried, and didst arise, save us by Thy Resurrection, O only Lover of mankind!

*And stichera of Mid-Pentecost, 3, the same Tone. Podoben: "O Lord, having ascended the Cross" (Гд҃и возше́дъ на кр҃тъ):*

*The midpoint of the days has arrived...*  
*Heard and rejoiced...*  
*Draw near, ye peoples, unto the Divine... (see fol. 372)*[^747]  

*And of the Samaritan Woman, idiomela, 3.*  
*Tone 1:*

*Sticheron 8:*
Unto the fountain didst Thou come, O Fountain of wonders, at the sixth hour, to capture the fruit of Eve; for Eve at that hour went forth from paradise by the deceit of the serpent;[^748] the Samaritan woman drew near to draw water, whom having seen, the Savior said: Give Me water to drink, and I will satisfy thee with flowing water; and having run into the city, the chaste woman immediately proclaimed unto the multitudes: Come, see Christ the Lord, the Savior of our souls![^749]

*Tone 2:*

*Sticheron 9:*
When the Lord came unto the well, the Samaritan woman entreated the Compassionate One: Give me the water of faith, and I shall receive the waters of the font, rejoicing and redemption; O Life-Giver, Lord, glory to Thee![^750]

*Tone 3:*

*Sticheron 10:*
The Son and Word of the Father, co-unoriginate and co-eternal, came unto the fountain, being the Fountain of healings; and a woman came from Samaria to draw water, whom having seen, the Savior said: Give Me water to drink, and go, call thy husband. But she, speaking as unto a man and not unto God, striving to conceal herself, said: I have no husband. And the Teacher said unto her: Truly hast thou said: I have no husband; for thou hast had five, and now he whom thou hast is not thy husband. But she, being amazed at His word, ran unto the city and cried out unto the multitudes, saying: Come, see Christ, Who grants unto the world great mercy![^751]

*Glory, Tone 6:*

*Doxasticon:*
At Jacob's well, Jesus, finding the Samaritan woman, asks water of her, He Who covers the earth with clouds.[^752] O wonder! He Who is borne upon the Cherubim conversed with a woman who was a harlot; asking for water, He Who suspended the earth upon the waters; seeking water, He Who pours forth springs and lakes of waters; desiring truly to draw her who was captured by the adversary foe, and to give her living water to drink, who was sorely burned in unseemliness, as the only compassionate One and Lover of mankind!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Dogmatic Theotokion, Tone 4:*
David the Prophet, who through thee became the forefather of God, cried out concerning thee in psalmody unto Him Who worked great things for thee: The Queen stood at Thy right hand;[^753] for God, Who was pleased without a father to become man from thee, showed thee forth as the Mother and mediatress of life, that He might renew His image corrupted by passions, and having found the sheep that went astray upon the mountains, taking it upon His shoulder, He might bring it unto the Father, and according to His own will, unite it with the heavenly hosts, and save the world, O Theotokos, Christ Who hath great and rich mercy.

*Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day:*  
*At the Litiya, sticheron of the temple.*  
*Glory, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 3:*

*Litiya Sticheron:*
Let heaven and earth rejoice radiantly today, for Christ hath appeared, being incarnate as man, that He might deliver Adam from the curse of the entire race, and is admired for His marvels, having come into Samaria; and He presented Himself unto the woman, asking for water, He Who arrays the clouds with waters; therefore all we faithful worship Him Who for our sake willingly became poor, by His compassionate counsel![^754]

*At the Aposticha, Resurrectional sticheron, Tone 4:*
O Lord, having ascended the Cross, Thou didst abolish our ancestral curse; and having descended into hades, Thou didst free those bound from the ages, granting incorruption unto the human race; therefore with hymns we glorify Thy life-creating and saving Arising!

*Then the Stichera of Pascha, with their refrains; seek on the Sunday of Pascha at Matins: (see fol. 205).*[^755]

*Glory, Tone 8:*
When Thou didst appear in the flesh, O Christ God, by Thine ineffable dispensation, the Samaritan woman, having heard the word of Thee, the Lover of mankind, left her water jar at the well and ran, saying unto those in the city: Come, see the Knower of hearts; is this not the expected Christ, Who hath great mercy?[^756]

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen.*  
*The day of Resurrection:*  
*And all the rest, as was prescribed in the other Sundays.*

*Dismissal Troparion, Tone 4:*  
The radiant proclamation of the Resurrection having learned from the Angel, the Lord's disciples cast off the ancestral condemnation, and boasting, said unto the Apostles: Death is overthrown, Christ God is risen, granting unto the world great mercy!

*Glory, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast, Tone 8:*  
At Mid-Pentecost, satisfy my thirsty soul with the waters of piety, for Thou, O Savior, didst cry aloud unto all: Whosoever thirsts, let him come unto Me and drink; O Fountain of our life, Christ God, glory to Thee![^757]

*If there be no vigil, at the Midnight Office the Canon to the Holy and Life-Originating Trinity, in the Octoechos, of the 4th Tone.*  
*Then "It is truly meet," and the rest.*

## ON THE FIFTH SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA, OF THE SAMARITAN WOMAN, AT MATINS

*At "God is the Lord," Resurrectional Troparion:*  
*Tone 4:*  
*The radiant proclamation of the Resurrection: Twice. Glory, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen.*  
*Of the feast: At Mid-Pentecost:*  
*Then the customary chanting of the Psalter.*

*After the 1st chanting of the Psalter, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4:*  
Beholding the entrance of the tomb, and unable to endure the flame of the Angel, the Myrrh-bearing women marveled with trembling, saying: Was He stolen away Who opened paradise unto the thief? Or is He arisen Who proclaimed His Arising even before the Passion? Truly Christ is risen, granting life and resurrection unto those in hades![^758]

*Verse: Arise, O Lord my God, let Thy hand be lifted up; forget not Thy poor unto the end.*[^759]

*Tone 4, Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*  
Thou didst arise from the tomb as immortal, O Savior; Thou didst raise up Thy world together with Thyself by Thy power, O Christ our God; Thou didst crush the dominion of death in strength; Thou didst show forth the Resurrection unto all, O Merciful One; therefore we also glorify Thee, O only Lover of mankind![^760]

*Glory, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*  
The mystery hidden from the ages and unknown unto Angels was revealed through thee, O Theotokos, unto those upon earth: God incarnate in inconfused union, Who willingly accepted the Cross for our sake, whereby having resurrected the first-fashioned man, He saved our souls from death.[^761]

*After the 2nd chanting of the Psalter, Sessional Hymn.*  
*Tone 4, Podoben: "Joseph was amazed" (Оу҆диви́сѧ І҆ѡ́сифъ):*  
Having descended from the heights on high, Gabriel came unto the stone where the Rock of life lay, and clothed in white, he cried unto the weeping women: Cease your lamentation and crying, ye who even now have compassion; for take courage, He Whom ye seek weeping is truly risen; therefore cry aloud unto the Apostles that the Lord is risen![^762]

*Verse: I will confess Thee, O Lord, with my whole heart, I will tell of all Thy marvelous works.*[^763]

*Sessional Hymn:*  
By Thy voluntary counsel Thou didst endure the Cross, O Savior, and mortal men laid Thee in a new tomb, Who didst establish the ends of the earth by Thy word; therefore the alien foe was bound; death was sorely despoiled, and all those in hades cried out unto Thy life-bearing Arising: Christ is risen, the Life-Giver Who abides unto the ages!

*Glory, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion, automelon:*  
Joseph was amazed, beholding that which was above nature, and he considered the rain upon the fleece in thy seedless conception, O Theotokos, the bush unburned by fire, Aaron's rod that budded; and thy betrothed and guardian, bearing witness, cried unto the priests: A Virgin gives birth, and after childbirth remains again a Virgin![^764]

*Then the reading in the Commentary on the Gospel of John: Homilies 31, 32, 33, and 34.*[^765]  
*After "Blessed are the blameless,"*[^766] *we say the Resurrectional troparia: "Blessed art Thou, O Lord," in Tone 5: "The Angelic Council," and the rest.*

*And immediately the Hypakoe, Tone 4:*  
Having run beforehand, the Myrrh-bearing women proclaimed Thy glorious Arising unto the Apostles, O Christ, that Thou art risen as God, granting unto the world great mercy.[^767]

*And immediately the ANTIPHONS OF ASCENT, Tone 4.*  
*Antiphon 1:*  
From my youth many passions war against me; but do Thou Thyself help me and save me, O my Savior!  
Ye that hate Zion, be put to shame by the Lord; for ye shall be withered up even as grass by fire.[^768]  
*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.*  
By the Holy Spirit every soul is quickened, and through purity is exalted; it is made radiant by the Triune Unity in sacred mystery.  
*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. The same.*

*Antiphon 2:*  
I cried unto Thee, O Lord, fervently from the depth of my soul, and let Thy Divine ears be attentive unto me for hearing.[^769]  
Whosoever hath acquired hope in the Lord is higher than all who grieve.[^770]  
*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.*  
By the Holy Spirit stream the floods of grace, watering all creation unto revitalization.  
*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. The same.*

*Antiphon 3:*  
Let my heart be lifted up unto Thee, O Word, and let none of the world's allurements beguile me unto faintness.  
Even as one hath love for his mother, so are we bound with warmer affection unto the Lord.  
*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.*  
By the Holy Spirit is the wealth of divine knowledge, contemplation, and wisdom; for in Him the Word reveals all the Father's decrees.  
*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. The same.*

*Prokeimenon, Tone 4:*  
Arise, O Lord, help us, and redeem us for Thy name's sake.[^771]  
*Verse: O God, with our ears have we heard.*[^772]  
*Then: Let every breath praise the Lord.*  
*Verse: Praise God in His saints.*  
*The Gospel according to John, 7th Matins Resurrection Gospel: "On the first day of the week..."*[^773]  
*Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ: Thrice. Psalm 50. And the rest.*

*Then the CANONS: Of Pascha, with the heirmoi and Theotokia, to 6; of Mid-Pentecost, to 4; and of the Samaritan Woman, to 4.*  
*Katavasia: The day of Resurrection:*  
*Canon of Pascha, Tone 1. Ode 1. Heirmos: The day of Resurrection:*  
*Second Canon of Mid-Pentecost.*  
*The work of Andrew of Crete.*[^774]  
*Tone 8. Ode 1. Heirmos:*  
Thou hast congealed the sea:

*Troparion:*
Clap your hands, ye nations; weep, ye Jews; for Christ the Life-Giver hath burst asunder the bonds of hades, and raised the dead, and healed infirmities by His word; this is our God, Who hath given life unto those who believe in His name![^775]

*Troparion:*
A miracle didst Thou show, water transformed into wine, O Master Who didst turn the rivers in Egypt into blood; and Thou didst raise the dead, having accomplished this second sign: glory, O Savior, to Thine ineffable counsel; glory to Thy self-emptying, whereby Thou hast renewed us![^776]

*Troparion:*
