Being the ever-flowing stream of true life, O Lord, Thou art our Resurrection; willingly didst Thou labor, O my Savior, and voluntarily didst Thou thirst, submitting unto the laws of nature; and having gone in the flesh unto Sychar, Thou didst ask water to drink of the Samaritan woman.[^777]

*Theotokion:*
Thou alone didst contain thy Creator in thy womb, O Mother of God, and didst ineffably bear Him in the flesh, and didst remain a Virgin, thy virginity being in no wise defiled; therefore, O Pure One, as thy Son and God, unceasingly pray unto Him ever for thy flock!

*Another Canon, of the Samaritan Woman. The work of Joseph.*[^778]  
*Tone 4. Ode 1. Heirmos:*  
Thou Who didst smite Egypt, and didst drown Pharaoh the tormentor in the sea, didst save the people from servitude, who sang a song of victory after the manner of Moses: For He is glorified![^779]

*Troparion:*
He Who was buried is risen, and hath raised up the human race with Himself; let all creation rejoice, and let the spiritual clouds today manifestly drop down righteousness![^780]

*Troparion:*
Having willingly accepted the Cross in the flesh, Thou didst arise on the third day from the dead, having shattered the strongholds of hades, O Life-Originating Lord, and having led forth the bound souls!

*Troparion:*
Beholding the Angel flashing in appearance, the Myrrh-bearing women fled from the tomb with fear; but having learned of Christ's Resurrection, they strive to proclaim it unto the disciples.[^781]

*Troparion:*
O Lord Who coverest the highest heavens with waters, being Thyself the Water of life, Thou didst give Thy precious waters unto the Samaritan woman who asked, who understood Thy compassion.[^782]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. Trinity Hymn:*  
O Trinity, O Father, Son, and Spirit, save those who honor and glorify Thee with faith, as Creator of all, and grant us cleansing of sins, as Thou art supremely good!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*  
Rejoice, O Fiery Throne; rejoice, O all-golden Lampstand; rejoice, O Cloud of light; rejoice, O Palace of the Word, and living Table, who didst worthily bear Christ, the Bread of life![^783]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*  
My heart was established:[^784]

*Troparion:*
Judge not according to appearance, ye Jews! the Master cried teaching, when He came into the temple, as it is written, at Mid-Pentecost of the lawful feast.[^785]

*Troparion:*
Judge not according to appearance, ye Jews! for Christ is come, Whom the Prophets foretold, coming forth from Zion, and calling the world.[^786]

*Troparion:*
Even if ye believe not His words, ye Jews, believe the works of the Master; why are ye deceived, rejecting the Holy One, concerning Whom Moses wrote in the law?[^787]

*Theotokion:*
Being One of the Trinity, Thou wast seen as flesh, without changing Thy essence, O Lord, nor burning the incorrupt womb of her that bore Thee, being wholly God and fire!

*Another, Heirmos:*  
My heart was established in the Lord, Who gives prayer unto him that prays; for the bow of the mighty hath grown weak, and the feeble have girded themselves with strength.[^788]

*Troparion:*
Willingly wast Thou lifted up upon the Tree, O Word; and beholding it, the stones were rent, and all creation bowed down, and the dead arose from the tombs as if from sleep![^789]

*Troparion:*
Beholding Thee having come into hades with Thy soul, O Word, all the souls of the righteous were loosed from their eternal bonds, singing of Thy power which is beyond understanding![^790]

*Troparion:*
Why are ye amazed? Why seek ye the Master in the tomb with myrrh, O women? He is risen, and hath raised up the world together with Himself! the flashing Angel cried unto the Myrrh-bearing women.[^791]

*Troparion:*
Being Life, O Lord, and the Fountain of immortality, Thou didst sit by the fountain, O Compassionate One, and with Thy all-wise waters didst fill the Samaritan woman who asked and sang unto Thee.[^792]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. Trinity Hymn:*  
One God over all in the Trinity is hymned, the Father, and the Son, and the Divine Spirit, Whom the heavenly ranks glorify with fear, clearly crying out: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, O Lord![^793]

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*  
Having ineffably conceived in thy womb the God of all, O Virgin Mother, thou didst give birth beyond thought and word, remaining a Virgin even as before childbirth, O Bride of God!

*Kontakion of Mid-Pentecost, and the Ikos: (see fol. 371).*[^794]  
*Sessional Hymn of the Samaritan Woman, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou Who wast lifted up upon the Cross" (Вознесы́йсѧ):*  
Let heaven rejoice, let earthly things be glad, for Christ hath appeared from the Virgin as man, and hath delivered all humanity from corruption by His death; and shining forth with miracles unto the Samaritan woman who asked for water, He grants a fountain of healings, as the only Immortal One![^795]

*Glory, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 4, the same Podoben:*  
O Bestower of wisdom and Master, Thou didst present Thyself at the lawful feast, and sitting in the temple, Thou didst teach, saying thus unto all: Come, ye that thirst, drink the water which I now give, whereby all men shall enjoy life from God and delight![^796]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*  
The Prophet Habakkuk:[^797]

*Troparion:*
If the Messiah must come, and Christ is the Messiah, O lawless ones, why believe ye Him not? Behold, He is come, and the things that He does bear witness: He made water into wine; He strengthened the paralytic by His word![^798]

*Troparion:*
Not understanding the Scriptures, ye are all deceived, ye lawless Hebrews; for truly Christ is come and hath enlightened all, and among you hath shown forth many signs and wonders, yet ye deny yourselves true Life![^799]

*Troparion:*
One work have I shown you, and ye all already marvel, cried Christ unto the Jews: Ye circumcise a man even on the Sabbath, He said: why then do ye slander Me further, Who raised up the paralytic by a word?[^800]

*Troparion:*
Many works have I done, and for which work do ye stone Me with stones? cried Christ rebuking the Jews: Is it because I made an entire man whole by a word? Judge not according to appearance, O men![^801]

*Another Heirmos:*  
I heard Thy report, O God, and was afraid; I considered Thy works and was terrified, O Lord; for the earth is full of Thy praise.[^802]

*Troparion:*
Let the heavens be glad, let all creation keep festival: the Lord is risen, and hath appeared unto all His all-wise Apostles!

*Troparion:*
Thy strength was swallowed up, O death, for Christ having died, the dead went forth from the tombs by His Arising, as if from bridal chambers![^803]

*Troparion:*
Why weep ye, O women? Why seek ye the Immortal One with myrrh? He is risen, even as He said! the Angel spoke unto the Myrrh-bearing women.[^804]

*Troparion:*
Unto the Samaritan woman who asked, O Lord, Thou didst give water, the knowledge of Thy dominion; therefore unto the ages she shall not thirst, singing praise unto Thee![^805]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. Trinity Hymn:*  
O transcendent Trinity, Father, Word, and Divine Spirit, of one power, co-unoriginate: save us all who hymn Thee with faith!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*  
The lawgiver of old beheld thee as the unburned bush, and Daniel contemplated the holy mountain, O only Virgin Mother, Sovereign Lady![^806]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*  
O Lord our God, peace:[^807]

*Troparion:*
With wonders hast Thou adorned Thine Apostles, marvelous hast Thou magnified Thy disciples, having glorified them in all the world, O our Savior, and having given unto them Thy Kingdom![^808]

*Troparion:*
The disciples enlightened all the ends of the earth by wonders and teachings, and in various manners proclaimed the word of Thy Kingdom, O Christ Savior!

*Troparion:*
Praise we send up unto Thy Kingdom, and hymnody we offer unto Thee, Who didst appear upon earth for our sake, and didst enlighten the world, and didst recall Adam!

*Theotokion:*
Thy womb became a Holy Table, having the Heavenly Bread; of which whosoever eats dies not, even as the Nourisher of all hath said, O Mother of God![^809]

*Another, Heirmos:*  
Make the light of Thy commandments shine upon me, O Lord, for unto Thee my spirit rises early and sings unto Thee; for Thou art our God, and unto Thee do I flee, O King of peace![^810]

*Troparion:*
Having reached Thy holy tomb very early in the morning, the Myrrh-bearing women beheld a young man flashing with light, and were terrified, having learned of Thy Divine Arising, O Christ![^811]

*Troparion:*
Death is put to death, hades is despoiled, those in bonds are set free by Christ's Resurrection; let us rejoice and clap our hands, celebrating radiantly![^812]

*Troparion:*
Leap for joy, ye Apostles, and dance, ye Angels; let all earthborn mortals rejoice: the Lord is risen, corruption is overthrown, and sorrow hath ceased, and Adam leaps for joy!

*Troparion:*
Being the Fountain of life, O Lord, Thou didst grant the water of remission and understanding unto the woman who asked of old, the Samaritan woman; therefore we sing of Thine ineffable compassions![^813]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. Trinity Hymn:*  
The three-hypostatic Monad, the consubstantial Trinity, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Spirit, indivisible in essence, we venerate as one God, Creator and Lord and Master of all!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*  
Thee do we name the Gate impassable, and the Field untilled, and the Ark bearing the Manna and the Jar, and the Lampstand, and the Censer of immaterial coal, O Pure One![^814]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*  
As the waters of the sea:[^815]

*Troparion:*
Upholding all the ends of the earth, Thou didst ascend, O Jesus, and didst teach the peoples in the temple the word of truth, at Mid-Pentecost, even as John cries aloud![^816]

*Troparion:*
The Father's work hast Thou accomplished, by works hast Thou confirmed Thy words, performing healings and signs, O Savior: making whole the paralytic, cleansing the lepers, and raising the dead![^817]

*Troparion:*
The unoriginate Son became originate, having assumed our nature, He became man, and in the midst of the feast He taught, saying: Come ye unto the ever-flowing Fountain, draw life![^818]

*Theotokion:*
A Virgin after childbirth we hymn thee, a Virgin and Mother we glorify thee, thee alone, O Pure Maiden, Bride of God; for from thee truly God was incarnate, having renewed us!

*Another. Heirmos:*  
Let not the waterflood drown me, neither let the deep swallow me up; for I am cast into the depths of the heart of the sea of my evils; therefore I cry as Jonah: Let my life arise from corruption unto Thee, O God![^819]

*Troparion:*
Upon the Cross the lawless ones nailed Thee, and pierced Thee with a spear, O Christ, and noble Joseph buried Thee in a new tomb; from which having risen with glory, Thou didst raise up together with Thyself all creation that sings of Thy dominion, O Savior![^820]

*Troparion:*
The bars and gates of hades hast Thou mightily shattered, O Master, and Thou didst arise as God; and having met the women, Thou didst say: Rejoice! and didst send them to tell these things unto the disciples: Life is arisen, and hath appeared, enlightening the ends of the earth![^821]

*Troparion:*
Why weep ye? Why carry ye myrrh as unto a mortal, O women? Christ is risen! cried of old the radiant white young man who appeared, having left the three-day winding sheets: Go, tell His friends of His Arising![^822]

*Troparion:*
Being the ungrudging stream of life, O Lord, and abyss of mercy, where having journeyed Thou sittest near the well of the oath,[^823] and Thou didst cry unto the Samaritan woman: Give Me water to drink, that thou mayest receive the waters of remission!

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. Trinity Hymn:*  
I sing of the unoriginate Father, and the co-enthroned Son, and the consubstantial Spirit faithfully: one substance, and nature, and glory, and one Kingdom, God of all and Creator, Sustainer of all, together with the bodiless powers!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*  
The only Virgin who gavest birth, and didst preserve thy womb incorrupt, we hymn thee, O Pure One, Throne of the Lord, and Gate, and Mountain, and spiritual Lampstand, all-radiant Bridal Chamber of God, and tabernacle of glory manifestly, Ark, and Jar, and Table![^824]

*Kontakion, Tone 8, Podoben: "As first-fruits of nature" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ нача́тки):*  
Having come with faith unto the well, the Samaritan woman beheld Thee, the Water of wisdom, whereof having drunk abundantly, she inherited the Kingdom on high eternally, as ever-glorious![^825]

*Ikos:*  
Let us hear the venerable mysteries, as John teaches us, that came to pass in Samaria: how the Lord conversed with the woman, having asked for water, He Who gathered the waters into their gatherings, Who is co-enthroned with the Father and the Spirit; for He came seeking His own image, eternally as ever-glorious![^826]

*Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*

*Verses:*  
*Coming to draw corruptible water, O woman,*  
*Thou drawest living water, whereby thou washest away the defilements of the soul.*[^827]

On this same day, the Fifth Sunday after Pascha, we celebrate the feast of the Samaritan Woman; because unto her Christ plainly confessed Himself to be the Messiah, which is Christ: [or the Anointed.][^828] For with the Hebrews the measure is oil; therefore, I think, it was appointed also for the week of Mid-Pentecost. And even as in the Sunday prior to this He worked a miracle at the pool,[^829] so in this present one, Christ conversed with the woman over Jacob’s well, which well Jacob himself dug and gave to Joseph his son;[^830] for this was an excellent place, where also near the existing Mount Somor, the Samaritans inhabited many cities. And Christ comes into Sychar, where Jacob had dwelt of old with his sons and with Dinah his daughter. Shechem, son of Hamor the Horrite, lusted after her, and having violated her, was with her; and from that cause her brothers, being provoked to great jealousy, suddenly entered into the city and killed them all together, both that Shechem and Hamor his father.[^831] Jacob therefore dwelt there, and dug the present well. Yet the Samaritans did not dwell near that mountain previously, but the Israelites, having provoked that anger, in the reign of Pekah, during the first and second captivities, when the Assyrians came, were subjected to tribute by them; and afterward, in the reign of Hoshea, they attached themselves to the Ethiopians; which when the Assyrian king learned, he deported them to Babylon. And he commanded various nations to dwell in that place; but God let loose lions upon those foreigners. And the Assyrian king, having learned this in turn, sent unto them priests from among the Jews, (for they were still captives there,) that they might also receive the laws of God. And from the idols indeed they quickly broke away. But only...[^832]

...the five books of Moses did they accept, rejecting the Prophets and the rest of the Scripture.[^833] These were also called Samaritans, as being from Mount Somor; and they were hated by the Hebrews returning from captivity, because they Judaized only in part and would not eat with them, abominating them unyieldingly; therefore also they often called Christ a Samaritan, as one who despised and broke certain things of the Law even as they did.[^834]

The Lord therefore comes into Sychar, and being weary from the journey, He sat down about the sixth hour of the day. And a certain woman from the city came to draw water, the disciples having gone away to buy food; Jesus therefore asks water. But she proposes not to touch Him, having recognized Him both from His speech and from His apparel. But He leads her upward, bringing spiritual water into the midst, which He shows to be inexhaustible and cleansing; for the Spirit is ever likened unto water and fire. But the woman, persisting importunately, that He had no such water, so as not to carry a vessel for drawing, and that the well belonged to Jacob, she replies; furthermore she also raises word concerning the forefather Jacob, that he himself dug the well, and he and his sheep drank of it, setting forth the rich abundance of the springs, and that the well was otherwise well-suited.[^835]

Christ therefore does not make Himself greater than Jacob, lest He terrify the woman, but speaks concerning the water, setting forth the abundance thereof prefiguratively: for he who drinks of that water shall by no means thirst.[^836] And the woman asks for the water. But He tells her to summon her husband, as she was in need of understanding more solid words. But she denies that she has a husband. And He Who knows all things says: Thou hast well said, for five husbands hast thou had, as the Law commands, and he whom thou now hast as the sixth, because thou cohabitest with him unlawfully, is not thy husband.[^837]

[Some indeed have thought the five husbands to be the five books of Moses, which the Samaritans accepted, and the sixth to be those words of Christ, which were not yet spoken, for grace was not yet poured out. Others say they were the five laws given by God: that in paradise, and that after the expulsion; that in the time of Noah; that in the time of Abraham; that in the time of Moses; while the sixth is the Gospel, which she did not yet possess. There are also those who say they are the five senses.][^838]

The woman answers Him, calling Him a Prophet. Then she also questions Him concerning the mountain, where it is proper to worship: in Somor or in Jerusalem? For the Samaritans did not deem that God is completely everywhere, but that God abides only there where they also worshiped, on Mount Gerizim, because the blessing was given there from God; or because there Israel first built an altar unto God; even as the Jews said in turn: In Jerusalem it is proper to worship the one God; therefore also those from all quarters gathered there for the feast.[^839]

And Christ answers: Salvation for the world, He says, is of the Jews; yet He said: God is immaterial, and those deemed worthy to worship Him are no longer to worship in sacrifices, but in spirit and in truth; or they shall know God thus: not as solitary, but in the Holy Spirit and the Son, for He is the Truth.[^840]

The woman says again: We hear from the Scriptures that Messiah comes, Who is called Christ. And Jesus says: I am He; having understood the noble disposition of the woman.[^841]

And the Samaritans knew also concerning the Messiah from the books of Moses, and especially from this: A Prophet shall the Lord God raise up unto you; and from many other passages.[^842]

And as the conversation was ending, the disciples also come, and they marvel exceedingly at His condescension, how He was speaking with a woman. Nevertheless they entreat Him to eat, both because He had toiled and because of the heat of the season. But He speaks unto them of eternal food, that is the salvation of mankind, and that they ought to reap the labors of the Prophets.[^843]

And when the woman reached the city and related what had befallen her, all were stirred up and came unto Christ, having believed; for the woman would not have put herself to shame unless she had understood something great. And having entreatingly besought Him to abide with them, they persuade Him to stay for two days. And having tarried, He wrought very many miracles, which indeed by reason of their multitude were not written in the Gospel.[^844]

And this is that Samaritan woman, who was afterward named Photina by Christ, who also was crowned with the wreath of martyrdom under Nero Caesar, together with her seven sons, after much dragging about, scraping, cutting off of breasts, crushing of hands, inserting of sharp reeds under fingernails, pouring of molten lead, and countless other torments, and at the end was tied to two trees and torn asunder.[^845]

Be it known also that the well-curb of that well, that is, its mouth, Emperor Justinian honorably brought thence, and placed it in the Great Church of the Word of God, Hagia Sophia; and the stone also whereon Christ sat as He conversed with the Samaritan woman; and both abide unto this day before the narthex from the east, on the left side to those entering the temple, healing every disease, and especially those who happen to suffer from burning fevers and are tossed with the ague, and they cleanse and drive away enchantments that are wrought.[^846]

By the intercessions of Thy martyr Photina, O Christ God, have mercy on us. Amen.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*  
The Chaldean furnace...[^847]

*Troparion:*  
In the flesh didst Thou toil, O Rest of all; of Thine own will didst Thou thirst, O Fountain of wonders; water didst Thou ask, announcing the water of life, O Jesus!

*Troparion:*  
Unto the Samaritan woman, O Lord, didst Thou converse, exposing the madness of the lawless Hebrews: she indeed believed Thee to be the Son of God, but they rejected Thee![^848]

*Troparion:*  
Eating the Bread of the Lord's Flesh, and receiving the Blood from His pierced Side, let us walk in renewal of the Spirit, living by grace![^849]

*Theotokion:*  
In thy womb thou didst contain the uncontainable Word, from thy breasts thou didst suckle the Nourisher of the world, in thine embrace thou didst bear our Creator, O pure Mother of God!

*Another. Heirmos:*

*Another. Heirmos:*  
Forsake us not utterly for Thy name's sake, neither disannul Thou Thy covenant, and cause not Thy mercy to depart from us, O Lord, the God of our fathers, praised and exalted above all unto the ages![^850]

*Troparion:*  
With the lawless, O compassionate Christ, of Thine own will wast Thou numbered at the time of Thy divine Passion; and beholding these things, the earth was shaken, and the rocks were rent by Thine all-working nod, O Incomprehensible One, and the dead from the ages arose![^851]

*Troparion:*  
Having descended with Thy soul into the nethermost parts of hades, with courage hast Thou led up all the bound whom death, that bitter tormentor, had seized from the ages, who cry unto Thee, O Christ God: Glory to Thy dread dispensation![^852]

*Troparion:*  
Why seek ye the Living among the dead unto the ages? He is risen, even as He said: behold, as ye see, the winding sheets are empty, the tomb is emptied! cried the radiant young man who appeared unto the Myrrh-bearing women: go quickly, tell the Apostles![^853]

*Troparion:*  
Thou art the Water of life, cried the Samaritan woman unto Christ: give me to drink therefore, O Word, who ever thirst for Thy divine grace, that I no longer, O Lord Jesus, be held by the scorching heat of ignorance, but proclaim Thy majesty![^854]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. Trinity Hymn:*  
We hymn the Father, and the Son, and the divine Spirit: the Trinity indivisible in essence, divided in Persons, one Substance, co-natural, unoriginate, Creator of all and God, Whom all the heavenly ranks do hymn!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*  
After thy dread childbirth, O pure Virgin, thou hast remained preserved, O holy Mother of God; therefore all the angelic choirs and all the generations of mankind hymn thee with unceasing voices, O pure dwelling-place of the Incomprehensible One!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*  
Angels and the heavens upon the Throne...[^855]

*Troparion:*  
Come, behold, ye people, Him Who is hymned upon the Throne of glory, blasphemed by the lawless people; and beholding, sing ye unto the Messiah foretold in the Prophets![^856]

*Troparion:*  
Truly Thou art Christ Who didst come into this world, from Whom is salvation and the remission of our ancestral transgressions; truly Thou art Life unto those who believe in Thee!

*Troparion:*  
When the feast was at Mid-point, as it is written, the Wisdom of God stood in the Sanctuary and taught: Truly this is our Messiah, Christ, by Whom is salvation![^857]

*Theotokion:*  
How gavest thou birth, speak, unto Him Who shone forth timelessly from the Father, and is hymned with the Holy Spirit? Even as He Who is One of all, Who was well-pleased to be born of thee, O Mother of God!

*Another. Heirmos:*  
With Thy majestic hand hast Thou framed all things in wisdom, and again hast Thou established the base of the earth as Thou knowest, setting the foundation upon the boundless waters; therefore we all cry aloud, chanting: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, unceasingly![^858]

*Troparion:*  
Death hast Thou endured of Thine own will, O Thou Who alone art immortal; Thou hast plundered hades, O Lord, and crushed the gates of brass, O heavenly King, and delivered the prisoners who were there from the ages, who unceasingly hymn the dominion of Thy goodness![^859]

*Troparion:*  
Thou wast lifted up upon the Tree of Thine own will, O Long-suffering One; and the rocks were rent, and the sun grew dark, and the veil of the temple was torn in twain, and the earth was shaken, and all-devouring hades trembled, and released all the prisoners![^860]

*Troparion:*  
Thou hast appeared unto those sitting in darkness, O Lord, Who art the unwaning Light and the Life of all; therefore when the assembly of the righteous beheld Thee, O Word, they leaped for joy and cried aloud: Thou hast come to release all from bonds who hymn Thy dominion![^861]

*Troparion:*  
Thou didst sit near the well, O Savior, at the sixth hour, and didst grant unto the Samaritan woman living water and the waters of understanding, by reason of Thine abundant tender mercy; with her we all cry aloud, chanting: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, unceasingly![^862]

*We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit: the Lord.*

*Trinity Hymn:*  
We hymn the unoriginate Father, the co-unoriginate Son, and the Holy Spirit: God, One in Three, unconfused, undivided, Creator of all, of one equal power, sovereign Dominion, and we cry aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, unceasingly!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*  
With a live coal was Isaiah cleansed, prefiguring the spiritual Coal Who is incarnate from thee beyond comprehension, O Virgin, consuming all the material sins of mankind, and through mercy deifying our nature, O all-blameless Lady![^863]

*Then: We praise, bless, and worship the Lord:*  
*and the Katavasia.*  
*More honorable than the Cherubim is not sung.*

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*  
Alien to mothers is virginity...[^864]

*Troparion:*  
When the Jewish feast was at Mid-point, Thou didst go up into Thy Sanctuary, O my Savior, and didst teach all; and the Jews marveled, saying: Whence knows this man letters, having never learned?[^865]

*Troparion:*  
Pouring forth gifts of healing, my Redeemer wrought wonders and signs, driving away diseases and healing the infirm; but the Jews were maddened by the multitude of His wonders![^866]

*Troparion:*  
The carnal Jew, understanding the Scriptures according to the flesh, is stumbled by the Scripture, and falls against the Spirit of Truth; but we, having cast this aside, understand spiritual things![^867]

*Theotokion:*  
Thou didst contain in thy womb, O Virgin Mother, One of the Trinity, Christ the Giver of life, Whom all creation hymns, and before Whom the heavenly thrones do tremble: entreat Him, O all-blessed Lady, to save our souls!

*Another. Heirmos:*  
He hath showed strength with His arm, for He hath put down the mighty from their thrones and exalted the humble, the God of Israel, wherein the Dayspring from on high hath visited us, and hath guided us into the way of peace![^868]

*Troparion:*  
Behold, Christ the Life of all was seen, hanging of His own will upon the Tree; and beholding this, the earth trembled, and many bodies of the sleeping saints visibly arose, and the strongholds of hades were shaken![^869]

*Troparion:*  
Fair as a bridegroom from the chamber didst Thou come forth from the tomb, having overthrown the tyranny of death, O Christ, and shattered the bars of hades by divine power, and enlightened the world with the spiritual light of Thy Resurrection![^870]

*Troparion:*  
Let us all now form spiritual choirs, and let us cry: The Lord is risen! Let the earth rejoice, let heaven be glad, let the clouds drop down showers of righteousness for us who celebrate radiantly and hymn Christ![^871]

*Troparion:*  
The Lord, the Life of the living, the Fountain of good things, richly pouring forth the water of teachings, cries unto the woman: Give Me water to drink, that I may give thee water which dris up the fountains of thy sins![^872]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. Trinity Hymn:*  
One Light indivisible, Trinity in three suns, unoriginate Father, Son, and Spirit, one Godhead, Life and Creator of all: Him let us, the faithful, hymn with the bodiless powers, sacredly chanting with thrice-holy hymns!

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*  
Having become the dwelling-place of Light, O Pure One, illumine the eyes of my soul which are darkened by the many snares of the enemy, and make me worthy to behold clearly with a pure heart the Light that shone forth from thee beyond understanding!

*Exapostilarion of Pascha, once:*  
Having fallen asleep in the flesh as a mortal, O King and Lord, on the third day Thou didst rise again, raising Adam from corruption and abolishing death, O Pascha of incorruption, the salvation of the world![^873]

*Glory, of the Samaritan Woman, Tone 2, Podoben: "Give ear, ye women" (Жены̀):*  
Into Samaria didst Thou come, O my all-powerful Savior, and having conversed with the woman, didst ask water to drink, Who for the Hebrews didst gush forth waters from the flinty rock; whom Thou didst receive unto faith, and she now enjoys life in the heavens unto the ages![^874]

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of Mid-Pentecost, Tone 2, the same Podoben:*  
When the feast was at Mid-point, Thou didst come into the Sanctuary, O Lover of mankind, and didst say: Ye that are filled with thirst, come unto Me and draw living and nourishing water, whereof having food, grace, and immortal life, enjoy ye all![^875]

*At the Praises, we chant: Let every breath. We set 8 verses, and chant the following Resurrection stichera.*  
*Tone 8:*  
Thou Who didst endure the Cross and death, and didst rise from the dead, O all-powerful Lord, we glorify Thy Resurrection![^876]

By Thy Cross, O Christ, hast Thou freed us from the ancient curse, and by Thy death hast Thou abolished the devil who tormented our nature; therefore we cry unto Thee: O Lord Who art risen from the dead, glory to Thee!

By Thy Cross, O Christ Savior, guide us unto Thy truth, and deliver us from the snares of the enemy: O Thou Who art risen from the dead, raise us who are fallen by sin, stretching forth Thine hand, O Lord and Lover of mankind, through the intercessions of Thy saints!

Without departing from the Father's bosom, O only-begotten Word of God, Thou didst come to earth for love of mankind, becoming man without change; and Thou didst endure the Cross and death in the flesh, Who art passionless in Thy Godhead; and having risen from the dead, Thou hast granted immortality to the human race, as Thou alone art all-powerful!

*Other Eastern Stichera [Anatolian].*  
*The same Tone.*  
Death hast Thou accepted in the flesh, obtaining immortality for us, O Savior, and Thou didst dwell in the tomb that Thou mightest free us from hades, raising us together with Thyself, having suffered indeed as man, but risen as God; therefore we cry: Glory to Thee, O Life-giving Lord, Who alone lovest mankind![^877]

The rocks were rent, O Savior, when Thy Cross was fixed upon the place of the skull, and the gatekeepers of hades were terrified when Thou wast laid in the tomb as a corpse; for having abolished the power of death, Thou hast granted immortality unto all the dead by Thy Resurrection, O Savior: O Life-giving Lord, glory to Thee![^878]

*Other Idiomelon Stichera of the Samaritan Woman.*  
*Tone 3:*  
*Verse: Bend Thy bow, and proceed prosperously, and reign: for the sake of truth and meekness and righteousness.*  
Let heaven and earth rejoice radiantly today, for Christ hath appeared, being incarnate as man, that He might deliver Adam from the universal curse; and He is marveled at with wonders, having come into Samaria, and He conversed with the woman, asking for water, He Who cloths the clouds with waters! Therefore let us, all the faithful, worship Him Who for our sake became poor of His own will, by His compassionate counsel![^879]

*Tone 6:*  
*Verse: Thou hast loved righteousness and hated iniquity.*  
Thus saith the Lord unto the Samaritan woman: If thou knewest the gift of God, and Who it is that saith unto thee: Give Me water to drink, thou wouldest have asked of Him, and He would have given thee to drink, that thou thirst not unto the ages, saith the Lord![^880]

*Glory, the same Tone:*  
The Fountain of the origin of life, Jesus our Savior, having come to the well of the Patriarch Jacob, was asking for water to drink from the Samaritan woman; and when she answered Him concerning the irreconcilability of the Jews, the wise Creator led her with sweet words rather to ask for the ever-flowing water, which having received, she proclaimed unto all, saying: Come, see the Knower of secrets and God, Who came in the flesh to save mankind![^881]

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen.*  
Most blessed art thou...[^882]

*Great Doxology. And the dismissal.*  
*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen.*  
*Evangelical Sticheron [Eothinon], Tone 7:*  
Behold, it is darkness and early dawn; and why, O Mary, art thou standing at the tomb, having much darkness in thy mind, inquiring where Jesus was laid? But behold the disciples running together, how by the winding sheets and the napkin they discovered the Resurrection, and remembered the Scriptures concerning these things: with whom and through whom we also, having believed, hymn Thee, Christ the Giver of life![^883]

*And the instruction of Theodore the Studite, and the First Hour. And the final dismissal.*

*At the LITURGY, the Beatitudes of the Tone.*  
*Tone 8:*  
By a tree was Adam banished from paradise, but by the tree of the Cross did the thief dwell in paradise: for the one, having tasted, rejected the commandment of the Maker; but the other, being crucified together with Him, confessed the hidden God, crying aloud: Remember me in Thy Kingdom![^884]

Thou Who wast crucified and didst rise as the Mighty One from the tomb on the third day, and didst raise the first-fashioned Adam, O Thou Who alone art immortal: make me also worthy, O Lord, to turn in repentance with all my heart, and ever to seek Thee with fervent faith: Remember me, O Savior, in Thy Kingdom!

Christ is risen indeed, and the tomb testifies unto you, O ye transgressors of the law: for having left His graveclothes, He arose on the third day; the stone was sealed, and the guards were standing before the tomb; hades was despoiled, death was slain, Christ was not stolen: believe with us in His Resurrection![^885]

Him Who arose from the dead, and despoiled the dominion of hades, and was seen by the Myrrh-bearing women, saying: Rejoice! let us, the faithful, entreat to deliver our souls from corruption, ever crying unto Him with the voice of the wise thief: Remember us also in Thy Kingdom!

*And from the Canon of the Samaritan Woman, Ode 3; and of the Feast of Mid-Pentecost, Ode 6. After the Entrance, the Resurrection troparion; and of the Feast of Mid-Pentecost. Glory, the kontakion of the Samaritan Woman; Both now, of Mid-Pentecost.*

*Prokeimenon, Tone 3:*  
Sing praises to our God, sing praises; sing praises to our King, sing praises!  
*Verse: All ye nations clap your hands; shout unto God with the voice of rejoicing.*

*The Apostle in the Acts, Pericope 28 [Acts 11:19–26, 29–30]: The Apostles who were scattered abroad...*[^886]

*Alleluia, Tone 4:*  
Bend Thy bow, and proceed prosperously, and reign: for the sake of truth and meekness and righteousness.  
*Verse: Thou hast loved righteousness and hated iniquity.*

*Gospel from John, Pericope 12 [John 4:5–42]: Jesus comes to a city of Samaria...*

*Instead of "It is truly meet," we chant the Heirmos: Shine, shine, O new Jerusalem...*[^887]  
*Kinonikon [Communion Hymn]: Receive the Body of Christ... Another: Praise the Lord from the heavens...*

*The service of the saint of the Menaion is chanted at Compline.*  
*It should be known that the service of the Samaritan Woman is chanted for 4 days: on Sunday, on Thursday, on Friday, and on Saturday.*[^888]  
*On Monday therefore, and on Tuesday, the service of Mid-Pentecost is chanted, and on Wednesday is its Apodosis; we chant even as on the feast itself, except for the entrance and the readings.*

## ON THE SUNDAY OF THE SAMARITAN WOMAN, AT VESPERS

*At "Lord, I have cried," we set 6 verses, and chant 3 stichera of Mid-Pentecost.*

*Tone 4, Podoben: "Rejoice" (Ра́дꙋйсѧ):*  
That all-holy Mid-point of the Savior's Resurrection, radiant and beautiful today, shining like bright noonday upon the world with divine graces of Christ's Arising, shedding light upon the wonders of incorruption: it causes signs to flash forth, and shows the Ascension on high, and reveals the longed-for coming of the Spirit, the most radiant festival of the all-honorable Pentecost, and grants peace and great mercy unto our souls![^889]

As a river of divine glory, the feast being now at Mid-point, the Lord, bestowing streams of compassion upon all, cries: Let him that thirsts come unto Me, and drink fervently; for being Himself the Fountain of compassion and the abyss of mercy, He gushes forth remission unto the world, washes away transgressions, and cleanses diseases; He saves those who celebrate His Resurrection, shelters with love those who honor His Ascension in glory, and grants peace and great mercy unto our souls![^890]

Standing in the midst of the sanctuary, God uncircumscribed and Lord—for He was God by nature, even though for our sake He became man, and appeared circumscribed in body—He poured forth life-flowing words unto all, and said unto all: Cleanse your souls, and cool the burning heat of passions, lest ye men by any means be deprived of drink; for I bestow divine grace of the immortal, better, and heavenly Kingdom, to partake with Me, the Creator, and to be glorified![^891]

*And of the Menaion, 3.*

*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 8:*  
When the feast was at Mid-point, before Thy Passion and glorious Resurrection, O Lord, Thou wast teaching in the sanctuary, O God, the disobedient Jews, Pharisees, and Scribes, crying aloud unto them: Let him that thirsts come unto Me and drink; he that believs in Me, rivers of living water of the divine Spirit shall flow from his belly! O the praise of Thine ineffable wisdom! O our God Who fillest all things, glory to Thee![^892]

*At the Aposticha, stichera of the Octoechos:*  
*Tone 4:*  
Unceasingly worshiping Thy life-creating Cross, O Christ God, we glorify Thy third-day Resurrection; for thereby hast Thou renewed the corrupted nature of mankind, O Almighty One, and renewed for us the ascent into heaven, as Thou alone art good and the Lover of mankind![^893]

*Verse: Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes, O Thou that dwellest in heaven: behold, as the eyes of servants look unto the hands of their masters, and as the eyes of a maiden unto the hands of her mistress, even so our eyes look unto the Lord our God, until He have mercy on us.*  
I desired with tears, O Lord, to blot out the handwriting of my sins, and for the remainder of my life to be well-pleasing unto Thee through repentance; but the enemy deceivs me and wars against my soul: O Lord, before I perish utterly, save me![^894]

*Verse: Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us: for we are utterly filled with contempt; our soul is exceedingly filled with the reproach of the prosperous, and with the contempt of the proud.*  
*For the Martyrs:*  
Thou Who art glorified in the memorials of Thy saints, O Christ God, being entreated by them, send down upon us great mercy![^895]

*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 6:*  
As the feast of Thy Resurrection is at Mid-point, O Christ, and of the divine coming of Thy Holy Spirit, having come together we hymn the mysteries of Thy wonders: wherein do Thou send down great mercy upon us![^896]

*Troparion of the Feast of Mid-Pentecost: In the midst of the feast... And the dismissal.*

## ON MONDAY OF THE SAMARITAN WOMAN, AT MATINS

*At "God is the Lord," the Troparion of the Feast of Mid-Pentecost, thrice.*

*After the first Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4:*  
Looking upon the entrance of the tomb, and unable to endure the angelic flame, the Myrrh-bearing women were amazed with trembling, saying: Was He stolen Who opened paradise unto the thief? Or is He risen Who even before the Passion proclaimed His Arising? Truly Christ is risen, granting life and resurrection unto those in hades![^897]

*Verse: O Lord, rebuke me not in Thine anger, neither chasten me in Thy wrath.*  
Visit my humble soul, O Lord, which has spent all its life in sins; and even as the harlot, receive me, O Savior, and save me![^898]

*Verse: Marvelous is God in His saints, the God of Israel.*  
*For the Martyrs:*  
Today the angelic hosts have come unto the memorial of the Passion-bearers, to enlighten the minds of the faithful and to illumine the universe with grace: being entreated by them, O God, grant us great mercy![^899]

*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*  
An invincible wall art thou unto us Christians, O Virgin Theotokos; for fleeing unto thee, we remain uninjured, and sinning again, we have thee as an intercessor: therefore with thanksgiving we cry unto thee: Rejoice, thou that art full of grace, the Lord is with thee!

*After the second Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "The Wisdom and Word" (Премꙋ́дрость):*  
The Wisdom and Word of the Father, Who also gave to the Apostles the divine word to preach unto the ends of the earth His coming upon earth, was insulted with madness by the deceiving Hebrews; and the Preacher was dreadfully set at naught as a deceiver, Who guilelessly cried unto them: Judge not judgment against Me Who am unjudged, O ye lawless ones! Unto Him therefore let us cry aloud: O Christ God, Lover of mankind, send down remission of transgressions unto those who hymn Thy matchless glory with faith![^900]  
*Twice.*

*Then: Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ... Psalm 50. Then,*  
*The Canon of the Feast of Mid-Pentecost with the Heirmos to 8, and of the Menaion to 4.*  
*Kontakion and Exapostilarion of the Feast of Mid-Pentecost.*

*At the Praises, we set 4 verses, and chant the Resurrection sticheron.*  
*Tone 4:*  
Thou Who didst endure the Cross and death, and didst rise from the dead, O all-powerful Lord, we glorify Thy Resurrection!

I am a sheep of Thy rational flock, and unto Thee do I flee, O good Shepherd: seek me who have gone astray, O God, and have mercy on me![^901]

*For the Martyrs:*  
Who would not marvel, O holy Martyrs, beholding the good contest wherewith ye struggled: how, being in the body, ye conquered the bodiless foe, having confessed Christ and armed yourselves with the Cross? Therefore ye were worthily shown forth as expellers of demons and conquerors of barbarians: unceasingly pray ye that our souls may be saved![^902]

*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 8:*  
When the Feast of Pascha was at Mid-point, Thou didst enter into the temple sanctuary, O our Savior, and standing in the midst of the people, Thou didst teach them with boldness, and didst say: I am the Light of the world; he that follows Me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of immortal life![^903]

*At the Aposticha, stichera.*  
*Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме Е҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*  
Having bowed the heavens, Thou didst come down, O my Savior, and without change didst take flesh from the Virgin, pouring forth remission unto me![^904]

*Verse: But God is our King before the ages; He hath wrought salvation in the midst of the earth.*  
Wholly in God art Thou, O Word; wishing to deliver me who am perishing from transgressions, having united Thyself unto me, O Lover of mankind.[^905]

*Verse: Remember Thy congregation, which Thou hast purchased from the beginning.*  
Thou hast come, O King, O great Wisdom, whereby the Father in wisdom created the world with the Holy Spirit.[^906]

*Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 8:*  
Having cleansed the treasuries of our thoughts, and having brightened the spiritual lamps, let us also behold the Life, Christ, Who came into the sanctuary through an exceeding abundance of goodness, that He might conquer the enemy and save our race by the Passion of the Cross and the Resurrection; unto Whom let us cry aloud: O Incomprehensible Lord, glory to Thee![^907]

*On Monday of the Samaritan Woman, the Three-Ode Canon,*  
*whose acrostic is: Doxa to Theo hemon [Δόξα τῷ Θεῷ ἡμῶν], that is: Glory to our God.*[^908]

*Tone 4. Ode 1. Heirmos:*  
O Thou Who wast born of the Virgin, drown, I pray Thee, the three parts of my soul in the depth of dispassion, even as the mighty captains; that unto Thee, as upon a timbrel, in the mortification of the body, I may chant a song of victory![^909]

*Troparion [Acrostic letter D]:*  
Having bound the destroyer's hostile power with bonds, which Thou didst endure for our sake, O Lover of mankind: by Thy Cross hast Thou made peace, O Lord, among those who were scattered, and destroyed the enmity of the middle wall; therefore we hymn Thee![^910]

*Troparion [Acrostic letter O]:*  
The Lord, even as He foretold before the Passion, arose with power, having as God plundered the realms of hades, and raised up all that slept there from the ages: unto Him that magnify Him![^911]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.*  
*Troparion [Acrostic letter X]:*  
Marveling at the vision and the appearance, the choir of the Myrrh-bearing women learned from the divine minister: Behold, Christ is risen! Go, proclaim unto the disciples who mourn and weep![^912]

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion [Acrostic letter A]:*  
Thou didst shine forth, O Pure One, as a bridegroom marvelously fair from the dead, He Who was incarnate from thy womb through goodness beyond understanding; therefore, having beheld Him with the Apostles, thou didst glorify His third-day Resurrection![^913]

*Tone 4. Ode 8. Heirmos:*  
O All-powerful Redeemer of all, having descended into the midst of the flame, Thou didst dew the pious youths, and didst teach them to sing: All ye works, bless and praise the Lord![^914]

*Troparion [Acrostic letter T]:*  
Having stretched forth Thy most pure palms upon the Cross of Thine own will, O Long-suffering One, Thou didst embrace all, and delivering them from the hand of the stranger; therefore with fear do we glorify Thee![^915]

*Troparion [Acrostic letter O]:*  
When Thou wast laid of Thine own will in the tomb, those who slept of old in the tombs arose together by Thy rising from the dead, crying with fear: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^916]

*Troparion [Acrostic letter Th]:*  
Beholding Thee working marvelous and most glorious deeds, O Christ, and enlightening the blind by Thy word, the assembly of the Hebrews condemns unto death the very Life of all, O compassionate Lord![^917]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.*  
*Troparion [Acrostic letter E]:*  
After forty days, O Christ, taking up Thine abode as it were with the wise and honorable Apostles, Thou didst entrust unto them the Divine dispensation, whereby Thou hast saved the world which hymns Thee.[^918]

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion [Acrostic letter O]:*  
How marvelous is Thy childbearing, O Undefiled One, whereby we all have been delivered from the fearful fall, crying aloud: Rejoice, the restoration of the fallen world![^919]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*  
Eve indeed, through the disease of disobedience, brought in the curse; but thou, O Virgin Theotokos, through the shoot of thy childbearing, didst make blessing to blossom forth unto the world; therefore do we all magnify thee![^920]

*Troparion [Acrostic letter I]:*  
Thou wast stretched out of Thine own will upon the Cross, and the sun beholding Thee, O Most Good One, hid its rays in fear, and the foundations of the earth were shaken, and the rocks were rent, O Master, and the veil of the temple was torn in twain![^921]

*Troparion [Acrostic letter M]:*  
Having anointed Thee of old, and wrapped Thee in a winding sheet, Joseph laid Thee in a new tomb; but Thou, the Life of all, didst arise on the third day, having despoiled the kingdoms of hades by Divine power, O Almighty One![^922]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.*  
*Troparion [Acrostic letter O]:*  
Thou wast seen by the Apostles, having arisen from the tomb on the third day, and Thou didst cry aloud: Go forth, My friends and disciples, proclaim among all nations the miracles that ye have seen and know, and My power which is beyond all utterance![^923]

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion [Acrostic letter N]:*  
Beholding Him Who breaths life into the dead arisen in glory from the tomb, the All-immaculate One was filled with joy, crying aloud: O My Son and My God, I magnify Thine ineffable condescension![^924]

## ON MONDAY OF THE SAMARITAN WOMAN, AT VESPERS

*At "Lord, I have cried," stichera prosomoia of Mid-Pentecost.*

*Tone 1, Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly ranks" (Нбⷭ҇ныхъ чино́въ):*  
The Root of all and Giver of life, the Word co-eternal with the Divine Father, taking flesh of His own will from the Virgin and becoming man, as One Who is good, poured forth streams of ineffable wisdom unto all as teaching.[^925]

When the Jewish feast was half over, O Christ, Thou didst stand in the sanctuary, the Master of the Law, teaching with authority and convicting the scribes, even as it is written, and astonishing them by the wisdom of Thy words and the display of miracles.[^926]

The Giver of wisdom and Dispenser of good things, pouring forth Divine streams from the ever-flowing fountain, cries aloud: Come unto Me, ye that thirst, draw water of life; and rivers of Divine gifts, saith He, shall flow out of your belly.[^927]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 2:*  
When Thou didst come into the sanctuary, O Christ God, at Mid-feast, then didst Thou teach the people, crying aloud: He that believs on Me, though he die, yet shall he live! But the Jews flared with rage, together with the Pharisees, Sadducees, and scribes, saying: Who is this that speaks blasphemy? Not considering that Thou art our God, Who art before all ages, glorified with the Father and the Spirit: glory to Thee![^928]

*At the Aposticha, stichera of the Octoechos.*  
*Tone 4:*  
The sentence of the tree of disobedience hast Thou loosed, O Savior, being nailed of Thine own will unto the Tree of the Cross; and having descended into hades, O Mighty One, Thou didst tear asunder the bonds of death as God: therefore do we worship Thy Resurrection from the dead, crying aloud with joy: O Almighty Lord, glory to Thee![^929]

*Verse: Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes, O Thou that dwellest in heaven: behold, as the eyes of servants look unto the hands of their masters, and as the eyes of a maiden unto the hands of her mistress, even so our eyes look unto the Lord our God, until He have mercy on us.*[^930]  
Who that is tempest-tossed and flees unto this harbor is not saved? Or who that is diseased and falls down before this clinic is not healed? O Creator of all and Physician of the ailing, O Lord, before I perish utterly, save me![^931]

*Verse: Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us; for we are utterly filled with contempt: our soul is exceedingly filled with the reproach of the prosperous, and with the contempt of the proud.*[^932]  
*For the Martyrs:*  
O Lover of mankind, Who didst accept the endurance of the holy Martyrs, accept also the hymnody from us, and through their prayers grant us great mercy![^933]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 3. By Germanus:*  
When the feast was half over, we glorify Him Who wrought salvation in the midst of the earth: for in the midst between two thieves, Life was suspended upon the Tree; and unto him that blasphemed indeed He was silent, but unto him that believed Thou didst cry aloud: Today shalt thou be with Me in Paradise! Thou didst descend into the tomb, Thou didst despoil hades, and didst arise on the third day, saving our souls.[^934]

## ON TUESDAY OF THE SAMARITAN WOMAN, AT MATINS

*Troparion of Mid-Pentecost, thrice.*[^935]

*After the First Stichology, Sessional Hymn.*  
*Tone 4, Podoben: "Joseph was amazed" (Оу҆диви́сѧ Їѡ́сифъ):*  
By Thine own voluntary will Thou didst endure the Cross, O Savior, and mortal men laid Thee in a new tomb, Thee Who by Thy word didst establish the ends of the earth; therefore the stranger was bound, death was fiercely despoiled, and all those in hades cried aloud unto Thy life-bearing Rising: Christ is risen, the Giver of life, Who abides unto the ages![^936]

*Verse: O Lord, rebuke me not in Thine anger, neither chasten me in Thy wrath.*[^937]  
Consider, O my soul, how we shall stand before the Judge! The dread thrones shall be set, and the deeds of each one shall be exposed, then the inexorable Judge; there fire shall fiercely confront thee, holding fast as a raging sea and covering the ends of the earth: with all these things in mind, O my soul, groan before the end![^938]

*Verse: Marvelous is God in His saints, the God of Israel.*[^939]  
*For the Martyrs:*  
Adorned with the blood of Thy Martyrs throughout the whole world as with purple and fine linen, Thy Church cries out unto Thee through them, O Christ God: Send down Thy compassions upon Thy people, grant peace unto Thy commonwealth, and unto our souls great mercy![^940]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*  
A dread mystery and a most glorious wonder, how the Virgin bore Thee, the Creator of all, and after childbirth again remained whole and Virgin! O Thou Who wast born of her, confirm the Faith, subdue the nations, and pacify the world, as Lover of mankind.[^941]

*After the Second Stichology, Sessional Hymn.*  
*Tone 8, Podoben: "The Wisdom and Word of God" (Премꙋ́дрости сло́ва):*  
Pouring forth the water of wisdom and life unto the world, Thou callest all men, O Savior, to draw the waters of salvation: for receiving Thy Divine Law, man quenches the coals of deceit within himself; therefore he shall never thirst unto the ages, nor cease from Thy satisfaction, O Master, transcendent King: therefore do we glorify Thy dominion, O Christ God, entreating Thee to send down richly unto Thy servants the remission of transgressions.  
*Twice.*[^942]

*Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ... Psalm 50.*[^943]

*Canon of the Feast of Mid-Pentecost with the Heirmos to 8; and of the Menaion to 4.*[^944]

*Kontakion, and Ikos, and Exapostilarion of the Feast of Mid-Pentecost.*[^945]

*At the Praises, we set 4 verses, and we sing stichera of the Octoechos.*  
*Tone 4:*  
By Thy Cross, O Christ, Thou hast delivered us from the ancient curse, and by Thy death Thou hast abolished the devil that tyrannized over our nature, and by Thy Rising Thou hast filled all things with joy; therefore we cry aloud unto Thee: O Lord risen from the dead, glory to Thee!  
*Twice.*[^946]

Wash me with my tears, O Savior, for I am defiled with many sins; therefore do I fall down before Thee, O Merciful One: I have sinned, have mercy on me, O God![^947]

*For the Martyrs:*  
Ye became companions of the Angels, O holy Martyrs, having manly proclaimed Christ in the contest: for having forsaken all the fair things in the world as non-existent, ye held fast to the Faith as a steadfast anchor; therefore, driving away deceit, ye pour forth gifts of healing unto the faithful, praying unceasingly that our souls may be saved.[^948]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 4:*  
O Lord, before Thy precious Cross, when the feast was half over, Thou didst enter into the sanctuary, teaching the Jews with boldness concerning the ordinances enacted through Moses and Thyself in the Law; and marveling at the ineffable mystery of Thy wisdom, O Christ, they stirred up murmuring against Thee among themselves out of envy, saying: How knows this Man letters, having never learned? Not knowing Thee, the Savior of our souls.[^949]

*At the Aposticha, stichera prosomoia of Mid-Pentecost.*  
*Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме Е҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*  
Being the End and the Beginning, and the Mid-point, Thou didst stand in the midst of the feast in the sanctuary, O my Christ, pouring forth remission unto me.[^950]

*Verse: Remember Thy congregation, which Thou hast purchased from the beginning.*[^951]  
Sion heard and was glad at the Divine dominion of Thy Resurrection, O Word, and rejoices with her children, chanting praises unto Thee, the Compassionate One.[^952]

*Verse: But God is our King before the ages; He hath wrought salvation in the midst of the earth.*[^953]  
O Word, Light having shone forth from the Father, but in these last times Thou hast appeared as man: grant unto me the remission of transgressions![^954]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 8:*  
When the feast of Pascha was half over, Thou didst enter into the sanctuary of the temple, O our Savior; and standing in the midst of the people, Thou didst teach them with boldness and say: I am the Light of the world; he that follows Me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of immortal life.[^955]

*On Tuesday of the Samaritan Woman, the Three-Ode Canon,*  
*whose acrostic is: Hymnodia Joseph [ΥΜΝΩΔΙΑ ΙΩΣΗΦ], that is: The Hymnody of Joseph.*[^956]

*Tone 4. Ode 2. Heirmos:*  
See, see, that I am God, Who put to death and make alive, Who gave water from the uncut rock, and rained down manna for food unto the people of Israel, for I am mighty![^957]

*Troparion [Acrostic letter Y]:*  
Moses lifted up the serpent, prefiguring Thy Crucifixion, O only God and King of all, Christ, Who wast crucified for our sake, and delivering men from venomous enmity and from hades, and crushing the all-destructive head![^958]

*Troparion [Acrostic letter M]:*  
Bearing myrrh with tears, the Myrrh-bearing women ran with haste unto the Divine tomb very early in the morning, even as the God-proclaimer said; and beholding a young man shining in countenance and raiment, they were terrified with fear.[^959]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.*  
*Troparion [Acrostic letter N]:*  
Them that were diseased Thou didst heal by Thy word, the paralytics didst Thou set upright, and the dead didst Thou raise, O Word; yet the Hebrew people condemned Thee to die: but Thou didst arise as God mighty in strength, destroying the realm of hades.[^960]

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion [Acrostic letter O]:*  
He Who is transcendent God appeared, being incarnate ineffably from thy blood, O All-honorable One; and being reckoned among the dead, He Who is the Life of all arose with sovereign might: beholding Whom, thou wast filled with joy, magnifying Him.[^961]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*  
In fiery flame the Cherubim and Seraphim stand before Thee, O Lord, and all creation chants a beauteous hymn unto Thee: Sing, bless, and highly exalt Christ, the only Creator, unto all ages, ye people![^962]

*Troparion [Acrostic letter D]:*  
Having torn asunder the handwriting of Adam by the Cross, O Lord, Thou hast now poured forth blessing unto us, becoming a curse of Thine own will, O Christ; therefore we bless Thee continually unto the ages.[^963]

*Troparion [Acrostic letter I]:*  
The assembly of holy disciples, O Lord, beheld Thee risen from the dead, and was filled with mystical consolation, unto whom Thou didst cry aloud: Knowing Me to be God the Giver of life, go forth, saith He, proclaim Me the King of all![^964]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.*  
*Troparion [Acrostic letter A]:*  
We hymn Thy precious Crucifixion, O compassionate Jesus, we glorify Thy Burial, and Thy dread Resurrection with faith, whereby we have been loosed from the insolvable bonds of hades, O Christ, God of all![^965]

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion [Acrostic letter I]:*  
Beholding Jesus, Whom thou didst bear incarnate beyond utterance, O Pure Lady, arisen from the dead, thou didst cry aloud: How fair is Thy beauty, O My Son, for the sake of which Adam hath now ascended unto his ancient beauty![^966]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*  
For He that is mighty hath magnified me, and holy is His name, and His mercy is on them that fear Him from generation to generation.[^967]

*Troparion [Acrostic letter O]:*  
When Thou wast lifted up upon the Tree, being nailed upon the Cross, the luminaries hid their light, and the earth was shaken, and they that were in the bonds of hades were set free, O Savior![^968]

*Troparion [Acrostic letter S]:*  
Having crushed the gates of death, O Christ, and its bonds, Thou didst arise with glory and sovereign power, snatching away the prisoners which it held before, who hymn Thee as God.[^969]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.*  
*Troparion [Acrostic letter E]:*  
The earth triumphs and heaven keeps festival at the Rising of the Creator of all, whereby He hath saved us who hymn Him from bonds and corruption.[^970]

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion [Acrostic letter Ph]:*  
By the rays of thy light, O Theotokos, dispel the gloom of my ignorance, that with voices of faith I may unceasingly hymn thy wonders![^971]

## ON TUESDAY OF THE FIFTH WEEK AFTER PASCHA, AT VESPERS
*Apodosis of the Feast of Mid-Pentecost.*

*We set 6 verses, and we sing 3 stichera of Mid-Pentecost, repeating them:*[^972]

*Tone 4, Podoben: "O Lord, having ascended the Cross" (Гдⷭ҇и возше́дъ на крⷭ҇тъ):*  
The mid-point of the days hath arrived, beginning from the saving Rising, and sealed by the Divine Pentecost; and it shines, possessing splendor from both sides, uniting both, and prefiguring the glory to come: it honors the Master's Ascension beforehand.[^973]

Sion heard and was glad when Christ's Resurrection was proclaimed as good tidings, and His faithful children rejoiced, beholding Him washing away the defilement of Christ-murder by the Spirit: the joyful mid-point of both feasts in preparation.[^974]

The bountiful outpouring of the Divine Spirit upon all draws nigh, even as it is written: the mid-point foretells beforehand the dispensation after Christ's Death and Burial and Resurrection, which was given by Him unto the disciples, showing forth the manifestation of the Comforter according to the unfailing promise.[^975]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 6:*  
At the mid-point of the feast of Thy Resurrection, O Christ, and of the Divine coming of Thy Holy Spirit, having assembled, we hymn the mysteries of Thy wonders, on which feast send down upon us great mercy![^976]

*At the Aposticha, idiomela, Tone 1. By the Monk John:*[^977]  
The mid-point of the days of Pentecost hath arrived, wherein Christ, revealing in part His Divine power, strengthened the paralytic by a word, raising him from his bed; and performing miracles in God-befitting manner in the body He had fashioned, He bestowed upon men eternal life and great mercy.[^978]

*Verse: Remember Thy congregation, which Thou hast purchased from the beginning.*[^979]  
Thou didst come into the sanctuary, O Wisdom of God, when the feast was half over, teaching and convicting the disobedient Jews, Pharisees, and scribes, and crying aloud with boldness unto them: Let him that thirsts come unto Me and drink living water, and he shall never thirst unto the ages; he that believs in My goodness, out of his belly shall flow rivers of eternal life! O Thy goodness and Thy compassion, O Christ our God, glory to Thee![^980]

*Verse: But God is our King before the ages; He hath wrought salvation in the midst of the earth.*[^981]  
*Tone 2:*  
When the mid-point of the feast arrived, Jesus went up into the sanctuary and taught the disobedient Jews, saying: Let him that thirsts come unto Me and drink living and eternal water, and he shall never thirst unto the age; he that believs on Me, rivers shall flow out of his belly, and he shall have the light of life![^982]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 8:*  
When the feast was half over, as Thou wast teaching, O Savior, the Jews said: How knows this Man letters, having never learned? Not understanding that Thou art the Wisdom that fashioned the world: glory to Thee![^983]

*Then, the dismissal troparion: "When the feast was half over..." The same also at "God is the Lord."*[^984]

## ON WEDNESDAY OF THE SAMARITAN WOMAN, AT MATINS

*After the First and after the Second Stichology, Sessional Hymns of the Feast.*[^985]

*Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ... Psalm 50.*[^986]

*And the Canons: of Tone 4, with the Heirmos to 8; and of Tone 8, to 6.*[^987]

*Kontakion, and Ikos, and Exapostilarion of the Feast.*[^988]

*At the Praises, "Let every breath...": We set 4 verses.*  
*Tone 4, Podoben: "As one valiant among martyrs" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*  
The Wisdom and Power, the Radiance of the Father, the Co-eternal Word and Son of God came into the sanctuary in the flesh, teaching the Jewish people, who were hard-hearted and ungrateful; and they marveled at the richness of His wisdom, crying aloud: Whence knows this Man letters, having never learned from anyone?  
*Twice.*[^989]

Stopping the mouths of the scribes, the Messiah and Lord convicted the Jews, crying aloud unto them: Judge not according to appearance as unrighteous transgressors of the Law! For on the Sabbath I raised the paralytic; therefore I am the Lord of the Sabbath and of the Law: why seek ye to kill Me, Who have raised the dead?[^990]

With stones did the fierce and lawless ones stone Naboth, even the ungrateful Jewish assembly; and Isaiah they sawed asunder with a wooden saw, and into the mire they cast the wise Jeremiah; and having lifted up the Lord upon the Cross, they cried aloud: O Thou that destroyest the temple, save Thyself, and we will believe![^991]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 4. By Anatolius:*  
Having been enlightened, brethren, by the Resurrection of Christ the Savior, and having attained the mid-point of the Master's feast, let us sincerely keep the commandments of God, that we may be accounted worthy to celebrate the Ascension, and to obtain the coming of the Holy Spirit.[^992]

*Great Doxology. And the dismissal.*  
*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of both Canons, Ode 9. Prokeimenon and Alleluia of the Feast. Epistle and Gospel of the day. Communion Verse: "He that eats My Flesh, and drinks My Blood, dwells in Me..." And the feast has its Apodosis. The service of the Menaion is chanted at Compline.*[^993]

## ON WEDNESDAY OF THE SAMARITAN WOMAN, AT VESPERS

*At "Lord, I have cried," we set 6 verses, and we sing stichera of the Samaritan Woman:*[^994]

*Tone 4, Podoben: "Being called from on high" (Зва́нный свы́ше):*  
Finding the Samaritan woman at the well, Christ asked of her water to drink, thirsting for her correction and salvation, which is understood as fulfilled by deeds; for as she was drawing a drink, He Himself drew her away from that drink and filled her with the living drink, as she proclaimed unto her fellow citizens: Behold, Christ the Messiah, Who of old was spoken of in the Law, hath appeared as man, revealing the ineffable secrets of our thoughts![^995]

Behold, Christ the Messiah hath appeared on earth! the Samaritan woman saith unto those in the city: The great Prophet written of old in the Law to come, God and man, Who told me the things that I have done, and all things hidden in the depth of my heart He declared unto me, even as I committed them! Therefore the city, having flocked together, sees that her words are true in every way, and is astonished at the matter, and strengthened by the sight.[^996]

The daughter of the ancestral mother, who of old at the sixth hour beheld Thee, God the Master, walking in Paradise, again beheld Thee at the sixth hour sitting where there was a spring of water and a dug well, asking of her to drink, that Thou mightest give her to drink of the water of incorruptible life, which indeed came to pass: for having drunk abundantly of Thy life-bearing water, she also proclaimed in the city what manner of wealth was Thine![^997]

*And of the Menaion, 3.*[^998]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 1:*  
Thou didst come unto the fountain, O Fountain of wonders, at the sixth hour, to ensnare the fruit of Eve: for at that hour did Eve go forth from Paradise through the serpent's deceit; the Samaritan woman drew near to draw water, whom the Savior beholding, said: Give Me water to drink, and I will fill thee with running water; and running chaste into the city, she straightway proclaimed unto the multitudes: Come, see Christ the Lord, the Savior of our souls![^999]

*At the Aposticha, stichera of the Octoechos, Tone 4:*  
The gates of hades hast Thou crushed, O Lord, and by Thy death Thou hast destroyed the kingdom of death, and delivered the human race from corruption, granting life and incorruption unto the world, and great mercy.[^1000]

*Verse: Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes, O Thou that dwellest in heaven: behold, as the eyes of servants look unto the hands of their masters, and as the eyes of a maiden unto the hands of her mistress, even so our eyes look unto the Lord our God, until He have mercy on us.*[^1001]  
The choir of the Apostles hast Thou enlightened by the Holy Spirit, O Christ; and through them wash away our defilement of sin, O God, and have mercy on us![^1002]

*Verse: Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us; for we are utterly filled with contempt: our soul is exceedingly filled with the reproach of the prosperous, and with the contempt of the proud.*[^1003]  
*For the Martyrs:*  
Having boldness before the Savior, O holy ones, pray unceasingly for us sinners, asking remission of transgressions and great mercy for our souls![^1004]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 2:*  
When the Lord came unto the well, the Samaritan woman besought the Compassionate One: Give me the water of faith, and I shall receive the gladness and deliverance of the waters of the font: O Lord and Giver of life, glory to Thee![^1005]

*Troparion: "When the disciples of the Lord learned from the Angel the joyful message of the Resurrection..."*[^1006]

## ON THURSDAY OF THE SAMARITAN WOMAN, AT MATINS

*At "God is the Lord," Resurrection Troparion.*[^1007]

*After the First Stichology, Sessional Hymn.*  
*Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou Who wast lifted up upon the Cross" (Вознесы́йсѧ на крⷭ҇тъ):*  
Having been crucified of Thine own will for our sake, and reckoned among the dead, O Giver of life, and having arisen on the third day, O Christ our God, Thou hast crushed the dominion of death by Thy power, quickening all those in hades by Thy Rising; therefore, singing praises, we all honor Thy Rising, O immortal Lord.[^1008]

*Verse: Their sound is gone out into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world.*[^1009]  
*Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*  
Thou hast shown forth Thy disciples as luminaries in the ends of the earth, O Savior, shining Thy knowledge upon souls that were in darkness, O Master; and having eclipsed idol deceit through them, Thou didst enlighten the world with the teachings of piety: through their prayers save our souls![^1010]

*Verse: Marvelous is God in His saints, the God of Israel.*[^1011]  
*For the Martyrs:*  
Armed with the Cross, Thy passion-bearers overcame the wiles of the evil-originating enemy, O Christ our God: they shone forth as luminaries, guiding men, and grant healings unto them that ask with faith: through their prayers save our souls![^1012]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion:*  
As thou art all-immaculate, having borne the all-good God, with the Apostles entreat Him unceasingly, that He grant remission of transgressions and amendment of life before the end unto us who with faith and love hymn thee as is meet, O only All-lauded One.[^1013]

*After the Second Stichology, Sessional Hymn.*  
*Tone 7, Podoben: "Hope of the world" (Оу҆пова́нїе мі́рꙋ):*  
As unto the faithful Samaritan woman, O Lord, Thou didst open the fountain of Thy Godhead, and didst pour out the knowledge of God upon her, giving her to drink of the God-pleasing drink: even so now send down upon us all the cleansing of transgressions, O All-Good One.[^1014]  
*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. The same.*[^1015]

*Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ... Psalm 50.*[^1016]

*Canon of the Samaritan Woman with the Heirmoi to 8; and of the Menaion to 4.*[^1017]

*Kontakion and Ikos of the Samaritan Woman, and Exapostilarion of the Samaritan Woman.*[^1018]

*At the Praises, we set 4 verses, and we sing stichera of the Octoechos.*  
*Tone 4:*  
Without separating from Thy Father's bosom, O only-begotten Word of God, Thou didst come upon the earth for love of mankind, becoming man without change, and Thou didst endure the Cross and death in the flesh, Thou Who art impassible in Godhead; and having arisen from the dead, Thou hast granted immortality unto the human race, as the only Almighty One.  
*Twice.*[^1019]

Thy Holy Spirit showed forth the unlettered disciples as teachers, O Christ God, and by the eloquent accord of tongues abolished deceit, as Almighty.[^1020]

*For the Martyrs:*  
How should we not marvel at your struggles, O holy Martyrs? For encompassed with mortal body, ye conquered the bodiless enemies: the torturers' threats terrified you not, nor did the assaults of torments dismay you; truly worthily were ye glorified by Christ: pray unceasingly that our souls may be saved![^1021]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 2:*  
The co-unoriginate and co-eternal Son and Word of the Father came unto the fountain, the Fountain of healings, and a woman of Samaria came to draw water, whom the Savior seeing, said: Give Me water to drink, and go, call thy husband. But she, speaking as unto a man and not unto God, seeking to hide herself, said: I have no husband. And the Teacher said unto her: Truly hast thou said: I have no husband; for thou hast had five, and now he whom thou hast is not thy husband. And she, marveling at the word, ran into the city and cried unto the peoples, saying: Come, see Christ, Who grants great mercy unto the world![^1022]

*At the Aposticha, stichera of the Samaritan Woman.*  
*Tone 4, Podoben: "As one valiant among martyrs" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*  
Being the Fountain of goodness and the Abyss, and Guardian of life, O only Compassionate One, how didst Thou utter discourse unto the Samaritan woman: Give Me water to drink, that thou mayest receive remission; we hymn Thy manifold compassion, whereby Thou savest the whole human race, for Thy great goodness.[^1023]

*Verse: Bend Thy bow, and proceed prosperously, and reign, for the sake of truth, and meekness, and righteousness.*[^1024]  
Come, see a Man Who told me today, sitting at the fountain, what things I have done: for He is a most true and most great Prophet, knowing all things hidden and revealed. But grant living water, which Thou givest unto them that thirst, that I may thirst no more for ever, O Lover of mankind![^1025]

*Verse: Thou hast loved righteousness, and hated iniquity.*[^1026]  
The ever-flowing Fountain, immortal Life, the inexhaustible and incorruptible Stream, having journeyed, sat near the well, having sent His disciples for food, and conversed with the woman drawing water, desiring to ensnare her, and to enlighten the eyes of her soul.[^1027]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Tone 3:*  
Let heaven and earth rejoice brightly today, for Christ hath appeared, being incarnate as man, that He might deliver Adam from the ancestral curse, and He is marveled at for wonders, having come into Samaria; and He stood before the woman asking water, He Who clothes the clouds with waters. Therefore let all of us the faithful worship Him Who for our sake voluntarily became poor by compassionate counsel.[^1028]

*On Thursday of the Samaritan Woman, the Three-Ode Canon,*  
*whose acrostic is: Ode Theo prepei [ᾨΔΗ ΘΕΩ ΠΡΕΠΕΙ], that is: A song befits God.*[^1029]

*Tone 4. Ode 4. Heirmos:*  
For the sake of the love of Thine image, O Compassionate One, Thou didst stand upon Thy Cross, and the nations melted away: for Thou, O Lover of mankind, art my strength and my praise.[^1030]

*Troparion [Acrostic letter O]:*  
When Thou wast lifted up of Thine own will upon the Tree, both the earth and the mountains and hills shook with trembling, beholding Thee suffering, O Compassionate and Long-suffering One.[^1031]

*Troparion [Acrostic letter D]:*  
Fearing Thy descent, O Savior, hades speedily gave up the dead which it held, who hymn Thy ineffable power.[^1032]

*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.*  
*Troparion [Acrostic letter I]:*  
The senseless Jewish assembly, beholding Thee, O Compassionate One, giving eyes unto the blind, put to death Him Who is Life and Resurrection.[^1033]

*Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion [Acrostic letter Th]:*  
Beholding Thy Son arisen from the tomb, O Virgin, with the Apostles thou didst rejoice in Him, O Pure One: with them do we glorify thee.[^1034]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*  
All ye works of God, and all creation, bless the Lord: for unto men from the earth hath light shone forth, and hath enlightened the whole universe, and granted eternal life unto the world; hymn, ye people, and exalt Him above all for ever![^1035]

*Troparion [Acrostic letter E]:*  
Beholding Thee upon the Cross, the wise thief cried aloud: Remember me, O Master! marveling at Thy power and at Thy dread dispensation which surpasses understanding.[^1036]

*Troparion [Acrostic letter O]:*
