of the feast. Instead of the Trisagion, we sing: "As many of you as have been baptized into Christ."[^2957] Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, and Gospel, first of the feast, then of Lazarus. Instead of "It is truly meet," we sing the Heirmos of the feast. Communion Hymn, first of the feast, then of Saint Lazarus.

## CONCERNING THE SAME FEAST, IF IT FALL ON THE SUNDAY OF PALMS[^2958]

On Saturday at Small Vespers, Stichera of Palms on 4; Glory... Both now: of the feast: "In the sixth month." At the Aposticha: Idiomela of the feast from Great Vespers with their verses; Glory... Both now: of Palms: "I hymn Thy terrible dispensation:" Troparion of the feast; Glory... Both now: "Giving assurance of the general resurrection:" Little Litany, and dismissal.

At Great Vespers, "Blessed is the man:" the entire Kathisma. At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the feast 6, repeating them; and of Palms on 4; Glory: of Palms: "Today the grace of the Holy Spirit:" Both now: of the feast: "The Archangel Gabriel was sent." Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day; and 5 readings of the feast, and 3 of Palms. At the Litiya, Stichera of the feast 6, and of Palms 3; Glory: of Palms: "Six days before the Passover:" Both now: of the feast: "Gabriel announcs good tidings." At the Aposticha, Idiomela Stichera of Palms, Tone 8, with their verses; Glory: of Palms: "Today the grace:" Both now: of the feast: "The mystery which was hidden from eternity." At the blessing of the loaves, Troparion of the feast twice, and of Palms once; and reading of the feast.

At Matins, at "God is the Lord," Troparion of the feast twice; Glory... Both now: "Giving assurance of the general resurrection." After the 1st Kathisma: Sessional Hymn of Palms; Glory... Both now: of the feast, and reading. After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn of Palms; Glory... Both now: of the feast, and reading. Then Polyeleos of the feast, and Sessional Hymn, and reading of the feast. Anabathmoi, the 1st Antiphon of Tone 4. Prokeimenon of Palms. "Let every breath." Gospel of Palms, Psalm 50. But "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ" we do not say. And when the brethren kiss the holy Gospel, the superior distributes the palms with candles unto the brethren, according to custom. Instead of "Through the prayers:" we sing Glory: "Today Christ enters the city:" Both now: the same. Then, "Have mercy on me, O God:" We sing the Sticheron, Tone 6: "Today the grace of the Holy Spirit." Canon of the feast with the heirmos on 8, and of Palms with the heirmos on 8. Katavasia: of both canons, each choir its own Heirmos. After Ode 3, Kontakion of Palms, and Ikos, and Sessional Hymn; Glory... Both now: of the feast, and reading of the feast. After Ode 6, Kontakion of the feast and Ikos. At Ode 9, we do not sing "More honorable," but we sing the refrain of the feast, as was prescribed before. And of Palms we sing according to custom the refrain: "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee." At the Katavasia, first we sing the refrain of the feast and Heirmos of the feast: "As unto an animated ark of God:" then of Palms. "Holy is the Lord our God" in Tone 1. Exapostilarion of the feast twice. At the Praises, Stichera of the feast 3, and of Palms 3; Glory: of the feast: "Let the heavens be glad;" Both now: of Palms: "Six days before the Passover." Great Doxology. Troparion: "Giving assurance of the general resurrection;" Glory... Both now: of the feast; litanies, and dismissal, and catechesis; and the First Hour in the narthex, and dismissal.

At the 20th hour of the day [2:00 PM], we go forth with a Litiya outside the monastery, as was indicated in the order; and having returned, we sing the Hours. At the Hours, Troparion of the feast; Glory: "Giving assurance of the general resurrection;" Both now: Theotokion of the Hours. After the "Our Father," we alternate the Kontakia. At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the feast, Ode 3 on 4; and of Palms, Ode 6 on 4. After the Entrance, we say the verse: "Blessed is He that comes in the name of the Lord; God is the Lord, and hath appeared unto us." Troparion of the feast, and of Palms: "Giving assurance of the general resurrection;" Glory: Kontakion of Palms: "Borne upon a throne in heaven;" Both now: of the feast: "To thee, the Champion Leader." Then Prokeimenon of Palms and of the feast; Epistle of the feast and of Palms; Alleluia, Gospel, and Communion Hymn of the feast and of Palms.

At the Liturgy, instead of "It is truly meet," the Heirmos of Palms: "God is the Lord, and hath appeared unto us." But if it be a temple of the Annunciation of the Theotokos: we sing instead of "It is truly meet," the Heirmos: "As unto an animated ark of God."

## IF THE ANNUNCIATION OF THE MOST HOLY THEOTOKOS FALL ON GREAT MONDAY[^2959]

On Palm Sunday at Small Vespers, at "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the feast on 4; Glory... Both now: of the feast. At the Aposticha, Stichera of the feast from Great Vespers; Glory... Both now: of the feast, and Troparion of the feast. At Great Vespers, we sing "Blessed is the man:" the 1st Antiphon. At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the feast on 6, and of Palms on 4; Glory: of Palms, Tone 6: "He that sits upon the cherubic throne:" Both now: of the feast: "The Archangel Gabriel was sent." Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day; 3 readings of the feast. At the Litiya, Stichera of the feast; Glory... Both now: of the feast: "Gabriel announcs good tidings." At the Aposticha, Idiomela Stichera of the day with their verses; Glory: of Palms: "With branches and palms:" Both now: of the feast: "The mystery which was hidden from eternity." At the blessing of the loaves, Troparion of the feast thrice, and reading of the feast.

At Matins, at "God is the Lord," Troparion of the feast thrice. After the 1st Kathisma and after the 2nd, Sessional Hymns of the day, and reading of the day. After the 3rd Kathisma, Little Litany, and both Sessional Hymns of the feast, and reading of the feast. Polyeleos, and Sessional Hymn, and reading of the feast. Anabathmoi, the 1st Antiphon of Tone 4. Prokeimenon: "Proclaim from day to day the salvation of our God." "Let every breath." Gospel of the feast, Psalm 50, Sticheron of the feast (the Gospel of the day is omitted, if the Annunciation fall on whatever day of this week). Canon of the feast with the heirmos on 6, and the Three-Ode Canon on 8. Katavasia: the Heirmos of the Triodion, both choirs together.

And where there is no Three-Ode Canon, we sing the Canon of the feast with the Heirmos on 12. Katavasia of the feast. After Ode 3, Kontakion of the day and Ikos, and Sessional Hymn of the feast, and reading of the feast. After Ode 6, Kontakion and Ikos of the feast. Prologue and Synaxarion. At Ode 9, we do not sing "More honorable," but we sing the refrain of the feast: "O earth, announce great gladness;" then the Heirmos of the feast: "As unto an animated ark of God;" unto the troparia of the Three-Ode Canon, the refrain: "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee."

Katavasia: we sing the Heirmos of the Triodion; after that, the refrain of the feast, and the Heirmos: "As unto an animated ark of God." Exapostilarion of the feast; Glory: of the day; Both now: of the feast. At the Praises, Stichera of the feast on 6; Glory: of the feast: "The mystery which was hidden from eternity;" Both now: of the day: "The dried-up fig tree:" Then the superior or reader says: "Glory to Thee Who hast shown us the light." Litany: "Let us complete our morning prayer:" At the Aposticha, Idiomela Stichera of the day, Tone 1: "The Lord comes:" Verse: "We were filled:" "Having attained, ye faithful:" Verse: "Make us glad for the days wherein Thou hast humbled us:" "Lord, coming unto the Passion:" Verse: "And look upon Thy servants:" "Lord, unto the mystery:" Verse: "And let the brightness:" "Lord, to mind most perfect things:" Glory: Tone 8: "A second Eve:" Both now: of the feast: "Let the heavens be glad:" Then, "It is good to give praise," once. After the Trisagion, Troparion of the feast. Litany, and 3 great prostrations. After this, "Come, let us worship," thrice. And the First Hour: Troparion of the feast; Both now: Theotokion: "What shall we call thee:" After the Trisagion: Kontakion of the feast, and at the end 3 great prostrations; then: "O Christ, the true Light," and dismissal.

At the 3rd hour of the day [9:00 AM], we make the Litiya outside the monastery. Having returned, we sing the 3rd Hour and the 6th with Kathismata and with reading; and we read the Tetra-Gospel.[^2960] And we say at them the Troparion of the feast, alternating the Kontakia of the day and of the feast; and at the end of each Hour, 3 great prostrations. Likewise we sing also the 9th Hour, and the Beatitudes simply without singing, and "Remember us, O Lord," and the rest; after the "Our Father," Kontakion of the day; Glory... Both now: of the feast; "Lord, have mercy," 40; Glory... Both now: "More honorable than the Cherubim;" and 3 great prostrations. And immediately: "Come, let us worship," thrice. And we sing Vespers without prostrations and without a Kathisma. At "Lord, I have cried," Idiomela Stichera of the day 5, and of the feast 5; Glory: of the day: "The dried-up fig tree;" Both now: of the feast: "The Archangel Gabriel was sent." Entrance with the Gospel. "O Joyful Light." Prokeimenon, and readings of the day, and two of the feast. Then the Little Litany, and the Trisagion. Prokeimenon, Epistle, and Alleluia of the feast. Gospel of the feast, and of the day; and the rest of the Liturgy of Saint John Chrysostom. And the Communion Hymn of the feast.[^2961]

*And where because of great necessity there is no Liturgy:*[^2962]
At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 10: and we sing of the day 3 in Tone 1, repeating the first two, and of the feast 5; Glory: of the day, Tone 8: "A second Eve;" Both now: of the feast. Entrance with the Gospel. "O Joyful Light." Prokeimenon, and reading of the day; and of the feast, two. Then Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, and Gospel of the feast, and of the day. "Vouchsafe, O Lord." Litany: "Let us complete our evening prayer." At the Aposticha of the day, Tone 5: "Lord, to mind most perfect things," twice, with the daily verses; and the other verse, Tone 8: "The dried-up fig tree;" Glory, Tone 5: "Lord, coming unto the Passion;" Both now: of the feast: "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart." Troparion of the feast. Litanies, and dismissal. Thus we sing also on the other days of Great Week. At the refectory, dispensation for oil and wine only. At Small Compline there are no prostrations, save only after "Glory to God in the highest," 3 bows; at the Trisagion, 3 bows. At the end, 3 great prostrations and 12 small bows. At the final Trisagion, 3 bows. And we sing also the Three-Ode Canon of Kyr Andrew.

## CONCERNING THE SAME FEAST, IF IT FALL ON GREAT TUESDAY[^2963]

On Monday evening we do not say a Kathisma. At "Lord, I have cried," Idiomela Stichera of the day 5, and of the feast 5; Glory: of the day: "A second Eve;" Both now: of the feast: "The Archangel Gabriel was sent." Entrance with the Gospel. "O Joyful Light." Prokeimenon, and readings of the day, and of the feast 3. "Let my prayer be set forth," and 3 prostrations. Gospel of the day; and the rest of the Presanctified. At the refectory we drink wine.

At the 1st hour of the night [7:00 PM], the great bell tolls, and all the heavy bells; and having gathered into the temple, we sing Great Compline: "God is with us," we sing to both choirs with chanting. The priest at the beginning censes according to custom. And after "Glory to God in the highest," procession into the narthex; and we sing at the Litiya the Idiomela Stichera of the feast; Glory... Both now: of the feast: "Gabriel announcs good tidings." At the Aposticha, Idiomela Stichera of the feast 3, with their verses; Glory... Both now: "Today is the joy." At the blessing of the loaves, Troparion of the feast thrice, and readings of the feast.

At Matins, at "God is the Lord," Troparion of the feast thrice. After their Kathismata, Sessional Hymns of the Triodion, and reading of the day. After the 2nd Kathisma, Little Litany, and Sessional Hymn of the feast, and reading. Polyeleos and Sessional Hymn of the feast. Anabathmoi, the 1st Antiphon of Tone 4. Prokeimenon: "Let every breath." Gospel of the feast, Psalm 50, Sticheron of the feast. Canon of the feast with the Heirmos on 12. Katavasia of the feast: the Heirmos, both choirs together. And where there is a Two-Ode Canon of the Triodion, we sing the Canon of the feast with the Heirmoi on 6; the Two-Ode Canon on 8. Follow the Heirmos of the Triodion, both choirs together. After Ode 3, Kontakion of the day and Ikos, and Sessional Hymn of the feast, and reading of the feast. After Ode 6, Kontakion of the feast and Ikos, and we read the Prologue. At Ode 9, we do not sing "More honorable," but we sing the refrain and Heirmos of the feast, as was indicated on Great Monday. Exapostilarion of the feast; Glory: of the day; Both now: of the feast.

At the Praises, Stichera Prosomoia of the feast on 6; Glory: of the day: "Through spiritual slothfulness;" Both now: of the feast: "The mystery which was hidden from eternity." At the Aposticha, Idiomela of the day with their verses, as was prescribed on Monday: "We were filled in the morning;" Glory: of the feast: "Let the heavens be glad;" Both now: of the day, Tone 6: "When Thou shalt come in glory:" Troparion of the feast. Litany, and 3 great prostrations; then "Come, let us worship," thrice. The First Hour; at the end thereof 3 great prostrations; and the prayer: "O Christ, the true Light;" and dismissal.

At the 3rd hour of the day [9:00 AM], we make the Litiya outside the monastery; and having returned, we sing the Hours with Kathismata, and the Tetra-Gospel is read. We say at the Hours the Troparion of the feast, and reading of the feast. We say the Kontakia alternating between the day and the feast; and at the end of each Hour, 3 great prostrations. And the 9th Hour without a Kathisma. The Beatitudes quickly without singing; and "Remember us, O Lord," and the rest as was prescribed before. After the "Our Father," Kontakion of the feast; "Lord, have mercy," 40; Glory... Both now: "More honorable than the Cherubim;" and 3 great prostrations, and immediately we say: "Come, let us worship," thrice. And we sing Vespers without a Kathisma and without prostrations: At "Lord, I have cried," Idiomela Stichera of the day 5, and of the feast 5; Glory: of the day; Both now: of the feast. Entrance with the Gospel. Prokeimenon, and readings of the day two, and of the feast two. Little Litany, and the exclamation of the Trisagion. Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia of the feast; Gospel of the feast, and of the day; and the rest of the Liturgy of Saint John Chrysostom. Communion Hymn of the feast.

At the refectory, we grant dispensation for olive oil and wine only. And we sing Small Compline without prostrations; and we sing also the Three-Ode Canon thereon by Kyr Andrew of Crete.

## CONCERNING THE SAME FEAST, IF IT FALL ON GREAT WEDNESDAY[^2964]

On Tuesday evening we sing Vespers without a Kathisma and without prostrations. At "Lord, I have cried," Idiomela Stichera of the day 5, and of the feast 5; Glory: of the day, Tone 7: "Behold, the talent unto thee:" Both now: of the feast. Entrance with the Gospel. Prokeimenon, and readings of the day, and of the feast 3. "Let my prayer be set forth," and 3 prostrations. Gospel of the day; and the rest of the Liturgy of the Presanctified. At the refectory, cooked food without oil; and we drink wine.

At the 1st hour of the night [7:00 PM], the great bell tolls, and all the heavy bells; and we sing Great Compline: "God is with us," to both choirs. The priest censes at the beginning according to custom. And after "Glory to God in the highest," procession into the narthex; and we sing at the Litiya the Stichera; Glory... Both now: of the feast. At the Aposticha, Stichera, and Glory... Both now: of the feast. At the blessing of the loaves, Troparion of the feast thrice, and reading of the feast.

At Matins, at "God is the Lord," Troparion of the feast thrice. After both Kathismata, Sessional Hymns of the Triodion, and reading of the day. After the 2nd Kathisma, Litany, and both Sessional Hymns of the feast, and reading of the feast. Polyeleos, and Sessional Hymn, and reading of the feast. Anabathmoi, the 1st Antiphon of Tone 4. Prokeimenon: "Let every breath." Gospel of the feast, Psalm 50, Sticheron of the feast. Canon of the feast with the Heirmos on 12. Katavasia of the feast: the Heirmos, both choirs together.

And where there is a Three-Ode Canon: we sing the Canon of the feast with the Heirmos on 6, and the Three-Ode Canon on 8. Katavasia: the Heirmos of the Triodion. After Ode 3, Kontakion of the day, and Ikos, and Sessional Hymn of the feast, and reading of the feast. After Ode 6, Kontakion of the feast and Ikos. At Ode 9, we do not sing "More honorable," but we sing the refrains of the feast as was prescribed before; Exapostilarion of the feast; Glory: of the day; Both now: of the feast. At the Praises, Stichera of the feast on 6; Glory: of the day, Tone 6: "Today Christ comes:" Both now: of the feast, Tone 2: "The mystery which was hidden from eternity."

At the Aposticha of the day, with their verses, as was prescribed on Great Monday; Glory: of the feast; Both now: of the day; and the rest according to what was shown before. At the 3rd hour of the day [9:00 AM], we make the procession outside the monastery; and having returned, we sing the Hours with Kathismata, and the Tetra-Gospel is read; and the rest of the Hours and of the Liturgy, as was set forth on Monday and Tuesday of this week. At the end of the Hours there takes place the mutual forgiveness of the monastery, according to custom. And we sing Small Compline without prostrations, and the Three-Ode Canon of Kyr Andrew of Crete.

## CONCERNING THE SAME FEAST, IF IT FALL ON GREAT THURSDAY[^2965]

On Great Wednesday we sing Vespers without a Kathisma. At "Lord, I have cried," Idiomela Stichera of the day 5, and of the feast 5; Glory... Both now: of the feast; and the rest as was indicated on Tuesday.

At the 1st hour of the night [7:00 PM], the great bell tolls, and all the heavy bells. And having gathered into the temple, we sing Great Compline: the priest censes according to custom. And after "Glory to God in the highest," procession into the narthex; and we sing at the Litiya the Idiomela Stichera; Glory... Both now: of the feast. At the Aposticha, Stichera; Glory... Both now: of the feast. At the blessing of the loaves, Troparion of the feast thrice, and reading of the feast.

At Matins, at "God is the Lord," Troparion of the feast twice; Glory... Both now: "When the glorious disciples." Then Polyeleos, and Sessional Hymn, and reading of the feast. Anabathmoi, the 1st Antiphon of Tone 4. Prokeimenon: "Let every breath." Gospel of the feast, Psalm 50, Sticheron of the feast.

Canon of the feast with the Heirmos on 8, the Heirmos twice; and of the day with the Heirmos on 8. Katavasia: the Heirmos of the day, both choirs together. After Ode 3, Kontakion of the day and Ikos, and Sessional Hymn of the day; Glory... Both now: of the feast, and reading of the feast. After Ode 6, Kontakion of the feast and Ikos, and Prologue, and Synaxarion. At Ode 9, we do not sing "More honorable," but we sing the refrains of the feast as was prescribed before; at the end, the Heirmos: "The Master's hospitality:" Then the refrain of the feast and Heirmos. Exapostilarion of the feast; Glory: of the day; Both now: of the feast. At the Praises, Stichera of the feast on 6; Glory: of the feast; Both now: of the day. After this, "Glory to God in the highest," and litanies. Then at the Aposticha, Stichera of the day with their verses; Glory: of the day; Both now: of the feast. After "It is good to give praise," and after "Our Father," Troparion of the day; Glory... Both now: of the feast. Litany: "Have mercy on us, O God;" and dismissal. Then: "Come, let us worship," thrice; and the First Hour: whereat the Troparion, and the Paremia of the day, and the catechesis of the feast, and dismissal.

At the 5th hour of the day [11:00 AM], there takes place the procession outside the monastery.[^2966] And having returned, we sing the Hours in the narthex: the 3rd, 6th, and 9th. At them we say the Troparion of the feast; Glory: of the day; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion of the Hours. After the "Our Father," we alternate the Kontakia: "Remember us, O Lord," and the rest. The other choir: after the "Our Father," Kontakion of the feast; "Lord, have mercy," 40; and the prayer: "All-Holy Trinity;" and dismissal. "I will bless the Lord at all times:" we do not say.

In the evening, the bell tolls for the great bell and for all the heavy bells at the 8th hour of the day [2:00 PM], and we sing Vespers. At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera Idiomela of the day 5, and of the feast 5; Glory: of the day; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. Entrance with the Gospel. "O Joyful Light;" and the reading of the day; and of the feast, two readings. Little Litany; then the Trisagion. Prokeimenon of the day, and of the feast. Epistle of the day, and of the feast; and the rest of the Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great.

Instead of "It is truly meet," the Heirmos: "The Master's hospitality." In temples of the Annunciation of the Most Holy Theotokos, the Heirmos: "As unto an animated ark of God." Instead of the Cherubic Hymn, we sing the Troparion, Tone 6: "Of Thy mystical supper," thrice; the same we sing also instead of the Communion Hymn, once.[^2967]

And when the brethren receive Communion, we sing, instead of "The Body of Christ:" the same: "Of Thy mystical supper," until the brethren have communicated; and instead of "Let our mouths be filled:" once, with the Alleluias.

At the refectory we do not grant dispensation for fish, but only for olive oil and wine.[^2968]

## CONCERNING THE SAME FEAST, IF IT FALL ON GREAT FRIDAY

On Thursday evening, at "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the day 5, and of the feast 5; Glory: of the day: "O brood of vipers;" Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast: "The Archangel Gabriel was sent." Entrance with the Gospel. Prokeimenon, and reading of the day, and of the feast 3 readings. Little Litany; and the Trisagion. Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, and Gospel of the day; and the rest of the Divine Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great, as was previously made known. At the refectory we grant dispensation for olive oil and wine. We sing Small Compline with the Three-Ode Canon. After the Trisagion, Kontakion of the day; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast.

At the 1st hour of the night [7:00 PM], the bell strikes the great bell and all the heavy bells. And we begin Matins. At "God is the Lord," Troparion of the feast, twice; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the day: "When the glorious disciples." Then the Little Litany. And immediately the Deacon or Priest says: "And that we may be accounted worthy to hear the Holy Gospel;" and the Superior reads the 1st Gospel, and after that the Antiphons and the Gospels of the Holy Passions according to their order.[^2969] And after the reading of the 6th Gospel, the reading of the day. After this, the Anabathmoi, the 1st Antiphon of Tone 4. Prokeimenon of the feast. "Let every breath." Gospel of the feast; and immediately of the Holy Passions, the 50th Psalm, Sticheron of the feast. Then the prayer: "O God, save Thy people;" and we: "Lord, have mercy," 12. Canon of the feast with the heirmos on 14. Katavasia of the feast, both choirs together.

And where there is a Three-Ode Canon, we sing the Canon of the feast with the Heirmos on 6: the Heirmoi twice; and the Three-Ode Canon on 8. Katavasia of the Triodion, both choirs together. After Ode 3, Kontakion of the day, and Ikos; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Sessional Hymn of the feast, and reading of the feast. After Ode 6, Kontakion of the feast, and Ikos, and Synaxarion. At Ode 9, we do not sing "More honorable," but we sing the refrain of the feast. Exapostilarion of the feast; Glory: of the day; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. Then the 6th Gospel. At the Praises, Stichera Idiomela of the day; Glory, Tone 2: "The reed is already dipped;" Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast, the same Tone: "Let the heavens be glad." Then the 7th Gospel. After this, "Glory to God in the highest;" Litany: "Let us complete our morning prayer;" and the exclamation. After this, the 8th Gospel. Then at the Aposticha, Stichera of the feast; Glory: of the day; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. Then the 9th Gospel. We sing: "It is good to give praise unto the Lord;" and after the "Our Father," Troparion, Tone 4: "Thou hast redeemed us;" Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. Litany: "Have mercy on us, O God;" Priest: "Wisdom;" and the dismissal. And we sing the First Hour, as was indicated for Great Friday. We say at it the Troparia of the feast, and of the day, and the Kontakion of the feast.

At the 5th hour of the day [11:00 AM], we make the procession outside the monastery; and having returned, we sing the 3rd, 6th, and 9th Hours: with troparia and paremias, with Epistles, and Gospels, and readings, and with the rest of their service. There are said at them the Troparia of the Hours of Great Friday (which is of the day) and of the feast; Kontakia of the day, and of the feast, and the rest as was indicated on Great Friday. Psalm 33 we omit, and we say it at the Liturgy.

At the 8th hour [2:00 PM], the bell tolls for the great bell and all the heavy bells. We begin Vespers, and the Priest performs the Proskomide. At "Lord, I have cried," we sing Stichera of the day 6, and of the feast 4; Glory: of the day: "O how the lawless assembly;" Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast: "The Archangel Gabriel was sent." Entrance with the Gospel. "O Joyful Light." Prokeimenon, and readings of the day, and of the feast, two readings. Then the Little Litany, and the Trisagion. Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, and Gospel: first of the feast, and of the day. Communion Hymn of the feast. And the Divine Liturgy of Saint John Chrysostom is celebrated.[^2970] Instead of "It is truly meet," we sing the Heirmos of the feast: "As unto an animated ark of God." At the refectory we eat dry food, and we drink wine.

## CONCERNING THE SAME FEAST, IF IT FALL ON GREAT SATURDAY

On Friday evening, at the 9th hour of the day [3:00 PM], the bell tolls for the great bell and for all the heavy bells.[^2971] And we sing Vespers. At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera Idiomela of the day on 6, and of the feast on 4; Glory: of the day; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. Entrance with the Gospel. "O Joyful Light." Prokeimenon, and readings of the day, and of the feast 5 readings. Then Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, and Gospel of the day. After this, the Litany: "Let us all say;" then: "Vouchsafe, O Lord, in this evening;" "Let us complete our evening prayer."

At the Aposticha, Stichera of the day with their refrains; Glory: of the feast; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the day. Then: "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart;" after the Trisagion, Troparion of the feast; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. "The noble Joseph." Priest: "Wisdom;" and dismissal. We sing Compline in the cell: Kontakion of the day; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. At the 1st hour of the night [7:00 PM], the bell strikes the great bell and all the heavy bells, and we sing Matins. At "God is the Lord," Troparion of the day, Tone 2: "The noble Joseph," once; Glory: "When Thou didst descend unto death," once; Glory: "Unto the myrrh-bearing women;" Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast: "Today is the fountainhead of our salvation." Then we sing the Blameless [Psalm 118] in Tone 2.[^2972] The Priest censes at the 1st Glory, and likewise at the 2nd, and at the 3rd, as is customary. At the conclusion of the Blameless, we sing the Resurrection Troparia: "The assembly of the Angels," and the rest. Then the Little Litany, and Sessional Hymn of the day. Then the Polyeleos, and Sessional Hymn of the feast, and reading of the feast. Anabathmoi, the 1st Antiphon of Tone 4. Prokeimenon of the feast. "Let every breath." Gospel of the feast, Psalm 50, Sticheron of the feast.

Canon of the feast with the heirmos on 8: the Heirmos twice; and of the day with the heirmos on 8. Katavasia: the Heirmos of the day, both choirs together. After Ode 3, Kontakion and Ikos, and Sessional Hymn of the day; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast, and reading of the feast. After Ode 6, Kontakion of the feast, and Ikos, Prologue, and Synaxarion. At Ode 9, we do not sing "More honorable," but we sing the refrain of the feast, as was indicated. At the end, the Heirmos of the day: "Weep not for Me, O Mother;" then the refrain of the feast, and the Heirmos. "Holy is the Lord our God," in Tone 2. Exapostilarion of the feast, twice.

At the Praises, Stichera Idiomela of the day 3, and of the feast Prosomoia 3. Then the Idiomelon of the feast, Tone 8: "Let the heavens be glad," with the refrain: "Proclaim from day to day;" Glory: of the day; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. "Most blessed art thou, O Virgin Theotokos." Great Doxology. And the entrance takes place, as is indicated in the Triodion. After this, Prokeimenon and Paremia of the day. Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, and Gospel of the day. Litany, and dismissal. And we sing the First Hour in the narthex. The other Hours are sung at their proper time. At the Hours, Troparion of the feast, and of the day, alternating the Kontakia. The Beatitudes quickly without singing: "Remember us, O Lord," and the rest. After the "Our Father," Kontakion of the day; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Kontakion of the feast; "Lord, have mercy," 40; and the prayer: "All-Holy Trinity;" and dismissal.

*On Holy and Great Saturday Evening, at the 9th hour of the day [3:00 PM]:*
The bell strikes the great bell and all the heavy bells; and having assembled in the temple, the Priest having given the blessing, we sing Vespers according to custom without a Kathisma. At "Lord, I have cried," we sing the Resurrection Stichera 3, Tone 1: "Our evening prayers;" and of Great Saturday Idiomela 3, Tone 8; and of the feast on 4; Glory: of the day, Tone 6: "Today secretly;" Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast: "The Archangel Gabriel was sent." Entrance with the Gospel. "O Joyful Light." Prokeimenon is not said; but immediately the Priest says: "Wisdom;" and the readings of the day according to their order. At the conclusion of the readings, the Little Litany and the exclamation. And we sing instead of the Trisagion: "As many of you as have been baptized into Christ: Alleluia." Prokeimenon of the day, and of the feast. Epistle of the day, and of the feast. Gospel of the day, and of the feast. Instead of the Cherubic Hymn we sing: "Let all mortal flesh keep silence." And in order, the Divine Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great.[^2973] Instead of "It is truly meet," we sing the Heirmos: "Weep not for Me, O Mother." But in a temple of the Annunciation of the Theotokos, we sing the Heirmos: "As unto an animated ark of God." Communion Hymn of the day, and of the feast.

Be it known that on whatever day of this Great Week the Annunciation occurs, we celebrate it together with Compline, and we eat cooked food with olive oil, and we drink wine, except on Great Friday; for on that day only we grant dispensation for wine, for the glory and intercession of the Most Pure Theotokos.

If the apodosis of the Annunciation of the Most Holy Theotokos fall on Lazarus Saturday, or on Palm Sunday, or on one of the days of Passion Week, or of Bright Week, the apodosis does not take place; but the Stichera and the Canon of the afterfeast and of the Archangel are sung at Compline in the preceding days of the Sixth Week.[^2974]

# TYPIKON APPENDIX: PASCHALTIDE MENAION COMBINATIONS AND GOSPEL PILLARS[^2975]

## INSTRUCTIONS ON HOW TO SING IN THE PENTECOSTARION FOR THE ANNUNCIATION, AND TO GEORGE, AND TO THE OTHER SAINTS

## IF THE ANNUNCIATION FALLS ON HOLY PASCHA (KYRIOPASCHA)[^2976]

It behooves to know: that when the Paschal Key is G [Key 3], then on March 25 the Annunciation of the Most Holy Theotokos coincides with the very Holy and Great Sunday of Pascha, which is called Kyriopascha: that is, divinely united together, Pascha and the feast of the Annunciation.

On Great Saturday evening, at "Lord, I have cried," we set 10 verses, and we sing the Resurrection Stichera 3, and of Great Saturday 3, and of the feast 4; Glory, Tone 6: "Today secretly;" Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast, the same Tone: "The Archangel Gabriel was sent." Entrance with the Gospel. "O Joyful Light." Prokeimenon is not said; but immediately the Priest: "Wisdom;" and the readings: first of the day: "In the beginning God made heaven and earth:" one paremia; then of the feast of the Annunciation 5 readings, and then the remaining readings of the day according to their order. And in order, the Divine Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great.

After the dismissal of the Liturgy, there takes place the repast, and the reading of the Acts of the Holy Apostles according to their order, as was indicated on Great Saturday. And the reading having reached its end, the Priest having given the blessing, we say the Trisagion. And after the "Our Father," "Lord, have mercy," 12; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. "Come, let us worship," thrice. Then Psalm 50. And we sing the Canon of the feast with the heirmos on 6, and of Great Saturday with the heirmos on 8. Katavasia: the Saturday Heirmos, both choirs together. After Ode 3, Kontakion and Ikos and Ikos of the feast, and Sessional Hymn of the day; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast, and reading of the feast. After Ode 6, Kontakion of the day, and Ikos, and reading of the day. After Ode 9, the Trisagion, and after the "Our Father," Troparion: "When Thou didst descend unto death;" Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast; Litany, and dismissal.

And if there be time before dawn: the reading of the day is added; during the reading thereof, the Superior distributes candles to the brethren. The candle-lighter, having taken the blessing from the Superior, goes and tolls all the bells. And after the reading we go forth into the narthex, the Superior preceded by lamps; and the doors being closed, he censes the whole brotherhood according to order; and standing before the great church doors, he censes crosswise thrice, and says: "Glory to the holy, consubstantial:" and when we have answered: "Amen," the Superior begins the Troparion, Tone 5: "Christ is risen from the dead," thrice. After this the brethren sing it thrice. Superior: 1st verse: "Let God arise:" and the brethren: "Christ is risen," once. Superior: 2nd verse: "As smoke vanishes:" and the brethren: "Christ is risen," once. Superior: 3rd verse: "So let the sinners perish:" and the brethren: "Christ is risen," once. Superior: 4th verse: "This is the day which the Lord has made:" and the brethren: "Christ is risen," once. And immediately the Superior with a loud voice: "Christ is risen:" And the doors being opened, he enters preceded by lamps, the Superior together with the brethren singing: "And upon them that are in the tombs bestowing life." When he has entered into the altar, we say: Glory: and we sing the Troparion of the feast, Tone 4: "Today is the fountainhead of our salvation;" Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. The same. Then the Great Litany: "In peace let us pray to the Lord." And after the exclamation, the Superior begins the Heirmos: "It is the day of Resurrection." And we sing the Canon of Pascha with the heirmos on 8: the Heirmos twice; and the Canon of the Annunciation with the heirmos on 8: the Heirmos twice. At the end, the heirmoi of the canons are doubled, each choir its own; then the Katavasia: "It is the day of Resurrection," both choirs together; and the Troparion: "Christ is risen," thrice.[^2977] And after each ode, the Little Litany and the exclamations according to their order. After Ode 3, Kontakion and Ikos of Pascha, and the Hypakoe; and the reading from the Theologian, whereof the beginning is: "Upon my watch I will stand."[^2978] After Ode 6, Kontakion of the feast of the Annunciation, and Ikos; and the reading from the Theologian, whereof the beginning is: "It is the day of Resurrection." Then the Prokeimenon of the feast, Tone 4: "Proclaim from day to day the salvation of our God;" Verse: "Sing unto the Lord a new song." "Let every breath." Gospel according to Luke, pericopa 4: "In those days, Mary arose;" then: "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ," thrice; and the Sticheron: "Jesus, having risen from the dead," thrice, in Tone 6. After this, Ode 7 and the other two. At Ode 9, we sing the refrains of Pascha, and of the feast; Exapostilarion of Pascha once, and of the feast twice. At the Praises, the Resurrection Stichera on 4, and of the Annunciation on 4, with their refrains. Then both choirs together, the 1st refrain: "Let God arise;" Stichera of Pascha, Tone 5, with their remaining refrains; Glory: of the Annunciation, Tone 8: "Let the heavens be glad;" Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of Pascha: "It is the day of Resurrection;" and the kiss according to custom. And the Catechetical Homily of Saint John Chrysostom; Litany, and dismissal. The procession outside the monastery does not take place. The Hours are sung according to the Typikon of Pascha. At the Liturgy, the Antiphons of Pascha. After the Entrance we say: "In congregations bless ye God, the Lord from the springs of Israel. Christ is risen," thrice; Glory: Troparion: "Today is the fountainhead of our salvation;" Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Kontakion: "Though Thou didst descend into the grave." Instead of the Trisagion, we sing: "As many of you as have been baptized into Christ." Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, and Gospel: first of Pascha, then of the feast.

*When the time arrives at the Liturgy to read the Holy Gospel:*[^2979]
The Priest reads the Paschal Gospel with the Deacon, as was indicated at the Liturgy on Sunday. Then a single Deacon reads the Gospel of the Annunciation according to custom, as always; and for this Gospel they do not strike the censer bells. And in order, the Divine Liturgy of Saint John Chrysostom. Instead of "It is truly meet," the Heirmos of Pascha. Communion Hymn of Pascha, and of the feast.

## CONCERNING THE SAME FEAST, IF THE ANNUNCIATION FALL ON BRIGHT MONDAY, TUESDAY, OR WEDNESDAY[^2980]

On the Holy and Great Sunday of Pascha: at Small Vespers, when the Priest has said: "Christ is risen," thrice, and the customary verses; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. "Christ is risen." At "Lord, I have cried," the Resurrection Stichera of Tone 2 on 4; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast, the same Tone: "The mystery hidden from eternity." Then: "O Joyful Light," without an entrance. Great Prokeimenon: "Who is a god as great as our God?" and its verse; then: "Vouchsafe, O Lord." At the Aposticha, the Resurrection Sticheron 1; then Stichera Idiomela of the feast 3, Tone 4: the Aposticha of Great Vespers, with their refrains; Glory: "Gabriel announces good tidings;" Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. "It is the day of Resurrection. Christ is risen," thrice; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Troparion: "Today is the fountainhead of our salvation;" Little Litany, and dismissal.

At Great Vespers: When the Priest has censed and said: "Glory to the holy, consubstantial," they sing: "Christ is risen," thrice, and its verses; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. "Christ is risen," thrice. Then the Litany. At "Lord, I have cried," the Resurrection Stichera 3, and Anatolian 1, and of the feast 6; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast: "The Archangel Gabriel was sent." Entrance. "O Joyful Light." Prokeimenon, Tone 7: "Who is a god as great as our God?" with its verses; and 3 readings of the feast. (If it be Sunday evening, the Priest proclaims: "And that we may be accounted worthy:" Gospel according to John, pericopa 65: "The same day at evening:" Ending: "they believed not.")[^2981] Then the Litany. At the Litiya, Stichera Idiomela of the feast; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. "Gabriel announces good tidings." At the Aposticha, the Resurrection Sticheron 1; then the refrain: "Let God arise;" and we sing the Stichera of Pascha with their refrains; Glory: of the feast: "Today is joy;" Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of Pascha: "It is the day of Resurrection;" and at the end: "Christ is risen," thrice; Troparion of the feast, thrice; and the blessing of the loaves, and distribution, and reading of the feast.

At Matins, when the Priest has given the blessing, we sing: "Christ is risen," thrice, and its verses; and at the conclusion: Glory: Troparion of the feast; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. The same. Then the Great Litany; and the Polyeleos, and Sessional Hymn, and reading of the feast. Anabathmoi, the 1st Antiphon of Tone 4. Prokeimenon and Gospel of the feast. "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ," thrice; Psalm 50 is not said, but immediately: Glory: "Through the prayers of the Theotokos;" Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. The same. After this the refrain in Tone 6: "Proclaim from day to day the salvation of our God;" and we sing the Idiomelon Sticheron of the feast, Tone 6: "The Archangel Gabriel was sent." Then the Priest says the prayer: "O God, save Thy people;" and we: "Lord, have mercy," 12. And after the exclamation we sing the Canon of Pascha with the Heirmos on 6, and of the feast with the Heirmos on 8: the Heirmoi of Pascha and of the feast twice each. Katavasia of the Annunciation: the Heirmos, both choirs together. After Ode 3, Kontakion of Pascha, and Ikos, and Sessional Hymn of the feast. After Ode 6, Kontakion of the feast, and Ikos, and reading of the day. Then: "Jesus, having risen from the dead," thrice. At Ode 9, the refrains of Pascha, and of the feast; Exapostilarion of Pascha once, and of the feast twice. At the Praises, the Resurrection Stichera 3, and of the feast Prosomoia 3. Then: "Let God arise;" and we sing the Stichera of Pascha with their refrains; Glory: of the feast: "Let the heavens be glad;" Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of Pascha: "It is the day of Resurrection. Christ is risen," thrice; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Troparion of the feast. Litanies, and dismissal. And holy oil is given to the brethren. And the procession takes place outside the monastery. The Hours are sung according to the custom of Pascha. At the Liturgy, the Antiphons of Pascha. After the Entrance we say the verse: "In congregations bless ye God, the Lord: Christ is risen," thrice; Troparion of the feast; Glory: Kontakion of Pascha; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. Instead of the Trisagion: "As many of you as have been baptized into Christ." Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, and Gospel: first of the Annunciation, then of the day; and in order, the Divine Liturgy of Saint John Chrysostom. Communion Hymn of the day, and of the feast.

## INSTRUCTION CONCERNING THE HOLY GREAT-MARTYR GEORGE[^2982]

It begins from the day of Great Friday, and ascends unto the Thursday of the 5th Week after Pascha. And if the Great-Martyr George fall on Great Friday, or on Great Saturday, or on Pascha itself, the Stichera of the Saint, and the Canon, and the rest of the service are sung on Bright Monday, together with the daily service.[^2983]

*If the Holy Great-Martyr George fall on one of the days of Bright Week:*
In the evening, at "Lord, I have cried," the Resurrection Stichera 3, and of the Saint 3; Glory: of the Saint, Tone 6: "Worthy of the name;" Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion: the 1st of Tone 6. Entrance. "O Joyful Light." Prokeimenon of the day, and 3 readings of the Saint. If it be on the very evening of Pascha, the Priest says: "And that we may be accounted worthy:" and the rest; and the Gospel is read according to order. At the Aposticha, the Resurrection Sticheron. Then the Stichera of Pascha with their refrains; Glory: of the Saint, Tone 4: "The spiritual adamant;" Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of Pascha, Tone 5: "It is the day of Resurrection. Christ is risen," thrice; Glory: Troparion of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion: the 1st of the Tone. Priest: "Wisdom;" and dismissal.

At Matins: after "Christ is risen" and after the verses; Glory: Troparion of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion: the 1st of the Tone. Then the customary Litany, and the Polyeleos. Then the Sessional Hymn of the Saint, twice; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion, and reading. Then the Anabathmoi, the 1st Antiphon of Tone 4. Prokeimenon: "Let every breath;" and the Gospel of the Saint. "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ," thrice; Glory: "Through the prayers of the Passion-bearer;" Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. "Through the prayers of the Theotokos." Then the verses: "The righteous man shall be glad in the Lord, and shall hope in Him." And we sing the Idiomelon Sticheron of the Saint, Tone 6: "Today the whole universe." Then the Priest says: "O God, save Thy people;" and we: "Lord, have mercy," 12. And after the exclamation, the Canon of Pascha with the Heirmos on 8, and of the Saint on 6. Katavasia of Pascha, both choirs together. After Ode 3, Kontakion of Pascha, and Ikos, and reading. After Ode 6, Kontakion of the Saint, and Ikos, and reading. "Jesus, having risen from the dead," thrice: we sing to both choirs. After Ode 9, Exapostilarion of Pascha; Glory: of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of Pascha. At the Praises, the Resurrection Stichera 3, and of the Saint 3. Then the Stichera of Pascha with their refrains; Glory: of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of Pascha: "It is the day of Resurrection. Christ is risen," thrice; Glory: Troparion of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion: the 1st. Litanies, and dismissal. The Hours are sung of Pascha according to custom. At the Liturgy, the Antiphons of Pascha. After the Entrance: "Christ is risen," thrice; then the Troparion of the Saint; Glory: his Kontakion; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of Pascha. Instead of the Trisagion: "As many of you as have been baptized into Christ." Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, Gospel, and Communion Hymn of the day, and of the Saint.

## CONCERNING THE MEMORY OF SAINT GEORGE, IF IT FALL ON THOMAS SUNDAY[^2984]

On Saturday of Bright Week: at Small Vespers, at "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the feast on 4; Glory: of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Saint with his refrains, from Great Vespers; Glory: of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. Troparion of the Saint; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast; Little Litany, and dismissal.

At Great Vespers: after the customary Kathisma, at "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the feast on 6, and of the Saint on 4; Glory: of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. Entrance, and reading of the Saint. At the Litiya, Stichera of the feast, and of the Saint; Glory: of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. At the Aposticha, of the feast; Glory: of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. At the blessing of the loaves, Troparion of the feast, twice;

twice, and of the Saint once; and reading from the Acts of the Apostles.

At Matins: at "God is the Lord," Troparion of the feast, twice; Glory: of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. After the Kathismata, Sessional Hymns of the feast, and reading. Polyeleos, and Sessional Hymn, and reading of the feast. Anabathmoi, the 1st Antiphon of Tone 4. Prokeimenon: "Let every breath;" Gospel of the feast: Matthew, pericopa 116: "The eleven disciples;" "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ," thrice; Psalm 50; Glory: "Through the prayers of the Apostles;" Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. "Through the prayers of the Theotokos;" Sticheron: "Jesus, having risen from the dead." Canon of the feast with the heirmos on 8, and of the Saint on 6. Katavasia of Pascha: "It is the day of Resurrection," both choirs together. After Ode 3, Kontakion of the Saint, and Ikos, and Sessional Hymn, twice; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast, and reading from the Theologian, whereof the beginning is: "To be honored by renewals."[^2985] After Ode 6, Kontakion of the feast, and Ikos, and reading. After Ode 9 we sing: "Holy is the Lord our God," in Tone 1. Exapostilarion of the feast; Glory: of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. At the Praises, Stichera of the feast 3, and of the Saint 3. We sing also the Idiomelon of the Saint: "Let them anoint righteousness," with his refrain: "The righteous man shall be glad in the Lord;" Glory: of the feast; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. "Most blessed art thou, O Virgin Theotokos." Great Doxology. After the Trisagion, Troparion of the Saint; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast; and litanies, and dismissal. And the Catechesis of Theodore the Studite; and the customary procession; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. The Gospel Sticheron; and the First Hour in the narthex. At the Hours, Troparion of the feast; Glory: of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion of the Hours. After the "Our Father," we alternate the Kontakia. At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the feast, Ode 3 on 4, and of the Saint Ode 6 on 4. After the Entrance, Troparion of the feast, and of the Saint; Glory: Kontakion of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, Gospel, and Communion Hymn: first of the feast, then of the Saint.

## IF THE MEMORY OF THE HOLY GREAT-MARTYR GEORGE FALL ON THE SUNDAY OF THE MYRRH-BEARING WOMEN, OR OF THE PARALYTIC, OR OF THE SAMARITAN WOMAN[^2986]

On Saturday at Small Vespers, at "Lord, I have cried," the Resurrection Stichera 4; Glory: of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion. At the Aposticha, the Resurrection Sticheron, and of the Saint the Aposticha of Great Vespers with his refrains; Glory: of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion. Resurrection Troparion; Glory: of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion; Little Litany, and dismissal.

At Great Vespers, after the customary Kathisma, at "Lord, I have cried," the Resurrection Stichera of Tone 3, of the feast 3, and of the Saint 4; Glory: of the feast, the Idiomelon of the Triodion; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion: the 1st of the Tone. Entrance, Prokeimenon of the day, and 3 readings of the Saint. At the Litiya, Sticheron of the temple, and the Idiomelon of the Saint; Glory: of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. At the Aposticha, the Resurrection Sticheron, and of Pascha; Glory: of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the Triodion. At the blessing of the loaves, Troparion: "O Virgin Theotokos, rejoice," twice, and of the Saint once; and reading from the Acts of the Holy Apostles.

If it be the Sunday of the Myrrh-bearing Women, at "God is the Lord:" the Resurrection Troparion: "When Thou didst descend unto death," once; "The noble Joseph," once; Glory: of George; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. "Unto the myrrh-bearing women."

But if on other Sundays: the Resurrection Troparion twice; Glory: of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion: the 1st, in the same Tone. After the Kathismata, the Resurrection Sessional Hymns, and their Theotokia; and reading in the Commentary Gospel. Polyeleos, and both Sessional Hymns of the Saint; Glory: Sessional Hymn after the Polyeleos; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion, and reading of the Saint. Anabathmoi, and Prokeimenon of the Tone. "Let every breath;" the Resurrection Gospel; "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ," thrice; Psalm 50; Resurrection Sticheron. Canon of Pascha with the Heirmos and with its Theotokia on 6, and of the Saint on 4, and of the Triodion on 4. We sing thus: at each ode, the Resurrection Troparion one, and of the feast one, and of the Martyr, and the Theotokion. Katavasia: "It is the day of Resurrection." After Ode 3, Kontakion of the Saint, and Ikos, and his Sessional Hymn twice; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast; and reading of the Saint. After Ode 6, Kontakion of the feast, and Ikos. At Ode 9, we do not sing "More honorable." Exapostilarion of Pascha; Glory: of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. At the Praises, the Resurrection Stichera 4, and of the Saint 4, with the Doxasticon, and with his refrains; Glory: of the feast; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. "Most blessed art thou, O Virgin Theotokos." Great Doxology. After the Trisagion, the Resurrection Troparion; litanies, and the Catechesis, and dismissal. And the customary procession into the narthex; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. The Gospel Sticheron; and the First Hour. At the Hours, the Resurrection Troparion; Glory: of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion of the Hours. After the "Our Father," we alternate the Kontakia.

At the Liturgy: the Beatitudes of the Tone on 4, and of the Triodion, Ode 3 on 4, and of the Saint, Ode 6 on 4. After the Entrance, the Resurrection Troparion, and of the Saint; Glory: Kontakion of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, Gospel, and Communion Hymn: first of the feast, then of the Saint.

## IF THE PASCHAL KEY BE Z, THEN ON APRIL 23 FALLS THE HOLY GREAT-MARTYR GEORGE, ON THE WEDNESDAY OF MID-PENTECOST; BUT IF THE KEY BE (Z), THEN ON MAY 8, THE MEMORY OF THE HOLY APOSTLE JOHN THE THEOLOGIAN: THIS INSTRUCTION APPLIES TO BOTH, AND UNTO THEIR AFTERFEASTS[^2987]

If the Superior desire, we make a Vigil. On Tuesday evening at Small Vespers, Stichera of the feast, or of the Saint on 4 (repeat the 1st, if there be 3 stichera); Glory: of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. At the Aposticha of the Saint, we sing the Stichera of Great Vespers, with his verses; Glory: of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. After the Trisagion, Troparion of the Saint; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast; Little Litany, and dismissal.

At Great Vespers, we chant "Blessed is the man:" the first Glory. At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the feast 4, and of the Saint 4. If there be no Vigil, then Stichera of the feast 3, and of the Saint three; Glory: of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day. All the readings of the feast, and of the Saint. At the Litiya, Sticheron of the temple, and of the Saint the Idiomelon. We sing here also the Aposticha of the Saint from Small Vespers, three verses, if they were not sung at Small Vespers; Glory: of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. At the Aposticha of the feast, with verses; Glory: of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. At the blessing of the loaves, Troparion of the feast twice, and of the Saint once. Reading of the Saint: if an Apostle, then in the Apocalypse.[^2988] When there is no Vigil, after the "Our Father:" Troparion of the Saint; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast; and dismissal.

At Matins, at "God is the Lord," Troparion of the feast, twice; Glory: of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. After the Kathismata, Sessional Hymns and reading of the feast. If of an Apostle, then after each Kathisma the reading is also of the Apostle. Polyeleos, and all the Sessional Hymns of the Saint, both those after the first and after the second chanting; Glory: Sessional Hymn after the Polyeleos; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. His Theotokion, or one of the Sessional Hymns of the feast; and reading of the Saint: if of an Apostle, we read his Life. Anabathmoi, the 1st Antiphon of Tone 4; Prokeimenon of the Saint. "Let every breath;" and the Gospel of the Saint. "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ," Psalm 50, Sticheron of the Saint. Canon of the feast, Tone 4, with the Heirmos on 6, and of the Saint on 4; and the second Canon of the feast, Tone 8, on 4. Katavasia: the Heirmos of the latter Canon, both choirs together. After Ode 3, Kontakion and Ikos of the Saint, and his Sessional Hymn twice; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast; and reading of the Saint. After Ode 6, Kontakion and Ikos of the feast; and we read the Prologue. At Ode 9, we do not sing "More honorable." Exapostilarion of the feast; Glory: of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. At the Praises, Stichera of the feast, three; and of the Saint, three; Glory: of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast: Great Doxology. After the Trisagion, Troparion of the Saint; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. Litanies, the Catechesis of Theodore the Studite, and the customary procession, and the First Hour in the narthex. At the Hours, Troparion of the feast; Glory: of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion of the Hours; after the "Our Father," we alternate the Kontakia. At the Liturgy: the Beatitudes of the feast, Ode 3 on 4; and of the Saint, Ode 6 on 4. After the Entrance, Troparion of the feast, and of the Saint; Glory: Kontakion of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Kontakion of the feast. Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, Gospel, and Communion Hymn: first of the feast, then of the Saint.

*If the Great-Martyr George fall on the Sunday of the Samaritan Woman:*
The service of Mid-Pentecost is omitted, and there is sung the Resurrection service, and of the Samaritan Woman, and of Saint George.

## INSTRUCTION CONCERNING THE FEAST OF THE HOLY AND ALL-PRAISED APOSTLE AND EVANGELIST JOHN THE THEOLOGIAN[^2989]

It begins from Thomas Saturday, and ascends unto the Friday of the Week of the Holy Fathers.

It behooves to know: that if the feast of Saint John the Theologian fall on the Sunday of the Myrrh-bearing Women, or of the Paralytic, or of the Samaritan Woman, or of the Blind Man, and likewise on Wednesday of Mid-Pentecost:
See the whole church order in the Typikon of the Holy Great-Martyr George, for evening and morning, as was indicated previously.

## CONCERNING THE SAME FEAST, IF THE HOLY APOSTLE JOHN THE THEOLOGIAN FALL ON THE WEDNESDAY BEFORE ASCENSION, AT THE APODOSIS OF PASCHA[^2990]

On Tuesday evening at Small Vespers, Stichera of the Apostle on 4; Glory: of the Apostle; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the day. At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Apostle from Great Vespers, with their refrains; Glory: of the Apostle; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the day. Troparion of the Apostle; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. "All beyond comprehension;" Little Litany, and dismissal. But if there be no Vigil, at Compline we say the Kontakion of the Apostle; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of Pascha: "Though Thou didst descend into the grave, O Immortal One."

At Great Vespers: After the customary Psalm, we sing "Blessed is the man:" the 1st Antiphon. At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the Blind Man on 6, and of the Apostle on 4; Glory: of the Apostle; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the day: "Who shall declare;" Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day, and reading of the Apostle. At the Litiya, Sticheron of the temple, and of the Apostle, Idiomela; Glory: of the Apostle; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. "Behold, it is fulfilled." At the Aposticha, the Resurrection Sticheron, Tone 5: "Unto Thee, Who wast incarnate;" then the Stichera of Pascha with their refrains; Glory: of the Apostle; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of Pascha: "It is the day of Resurrection. And Christ is risen," once. At the blessing of the loaves, Troparion of the Apostle twice, and "O Virgin Theotokos, rejoice," once; and reading in the Revelation of the Apostle John. But if there be no Vigil, after "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart" and after the Trisagion, the Resurrection Troparion of the Tone; Glory: of the Apostle; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion; and dismissal. And we sing the Midnight Office according to custom. After the 1st Trisagion, instead of "Behold, the Bridegroom," we say the Resurrection Troparion: "The Word, co-beginningless;" Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. His Theotokion. After the 2nd, instead of "Remember, O Lord," the Kontakion of Pascha: "Though Thou didst descend into the grave;" after this: "Lord, have mercy," 12; and dismissal. But the prayers: "Remember, O Lord," we do not say.

At "God is the Lord," the Resurrection Troparion, twice, Tone 5: "The Word, co-beginningless;" Glory: of the Apostle; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. "All beyond comprehension." After the 1st Kathisma, the Resurrection Sessional Hymn, and reading. After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn of the Blind Man, and reading. Polyeleos, and all the Sessional Hymns of the Apostle once each, and reading. Anabathmoi, the 1st Antiphon of Tone 4. Prokeimenon of the Apostle; and: "Let every breath;" Gospel of the Apostle. "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ," Psalm 50, Sticheron of the Apostle. Canon of Pascha with the heirmos without Theotokia on 6, and of the Apostle on 4, and of the Blind Man on 4. We sing at each ode the Troparia of the Blind Man, two each; Glory: Triadicon; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion. Katavasia: Heirmos: "Unto God the Savior," both choirs together. (The Canon of the Forefeast is omitted here, and we sing it on Tuesday in advance.) After Ode 3, Kontakion of the Apostle, and Ikos; then the Hypakoe of Pascha: "They that anticipated the morning;" Glory: Sessional Hymn of the Apostle; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the Blind Man; and reading of the Apostle. After Ode 6, Kontakion of Pascha, and Ikos. At Ode 9, we do not sing "More honorable." Exapostilarion of Pascha; Glory: of the Apostle; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the Blind Man.

At the Praises, Stichera of the Apostle on 4. Then: "Let God arise;" and the Stichera of Pascha, with their refrains; Glory: of the Apostle; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of Pascha, Tone 5: "It is the day of Resurrection. Christ is risen," once. Great Doxology. Resurrection Troparion; Glory: of the Apostle; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. "All beyond comprehension." Litanies, and the Catechesis, and dismissal, and procession, and the First Hour in the narthex. At the Hours, the Resurrection Troparion; Glory: of the Apostle; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion of the Hours. After the "Our Father," we alternate the Kontakion of Pascha and of the Apostle.

At the Liturgy: the Beatitudes from the Canon of Pascha, Ode 3 on 4, and of the Apostle, Ode 6 on 4. After the Entrance, the Resurrection Troparion, and of the Apostle; Glory: Kontakion of the Apostle; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of Pascha. Prokeimenon and Alleluia of Pascha, and of the Apostle; and Gospel of the day, and of the Apostle. Communion Hymn: "The Body of Christ;" another: "Into all the earth."

## CONCERNING THE SAME FEAST, IT BEHOOVES TO KNOW: IF THE HOLY APOSTLE JOHN THE THEOLOGIAN FALL ON ASCENSION THURSDAY[^2991]

At Small Vespers, Stichera of the feast, Prosomoia 3, on 4; Glory: of the Apostle; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Apostle with their refrains, from Great Vespers; Glory: of the Apostle; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. Troparion of the Apostle; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast; Little Litany, and dismissal. But if there be no Vigil, at Compline Kontakion of the Apostle; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast.

At Great Vespers: "Blessed is the man:" the 1st Antiphon. At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the feast on 6, and of the Apostle on 4; Glory: of the Apostle; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day, and readings of the feast, and of the Apostle.

At the Litiya, Stichera of the feast, and of the Apostle; Glory: of the Apostle; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. At the Aposticha, Stichera of the feast with their refrains; Glory: of the Apostle; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. At the blessing of the loaves, Troparion of the feast twice, and of the Apostle once; and reading of the feast.

At "God is the Lord," Troparion of the feast twice; Glory: of the Apostle; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. After the Kathismata, Sessional Hymns of the feast, and reading. Polyeleos, and Sessional Hymns, and reading of the feast. Anabathmoi, the 1st Antiphon of Tone 4. Prokeimenon and Gospel of the feast. "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ," once; Psalm 50, Sticheron of the feast. Canon of the feast, Tone 5, with the Heirmos on 6, and of the Apostle on 4, and the other of the feast on 4. Katavasia: "Covered with divine protection," both choirs together. After Ode 3, Kontakion of the Apostle, and Ikos, and Sessional Hymn twice; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast; and reading of the Apostle. After Ode 6, Kontakion of the feast, and Ikos. At Ode 9: we do not sing "More honorable," but we sing the refrains of the feast; and to the Troparia of the Apostle: "Holy Apostle and Evangelist John the Theologian, pray to God for us." Exapostilarion of the feast; Glory: of the Apostle; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast.

At the Praises, Stichera on 6: of the feast 3, and of the Apostle 3; Glory: of the Apostle; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. Great Doxology. After the Trisagion, Troparion of the Apostle; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. Litanies, and the Catechesis, and dismissal. And holy oil is given to the brethren from the lamp of the Saint. And the customary procession, and the First Hour in the narthex. At the Hours, Troparion of the feast; Glory: of the Apostle; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion of the Hours. After the "Our Father," we alternate the Kontakion of the feast and of the Apostle.

At the Liturgy: the Typika; and from the Canon of the feast, Tone 5, Ode 3 on 4, and of the Apostle Ode 6 on 4. Entrance Hymn of the feast. Troparion of the feast, and of the Apostle; Glory: Kontakion of the Apostle; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, Gospel, and Communion Hymn: first of the feast, and of the Apostle. The service of Saint Arsenius is omitted, and is sung when the Ecclesiarch decides.

## CONCERNING THE SAME, IT BEHOOVES TO KNOW: IF THE HOLY APOSTLE JOHN THE THEOLOGIAN FALL ON THE SUNDAY OF THE 318 HOLY FATHERS[^2992]

The service of the Ascension is omitted, and there is sung the Resurrection service, and of the Theologian, and of the Holy Fathers. On Saturday at Small Vespers, the Resurrection Stichera on 4; Glory: of the Apostle, Tone 2: "The Son of Thunder;" Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion of Small Vespers. At the Aposticha, the Resurrection Sticheron. Then the Aposticha of the Apostle from Great Vespers, with their own refrains; Glory: of the Apostle; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion, according to the Tone. After the Trisagion, the Resurrection Troparion, and of the Fathers; Glory: of the Apostle; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast; Little Litany, and dismissal.

At Great Vespers: after the customary Psalm and after the Kathisma, at "Lord, I have cried," the Resurrection Stichera 3, and of the Fathers 4, and of the Apostle 3; Glory: of the Fathers; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion: the 1st of the Tone. Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day, and reading of the Fathers, and of the Apostle. At the Litiya, Sticheron of the Fathers, Tone 3, and of the Apostle, Idiomela; Glory: of the Apostle; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. At the Aposticha, the Resurrection Stichera; Glory: of the Fathers; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. At the blessing of the loaves, Troparion: "O Virgin Theotokos, rejoice," twice, and of the Apostle once; and reading. At "God is the Lord," the Resurrection Troparion, and of the Fathers; Glory: of the Apostle; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion. After the Kathismata, the Resurrection Sessional Hymns with their Theotokia; and reading in the Commentary Gospel. Polyeleos, and all the Sessional Hymns of the Saint, and reading of the Apostle. Anabathmoi, and Prokeimenon of the Tone. "Let every breath;" the Resurrection Gospel; "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ," Psalm 50, the Resurrection Sticheron, and the rest. The Resurrection Canon with the Heirmos on 4, and of the Apostle on 4, and of the Fathers on 6. Katavasia: "Covered with divine protection." After Ode 3, Kontakion of the Apostle, and Ikos, and Sessional Hymn of the Fathers; Glory: of the Apostle; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion; and reading of the Apostle. After Ode 6, Kontakion of the Fathers, and Ikos, and the Prologue. Exapostilarion: the Resurrection one, and of the Fathers; Glory: of the Apostle; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion. At the Praises, the Resurrection Stichera three, and of the Fathers 2, and of the Apostle with the Doxasticon 3; Glory: of the Fathers; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. "Most blessed art thou;" Great Doxology; the Resurrection Troparion; litanies, and the Catechesis, and dismissal, and the customary procession; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. The Gospel Sticheron;

and the First Hour in the narthex. At the Hours, the Resurrection Troparion; Glory: of the Fathers; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion of the Hours. After the "Our Father," Kontakion of the Fathers. At the 3rd Hour, the Resurrection Troparion; Glory: of the Apostle. After the "Our Father," we alternate the Kontakion of the Apostle and of the Fathers.

At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the Tone on 4, and of the Fathers Ode 3 on 4, and of the Apostle Ode 6 on 4. After the Entrance, the Resurrection Troparion, and of the Fathers, and of the Apostle. Then the Kontakion of the Fathers; Glory: of the Apostle; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, and Gospel: of the Fathers, and of the Apostle. Communion Hymn: "Praise the Lord from the heavens;" another: "Into all the earth."

## IF THE FINDING OF THE HEAD OF JOHN THE FORERUNNER FALL ON THE SUNDAY OF THE HOLY FATHERS, THE SEVENTH AFTER PASCHA[^2993]

The service of the feast of the Ascension is omitted, and there is sung the Resurrection service, and of the Forerunner, and of the Holy Fathers. On Saturday at Small Vespers, we sing as for the Theologian. At Great Vespers, after the customary Kathisma, at "Lord, I have cried," the Resurrection Stichera 3, and of the Forerunner 3, and of the Holy Fathers 4; Glory: of the Fathers; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Resurrection Theotokion of the Tone. After the Entrance, readings of the Fathers, and of the Forerunner. At the Litiya, Sticheron of the temple, and the Praises Stichera of the Forerunner; Glory: of the Fathers; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion. At the Aposticha, the Resurrection Stichera; Glory: of the Fathers; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion. At the blessing of the loaves, Troparia: "O Virgin Theotokos, rejoice," twice; of the Fathers, once. Reading in the Acts of the Apostles.

At Matins, at "God is the Lord," the Resurrection Troparion, and of the Fathers; Glory: of the Forerunner; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion. After the Kathismata, the Resurrection Sessional Hymns, and reading in the Gospel. Then the Polyeleos, and both Sessional Hymns of the Forerunner once each, without a Theotokion; Glory: Sessional Hymn after the Polyeleos; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion, and reading of the Forerunner. And the rest we sing at Matins, and at the Hours, and at the Liturgy, as for the Theologian.

It behooves to know: If the memory of the Finding of the honorable head fall on the Memorial Saturday of the Departed, or on the Sunday of Pentecost, we sing his service on Thursday of the Holy Fathers of the 7th Week.[^2994]

*And if the Finding of the honorable head of John the Forerunner fall on the Monday of Pentecost:*
We sing at Matins on Tuesday together with the festal service.

*If the Finding of the head of the Forerunner fall on Friday, at the Apodosis of the Ascension of Christ, and on the Saturday before the Sunday of All Saints, at the Apodosis of the Feast of Pentecost:*
We sing his service in order on Saturday, together with the Apodosis of the feast. On Friday evening, we sing "Blessed is the man:" the 1st Glory. At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the feast on 6, and of the Saint on 4; Glory: of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day, and 3 readings of the Saint. At the Litiya, Stichera of the feast, and of the Saint; Glory: of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. At the Aposticha, Stichera of the feast, with their refrains; Glory: of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. After the Trisagion, Troparion of the Saint; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast; and dismissal.

On Saturday, at Matins, at "God is the Lord," Troparion of the feast twice; Glory: of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. After the Kathismata, Sessional Hymns and readings of the feast. Polyeleos, and all the Sessional Hymns of the Saint; Glory: Sessional Hymn after the Polyeleos of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast, and reading of the Saint. Anabathmoi, the 1st Antiphon of Tone 4. Prokeimenon, and Gospel of the Saint, Psalm 50, and Sticheron of the Saint. Canon of the feast with the Heirmos on 6, and of the Saint on 4, and the other of the feast on 4. Katavasia of the feast. After Ode 3, Kontakion of the Saint, and Ikos, and Sessional Hymn of the Saint, twice; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast, and reading of the Saint. After Ode 6, Kontakion of the feast, and Ikos. At Ode 9, we do not sing "More honorable." Exapostilarion of the feast; Glory: of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast.

At the Praises, Stichera of the feast 3, and of the Saint 3; Glory: of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. Great Doxology; after the Trisagion, Troparion of the Saint; Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. Litanies, and dismissal, and the First Hour. At the Hours, Troparion of the feast; Glory: of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion of the Hours. After the "Our Father," we alternate the Kontakia of the feast and of the Saint.

At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the feast, Ode 4 on 4, and of the Saint, Ode 3 on 4. After the Entrance, Troparion of the feast and of the Saint; Glory: Kontakion of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. Prokeimenon, Alleluia, and Communion Hymn of the feast, and of the Saint; Epistle and Gospel of the day, and of the Saint.

*Concerning the same feast, it behooves to know: if the Finding of the honorable head fall on the Sunday of All Saints: we sing his service on Friday.*

*Or if of any great saint, for whom a Vigil is indicated in the Typikon:*
We sing the service of the great saint on this present Sunday of All Saints, as for John the Theologian on the Sunday of the 7th Holy Fathers after Pascha, in order with the Holy Fathers; so likewise is it sung here.

## IT BEHOOVES TO KNOW: HOW THE TRIODION IS SUNG WITH THE MENAION FROM THOMAS SUNDAY THROUGHOUT ALL PENTECOST, ON WHICH WEEKS, UNTO THE APODOSIS OF PENTECOST, SAVE SATURDAYS AND SUNDAYS, AT VESPERS AND AT MATINS[^2995]

For there precede at "Lord, I have cried," and in the Weeks of the Triodion, Stichera Idiomela, or Prosomoia, of the feast 3, and of the Saint from the Menaion 3; Glory: of the Saint, if there be one; but if not, Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. At the Aposticha, of the Triodion of the day.[^2996]

If two saints coincide, we sing the Stichera of the saints on 6; Glory: of the Saint; Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast.

If not: Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. But the Stichera of the feast from the Triodion we sing at the Aposticha with the refrains of the feast; Glory: of the saints, if there be one; but if not, Glory... Both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. Of the feast. For the Aposticha of the Triodion is not sung then.
